Though I spied naught else of note, closer scrutiny revealed that this machine is filled with remarkably elaborate bits!
Huge gears are attached to its arms and legs, and atop its torso are chimneys ceaselessly discharging steam!
‘Tis akin to a colossal factory given life and mobility, is it not? Quite the fetching specimen, if I do say so myself!
→ …? We’re letting the lass write this report? Are we okay with this? (Heathcliff)
→ I doubt she will attempt to ingest this entity. This will not be like the incident with the chickens. There is no need for concern. (Faust)

2. We had a kerfuffle with the machine!
Its approach was, as expected, to pound us using its large and hefty body!
Alas, there was one little aspect which I have failed to foresee…
Its assault of hot steam, exploding from its arm—chimneys!
High-pressure steam bombarded us, like water from a fireman’s water hose. ‘Twas hot enough that mine own eyeballs were thoroughly boiled to blindness!
Ah… and another detail to call thine attention to!
I believe its steam escalated in strength and heat the higher the numbers on its torso rose. I recall it vividly, as the time it took for mine eyeballs to thoroughly cook varied depending on the number!
→ I think the numbers represent the time we took to get here… The number on the machine was the same as the one we saw on the train. (Sinclair)
→ Interesting… We’ll have to hurry if we want to get out of this station. (Gregor)
→ Guys? Are we just going to ignore how the kid said it cooked her eyeballs off like it was nothing? Guys? (Rodion)

3. I scribble on, for I have further findings to share!
I witnessed the machine repair itself, though I understand not its exact workings.
Ah, and the number on its torso changed also!
Hohmm… ‘twasn’t that it released tiny machines to repair itself; it was as though it un—did the damages that had already transpired.
Ah! ‘Tis similar to how Manager Esquire revives us, is it not? Mayhaps I must inquire them to learn further!
→ Ohh… Is that why you requested a meeting? Sorry, but I don’t exactly know how my rewinding works, either… (Dante)
→ We do not have enough data to determine if any links exist between these two regeneration methodologies. I am unable to draw a conclusion at this time. (Faust)
→ Shattering its vacuum tubes seemed to prove effective against this entity. It was unable to reconstruct itself once they were destroyed. (Meursault)

entries.name: Sign of Roses
entries.content:
Sign of Roses (O-04-21-22) is a WAW-06 class Abnormality. 

It is the source of the E.G.O Garden of Thorns.

Sign of Roses is a lump of white flesh, covered in eyes of varying sizes and orientations. The eyes are bloodshot with small constricted red pupils. The flesh appears vaguely humanoid, with a visible head, though it lacks any sort of limbs.

A mass of thorny vines restrain the flesh onto a wooden X-shaped cross, or signpost. Red roses can be seen blooming from the vines, wrapping around both the signpost and flesh.

During combat, it is seen blooming roses of various colors corresponding to the seven sins. It also directly fights opponents using its vines.

Log(Written by Hong Lu):

1. Okay, let’s see~
So I gotta write about the weird, messy, rose—infested wooden planks?
My, my. I’ve not seen a more slapdash flower arrangement work in my entire life. Whoever made that thing should feel lucky they don’t work for my family.
Well… I guess every gardener has different standards of beauty. But from what I can see, I don’t really get what kind of beauty they were going for?
Like, the… the thing? Object? They hung in the middle of the wooden planks. I think it has eyes, or something.
Maybe they were trying to say something with this work. Like ‘Surveillance and Bondage’, or something?
Anyway, I don’t really enjoy artworks that are this hideous~
→ It’s all sunshine and rainbows with you, innit? Gardener? Piece of art? What is wrong with you? It’s a monster that skewers people! (Heathcliff)
→ Disagreed. T.I.A. (Someone scribbled ”I think she’s saying ‘This Is Art’!” here.) From grotesqueries rises artistic merit. I’m surprised that you caught on. (Ryōshū)

2. Its attack patterns…
I think it’s pretty similar to the apple—headed thing... oh, or the tree with aggressive roots that we met earlier in this train trip.
Oh, but I don’t think we’ve ever been slapped by a plank of wood that falls from the sky. I guess that’s what’s so special about this ugly thing.
As soon as we encounetered them, they tied us down here, like they were trying to stop us from going any further.

3. I had no idea… that getting wrapped up in those rose brambles could hurt that much.
Back home, I saw some people get roped up and made to kneel for their wrongdoings… I never realized how merciful my family was. We used plain ropes for that.
And those thorns… it was like they were draining my blood. Like it was hungry for nutrients.
And there’s more. You know how we sometimes… die, during these fights?
Bodies weren’t the only things falling—people’s resolve did, too. Oh, it’s not like being stressed or psychologically pressured. It’s completely different. It was like some… emotion in me was getting snapped in half.
And the way they died was also unusual. Its vines crawled up their legs, binding them… Soon blooming with Roses.
Oh, and... the color of those roses changed as well. Everyone told me that it was as though the bottled—up feelings inside them were melting away. And so did I.
And when we killed it… Everyone who fell in the battle exploded along with it.
Leaving behind nothing but… petals.

entries.name: Garden of Thorns
entries.content: Garden of Thorns is the name of the E.G.O for the Abnormality Sign of Roses. All the people that utilize this E.G.O wears a white robe with roses on parts of their body.

entries.name: Blubbering Toad
entries.content:
Blubbering Toad (T-01-23-04) is a ZAYIN-01 class Abnormality.

It is the source of the E.G.O Cavernous Wailing.

Blubbering Toad has the appearance of a giant, gray rock-colored toad with blue warts covering its back. It has two huge, blue bulging eyes that periodically dart around independently of each other. It is able to retract its eyeballs into its body, as well as extend them out of its eye sockets to attack opponents. The inside of its mouth is coated with a blue goopy substance and houses a long, thick blue tongue that is also covered with this substance.

Rather than croak, it makes crying noises which can be heard throughout the battle with it.

Log(Written by Ishmael):

1. It wasn't the most pleasant encounter.
You might say that this would apply to facing any Abnormality in battle, but this one just...felt unusual, somehow.
It was sitting languidly still and crying strange noises, looking like it had given up on everything.
The protruding blue eyeballs were shifting around with no confidence...
Yeah. It was kinda getting on my nerves. I thought I might go crazy if I had to hear its cry any longer.
I would rather just...
→ Is that the reason you swung your mace against the orders? I find it hardly convincing. (Outis)
→ Nah, I'm with her. I'd snap too if I kept listening to that bloody croak. 'Sides, we're supposed to beat those Abnormalities or whatever until they're eggs, aye? What's the problem here? (Heathcliff)
→ I, I thought so, too… I agreed it would've been better off to reduce it to an egg quickly… (Sinclair)
→ What's clockface on about now. They're ticking an awful lot. (Heathcliff)
→ …Executive Manager asks for some respect for salvaging you tools after you got yourselves killed in an idiotic charge. (Outis)

2. I think I've learned one thing.
I don't know how it came to attack its foes with its own eyeballs, but it looks like getting hit by it drains your energy (on top of it being incredibly gross).
…Does it? Gimme a moment.
Hmm… I asked a few other Sinners about this.
In conclusion… The more times you're hit by its tongue, the deadlier the eyeball seems to be.
I couldn't figure out further details, but I think it's safe to plan our tactics around avoiding its tongue, manager.
Which is good. It did not feel good to get hit.
→ Talk about a weirdo. It's not really tough at all, but it makes me feel all weak and drowsy~ (Rodion)
→ Really? I, I felt a little different… Doesn't it make you more gloomy than anything? (Sinclair)
→ Huh? How? (Rodion)
→ Like… Past memories popping up, or… Wanting to give up and die… (Sinclair)
→ …Um, Faustie? Looks like our kiddie needs some mental aid? (Rodion)

3. The left eye reduces health, and the right eye damages sanity.
So that's how they worked.
Well... Not like this changes the fact that it's best to avoid both.
In any case, we now know why dragging on doesn't do us any favor.
I felt like I was being dragged deeper into the swamp of gloom as the fight went on.
I suggest we make quick work of it with fast and powerful attacks, manager.
P.S. This just occurred to me...
I wonder what would've happened we just waiting until it's finished crying?
No, I'm not saying we should try it. I don't see it being efficient, either.
It's just... I remember someone doing the same for me a long time ago, and it helped me back then.

entries.name: Cavernous Wailing
entries.content: Cavernous Wailing is the name of the E.G.O extracted from the Abnormality Blubbering Toad. All the people that utilize this E.G.O wears Oriental armor and helmets seemingly made of the Abnormality's skin, with a blue cloth belt and shoulder decorations resembling the Abnormality's eyes. Both Sinclair and Hong Lu wields a staff topped by a ball of blue resin.

entries.name: Rising Ashes
entries.content:
Rising Ashes is an Abnormality.

Rising Ashes appears as a mound of gray ash with large, hollow gaps in the visage of a wailing face. From the sides of the mound's base, two long, ashen arms extend outwards and onto the ground.

entries.name: Four-hundred Roses
entries.content:
Four-hundred Roses (F-04-16-04) is a WAW-05 class Abnormality. It was presumably contained in the L Corp. Branch in P Corp. built on top of La Manchaland and later overtaken by the amusement park.

While it is not fought directly, a number of Bloodfiends and Fixers underwent E.G.O Corrosion while trying to utilize its E.G.O, and are encountered in the Canto VII dungeon.

It is the source of the E.G.O Yearning-Mircalla.

Four-hundred Roses has the appearance of a giant rose. The Abnormality possesses a pair of thin, crooked arms covered in thorns, almost as long as its stem (also thin, crooked, and thorns-covered). Numerous beady red eyes can be seen in the crevices between the large, dark petals of the flower, which is crowned with wilted, thorny sepals. A mouth rests in the center of the flower, lined with sharp teeth. A spring of blood can be seen dripping from the mouth.

Log(Written by Don Quixote):

1. The smell of blood is suffocating.

It looks like an average rose at a glance, indeed…

… but there are eyes glistening between each petal. Eyes with looks that I find familiar.

Glinting eyes of insurmountable desire, the eyes not so dissimilar from those of my blood-starved Family.

It desires not to slay, nor does it to harm. That creature… it merely yearns for blood.

I don’t suppose that flower was always such a beastly thing.

… Hah. It’s not like I’m in any position to pity that creature.

Hm. Let’s see what we’re working with… Shall it strike us with its vines? Yet such simple strategies will pose little to no risk to us.

Indeed, the red, blood-drenched petals most likely will utilize its sanguine resources to attack us. We will have to watch out for that angle.

Hm, how should I word these observations to naturally convey these findings to Manager Esq—

… Hold on. I-is this thing— Halt, hath this contraption already begun… recording?

Y-young Faust, I must bid thee a favor—perchance, wouldst thou avail me a chance to discard this record in favor of a new…

→ With good reason, yes. It is possible. (Faust)

→ Ooh! Then prithee, young Faust! A teeniest mistake was made here, on account of mine inexperience with this particular method of vocal recording. (Don Quixote)

→ Denied due to insufficient cause. This record will be maintained as-is. (Faust)

→ (Following are several dozen requests from Don Quixote to re-do this recording, every single one of them followed by Faust’s messages of denial.)

2. For-sooth! There was a battle of most epic proportions!

The beast seeketh in desperation to wound us!

‘Tis clear as the blue sky that this foe maketh use of spilled blood for the purposes of zapping us with them!

Alas, thus all would come to believe that it should be inadvisable to feed this terrible foe blood… yet I, Don Quixote, have devised an idea most splendid!

Heh heh. Gird thy loins, for I am to suggest a new strategy…

This foe… forsooth, it groweth increasingly docile by imbibing more blood!

Marry, 'tis plain that the creature may become slightly harder to slay, yet this appeareth to be a most wonderful opportunity to strike two birds with one stone; to protect our allies while bringing judgment to this evil Abnormality!

‘Twas quite the impressive display of intelligence, wouldst thou not say?

→ Uh, I think the creature’s becoming exceptionally harder to slay the more blood it drinks. (Ishmael)

→ Yeah… W-what if we just… put it down as fast as we can and not feed it any blood? (Sinclair)

→ Mm. However, the entity has been observed to become highly aggressive in lieu of blood. (Meursault)

→ Hm. Then we can feed it just the right amount of blood. How about that, fellas? Giving it so much blood was a pain anyway. (Gregor)

3. For-sooth! There was a battle of most epic proportions!

The beast seeketh in desperation to wound us!

‘Tis clear as the blue sky that this foe maketh use of spilled blood for the purposes of zapping us with them!

Alas, thus all would come to believe that it should be inadvisable to feed this terrible foe blood… yet I, Don Quixote, have devised an idea most splendid!

Heh heh. Gird thy loins, for I am to suggest a new strategy…

This foe… forsooth, it groweth increasingly docile by imbibing more blood!

Marry, 'tis plain that the creature may become slightly harder to slay, yet this appeareth to be a most wonderful opportunity to strike two birds with one stone; to protect our allies while bringing judgment to this evil Abnormality!

‘Twas quite the impressive display of intelligence, wouldst thou not say?

→ Uh, I think the creature’s becoming exceptionally harder to slay the more blood it drinks. (Ishmael)

→ Yeah… W-what if we just… put it down as fast as we can and not feed it any blood? (Sinclair)

→ Mm. However, the entity has been observed to become highly aggressive in lieu of blood. (Meursault)

→ Hm. Then we can feed it just the right amount of blood. How about that, fellas? Giving it so much blood was a pain anyway. (Gregor)

entries.name: Yearning-Mircalla
entries.content: Yearning-Mircalla is the name of the E.G.O extracted from the Abnormality Four-hundred Roses. All the people that use this E.G.O wear a long flowing red robe similar to a vampire's, their lower legs are turnedd into vines and they stand on top of thorny vines adorned with roses. The users also hold a bloody rose that constantly seeps with blood.

entries.name: Nymph
entries.content:
Nymph is an Abnormality.

Nymph resembles that of a fleshy, inhuman nurse. It possesses a chilling smile, however in place of its upper face the Abnormality's head opens to reveal a partially-missing brain lined with many teeth. It wears a classic white maid uniform, although tattered and dirty. Nymph's right arm is long and disfigured, wrapped in bandages, and ends in a large, four-pronged claw holding a decently sized pair of scissors. Its left arm, considerably closer to that of a normal human's, grasps onto an IV drip whose two liquid packs run through tubes into its body. Nymph's lower half is a disfigured jumble of vine-like flesh which wraps around the drip stand.

entries.name: Wailing Coffin
entries.content:
Wailing Coffin is an Abnormality.

Wailing Coffin is a bloodied wooden coffin that's tied shut with ropes that are adorned with yellow, red, blue and white ribbons. It has numerous dripping, blood-red arms reaching out through the crevices of the coffin lid, and many blood-red beetles swarm on and around the coffin.

entries.name: Paper Chairman
entries.content:
Paper Chairman is an Abnormality.

Paper Chairman is an Abnormality that takes the form of a tall humanoid with a yellow origami crane head. It wears a white dress shirt with red striped patterns and a black tie beneath a long, buttoned black coat with four gold buttons. Paper Chairman also wears a pair of long black pants, brown loafers, and a pair of black gloves that covers its hands. In its right hand, it holds a red cup adorned with a white rectangle pattern on the front side that's filled with steaming coffee. Five small yellow origami cranes are seen floating around Paper Chairman.

Two paper soldiers are seen accompanying the Chairman itself. The first paper soldier is colored blue, holding a one-handed sword on its right hand and a shield on its left hand. The second paper soldier is colored red, using both hands to hold a spear.

entries.name: Sunset Wayfarer
entries.content:
Sunset Wayfarer is an Abnormality.

Sunset Wayfarer appears as a large, orange, blob that glows with four short limbs on it. At the top of its body, it has a small spiral of yellow that appears to mimic a face. Floating around the entity are small moths with a similar color to the central Abnormality, and are the ones present in its E.G.O Gift.

entries.name: Tomorrow's Expression
entries.content:
Tomorrow's Expression is an Abnormality.

It is related to Today's Shy Look from Lobotomy Corporation.

Tomorrow's Expression has a humanoid upper body wearing a brown cloak with multiple, large spider-like legs stemming from under its cloak. Hanging from the underside of the Abnormality's body is a mass of mismatched eyeballs held by their optic nerves. Lastly, Tomorrow's Expression wears a flesh mask with a blank expression that is reminiscent of the faces worn by Today's Shy Look.

entries.name: Drunkard
entries.content:
Drunkard is an Abnormality.

Drunkard has the appearance of a man with a long braided beard with a fat gut and scrawny arms. It is wearing a brown cloak and a pair of trousers, and is seen holding and drinking booze from different containers, also wrapping its left arm around a flowing keg.

entries.name: Heavenly Executor's Scribe
entries.content:
Heavenly Executor's Scribe is an Abnormality.

It is the source of the E.G.O Pursuance.

Heavenly Executor's Scribe has the appearance of an angelic humanoid whose body is pale and stone-like with several cracks. A pair of eyes appear to be sculpted in its otherwise featureless face, though it has one big glowing yellow eye on its robe. The robe also contains writing of an unknown language, resembling hieroglyphics.

It holds a scepter in one hand while the other hand holds the Emerald Tablet "Lithograph" that acts as its E.G.O Gift. It also possesses a set of glowing bright yellow wings (though its E.G.O art depicts it with two sets of wings).

entries.name: Pursuance
entries.content: Pursuance is the name of the E.G.O for the Abnormality Heavenly Executor's Scribe. All the peple that utilize this E.G.O wear a heavenly gold and yellow jacket and robe covered with possibly scribes, black greaves, and a gold laurel crown. Additionally, ethereal golden wings sprout from their back.

entries.name: Wandering Mind
entries.content:
Wandering Mind is an Abnormality.

Wandering Mind is a featureless and armless statue-like humanoid, cracked in multiple areas. In place of the statue's chest is a gaping hole, where a black orb floats inside from the middle. Emerging from the statue's back are six long, black, tarlike arms.

entries.name: Monkey Tree
entries.content:
Monkey Tree is an Abnormality.

Monkey Tree appears as a tree with purplish-black wood that's devoid of any leaves. It takes root in a cracked, dry landscape. Some of its roots resemble hands trying to climb out of the ground.

The Abnormality likely is in reference of Canto XIII of Dante's Inferno. In the Canto, Dante and Vergil travel through the second ring of the seventh circle of Hell, which houses the violent against the self. In it, people who died by suicide are transformed into dark, leafless trees, and are tormented by Harpies. Dante's first interaction with one of the damned involves the poet snapping a twig from one of the trees, causing the twig to bleed and the soul trapped in it to scream out in agony.

entries.name: Hole-in-the-Man
entries.content:
Hole-in-the-Man is an Abnormality.

Hole-in-the-Man is an incredibly thin black humanoid with jagged limbs. It has a ragged head with no facial features, save for a white hole in the left side. It wears a black trench coat with eight white buttons with a luminous white zig-zag form near its left shoulder. In the Abnormality's right hand is a handgun.

entries.name: Blue-ish Star
entries.content:
Blue-ish Star is an abnormality.

It is related to Blue Star from Lobotomy Corporation.

It is an amalgamation of a blue crystal shard cluster surrounded by whitish-grey, doll-like legs radiating outwards in all directions. A small blue spherical light glints from a gap within the crystal cluster.

entries.name: Spider of Marriage
entries.content:
Spider of Marriage is an Abnormality.

Spider of Marriage consists of a feminine and masculine humanoid stitched together through their backsides. Both don near featureless, white masks; the man wears a traditional black suit and tie, while the woman wears a white wedding gown and veil. While they swap positions according to the event encounter, when the bride half is inactive, its arms rest unnaturally in the air with blackened, clawed hands. Both halves carry a wedding ring on the expected finger.

entries.name: Chattering Teeth
entries.content:
Chattering Teeth is an Abnormality.

Chattering Teeth is a trio of disembodied skulls with different expressions. One is laughing, the second appears angry, and the third has a deranged expression.

entries.name: Will You Play?
entries.content:
Will You Play? is an Abnormality.

Will You Play? has the appearance of a ghostly little girl with purple hair, a shrouded face, and a wide, creepy smile. Alongside the normal-appearing hair, her hair extends far behind her into an unkempt, scribbly black, bending to trail above the ground behind her knees instead of reaching the ground. She wears a white dress, with the bottom stained by a pink, bloodlike substance prominent on her legs and trailing from her feet. In her arms, she holds a big, crudely made purple doll with nails stuck in it.

entries.name: Children in the Flask
entries.content:
Children in the Flask is an Abnormality.

Children in the Flask is an intertwined meshing of glass chemistry flasks, conjoined into one construct. Tube sections that extend outwards are plugged with corks. The glass form is filled with a pink liquid composed entirely of personified droplets, each with their own faces and wills.

entries.name: All-Around Cleaner
entries.content:
All-Around Cleaner is an Abnormality.

It is related to All-Around Helper from Lobotomy Corporation.

All-Around Cleaner is a floating robot with a white, oval-shaped body. It has a pair of bright blue eyes and a happy smile. Three long, metal arms extend out from its body. Each arm is outfitted with a canister connected to a nozzle.

entries.name: Smokey Old Man
entries.content:
Smokey Old Man is an Abnormality.

It is related to Old Lady from Lobotomy Corporation.

Smokey Old Man is a gray-scale humanoid sitting in a gray-scale room, with the only splash of color coming from the landscape painting he stares fixated on. He has dark skin and wears a black suit and bowler hat, with pointy elf-like black shoes, a cane, and a white goatee. In his Mirror Dungeon event he is seen sitting on a small dark stool with a curled posture. Black smoke emanates upward from his back and shadow.

entries.name: Star Luminary
entries.content:
Star Luminary is an Abnormality.

It is related to Blue Star from Lobotomy Corporation.

Star Luminary is a headless humanoid with a gaunt figure. It wears a tattered cape and has six arms outstretched in a way that resembles a spiral galaxy, and a bright light akin to a star emits from its chest. In each of its hands, it holds a crystal ball.

entries.name: Centipede Apostle
entries.content:
Centipede Apostle is an Abnormality.

Centipede Apostle takes the form of a large, garbed centipede with an as-of-currently uncertain upper half, and what appears to be scribbled, bloody pages draped over its head. Other smaller yet sizable centipedes seem to writhe from out of the sleeves of its robe. The Abnormality dons a multitude of prayer books and booklets all over its body.

entries.name: The 4th Front of the Smoke War
keys: The 4th Front of the Smoke War
The Fourth Front of the Smoke War
Fourth Front of the Smoke War
entries.content:
The 4th Front of the Smoke War is an Abnormality.

It is based on the trauma of The Smoke War.

The 4th Front of the Smoke War takes the appearance of a serpent-like amalgamation made out of corpses of soldiers, wrapped and intertwined by barbed wire.
entries.comment: The 4th Front of the Smoke War

entries.name: Forsaken Employee
entries.content:
Forsaken Employee is an Abnormality.

It is related to Forsaken Murderer from Lobotomy Corporation.

Forsaken Employee resembles a humanoid wearing a red suit and tie, with a box of Enkephalin encasing its head and a rubber O-ring around its neck preventing any Enkephalin from spilling. Its body is completely wrapped in chains, binding the Abnormality's arms and legs.

It more specifically resembles an employee who worked at one of L Corp.'s branches. Following the completion of the Seed of Light Project, all of L Corp.'s branched initiated site burials, trapping the employees inside. Forsaken Employee appears to be a manifestation of how the employees felt abandoned and forsaken by the company.

entries.name: Heavenly Commander's Throne
entries.content:
Heavenly Commander's Throne is an Abnormality.

Heavenly Commander's Throne is a beast resembling a giant chameleon, with golden eyes like that of an insect's, gill-like extensions over its head, a large, thorny tongue, and a long, golden and ropelike tail ending in a large mechanical hand. The four quadrupedal limbs also have golden rings around them near their base beside the torso. Additionally, the top of its back has a massive eye with a brown iris. Most of the Abormality's skin is a silver color, though the underside is amber with black markings.

entries.name: Pagoda Veneration
entries.content:
Pagoda Veneration is an Abnormality.

It is the source of the E.G.O Wishing Cairn.

Pagoda Veneration has the appearance of a tall humanoid with stone-like skin wearing a hat, possibly a jeol-lip or jung-nip.

Its possesses six long spider-like limbs, four arms and two legs. The Abnormality is mainly seen hunched over, precariously stacking stones to make stone towers.

entries.name: Wishing Cairn
entries.content:
Wishing Cairn is the name of the E.G.O extracted from the Abnormality Pagoda Veneration. All the people who utilize this E.G.O sport a black hanbok with grey norigae and grey bandages that are wrapped around their arms and legs.

The method of attack usually consists of throwing pebbles at enemies. Yi Sang throws them along with knives while Don Quixote utilizes a sling for throwing pebbles.

entries.name: Time Duck
entries.content:
Time Duck is an Abnormality.

It is the source of the E.G.O Everlasting.

Time Duck is an amorphous entity mainly composed of a viscous, white liquid, vaguely in the form of a bird. Golden clockwork gears can be seen inside it, while clock faces are seen on its surface. According to its Mirror Dungeon Event, its form resembles that of both a duck and a rabbit.

entries.name: Everlasting
entries.content:
Everlasting is the name of the E.G.O for Time Duck, a non-fightable Abnormality in the Mirror Dungeon dungeon encounters.

Users of this E.G.O. will be dawned in a white, viscous and transparent garb adorned with golden gears, and a gear-like sword.

entries.name: Dimensional Oxidation Variant
entries.content:
Dimensional Oxidation Variant is an Abnormality.

It is related to Dimensional Refraction Variant from Lobotomy Corporation.

Dimensional Oxidation Variant typically has no visible appearance, though once put into darkness it can be seen as a fizzling figure, existing within the viewer's mind.

entries.name: Dimensional Orbit Stabilizer
entries.content:
Dimensional Orbit Stabilizer is an Abnormality.

Dimensional Orbit Stabilizer is composed of two individually-thinking segments: one is the transparent, tesseract-like shard with glowing edges and a nebulous blue mist in its center. Then are the three golden concentric rings surrounding the shard, with the middle ring perpendicular to the inner and outer rings.

entries.name: Tomb of Bone
entries.content:
Tomb of Bone is an Abnormality.

Tomb of Bone appears as a collection of assorted skeletal remains of creatures, both human and animal in appearance. The central design seen during its Mirror Dungeon Event appears as a hunched-over skeleton with large, protruding bones along its spin and a missing head besides its lower jaw.

entries.name: Funeral of a Dying Butterfly
entries.content:
uneral of a Dying Butterfly is an Abnormality.

It is related to Funeral of the Dead Butterflies from Lobotomy Corporation.

Funeral of a Dying Butterfly is a tall humanoid wearing a white buttoned-up shirt, black pants, shoes, and gloves. In its right arm it holds his suit jacket and in its left carries a plastic bag dripping blood. Though Funeral of the Dead Butterflies has five arms, Funeral of a Dying Butterfly possesses only three; its third one, wearing a black sleeve, protrudes from the base of its neck and holds a lit phone in its hand. The Abnormality's head resembles that of a newspaper opened and cut into the shape of butterfly wings.

entries.name: Der Fluchschütze
entries.content:
Der Fluchschütze, also known as F-01-16-13, is a HE-04 class Abnormality.

It is related to Der Freischütz from Lobotomy Corporation, and is the source of the E.G.O Fell Bullet.

Der Fluchschütze is a humanoid with a crimson colored, flamelike wispy head and glowing white eyes. The Abnormality is wearing soldier's attire with a beaten, torn cape, and wields a shotgun.

User's of the E.G.O dawn a similar outfit and weapon to the abnormality with some even having half their head becoming flamelike also.

Log(Written by Heathcliff):

1. Oi! So we’re makin’ audio logs now, eh? Fine by me! Great!

But I don’t know how this thing can record a word I’m sayin’ in this racket!

Ah, that fu— That crazy bastard won’t stop blasting his bloody gun in our direction! I can’t even hear myself think, shite!

Tsk… I suppose they’ll deal with the noise somehow in post. Here we go, I guess!

He’s got some bizarre smoke or fire or some shite burning from the head! Dressed in some soldier getup, too!

I've been listening to him blather on and on, and apparently he’s been in some kinda war or something!

I guess he’s goin’ for our heads, but that ain’t too unique of a thing, is it? Anyone going for the kill would go for the head anyways!

I do too, especially when I want to make sure they’re dead for good!

Doesn’t seem like the most complicated enemy, though! I can clearly see who that sod’s aiming for.

→ So, Heath, about famous last words… (Rodion)

→ Mm. Audio-to-text seems to be functional. Good work. (Faust)

→ Haah… yeah, whatever. I thought I knocked ‘em down when we clashed, so what the hell happened? (Heathcliff)

Observation: once targeted by the entity, its bullets will always strike the target regardless of the outcome of their clash.

→ Hoh? Then wherefore didst thou not simply evade the bullet?! (Don Quixote)

→ … You think I got shot in the face on purpose, lass?! (Heathcliff)

2. Speaking of which, I heard that the Abnormality’s bullet hit everyone around me, too when it killed me.

Buggy bloke tells me that he’s using something called a ‘shotgun’.

Apparently it makes up for its short range with a wider bullet spread that can hit more than one enemy at once, so… that must’ve been it.

Now that I think about it, this bastard went for the closest one to him first when choosing his target.

… Hm. It didn’t hurt much when he hit me from a distance.

We just gotta make sure that our heads are intact throughout the fight, yeah?

Wait, he just summoned some bughead outta nowhere. Where have I seen him before…?

Oh, no matter. I’ll focus on thrashing the bloke with the gun.

→ Yeah, so about second famous last words, Heath… (Rodion)

→ Huh. It’s summoning allies now… just to kill them? What? (Sinclair)

→ W-what the hell… He’s the old G Corp. Head Manager, isn’t he? What’s going on here? (Gregor)

→ This is the Refraction Railway. Therefore, he is most likely a reconstruction of a unit necessary for the Abnormality, taken from shards of the fathoms. (Faust)

→ … So he got dragged into another war, huh. Tsk. Even in death, he can’t… (Gregor)

3. Oi, did you all see that? How it acted after we told ‘em to check out his pendant?

He screamed, raged, then… kind of lost all steam.

It’s like all motivation drained right out of ‘em. Half-hearted shots, half-hearted defenses…

Dammit, why’d you even wear the pendant if you never wanted to remember them?

Well, that sure did make things simple for us, but… I don’t like this.

And before you say anything… I remember, Faust, Ms. smartarse. You’ve given me enough reminders.

He’s just an Abnormality, and Abnormalities’ stories aren’t worth lending my ear to.

Hah. It’s just… it’s not so easily said and done, you know?

I don’t think he knew when he said it. It’s not like he said it directly to my face, either.

All he said was that he still remembers the ones he loves.

… So… now that’s done and over with…

Remember how it blew my head to red paste early on?

It’s gotta mean that my memory’s just fine, right? Heh, and that’s… that’s not so bad, is it?

→ What? Uh… a-are you saying that you… liked the feeling of your head getting blown to bits? (Sinclair)

→ Huh? Yeah. If you wanna be technical about it, lad. (Heathcliff)

→ … But why? A fool you may be, but you are not one to revel in the Executive Manager’s suffering. (Outis)

→ What the hell are you prattling on about? Look, I ain’t saying that I like watching Clockhead suffer, it’s… (Heathcliff)

→ Young Heathcliff… ‘tis a foul habit to find joy in the suffering of others. (Don Quixote)

→ Agh! You’re all getting it wrong! Oi, manager! You know what I’m talking about here, don’t you?! (Heathcliff)

→ W-well, of course I do. But… (There was something written here, but it’s been hastily erased.) (Dante)

→ … Nevermind. Let’s talk about it later during the consultation. (Heathcliff)

entries.name: Sleeping Bag of a Bygone Day
keys: Sleeping Bag of a Bygone Day
entries.content:
Sleeping Bag of a Bygone Day, also known as T-03-16-15, is a TETH-03 class Abnormality.

It is comprised of two distinct parts: one being a skeletal entity with the body of an elongated ribcage, where the bottom half of the ribcage juts forward to wrap into a bony spiral, while part of a spine connects to the back of the ribcage from its top. The spine serves as the neck of a large, hollow human skull, with blood constantly leaking from its eye sockets. The other part of the Abnormality is the figure of a pitch-black, human-shaped shadow with completely red eyes, standing within the cavity of the skeleton's ribcage.

The Thoracalgia E.G.O is extracted from Sleeping Bag of a Bygone Day. The user is wrapped in a puffy white sleebing bag-like jacket with very long and large sleeves that drag against the floor, the jacket is also wrapped in black belts with half of the user's face being wrapped in a bandage at an angle. a giant floating ribcage surrounds the user and it's open from the front, the ribcage is sharpened and the "blades" can extend and drag people in. A piece of medical equipment used for breathing also floats behind the user with a mask similar to the one used in a nebuliser machine hanging off one of the fluid bags on the equipment. For some user's of the E.G.O the belts are gone and the jacket is open.

Log(Written by Outis):

1. Performing the post-mortem report as ordered by the Executive Manager.

The entity was encountered around 1040 hours today.

It assumes the form of a gigantic skull, which explains our ease of identifying this enemy.

(Heavy breathing) The size of the skull is rather intimidating, and it features what appears to be a support of sorts that looks like a spine surrounded by ribs.

Though I may be making a rather large leap in logic here… (Heavy breathing) it can be assumed that the rest of its shape is not so dissimilar to that of human bone structure.

Initially, we had attempted to exploit the equivalents of the usual weaknesses identified on human bodies based on this similarity. However…

… once we observed its extendable spine (Heavy breathing) and morphing of its ribs into arm or wing-like forms, the plan was immediately discarded.

Once again, it holds true that(Heavy breathing) tactics based on the normal understanding of the common senses(Heavy breathing) are not always useful against these monsters. It wasn’t all for nothing, however.

In the process of analyzing this foe, we were able to identify a dark entity of humanoid figure within its body(Heavy breathing). While its exact functions are yet to be identified, our current assumption leads us to believe that it may be the entity’s main form, or its core.

I presume that its means of aggression will primarily prioritize attacks of physical nature using its bone structures, but… on account of the lack of evidence, I cannot say for certain.

Any missing information will be(Heavy breathing) supplemented by subsequent observations; please consult this guide in your(Heavy breathing) future commands.

Thank you.

→ Damn… by the book as always. How'd you even bring your whole template to a voice recording? (Rodion)

→ Easily. It is a skill to be expected from those in service of the Executive Manager. (Outis)

→ Yeah, I bet… Take some time to breath though, huh? There was a distracting amount of ‘Heavy breathing’ in this report. (Rodion)

→ Hmph. Must be the nervous breathing of inexperienced chicks. I, Outis, do not let such simple reports take my breath away. (Outis)

→ I-it wasn’t me. It’s been coming from that skull the moment we found it… (Sinclair)

→ Hmm. It has not the lungs nor the trachea, yet it breathes. Through where does its air travel, one wonders—how utterly bizarre. (Yi Sang)

2. We engaged with the entity in a meaningful capacity around 1100 hours today.

Its first actions in battle were to attempt to strike us physically using its bones. Just as we had expected.

Its most prominent form of attack involved extending its spine to maul its foes with its sizable jaws. However, another, unexpected form of attack was also observed.

It intermittently lets out a breath. The exhale carried an extraordinary level of shock and air pressure that dealt rather significant damage to any Sinners who were caught directly in its blast radius.

Our allies are far from the most reliable martial force, but a numerical disadvantage may easily lead to fatal results; please do take this advice into account.

However… it does not seem that this entity requires a high level of strategizing to defeat. Maintaining high pressure should be more than enough.

Another thing to keep in mind: after some time, it released a large volume of ‘air’ by exhaling.

The ‘air’ seemed to improve the poise of whomever breathed it in, enhancing the keenness of their attacks. This is when the shadow entity within the skull began to mobilize, attempting to steal the ‘air’ from all those who had it.

Various strategies were attempted to stop this process, but they were to no avail.

The most optimal, and the only strategy against losing this air would be to ensure that every unit individually resist the entity to the best of their abilities.

The entity’s attacks became highly augmented once it inhaled a large volume of this air; preventing this outcome must be the primary objective of this battle.

Concluding the report.

Thank you.

→ Recognition of 'Heavy breathing' was disabled in this report for the sake of legibility. However, the ‘Heavy breathing’ records of the previous report will not be removed in service of enhancing the sense of realism of the earlier report. (Faust)

→ Oh, yeah. The shadowy humanoid dragged Gregor in earlier… are you okay? (Sinclair)

→ … It’s not a good time, fellas. I thought the thing was tearing me apart limb from limb. (Gregor)

3. I write to inform you that further intel has been gathered during our encounter with the entity.

It was learned that, upon losing its ribs, the entity begins to prepare a highly fatal attack.

However, with the elimination of its protective skeleton, its defenses become highly porous, meaning that it became much more susceptible to our assaults.

On the other hand, while not destroying the ribs would inevitably lead to a prolonged battle, it would save us the trouble of having to come up with countermeasures against highly dangerous attacks.

Mm. This moment calls for a strategic judgment call.

I have faith in the Executive Manager that, as they have always done, they would come up with an excellent decision that takes the entity’s behaviors and other battlefield factors into account.

Thus, I leave this part of the battle to the Executive Manager’s brilliant strategic mind.

Concluding the report.

Thank you.

→ Cool… thanks. (Dante)

→ Is it just me, or does Dante seem a lot less… enthusiastic when replying to Outis? (Rodion)

→ No, no… that’s not what’s happening here! I’m very enthusiastic. (Dante)

→ Your alienation tactics will fail to drive even the smallest wedge between the Executive Manager and myself. Your efforts are for naught. (Outis)

→ No… I don’t think that’s what she’s trying to do either. Anyways, I want you to know that I really do appreciate these detailed reports… (Dante)
entries.comment: Sleeping Bag of a Bygone Day

entries.name: Overdue Assignments
entries.content:
Overdue Assignments is an Abnormality.

Overdue Assignments is a grand collection of paper sheets clumped together in the shape of a rearing serpentine monster. This worm-like figure possesses a single glowing red eye at its "head". Various sheets of paper fly in a circular whirlwind about the creature's base as the gusts of wind disrupt the looming stacks of paper surrounding it.

entries.name: Handshake of Handshakes
entries.content:
Handshake of Handshakes is an Abnormality.

Handshake of Handshakes is a huge stone hand. At the tip of each of the Abnormality's fingers is another normal sized hand with gilded fingernails. The middle finger is wearing a gold-and-black wrist guard just before its smaller hand, and the middle of that hand's palm has a structure with the same golden metal as on the wrist guards, forming a triangle with an eye in it and a vertically slit pupil.

entries.name: Centaur
entries.content:
Centaur is an Abnormality.

It bears a striking resemblance to Nymph.

Centaur resembles a nurse with a face bandaged with its own flesh. It wears a normal nurse's white blouse and hat, however its skirt is ripped where the Abnormality's lower body extends into the rusty frame of a hospital bed. Centaur's upper body possesses arms extending from its torso, with the right arm holding a massive pair of metal scissors, and the left arm extending into a giant, long three-pronged claw. Flesh melds with the legs of Centaur's bed, with hands replacing the stems and mounts of the bed's caster wheels. On the left rear side of the bed frame, an IV stand holding three skulls on one side and a blood pack on its other sticks outwards. From the blood pack, a tube siphoning blood coils down the IV stand, sticking back up into the left side of the nurse's head.

entries.name: Hydra
entries.content:
Hydra is an Abnormality.

Hydra takes the form of seven crazed surgeon heads with extensive fleshy necks coming together at the base of a large stethoscope. Two smaller stethoscopes extend out from the sides. Behind the Abnormality's front lies a large, strong light which the creature appears to be attached to. The surgeon's heads and necks, as well as the stethoscope base, are messily slathered in blood.

entries.name: Sleepyhead
entries.content:
Sleepyhead is an Abnormality.

Sleepyhead is a wooden construct resembling a drinking bird toy in the shape of the front half of a giraffe. In place of the beak is spiky metal stained with blood, and there is a blood-soaked clear tube poking out from its body that connects the beak to the tail.

entries.name: Golden Grip
entries.content:
Golden Grip is an Abnormality.

Golden Grip is a gray-skinned humanoid Abnormality that has its head stuck inside an ornate, golden urn. Because of this, it appears upside down, with the urn placed on the ground. Its limbs appear to be jagged, and its chest has a gaping maw with various spikes around the rim.

entries.name: Highway Devotee
entries.content:
Highway Devotee is an Abnormality.

Highway Devotee is a tall humanoid wearing an oversized brownish-green cloak, its body consisting of upwards of eighteen bald, gray and emotionless heads stacked neatly upon one another. It possesses long and thin gray arms outstretching from somewhere within the cloak. The Abnormality holds up a wooden milepost in its right hand.

entries.name: Broken Wings
entries.content:
Broken Wings is an Abnormality.

Broken Wings takes the appearance of a tall winged statue, with a short-haired head and arms formed out of a golden, translucent light unlike the rest of the marble body. Piercing its right hand is a trumpet being blown, and piercing its left, a sword that is tip-first into the ground, supported in a resting state behind the statue's side, with its open resting palm in the sword handle. Both instruments are also formed from the same golden light.

entries.name: Cyclops
entries.content:
Cyclops is an Abnormality.

Cyclops is a towering, bulky humanoid with peachy-gray skin, parted black hair, and stubble with a cigarette in its mouth, wearing a light blue button-up shirt and jeans. There is a long chain of wristwatches wrapped multiple times around the Abnormality's arms, with the link connected between the arms held by both hands, alongside a brown briefcase in its left hand. The Abnormality has a single bloodied eye, with what appears to be either a writing utensil or spike stabbed in from the back end.

entries.name: Clockwork-Time-Roly-Poly
entries.content:
Clockwork-Time-Roly-Poly is an Abnormality.

It is the source of the E.G.O Asymmetrical Inertia.

Clockwork-Time-Roly-Poly appears as a large mass of brass gears and clock parts, mostly contained in a metal casing in the shape of a bell with an opening at the front, giving it the appearance of a cloak. A wooden head with the shape of a cuckoo wall clock is mounted upon the bell via a golden metal stand, featuring a yellow human eye in place of the clock face, framed by three golden gear half-circles: one smaller half-circle to the right of the eye, and two both above and below, resembling eyelashes.
Numerous silky red strings or blood vessels lead from the eye and can be seen emerging from the back of the head. Bundles of the strands are also tied to the stand supporting the head, dangling to the floor below the otherwise floating Abnormality.

Asymmetrical Inertia's dawns the user in an old brown victorian suit, their arm becoming a mess of different sized golden gears and red ribbons. They're also given a monocle

entries.name: Explorer on a Bereaved Road
entries.content:
Explorer on a Bereaved Road is an Abnormality.

This Abnormality appears as a frozen, several-headed, collective of corpses dressed in hiking gear, with many arms emerging from the primary body that point in several different directions.

entries.name: Resident of Metropolaris
entries.content:
Resident of Metropolaris is an Abnormality.

Resident of Metropolaris appears as a silver and gold machine with a long, pointed silver torso with gold vertical stripes and silver arms with pointed ends. Its back has a circular piece of steel that has two upwarsds pointed tips on either side. Atop its body is a head with four gold eyes and a front-facing ring of pointed steel.

entries.name: Basilisoup
entries.content:
Basilisoup is an Abnormality.

It is the source of the E.G.O Lifetime Stew.

Basilisoup has the appearance of a basilisk, or cockatrice. Its white skin, which appears to lack any feathers, is seen to be tearing at places, seeping out soup.

It has a long neck which connects to a bronze cauldron that serves as its head, complete with a comb and wattle. The bottom of the cauldron is split open, giving it the appearance of a beak. The cauldron is filled with the same soup from its body, spilling out from its mouth.

Basilisoup also possesses a pair of large dragon wings, and what appears to be a long reptilian tail.

entries.name: Lifetime Stew
entries.content: Lifetime Stew is the name of the E.G.O for Basilisoup. All the people that utilize this E.G.O don a medieval-esque mix of chef's costume with brass shoulder pads and gauntlets with a chef's hat and waist apron.

entries.name: Sandolph
entries.content:
Sandolph is an.

It is related to Rudolta from Lobotomy Corporation.

It is the source of the E.G.O Holiday.

Sandolph appears to be a massive, bulky Abnormality with piercing eyes held open by stiches, with a bright red nose between them. Atop its head are two small Santa caps on the opposite sides. Sporting only a upper jaw, a large white beard lines the head. Sandolph's skin is made up of patchwork pieces of green and red cloth layered onto graying red skin beneath, along with a coat of white fur attached to its skin. In its E.G.O portraits, it appears to hold a large black sack.

Holiday is the name of the E.G.O for Sandolph. All the people that utilize this E.G.O wears patchy winter attire sewn together from pieces of white, green, and red leather and a Santa hat, and uses a black gift sack dripping with blood and decorated with golden ribbons and bells as a weapon.

entries.name: Cozy Bed
entries.content:
Cozy Bed is an Abnormality.

It is the source of the E.G.O Christmas Nightmare.

Cozy Bed appears to be a wooden bed, laid with thick winter sheets and covers in a predominantly red and green color scheme. The frame of the bed is decorated with Christmas ornaments, including stockings and garlands. An unknown entity, comprised of numerous colorful eyes, sharp teeth, and possibly red-and-green tentacles, resides under the bed.

Due to the fact that the bed looks different in all its appearances, it's possible that the Abnormality is the entity lurking within rather than the bed itself.

User's of the E.G.O dawn a christmas themed outfit / night garb with hidden monstrous parts that stick out under the flowing robes they were given, the form of the monstrous parts depend on the user, e.g for ishmael it's candy-cane coloured tentacles and for Gregor it's a christmas coloured insect arm / mandible.

entries.name: Stats
entries.content:
The employees have a different list of Stats. The 'Stat Levels' of the Agents, which can be seen in their info, are divided into 4 main Stats referred to as Virtues: Fortitude, Prudence, Temperance, and Justice. The levels of these Virtues can be improved by performing the works: Instinct, Insight, Attachment and Repression.

Fortitude: Fortitude is a Virtue which represents itself as a level and determines the Health stat. The stats of this level can be increased by performing Instinct Instinct work. This feature is used by Abnormalities and E.G.O. Equipment to limit or target employees of a certain level.

Health: Health, Max Health or Max HP, is the amount of Red Damage, Black Damage or Pale Damage that an Agent can take before reaching zero.

Prudence: Prudence is a Virtue which represents itself as a level and determines the amount of sanity a person has.

SP: The Sanity Points, Sanity Gauge, SP or Max SP, is the amount of White Damage or Black Damage that an Agent can take before reaching zero. When this gauge is completely depleted, the Agent will enter a state of Panic, acting according to their Panic response and becoming uncontrollable. Other agents must suppress the panicked employees with white or black damage to heal the sanity of a person. When using E.G.O, low sanity can cause E.G.O corrosion.

Temperance: Determines the success rate and speed of work done.

Justice: Determines attack and movement speed.

entries.name: Abnormality Physiology
entries.content:
Abnormalities are beings born from the subconscious of mankind. While natural examples of Abnormalities exist, a vast majority of them were created by Lobotomy Corporation itself by taking the "Light" deep within humanity and manifestating it physically. In all cases, Abnormalities originate from the "Well of Humanity", the realm containing the collective unconscious of humanity.

Their shape and powers vary wildly, but they generally take the form of monsters, supernatural humans or anomalous objects. Regardless of their appearance, all Abnormalities possess a will and some degree of human emotion, as they come from the human mind and usually represents a repressed desire.

Weakened Abnormalities inside of their book should have:

1. Superhuman Physical Characteristics (All of the weakened Abnormalities should minimally be capable of fighting superhuman fixers).
2. Immortality.
3. Limited Abstract Existence (Type 2; Their true selves exist as mental concepts. While they can survive their body being destroyed, they cannot regain a physical form after this without the immortality granted by Angela).
4. Acausality.
5. Resistance to: Information Analysis (Should have similar properties to Distortions, meaning they cannot be analysed).

Weakened Abnormalities outside of their book should have:

1. Abstract Existence (Abnormalities in this state exist solely as mental concepts. They can only interact with the physical world through the Distortion phenomenon).
2. Incorporeality.
3. Mind Manipulation, Empathic Manipulation & Morality Manipulation (Abstract Abnormalities can inhabit the mind of some psychologically unstable people. Their prolonged existence inside the mind of others can twist their emotions and mindset to resemble the desire the individual Abnormality incarnates).
4. Transformation (An individual drawing too much power from an Abnormality that has inhabited them will be changed physically, up to and including being completely turned into the Abnormality in question).
Creation (A person with an Abnormality inside of them can draw from their power and create E.G.O. weapons or armor out of them).
5. Acausality.
6. Resistance to: Information Analysis.

Abnormalities at their peak should have:

1. All of the previous, excluding Abstract Existence, Incorporeality, Dimensional Travel and Teleportation plus:
2. Immortality (Type 2; Abnormalities are stated to be unable to die even after losing a head or spinal cord, and are shown to be capable of casually moving and fighting even after losing parts of their body)
3. Limited Transformation (The shape of Abnormalities can change over time through unknown mechanisms, but implied to be related to perception)
4. Abstract Existence (Abnormalities are physical manifestations of archetypes from humanity given physical form. They are very similar to Ordeals and can survive being reduced to a non-physical state should they run out of energy, existing solely mentally)
5. Resistance to:
6. Mind Manipulation, Madness Manipulation, Morality Manipulation, Fear Manipulation & Perception Manipulation (All Abnormalities are immune to the passive fear aura of Abnormalities, even CENSORED's, and are incapable of entering a panic state even after being hit by attacks that reduce sanity)
7.Limited Resistance to:

Power Nullification (Abnormalities can, over time, overpower Qliphoth Deterrence and escape, which would usually weaken and pacify them. More powerful Abnormalities can do it in far shorter time periods, only requiring slight mistakes by Employees to escape)

entries.name: E.G.O
entries.content:
E.G.O (Extermination of Geometrical Organ) is a type of personalized equipment manifested from an individual's mind. They usually take the form of massively powerful weapons and/or armor.

There are two main types of E.G.O: E.G.O extracted and borrowed from an Abnormality, and E.G.O manifested by oneself. Limbus Company Sinners makes use of the former.

Abnormality E.G.O: This refers to the E.G.O that was extracted and borrowed from Abnormalities by Lobotomy Corporation in various forms, with further detail for L Corp.'s usage below. Limbus Company has also been able to extract this type of E.G.O as well through the Mirror. It also utilized within The Library in the same manner, extracted from Realizing each librarian's floor, likely sourced from the Library's unique connection to the Abnormalities.

Lobotomy E.G.O: The term “Lobotomy E.G.O” was first coined with the names of Technology Liberation Alliance members who were able to extract the E.G.O Gear from Abnormalities contained in one of L Corp.'s branches.

It is a refined form of E.G.O more akin to regular equipment that has been compressed for general utility. While its capabilities and power are more limited in comparison to regular E.G.O, it is also more stable, allowing the user to wield it for extended durations without being affected by corrosion.

LCE E.G.O: LCE E.G.O refers to the E.G.O extracted and utilized by Limbus Company's LCE department. It is largely comparable to Lobotomy E.G.O in way of its form and function, given that the LCE aims to copy and surpass much of the fallen Lobotomy Corporation's work. Like L Corp., the gear is composed of Weapons and Suits. However, there are still distinguishing features. In Faust's ID story, Carmen describes the LCE's E.G.O attunement to be "closer to the usage of actual E.G.O [compared to the] E.G.O gears of Lobotomy Corporation."

LCE E.G.O allows for a higher rate of attunement and synchronization with the relevant Abnormality, which can be deliberately achieved through extending understanding and empathy towards it. This allows for more impressive benefits than L Corp. had been able to achieve with its E.G.O, such as flight and shape fluctuation. Additionally, LCE E.G.O gear can cause its user to sprout inhuman features like tails. Yi Sang's LCE Identity, for example, depicts him as having sprouted twigs from his head. His evade sprite also shows that it is even possible to completely change one's form in tune with the Abnormality.

However, regulating one's level of synchronization with the LCE E.G.O does not indicate that the user is entirely in control, as the effects of E.G.O Corrosion are still inevitable. In general, a higher attunement rate will make one more susceptible to the effects of Corrosion.

Origin: Before the events of Lobotomy Corporation, Carmen had been researching Cogito in the interest of the Seed of Light Project. Along the way, her and her team discovered the existence of Abnormalities, the means of creating them, and the existence of E.G.O. The very first Abnormality-extracted E.G.O was the Mimicry sword the Red Mist would become famous for wielding.

The team did not have an immediate grasp of how E.G.O functioned; Carmen would describe the weapon as unstable, saying that it was a miracle they had been able to extract it at all. However, they would come to understand it well enough by the time Ayin took over L Corp. Under A's foundership, employees would regularly yield the E.G.O which had been extracted from the Abnormalities by Binah and the aptly-named Extraction Team.

Following the White Nights and Dark Days and later The Library's exile from District 12, collapsed Lobotomy Corporation branches became available for scavenging. This allowed for the stealing and use of their old Abnormality-issued E.G.O by random factions.

Function: Lobotomy E.G.O's most attractive benefit is its malleability. It can be used effectively by anyone and requires no special training to wield. This allowed for the average Lobotomy Corporation employee to skillfully contest threats, despite the job not requiring any combat ability.

The E.G.O is more than equipment separated from the Abnormality it's derived from. It is the "shell" of someone else's ego, to be temporarily borrowed by the wearer. As such, when a person uses Lobotomy Corporation E.G.O, they are essentially synchronizing with the Abnormality it originated from. While donning the equipment is more than enough to borrow power from it, it is also possible to take greater advantage of the E.G.O by taking the power and claiming it as one's own. This was, in Binah's words, something the L Corp. employees were incapable of, and the achievement which made the Red Mist so strong.

Lobotomy Corporation called the extracted armor "E.G.O Suits" and the extracted weapons "E.G.O Weapons". Although E.G.O Suits varied considerably in color and design, all of them had an upper body garment reaching past the waist, and (with four exceptions) included a collar and a tie. E.G.O Weapons could be both melee and ranged, ranging from gauntlets to cannons.

Additionally, there was a third tool to gain from the Abnormalities called "E.G.O Gifts". As the name implies, E.G.O Gifts could be considered a literal present from the Abnormalities. They were small trinkets to be worn on different parts of the body to gain benefits such as increased HP or Movement Speed. In Limbus Company, they possess a wider variety of benefits and are available to collect in dungeons. Though E.G.O Gifts are weaker than Suits and Weapons, they are still a part of the ego pertaining to Abnormalities, and run the risk of negatively affecting someone who wears too many.

entries.name: E.G.O Corrosion
entries.content:
E.G.O borrowed from an Abnormality possesses one major drawback in the possibility of losing one's self to the equipment. This phenomena is known as E.G.O Corrosion, where the user's appearance and behavior transform to reflect the personality and destructive nature of the Abnormality the E.G.O originated from.

While the synchronization between the E.G.O and its user represents the key advantage of E.G.O over other City gear, it also allows for the user to have their ego overridden by it. If insufficient in mental strength, they may "fuse" with the equipment when lacking the personal virtues of Prudence, Fortitude, Temperance, or Justice (as measured in Lobotomy Corporation) required to stave off the metamorphosis. This can also occur if the user undergoes severe mental degradation while using the E.G.O.

During the process of using E.G.O, the individual will hear the voice of the Abnormality it had come from. To "Corrode" is to allow the voice and its mindset to take over, replacing the user's ego with its own. Alongside the loss of self, corroding also incites a physical transformation. This turns its victims into beasts not dissimilar to Distortions.

E.G.O Corrosion is seen in-game, where the Sinners may corrode from repeated usage of Abnormality E.G.O or when reaching low levels of Sanity. Canto III also demonstrates the result of several members of the N Corp. Inquisition voluntarily undergoing Corrosion.

entries.name: Effloresced E.G.O
entries.content:
This refers to the E.G.O that is personally manifested and wielded by the same individual, which became associated with Distortions following the White Nights and Dark Days.

The term “Effloresced E.G.O” was first coined in the name of Dongrang's Farmwatch E.G.O.

Origin: Manifesting Effloresced E.G.O was possible even before the White Nights and Dark Days. However, it was rare to the point of even Arbiters of the Head being unfamiliar with how it worked.

Special as she was, Kali the Red Mist was not only the first known wielder of Abnormality-extracted E.G.O, but also of personally manifested E.G.O. She received the former first (the Mimicry greatsword), given to her from Carmen. Extended use of the E.G.O eventually put her at high risk of undergoing E.G.O Corrosion. When Kali managed to fight off the corrosion, expanding her ego onto the sword instead of the other way around, she manifested her own E.G.O in the form of full-body black armor with glowing red highlights. It was the wielding of these two types of E.G.O, previously more or less unknown to the City, that allowed the Red Mist to fare so well against the Head during their attack on Carmen's lab. There are no other known cases of someone manifesting E.G.O before the White Nights and Dark Days.

Library of Ruina elaborates that Lobotomy Corporation's Seed of Light Project intended to allow everyone in the City to manifest their own E.G.O. The idea was to make it widely permissible, instead of manageable to only a select few such as Kali. In theory, this would give all citizens a proper means to protect themselves, eliminating meaningless deaths in the City. Angela's decision to take the Light for herself and the subsequent aftermath stopped this plan from coming to fruition, however.

Researchers Carmen and Ayin became one with the Light not long before this. Carmen's position in the Light would allow her to watch over the City (and all versions of it across different Mirror Worlds) and reside over both the E.G.O and Distortion phenomena. She would ultimately choose to embrace Distortions as the ideal form of humanity and attempt to distort Cityfolk by her own hand. As such, after the White Nights and Dark Days, manifesting Effloresced E.G.O would be a matter of denying Carmen's temptations.

Function: Effloresced E.G.O is distinct and personal from person to person. While Abnormality-extracted E.G.O will reflect the ego of the relevant Abnormality, E.G.O manifested by oneself will match their ego. As a result, they vary widely in both appearance and function. Generally, manifested E.G.O takes the form of some kind of armor, weapon, or both. It compliments the individual rather than overtaking them.

Like the other form of E.G.O, Effloresced E.G.O is extremely powerful. However, it represents familiarity and dominance over one's own ego, rather than the borrowing of someone else's. It can still be wielded in ways which farm more power from it, like Lobotomy E.G.O. Additionally, once having manifested E.G.O, it can be manifested again at any point, on will. Kali describes having to "get used" to her Effloresced E.G.O over time, learning how to use it for longer periods and draw out its full strength.

Ayin and Angela's personal E.G.O are notable outliers to the usual weapon/armor, having instead manifested entire buildings from their mind, and pertaining to even greater possibilities. In Ayin's case, it was the Lobotomy Corporation headquarters, and in Angela's, the Library.

Once someone has managed to manifest E.G.O, they gain an immunity to the Distortion Phenomenon.

Volatile E.G.O: It is also possible to manifest E.G.O partially. This is referred to as Volatile E.G.O.

Volatile E.G.O manifests upon denying Carmen without full commitment, and allowing one's heart to waver. Manifesting Volatile E.G.O does not count as proper manifestation, and will not give the individual immunity to the Distortion Phenomenon like Effloresced E.G.O will.

entries.name: E.G.O Vs Distortions
entries.content:
Following the White Nights and Dark Days, E.G.O became intrinsically linked to the Distortion Phenomenon. Both phenomena require the same set up: a world-shattering event leading to intense emotion, and a visit from Carmen. However, while Distortions are formed by the target agreeing with Carmen's words, E.G.O is instead manifested by denying them. This might include choosing to act differently from what she encourages, directly telling her she's wrong, or just outright ignoring her.

As such, the line between distorting and manifesting E.G.O is a thin one, similar to walking a tightrope. Still, it is not equally easy to end up on either side. The outcome is considerably rigged in favor of the target distorting, considering they would be both in a very fragile state of mind and being talked into it by Carmen. It is not an easy feat to reject Carmen's comforting words and manifest one's own E.G.O.

While Distortions are primarily associated with "evil thoughts" and E.G.O with "good thoughts", there is no such rule of thumb. Dongrang, for example, would manifest E.G.O on the basis of killing Yi Sang and destroying everything weighing him to the past. What mattered was that Carmen was telling him it was hopeless, and Dongrang disagreed with that.

entries.name: E.G.O of the Sinners
entries.content:
While Limbus Company's Sinners all primarily use Abnormality E.G.O, they also all possess personal E.G.O that they manifest in a similar manner. They are very clearly not Abnormality E.G.O; where those are labeled with the name of the Abnormality, these bear the name of the Sinner instead, and are also far too particular to their users to be derived from another entity. While they all wield unique weapons and some possess special abilities, such as Yi Sang's Crow's Eye View allowing for short-ranged teleportation, their clothes while using them are semi-uniform in a manner akin to L Corp's E.G.O Suits, all of them carrying the same sort of red-and-white vertical-striped pattern, vaguely akin to prison garb.

While the exact function behind these particular E.G.O is unknown, its semi-uniform nature akin to Lobotomy E.G.O hints at them being manifested artificially, likely by means of the same technology that allows for the Sinners to use Abnormality E.G.O. However, they appear to only be capable of manifesting for a moment, typically only usable for a single attack. More importantly, just like the aformentioned Volatile E.G.O, these seemingly-artificial manifestations do not count as proper Effloresced E.G.O and similarly don't act as a safeguard against Distortion, as shown with Heathcliff in Canto VI: The Heartbreaking. In fact, they are actually capable of E.G.O Corrosion, which - while not changing the user's appearance any more than its regular usage - appears to herald them Distorting soon after.

entries.name: Shin
entries.content:
A means of discreetly using the Light, rather than needing it to all manifest at once as an E.G.O. or Distortion, which allows one to achieve massively increased effectiveness by striking more with willpower than with the body. 

Shin (心) is a technique related to the powers of the Light and Sin that is a type of energy projection. It has largely been shown being used to create Mang (望), a power enhancing ability that visually manifests as warm rings of light that appear around the weapon being used to attack, but can seemingly be used in a way to strengthen the body as well without the use of Mang, forming a golden aura.

In order to use Shin, one must clear their mind of all emotions and then tap into their most intense memories and allow the emotions that are invoked by those memories to take fill their head. The more Mang used in an attack, the higher degree of control over Shin is needed by the user. The path to learning how to properly utilize Shin is difficult, but it can be taught to others and even self taught through enough diligence.


The more rings used the more power the attack has. Shin can also be imbued into projectiles, weapons and E.G.O in the for, of Mang.

The power of Shin is measured in "Mang" and is quantified by the number of rings of light present.

Known Users:

Vergilius — has been shown utilizing three Mang.
Lion — has been shown utilizing two Mang.
Panther — has been shown utilizing two Mang.
Wolf — has been shown utilizing one Mang.
Demian — has been shown utilizing seven Mang.
The Indigo Elder — has been shown utilizing three Mang.
Zilu — has not been shown utilizing Mang, but uses Shin in a defense manner.
Lei Heng — has been shown utilizing one Mang.
Kong Qiu — has been shown utilizing five Mang.

entries.name: Enkephalin
entries.content:
Enkephalin was the energy resource which Lobotomy Corporation produced. It was extracted from the Abnormalities created through its Singularity, which produced Enkephalin when their needs were met. Enkephalin was stored in PE-boxes, and was considered an efficient and eco-friendly resource, making it popular with both other Wings and City denizens.

Enkephalin is also digestible. While it can have a calming effect, Enkephalin was a highly-addictive substance capable of creating drug addicts of both the Lobotomy Corporation employees and Sephirot, and is also known to cause hallucinations. Additionally, it is stated that repeated injecting of Enkephalin into machinery will rust it.

As of Limbus Company, the collapse of Lobotomy Corporation has made Enkephalin into a precious and limited resource. Fixers and Syndicates may scavenge collapsed L Corp. branches in search of Enkephalin and other findings, with phrases like "Lobotomy Dream" and "Enkephalin Rush" beginning to catch on.

Enkephalin Box: Recovers 60 Enkephalin when used.

A stable container storing liquid Enkephalin.
[CAUTION] Handling this box without following the prescribed procedures may result in accidents such as Enkephalin leakage.
Unregulated ingestion of Enkephalin may cause a wide range of unverified psychopathological symptoms.

Enkephalin Module: Used for entering dungeons.

A spherical module designed for special containment.
[NOTE] Utilizing a dosage of liquid Enkephalin allows for more stable usage compared to its gaseous form. The Enkephalin can be converted into energy by plugging the module into a designated socket.
[CAUTION] Modularization of Enkephalin is an irreversible; the module may only be expended via a socket. Usage outside of intended purposes or modification is strictly forbidden.

entries.name: Qliphoth Counter
entries.content: Qliphoth Counter and Anomalous Effects: Abnormalities are entities that possess unusual abilities that can harm or benefit employees and/or the facility. This vary from simple Healing to breaching containment. A way to measure the triggering of a effect is via their Qliphoth Counter, which, when reaching a number (usually 0), will trigger its ability. Most abilities will include the Abnormality breaching the containment unit. However, not all the Abnormalities use the Qliphoth Counter to use their abilities. Unused Qliphoth Counters are marked with a 'X' instead of a number.

entries.name: Qliphoth Meltdown
entries.content:
Qliphoth Meltdowns or Qliphoth Meltdown Levels, are events linked to the amount of works performed during the Management Phase. This is contained and divided in 3 parts, that are present during the entire process of the Management Phase.

The Qliphoth Meltdown Level determines the number of Qliphoth Meltdowns to apply in the facility or what type of Ordeal to summon. The Level starts at Level 1, and can increase to a maximum of 10. Beyond Level 10, the level will begin to loop at that level, applying the same number of Qliphoth Meltdowns at the end of each Level and no longer spawning Ordeals.

The Qliphoth Meltdown Gauge is a gauge that counts the number of works started in the facility. When a work is started on a non-Tool Abnormality that is not undergoing a Qliphoth Meltdown, the gauge will increase by 1. After a certain number of works, upon filling the entire gauge, a Qliphoth Meltdown will occur and the Qliphoth Meltdown Level will be increased by 1.

An effect will be triggered on the facility, either applying Qliphoth Meltdowns to Abnormalities or summoning Ordeals. The maximum number of works required to fill the gauge will increase as more days pass, and only 1 of each type of Ordeal will occur per day, under the following conditions: Dawn Ordeals can spawn from Day 6 onwards, Noon Ordeals from Day 11 onwards (with the exception of Indigo Noon), Dusk Ordeals from Day 21 onwards and Midnight Ordeals plus Indigo Noon from Day 26 onwards.

The Qliphoth Meltdown is a containment effect that is applied during the increase of the Qliphoth Meltdown Level. When a number appears on the side of the gauge, that is the amount of Meltdowns that are going to occur. During the trigger, a number of random containment units in the facility will receive the Qliphoth Meltdown, with an alarm sound. A warning effect will be visible around the containment unit and a timer will appear above it, with a bar decreasing over 60 seconds (which changes upon recieving the Central Command Clerk Benefit), that once being depleted, it will subtract an amount of energy proportional to the current Qliphoth Meltdown Level (5 times the Level) from the energy quota and fully deplete the Qliphoth Counter of the Abnormality, if it has one.

Qliphoth Meltdowns are removed once an employee enters the containment unit. If the containment unit affected by the Qliphoth Meltdown already has an Agent within it or during the period of time where an Abnormality cannot be worked after having just completed a work on it, the timer will be paused until these conditions no longer apply. Qliphoth Meltdowns will not affect empty Tool containment units, containment units with breaching Abnormalities and departments with immunity to the meltdowns. The amount of Qliphoth Meltdowns will increase with every Qliphoth Meltdown Level, and the amount spawned is proportional to the number of containment units in the facility.

entries.name: Qliphoth Overload
entries.content:
Qliphoth Overload is a containment effect that occurs upon finishing a work with a non-Tool Risk WAW or Risk ALEPH Abnormality. It will decrease the Success Rate of that Abnormality's next works by a percentage (4% for Risk WAW. 6% for Risk ALEPH), that can stack a number of times (Max 32% for Risk WAW, after 8 works, Max 30% for Risk ALEPH, after 6 works). The Qliphoth Overload will reset to 0 upon reaching the next Qliphoth Meltdown Level.

If all Agents in a department die, all Clerks in the Department will commit suicide, and every Abnormality in the Department will have their Success Rate decreased by 50% until the end of the day.

entries.name: Damage Types
entries.content:
RED Damage: This type relates to physical damage. This involves bloodshed. Some may leave small scratches, others may shatter the body with devastating strikes. An Abnormality with high RED value could turn an employee into an unrecognizable mess with a single blow, no matter how small and cute they may seem.

WHITE Damage: While RED represents physical damage, WHITE represents psychological damage. The severity may range from sweaty nightmares to semi-permanent trauma that tortures the employee for the rest of their life. It could even be a mental breakdown followed by suicide.

BLACK Damage: A complex of physical and psychological damages. BLACK erodes a targets being. According to the few that have survived the damage, it felt as if dark thorns were burrowing into their body and brain.

PALE Damage: Death itself. PALE shaves away the soul. Even the toughest body and wisest mind will not matter. All are equal in the face of death.

Resistances to one form of damage will not allow you to resist another.

entries.name: A Corp
