This parallel to how Angela tirelessly searches for the "one true book" she seeks, coming across many books that are useless to her in an infinite and ever-growing library.

The abnormalities related to and used as e.g.o pages in this floor include: Bloodbath, Heart of Aspiration, Pinocchio, The Snow Queen, Silent Girl.

The Abnormalities and their Pages are related to A, Angela, or Carmen, being in origin or meaning. Clear examples are Bloodbath and The Snow Queen (Mentioning Carmen's fate in their Story Entries).

entries.name: Floor of History
entries.content:
The Floor of History, also known as Malkuth's Floor, is located on the first story of the library. Its Patron Librarian is Malkuth, and its main color is Light Yellow.

This Floor is designated for sorting books related to history, documented events, and the past. The Battle Stage resembles a large divided section into various lanes, adorned with display cases at the sides with objects in them. The lanes can elevate from the ground, showing bookshelves below them. In the background, there are 3 structures connecting to the respective next 3 Floors, from left to right: Floor of Literature, Floor of Technological Sciences, and Floor of Art. The background walls are made of more bookshelves.

The abnormalities related to and used as e.g.o pages in this floor include: Scorched Girl, Happy Teddy Bear, Fairy Festival, Queen Bee, Snow White's Apple.

The Abnormalities and their Pages represent abandonment (Scorched Girl and Happy Teddy Bear), loyalty (Queen Bee), and betrayal (Fairy Festival, Snow White's Apple).

entries.name: Floor of Technological Sciences
entries.content:
The Floor of Technological Sciences, also known as Yesod's Floor, is located on the second story of the library. Its Patron Librarian is Yesod, and its main color is Purple.

The Battle Stage used resembles a paved road on a large bridge located above a city. On the road itself there are lamp posts, stopped cars and roadblocks, also on the edges there is an iron guardrail. The supporting pillars of the "bridge" are bookshelves and are connected to each other by chains leading downwards. The background consists of a cityscape with huge gears in different places, which from time to time activate a mechanism that moves the city blocks up and down. In the distance you can see a large curved tower with a lamp on top, from which chains emanate in different directions, similar to the chains on the bridge. According to Yesod, some of the moving gears found in the background of this Floor "don't quite mesh well together", producing loud noises which Yesod finds irritating.

The abnormalities related to and used as e.g.o pages in this floor include: Forsaken Murderer, All-Around Helper, Singing Machine, The Funeral of the Dead Butterflies, Der Freischütz.

The collective theme of the Abnormalities of this floor in some way reflect killing innocents, whether it be out of urge or necessity.

entries.name: Floor of Literature
entries.content:
The Floor of Literature, also known as Hod's Floor, is located on the third story of the Library. Its Patron Librarian is Hod, and its main color is Orange.

The battle stage used in Reception resembles a wooden bridge or pier, with iron railings on the sides. On the platform itself are boxes and wooden poles with light bulbs hanging from them. The supporting poles of the "bridge" are also hung with ropes and light bulbs. The background consists of several towers on a wooden or iron base, with long ladders between them. All of this is also hung with light bulbs. In the tower in the center, some large and bright light source is burning.

The abnormalities related to and used as e.g.o pages in this floor include: Today’s Shy Look, Red Shoes, Spider Bud, Laetitia, Dream of a Black Swan.

entries.name: Floor of Art
entries.content:
The Floor of Art, also known as Netzach's Floor, is located on the fourth story of the library. Its Patron Librarian is Netzach, and its main color is Green. Docile small green blob-like humanoids that glow are present on the floor.

This Floor is designated for collecting books related to the arts. It is also one of the floors connected to the Floor of History, along with the Floor of Technological Sciences and Floor of Literature.

The Battle Stage resembles a green bridge-like platform that seems to be made of large roots. In the background, 6 structures similar to pillars being used as bookshelves, with one of them connecting to the Floor of History. From time to time a creature, similar to the one on the painting that is seen during Netzach's episodes, will appear behind some of those 6 structures and slowly slide from right to left until it is out of sight and disappear without interfering.

The abnormalities related to and used as e.g.o pages in this floor include: Fragment of the Universe, Child of the Galaxy, Porccubus, Alriune, The Silent Orchestra.

The abnormalities of this floor seem to have a shared attribute of their actions or backstory having something to do with compassion and desire to help and befriend humans, yet turning out to be violent in nature. Fragment of the Universe wanted to share its knowledge with human race, Child of the Galaxy wanted to make friends, Porccubus is not actually hostile to anybody, Alriune was trying to become human and was adored by many, and The Silent Orchestra is merely an "artist" abnormality who is trying to get others to listen to its majestic music. Aside from that, all of them mostly hurt people in mental ways.

entries.name: Floor of Natural Sciences
entries.content:
The Floor of Natural Sciences, also known as Tiphereth's Floor, is located on the fifth story of the library. Its Patron Librarian is Tiphereth, and its main color is Yellow.

The battle scene used in Reception resembles a large area of ​​luxurious tiled road covered with a red carpet. The background is the inside of a large dome with many holes with candles in them. Under the very center of the dome roof is a kind of altar or pedestal with four cups on it. Each cup symbolizes the Red damage,White damage, Black damage and Pale damage types. Periodically, the lights in the hall go out and daylight starts to leak through the holes in the dome, and the platform itself changes a little.

The abnormalities related to and used as e.g.o pages in this floor include: The Queen of Hatred, The Knight of Despair, The King of Greed, The Servant of Wrath, The Jester of Nihil.

Abnormalities found on the Floor of Natural Sciences share actions within the City: Hatred, Despair, Greed, Wrath, and Nihilism.

entries.name: Floor of Language
entries.content:
The Floor of Language, also known as Gebura's Floor, is located on the sixth story of the library. Its Patron Librarian is Gebura, and its main color is Red.

The battle scene used in Reception resembles a massive iron elevator surrounded by a concrete, broken fence. The fence itself is destroyed down to the foundation, from which rusty reinforcement protrudes. In the background, buildings are illuminated by the red light of a lake of hot iron, which makes the appearance of the unremarkable buildings very powerful. The iron lake itself is formed by a giant cauldron from which hot metal flows.

The abnormalities related to and used as e.g.o pages in this floor include: Little Red Riding Hooded Mercenary, Big and Will be Bad Wolf, Mountain of Smiling Bodies, Nosferatu, Nothing There. 

Abnormalities found on the Floor of Language hare a common theme of an endless cycle of violence, which shares similarities with the rampageous acts of those within the City.

entries.name: Floor of Social Sciences
entries.content:
The Floor of Social Sciences, also known as Chesed's Floor, is located on the seventh story of the library. Its Patron Librarian is Chesed, and its main color is Blue.

In the background of the battle scene during the Reception, structures are visible, obscured by swirls of blue. Broken cars float along the swirls, giving the picture a grotesque appearance. The area where the battle takes place is stylized as a wrecked ship - a broken deck, tied ropes and seaweed.

The abnormalities related to and used in this floor include: Scarecrow Searching for Wisdom, Warm-hearted Woodsman, The Road Home & Scaredy Cat, Ozma, The Adult who Tells Lies.

The Abnormality battles and Realization are seemingly based on the fictional story "The Wizard of Oz." They also represent the dreams and desires of the people within the City. They search for wisdom, emotion, courage, and a place to call home. Ozma represents those in the City who have had all of these things taken away by the City itself, represented as the Adult Who Tell Lies.

entries.name: Floor of Philosophy
entries.content:
The Floor of Philosophy, also known as Binah's Floor, is located on the eighth story of the library. Its Patron Librarian is Binah, and its main color is Golden Brown.

The battle scene used in Reception resembles a platform floating above a cityscape, held aloft by a black haze. The battle site is dotted with lights. The cityscape itself is very blurry due to the platform being so high in the air. Above the platform, one can see the vastness of outer space, obscured by clouds. The top of the moon is visible above the fog.

The abnormalities related to and used as e.g.o pages in this floor include: Big Bird, Punishing Bird, Judgement Bird, Apocalypse Bird.

All three of the birds have a correlation to A Corp(Judgement Bird), B Corp(Big Bird), and C Corp(Punishing Bird). This is a reference to Binah's former life as an Arbiter.

entries.name: Floor of Religion
entries.content:
The Floor of Religion, also known as Hokma's Floor, is located on the ninth story of the library. Its Patron Librarian is Hokma, and its main color is grey.

The battle scene used in Reception is a tiled road supported by supports. The background is a mechanism of many giant clocks, with standing dials. Three pendulums can also be seen, which begin to swing during the battle. During the battle, black particles appear, floating in the air.

The abnormalities related to and used as e.g.o pages in this floor include: Burrowing Heaven, The Price of Silence, Blue Star, WhiteNight.

entries.name: E.G.O. Pages
entries.content: E.G.O. Pages are unique and powerful singular Combat Pages that can be used by Librarians after completing the corresponding Floor Realization. Once used, the E.G.O. page has a "cooldown" that must be recharged by earning 9 Emotion Coins per living Librarian emotion coins. E.G.O pages allow one to temporarily partially use the power of and become the abnormality that the page draws the power from. Some pages allow "synchronisation", making the user become the abnormality for a period of time.

entries.name: The Black Forest
entries.content:
The Black Forest was a forest located in the Outskirts discovered by L Corp where Punishing Bird, Big Bird, and Judgment Bird originated from. While not appearing proper in-game itself, its environment were simulated in the books the birds were kept in, along with manifesting the other inhabitants that fought alongside the birds in their fights.

According to the legends, it was once a populated area that became abandoned when the three birds eventually became Apocalypse Bird in an effort to protect the forest from the very monster they wanted to prevent.

entries.name: Rivers
entries.content:
"It is said that when an efflorescent tree comes to blossom, steeped and nurtured in the waters of many rivers since its saplinghood, it becomes imbued with a special power."

The River is a major location and overarching plot element in Lobotomy Corporation and Limbus Company, which is said to span the entirety of The City's underground.

This River is known to flow beneath the City, branching out into smaller Rivers, and reaching out even beyond the Outskirts into the Ruins. The River appears to have various tributaries, with waters that have special effects on the human mind both when drank from, and when gazed upon.

The River is described as a "primordial sea of possibility", containing all of human consciousness, as well as all possibilities of the past, present and future. It is implied that plants watered by the River and its tributaries acquire special properties, a likely example being the Golden Boughs.

The River is noted to resurface through small gaps in the world, such as the Black Forest of the Outskirts, causing Abnormalities to emerge from it. The manor of Wuthering Heights is heavily implied to be built upon this River, with its waters causing the spontaneous manifestation of Identities —fragments of possibility— from other Mirror Worlds, appearing as afterimages resembling ghosts.

While there are few who still carry the knowledge of the River's existence, the phenomenon itself stated to have been forgotten by humanity. Before the events of Lobotomy Corporation, the River was discovered by Ayin and used by L Corp. to create and manage Abnormalities. Lobotomy Corporation's Singularity, Cogito, allowed them to siphon from the River, and create Abnormalities from the human mind.

Mirae-Mirae River: A tributary of the river referred to as the "Mirae-Mirae" or "Future-Future River" by Bari. Drinking from its waters will give the drinker a vision of the future, though at the same time, make them blinded to all but the prophesized future, leading them to madness. Sancho, on her journey to Lethe with Bari, looked into the river and obtained a vision of the contract she would form with Dante.

River of Oblivion: The River of Oblivion, known as Lethe, is one of the tributaries of the River. Those who drink from the River are said to completely lose memory of their past. This River was visited by Sancho and Bari before the events of Limbus Company, with Sancho drinking from its waters and forgetting her life as a Bloodfiend. The River's effects are shown to be reversible.

River of Immortality: A mysterious, currently unnamed tributary of the River is mentioned by Jia Xichun, noted to grant immortality of the mind to those who drink from it. Jia Xichun and presumably other members of her family are searching for it under the orders of their elders, who desire its power.

entries.name: Santata's Gift Factory
entries.content:
Santata's Gift Factory is a location found within the Outskirts, located an unknown amount of distance south of Cloud Town. Located within is a massive system of conveyors and assembly lines, that which are managed by the gnomes that reside inside. Gnomes make raids to the settlements within the Outskirts, such as Cloud Town, kidnapping, killing, and dismembering civilians to use as material for the gifts that the factory produces.

The gifts are said to be later distributed to those that live in the Outskirts, created out of malice for those that discriminate the species that are not human.

Notable Members:
Santata (Owner)
Dodoru (Manager)

Gnomes:
Making up the workforce of the facility are Gnomes, which come in 3 festive-colored varieties. The gnomes gather ingredients and make gifts under the watchful eye of their Manager Gnomes.

entries.name: The Great Lake
entries.content:
The Great Lake is giant ocean which extends to the Outskirts.

The Great Lake occupies a large territory, extending through most of U Corp., and touching T Corp., S Corp. and V Corp. It is split into numerous distinctly separated Lakes, each of which possesses unique qualities, including varying water color, landmarks, and most importantly, "Laws".

The Laws of a Lake determine the course of travel through a Lake, such as how much time can be spent in one and when a vessel in the Lake can pass over to another. If a Law is broken, the Lake will send its "Waves" after the rulebreaker: in this event, the resident Whale of a Lake and its Mermaids will attack a ship that has broken a Law of the Lake, trying to consume the people within and convert them into Mermaids.

Five of the Whales of the Great Lake are not restricted to a single Lake, instead being capable of freely roaming the Great Lake: these are known as 'The Five Calamities', which cause havoc and chaos throughout the Great Lake. Only two of these Calamities have been named, these being "The All-Piercing Marlin Whale" (killed by the Indigo Elder), and "The All-Consuming Pallid Whale", whose hunt is the focus of the third part of Canto V. The Pequod Captain Ishmael's Identity story also mentions the "All-Withering Crimson Whale" although it is unknown if it is exclusive to that Mirror World.

entries.name: Ruins
entries.content:
Located either beyond the outskirts or the fogotten old corps beneath the city. The's City's Ruins are different in that the threat level increases as you go deeper, while the Outskirt's Ruins contain things incomprehensible to the human mind. Expeditions sent here have a low chance of survival, and those that do are often shaken from the experience.

Since these are one of the most dangerous places to go to, its quite possible the forbidden relics and technology found here would be worth killing for. There is also supposedly "Magic" in the Ruins, artifacts containing unknown powers that can unleash potent effects.

Inhabitants: Monsters - these creatures are very dangerous, their power level is equal to the abnormalities of the class Risk ALEPH or City Star level threats.

Places in the ruins:

Abyss of Ruin - It is unknown what this place looks like, but monsters live there. The Rabbit Team came there to destroy monsters. Also in the abyss there are many mysterious and different rivers with different properties.

entries.name: Inhumans / Non-humans
entries.content:
The War Against the Inhumans is a large-scale war that took place in the past. The war involved the Head with Wings against the Inhumans, who were similar to robots.

At an unknown time, the Head decides to destroy the Inhumans, because they were robots-androids that are too similar to humans, revolting and wanting independence. As a result, the Inhumans and Humans who coexisted together began to feud. The war against the Inhumans took place in the City and the non humans were forced out into the outskirts and beyond it.

Sometime afterward, the AI Ethics Amendment was put into law, forbidding any AI or machine to have any human resemblance. This could mean the Non-Humans were some form of mechanical beings who had human-level intelligence and appearance.

entries.name: Bloodfiend War
entries.content:
An old conflict between two sides of Bloodfiends, those who wished to coexist alongside humans in peace, and those who saw them only as prey and cattle. The side that wanted to feast on human blood had bloodfiends that were apparently giants, likely due to the amount of blood they consumed. The more Peaceful Bloodfiends won the battle.

Notable participants of the battle include:

Manchegan Family:
Don Quixote (First Kindred of the Primogenitor, P Corp. Elder),
Sancho (Second Kindred of Don Quixote),
Dulcinea (Second Kindred of Don Quixote),
Nicolina (Third Kindred of Dulcinea),
Curiambro (Third Kindred of Dulcinea).

entries.name: Casino Security
entries.content: The Casino Security are the security for the casino that houses Branch J-03. There is not just a group of security in charge of the first floor of the Casino, but also a squadron based on the first floor of the Dungeon, watching over the slaves. Each squad is led by a Casino Security Chief.

entries.name: K Corp. Security
entries.content:
The K Corp. Security are the security force that is active in District 11. It includes the Checkpoint Security, Class 3, and the K Corp. Fixer Siegfried. All K Corp personnel wear advanced black and green suits with various weapons.

K Corp. Checkpoint Security
The K Corp. Checkpoint Security, also known as Class 2 Staff are the security force that gatekeeps the entrance to the District 11 Nest, as well as the primary security force for internal affairs. There is no leader fought for this squadron, but the K Corp Fixer Siegfried is a powerful ally that assists in emergencies.

K Corp. Class 3
The Class 3 Staff is a tier of elite defense force even more powerful than the Class 1 and 2 below them. They are shown to assist the Checkpoint Security in the Refraction Railway, and are currently exclusive to that game mode.

K Corp. Class 1
The Class 1 Staff are among the weakest members of the security force employed by K Corp. They are used for search and rescue as opposed to direct combat, but will still fight if required or forced to.

K Corp. Drones
The K Corp. Drones are automated drones used by K Corp. for a variety of purposes. The Filming Drones are designed for filming crime or disaster scenes, and creating a blockade to warn off anyone who dares approach danger. The Regen Drones are used to administer HP Ampules to combatants and Decay Ampules to deserters and adversaries in combat scenarios.

entries.name: Dead Rabbits
entries.content:
The Dead Rabbits were a Syndicate of the District 20 Backstreets that Heathcliff joined after leaving Wuthering Heights.

The Dead Rabbits Syndicate, led by Matthew, originally operated uniquely in the Backstreets of District 20. They were known as being vigilantes of sorts, being notable among the gangs of T Corp. for actually protecting those they exorted protection money (in the form of time) from. The Dead Rabbits' distinctive sign was the scarf they'd warp around their arms, resembling rabbit ears, and their preferred weapons were long metal bats. The Syndicate prized its loyalty and was tightly-knit, with their members often frequenting pubs (particularly The Wolf's Fall) and Hamhampangpang restaurants together, and with their boss Matthew taking care of Time Taxes for his underlings.

Sometime after Heathcliff had left the Dead Rabbits, the Syndicate was wiped out. Years later, the Dead Rabbits were reborn with support of The Ring and rose to an Urban Plague classification. Members of this Syndicate under this revival were not willing participants of the Syndicate, but were Identities that were created and overlaid over the bodies of civilians taken from the Nest of T Corp. They could be recognized by their red rabbit masks and brown coats. In this iteration, they wielded spiked bats, and their leader went by the name Matt. However, it seems most of them suffer from the strain or degradation of their identities, having slurred speech and a lack of free will. In addition Matt is a fake persona, the real one being Erlking Heathcliff, a person from a mirror world who was imitating Matt in order to decieve Limbus Company's Heathcliff.

Outfit: Dull Brown and Dull Red suit coats, with a Rusty Orange stitched rabbit mask.

When a Dead Rabbit dies, mirror shards are notably included in their deaths. Additionally, the corpses left behind are identical to that of T Corp. Gangsters.

entries.name: Los Mariachis
entries.content: Los Mariachis is a Syndicate located in the Backstreets of District 10. It is one of the primary Syndicates located around the casino that houses Branch J-03. The members, known as Mariachis, wear ponchos and fight as though they are dancing. They are led by the Jefe de Los Mariachis, Aida.

entries.name: Researchers of the Ring?
entries.content: The Researchers of the Ring? are a group of former Ring researchers who were involved with maintaining the Glass Pods in the basement of Wuthering Heights. They were disguised as members of Öufi Association and wore the uniform worn by fixers of the Association, although instead of wielding the signature halberds they instead battle with paintbrushes.

entries.name: District 20 Yurodiviye
entries.content: The District 20 Yurodiviye is the branch of the Yurodiviye that is operating in District 20 (T Corp.). Members primarily don brown coats and white pants, along with the signature white scarf of the Syndicate, and fights with black-and-gold spanners or clamps. They also act as detectives for-hire in the district.

entries.name: Technology Liberation Alliance
entries.content:
The Technology Liberation Alliance is a terrorist group located in the Nest of District 11. It was created by former K Corp. employees. Their end goal is to turn their technological knowledge against the Corporations of the City, in their own words "use vile machines to get rid of their vile creators" and create a peaceful world without any advanced technologies. They have taken and repurposed the leftover Lobotomy E.G.O from the fallen L Corp branch in the district.

Dongbaek's Subgroup:
Dongbaek (Leader),
Marile,
Ran,
Shrenne (Sympathizer).

entries.name: Yurodiviye
entries.content:
The Yurodiviye is a Syndicate led by Sonya, aiming to redistribute goods from the rich to the needy and widely prevent the concentration of wealth.

The Yurodiviye is first introduced in Canto II: The Unloving as a Syndicate Rodion was formerly associated with and competition for the LCB in their race for the Golden Boughs.

Yurodiviye was founded by Sonya and Rodion in the Backstreets of District 25 in response to the poor circumstances of those without wealth. Individual members are known as "Yurodivy" (Юро́дивый, Juródivyj), and most exhibit magnanimous ideals rarely seen in the harsh, greedy landscape of the City. The events of Intervallo IV: Timekilling Time and the District 20 Yurodivy Hong Lu and Ryōshū Identity Stories, however, evidence that not all members the Yurodiviye share the same ideals. Some of its members join with the simple desire to express their discontent towards the rich, and there are somewhat frequent debates between members with varying political views.

In the present day, Yurodiviye can be found throughout both the Backstreets and Nests of the City, roughing up peddlers they deem greedy people keeping money to themselves. Its members claim that this is only a transitory occupation that they perform while waiting for "the right moment".

Being the leader of the group, Yurodiviye's goals appear to align with Sonya's. In his words, they aim to destroy the system of oppression and exploitation, preventing the concentration of wealth. In order to attain this, they work to create a new world, as opposed to fixing the current one.

They seek the Golden Boughs for the sake of using its power in order to achieve this new world. Despite this, Sonya ultimately ends up allowing Rodya and the Sinners to obtain the one they sought at Branch J-03.

The Syndicate was formed as a result of dissatisfaction with the way the poor of District 25's Backstreets only ever got poorer while the pawnbrokers only got richer. With charming speeches consisting of big words, Sonya managed to rally all kinds of people under the promise of paving a better world, and together, they organized Yurodiviye. With his group, Sonya aimed for a world where the destitute could escape from the oppression and exploitation of the ruling class, at last finding true liberation.

However, according to Rodya, the Syndicate ultimately warped into an organization that cared more for debating about how best to change the streets and the Nest, rather than actually going out and helping those in need. Sonya believed that it was only the future which could be changed, and focused exclusively on what could be improved going forward. Rodya was disgusted by this mindset which abandoned the sufferers of the present and chose to leave the group. Still, Timekilling Time suggests that this was her own personal bias, and that the Syndicate has continued to grow and better the City on account of Sonya's long-term planning.

entries.name: Yurodiviye & Hermann's Group
entries.content: Yurodiviye is affiliated with Hermann and her faction, as seen in Canto II's post-credits scene. While the relationship between the two groups is unclear, they are shown to be on good terms, with Hermann treating Sonya with a notable amount of fairness even after he failed to claim the Golden Bough they sought.

entries.name: Yurodiviye & Demian's Group
entries.content: The Yurodiviye and Demian's faction appear to be allies. Sonya and Demian are at least acquainted with one another, well enough that Sonya knows of his relationship with Sinclair[1]. Additionally, at the end of Canto III: The Unconfronting, Demian tells Sinclair that "the world is about to head for a new birth. And, only a few individuals can get there", a statement which aligns closely with Yurodiviye's goals of building a new and better world.

entries.name: Yurodiviye & Limbus Company
entries.content: Yurodiviye opposes Limbus Company in their quest to claim the Golden Boughs. They are also affiliated with Hermann's group, who hold a harsh rivalry with the Sinners. However, Sonya ultimately decides to give up the Bough to Rodion and the rest of the LCB, and never treats them with any particular harshness or hostility. The Yurodiviy of District 20 seen in Timekilling Time also show a dedication to their work with no interest in attacking the LCB without provocation. The captain even goes out of his way to offer Rodya advice after affirming that she held a friendship with Sonya.

entries.name: Hermann's Group
entries.content:
Hermann's group is an unofficially named faction based in N Corp., led by Director Hermann. Much like Limbus Company, they seek to obtain the Golden Boughs located all across the City.

Hermann's group was created as an attempt to reunite the former researchers of the League of Nine under a new lead, starting with the Littérateurs Gubo, Yi Sang, and Aseah; because of this, it is at times referred to as a new League of Nine. Its current members are Gubo, Hermann's co-director, the researcher Aseah, and Jia Huan.

The goals of Hermann's Group is largely unknown at this time, though the faction expresses clear interest in the search for the Golden Boughs. Hermann's Group is heavily involved in the study of Mirror Technology, with Hermann directing her researchers to find a way to destroy all the worlds and the possibilities reflected in the Mirror. Whether this is the ultimate goal, or a milestone in the process of achieving said goal, is currently unclear.

entries.name: Twinhook Pirates
entries.content:
The Twinhook Pirates is a Syndicate located in District 21.

The Twinook Pirates are a subsidiary of The Middle, and they conduct business in various parts of the U Corp. Backstreets. Their Captain at sea is Hook, although their First Mate, Smee, is the person who is actually in charge of the Syndicate's business while on land.

While their "business endeavours" at sea is largely unknown, the Twinhook Pirates' revenue on land comes mainly from kidnapping. Their modus operandi in this involves kidnapping non-locals (mainly tourists, but also people on business missions), then extorting their family, friends, or backers with increasing amounts of ransom money. Once the people behind the hostages run dry of funds, they kill the hostages and leave their bodies to rot within the shipping containers that they use to imprison them.

The Twinhook Pirates are also involved in dealing of various District 21 specialty products, such as Mermaid perfume, whale oil, and Marlin Port's specialty ice cream.

entries.name: Tingtang Gang
entries.content: The Tingtang Gang is a Syndicate located in the Backstreets of District 10. It is one of the primary Syndicates located around the casino that houses Branch J-03. The members, known as Tingtangers, wear Hawaiian shirts, and are notorious for their towering car pagodas around the casino and their stolen Wish Canister. They are led by the Tingtang Boss.

entries.name: Tieqiu Crew
entries.content: The Tieqiu Crew is a Syndicate located in the Backstreets of District 10. It is one of the primary Syndicates located around the casino that houses Branch J-03. The members, known as Tieqiu Crewmen, are notorious for their extremely vulgar language. They were led by the Tieqiu Boss.

entries.name: N Corp. Inquisition
Old G Corp. Soldiers
entries.content:
Old G Corp. Soldiers are enemies found in the Backstreets of District 4. They were involved in the Smoke War against several other corporations, including the previous L Corp. They possess bug genetic alternations that give them hardened carapaces and insect limbs, which they use in combat.

This is a faction of old G Corp. Veterans that had found refuge in the ruins of Branch D-02, an old branch of L Corp. They had been discarded after the Smoke War and their Wing had fallen, and found refuge in the backstreets of District 4. They were initially indifferent to the sinners, but grew antagonistic when they saw that Gregor was among their ranks, viewing him as a traitor and a deserter to their cause. They were led by the Old G Corp. Head Manager.

entries.name: Headchicken a.k.a. Bongy
entries.content:
Headchicken (O`-01-11-28), also known as Bongy, are ZAYIN-class Distortions that spawned from the Eunbong’s Bar & Fryers Owner's Distortion, Papa Bongy. They are encountered throughout Intervallo I, acting as the main enemies of the chapter.

Their appearance is based on Bongy, the mascot of Eunbong's Bar & Fryers.

These minions disappeared when the restaurant owner undistorted and returned to normal.

Log(Written by Don Quixote): 
I shall now begin to describe those cute yet bewildering things!
They are typically naked!
Awkward though it is to describe those things as entities of note...but nevertheless! Think of them as raw chickens well prepared for cooking, adorned with a pair of round, plump eyes!
Behold their adorable behinds!
Oh, do they reek of sweets and salts when they charge in!
Some taste of spicy seasonings, and some harbor the flavor of soy sauce!
Though the teeth on their maws may prick the mouth, 'tis inconvenience worth enduring!
→ Wait a minute, is that why I saw you mumbling sometimes…? You…took a bite out of 'em…? (Gregor)
→ You…didn't actually eat the raw chicken meat, did you? (Sinclair)
→ Poultry may cause infection when consumed uncooked. Please refrain from adding unnecessary strain to the manager outside of battle wounds. (Faust)
→ Oi! Don Quixote! Don't got anything to say about this? (Heathcliff)
→ She must think we will not recognize that this log is hers if she doesn't confirm it. (Outis)
→ Come on, she can't possibly have her head in the sand like that. Who do you think she is, an ostrich? (Ishmael)

entries.name: Rosespanner Workshop
entries.content:
The Rosespanner Workshop is a manufacturer of weapons that also doubles as a Fixer Office. They acted as antagonists to Limbus Company during their K Corp golden bough retrieval.

The Rosespanner Workshop is a small Workshop specializing in weapon-creation, that also takes on requests as a Fixer Office. Their work is referred to as tuning up and scrapping, possibly referring to their work as a Workshop and their work as a Fixer Office respectively. At one point, they are hired by K Corp. to work as bodyguards, but are wiped out by the Sinners.

Members: Niko (Workshop Representative).

entries.name: J Corp Slaves
entries.content:
Slaves are found in the dungeon of Branch J-03. They are people who gambled away their money, and must work off their debts in the mines below the casino. Slaves are all subordinates to stronger foes, with the first slaves encountered being watched over by a Casino Security Chief.

Further in the dungeon, Slaves are abused by the Abnormalities and converted into their subordinates, with both Have You Become Strong and Baba Yaga turning slaves into their minions. Pink Shoes also accomplishes this indirectly by re-animating slaves formerly manipulated by Have You Become Strong.

entries.name: Pequod Town
entries.content:
Pequod Town, is an entire settlement of partially-pallidified sailors that were eaten, but managed to survive inside the Pallid Whale for several years.

The town consists entirely of the former crew of The Pequod whaling ship, surviving their encounter with the whale. They've all managed to cling onto their humanity through their absolute loyalty towards their captain Ahab, who religiously steers them towards her singular goal of killing the Pallid Whale.

Leading them on with the promise of escaping and returning to The City, Ahab with her town of over 40 crewmen have explored the whale's organ system in the vain hope of slaying it once and for all.

entries.name: The Wild Hunt
entries.content:
The Wild Hunt is the personal army of Erlking Heathcliff, comprised of the corpses of every Wuthering Heights tormentor the Erlking has taken over and destroyed. Members of the Wild Hunt are essentially weakened versions of their normal counterparts.

Similar to Dead Rabbits Henchmen, Wild Hunt members emit a shattering mirror effect upon death, and leave behind corpses identical to that of T Corp. Gangsters.

entries.name: Cassetti's Kindred
entries.content:
Cassetti's Kindred are the "offspring" of Cassetti, a Bloodfiend who is responsible for numerous passenger disappearances on WARP Trains. Passengers, Fixers, and WARP Cleanup Agents converted to Bloodbags by Cassetti retain most of their former appearance, with the main difference being bright-red crystals of blood sprouting from various parts of their body, particularly the lower limbs and face; a piece of shoulder armor made of crystallized blood is also visible on the left shoulder of most Bloodbags. Blood crystal growth on the weapon is also observed if the Bloodbag wields one. The Bloodbags' eyes are also changed to a glowing, blood-red hue.

Sasha, despite being a Kindred of Cassetti instead of a Bloodbag, appears similar to the Bloodbags, with a large amount of blood crystal formations on her face, completely obscuring her features while in her "crystallized" form.

entries.name: Corroded Inquisitors
entries.content:
The Corroded Inquisitors are a group of enemies found in Branch K-02 of L Corp. Though they are treated as Abnormalities, having risk levels and classification codes, they are actually N. Corp Inquisitors that have voluntarily undergone E.G.O Corrosion.

All the Corroded Inquisitors are classified as TETH-classes, with the exception of Crawling Inquisitor which is classified as a ZAYIN-class.

Feral Mane Corrosions
Crawling Inquisitor and Four-Legged Beast (O-02-04-13-TE) are Kleinhammers that have been Corroded by E.G.O belonging to an unknown Abnormality with the classification code O-02-04-13. They walk on all all-fours with muscle fibers sprouting out like fur from their limbs and backs, giving them a wolf-life appearance. Large claws protrude from their hands, and their helmets have been split in two, giving way to a row of sharp teeth. Their ribs are inverted and stick out from their backs.

The Four-Legged Beast appears to be even further Corroded, having extra 'fur' sprouting from even its head, a noticeable tail, and a visible spine down its back.

Mimicry Corrosions
Both forms of Nothing There from Lobotomy Corporation.
Proceeding Inquisitor and Everything There of an Inquisitor (O-06-20-TE) are lesser Mittelhammers Corroded by Mimicry E.G.O originating from Nothing There (O-06-20), an ALEPH-class Abnormality that appeared in Lobotomy Corporation. The most noteworthy feature of these Corrosions is the giant bundle of muscles that has replaced the right arm. This new arm has its own set of eyes along with a toothy mouth. Bones jut out from the arm, giving it a scythe-like appearance. The Inquisitor's helmet has been discarded, as the muscle from the arm connects to the now defunct face.

Coil Corrosions
Wriggling Beast and Slithering Inquisitor (O-02-11-10-TE) are greater Mittelhammers that have been Corroded by E.G.O from an unknown Abnormality with the classification code O-02-11-10. The Wriggling Beast does not appear all too different from a regular Inquisitor, with the main difference being the giant green snake that has replaced its right arm. Additional snakes can be seen poking out from its armor, which has been stained by some green substance.

In the case of the Slithering Inquisitor, its left arm has also been replaced by another snake. Its helmet has been partly cracked revealing a beady red eye, and a long forked tongue. Even more snakes can be seen poking out from various places in its armor.

entries.name: Edgar Family
entries.content:
The Edgar Family appears in Canto VI: The Heartbreaking. Its staff serves as minor antagonists during the chapter.

he Edgar Family is an affluent family hailing from T Corp.'s Nest. Outside of District 20, the Edgar Family is famous in Fixer circles, with their members at times appearing in Fixer magazines. This fame appears to trace back to the previous generation, and it does not extend to the family's current heir, Linton Edgar. Their manor is located at a short distance from Wuthering Heights, although it is not subject to the windy weather characteristic of the latter, and its gardens are guarded by large hounds. Following Catherine Earnshaw's marriage to Linton Edgar, the title of Chief Butler of the Edgar Family was claimed by Nelly.

The Butlers of the Edgar Family wear two types of uniforms: the men's uniform consists of a black suit over a white shirt, tied with a black cravat around the neck, and a silver pin on the left lapel, possibly the family crest; the women's uniform resembles a french maid uniform, consisting of a black floor length dress, a white apron, a white headband, and a grey ribbon around the neck. The Butlers carry a brown dimensional attache case with a silver crest, in which they store their combat cutlery.

entries.name: La Manchaland
entries.content:
La Manchaland is an amusement park known to manifest in the Backstreets of District 16.

La Manchaland is an amusement park built and staffed entirely by Bloodfiends, specifically the Manchegan Bloodfiends, the Family of the First Kindred Don Quixote. Although it advertises itself to be "a place of freedom to dream side-by-side with Bloodfiends", at this point in time its staff are hostile to entering humans, attacking them and turning them into Bloodbags. Notably, all architecture in La Manchaland is composed of solidified human blood.

The amusement park was theorized by the P Corp. Archival Department to have been constructed over 200 years in the past, but have only been starting to manifest in October 984. As of the events of Canto VII: The Dream Ending, it is an Urban Nightmare-class phenomenon.

La Manchaland manifests once every day at around 1600 hours, during which time merry carnival music can be heard emanating from it. Music announcing closure will start playing 6 hours later, at 2200 hours, and the park disappears after a further 30 minutes. Individuals trapped within La Manchaland during closure will not be able to exit until its remanifestation the next day.

La Manchaland is divided into four areas: Pretty and Wonderful (Area 1), For Your Mental Health (Area 2), Eternal Carnival (Area 3), and an unlabelled Area 4 in the center of the amusement park.

Area 4, the Wheel of La Manchaland, is closed by a mechanism; a device is located in each of the other three areas, and must be activated to open the way to Area 4. Device activation progress resets after the park's disappearance, so all three devices have to be activated during one opening for Area 4 to be accessed.

Pretty and Wonderful (Area 1) has a red color scheme, and consists of various carnival attractions, including various dressing-up attractions. The main attraction of the area is "Fantasy Blood-shooting", which consists of a narrated fighting game in which guests would "fight" staffing Bloodfiends dressing up as "evil Bloodfiends" with wooden or foam props. The game is framed in a skit narrating a modified version of the history of La Manchaland.
This area is overseen by The Barber. Bloodfiends staffing this area wield giant scissors, one of which blades are made of hardblood and can be enhanced. They wear red outfits and beaked masks.

For Your Mental Health (Area 2) has a blue-grey color scheme. Its main attraction is The Haunted: Bloody Mary, a haunted house attraction with mystery solution elements, described by the Barber as a highlight of La Manchaland. The infirmary of the amusement park is also located here, along with a confessional for the management of the mental health of La Manchaland staff and any visiting guests, run by the Priest.
This area is overseen by The Priest. Bloodfiends staffing this area wield canes, and wear black suits and masks shaped like goat skulls. Notably, Bloodfiends in this area appear much less hostile than those in other areas in relevant Story Episodes.

Eternal Carnival (Area 3) has a purple color scheme. On the map, it features a roller coaster ride. Bloodfiends and Bloodbags inhabiting this area partake in an everlasting parade, with fireworks, singing, and decorative poles topped with human corpses. This area is the source of the music heard emanating from La Manchaland. Before the events of Canto VII: The Dream Ending, its device had never been activated.
This area is overseen by Dulcinea, who also plays the Lady of the Parade. Bloodfiends in this area carry parasols as their weapon, and wear gaudy purple clothing and masks shaped roughly like butterflies. Cassetti played Prince of the Parade in this area alongside Dulcinea (then Princess of the Parade) before his escape.

Area 4 (unlabelled on the map; dubbed The Wheel of La Manchaland or La Mancha Eye) lies at the center of La Manchaland. It is a Ferris wheel resembling a tattered windmill, depicted on the map as a black silhouette framed in yellow. In this area is kept the First Kindred and Founder, Don Quixote of La Manchaland, having been staked to the Wheel during the rebellion of his Kindred.

entries.name: Trash Crabs
entries.content: Trash Crabs are a species of mutant located in the Backstreets of District 21. It is one of the types of mutant found on the beaches of the backstreet. They have evolved to collect garbage that washes up on the beach and weaponize it, using everything from blades to artillery.

entries.name: Four-hundred Roses Corrosion
entries.content:
Log(Written by Meursault):

1. - No meaningful distinguishing features could be identified when comparing this entity to sub-entities of other Abnormalities.

- Their exteriors, while partially hinging on the host's original appearance, share the following commonalities: bodies bound by vines and a flower bloomed upon their heads.

- Upon corrosion of the hosts, the following symptoms could be observed: major loss of rationality and a constant yearning for blood.

- However, another observed aspect of this corroded state is that their consciousness is not completely lost, and a rudimentary level of communication could be established.

- In the case of corroded humans, transformation into a state similar to that of ravenous Bloodfiends could be observed; it was also observed that corroded humans' ability to maintain consciousness was relatively diminished compared to corroded Bloodfiends(however, due to the small sample size, contradictory findings may be present in future research).

- In the case of Bloodfiends, uncorroded subjects have also demonstrated the blood-craving characteristic. It appears that the long period of starvation lowers their ability to rationalize.

- Thus, a deeper level of observation of study is required to determine the distinguishing factors between ravenous Bloodfiends and rose-corroded Bloodfiends.

- Will note new discoveries in a future report.

2. - Other Sinners have posited that the corroded entities would attack utilizing their roses or briar vines.

- It has been confirmed, however, that they employ the same method of combat prior to their corrosions.

- The entity who wielded a greatsword continued to wield it, and entities wielding umbrellas continued to wield them.

- Their combat capabilities do not appear to have changed in a meaningful metric when compared to themselves prior to corrosion.

- There have been two discoveries of note: all corroded entities were surrounded by lights of unidentified sources, and they have been observed to siphon a portion of blood lost from the Sinners.

- The siphoned blood is used to reconstruct itself, but a part of it seems to be channeled to a separate entity.

- Will note new discoveries in a future report.

→ It is likely that the entity that receives the channeled blood is the Abnormality itself. (Faust)

3. - After compiling and referencing all available data that has been gathered through encounters, it can be concluded that these entities are very similar to Bloodbags.

- There is a high probability that siphoned blood is channeled to the source Abnormality that corroded them.

- Sinner #11 made the following query: what happens when a corroded Bloodfiend attempts to create a Kindred or a Bloodbag?

- However, as corroded Bloodfiends have not attempted such activities, no further deductions could be made in that avenue.

- Upon post-mortem inspection of deceased entities, small roses could still be observed on their bodies.

- The roses subsist on the remaining blood on the cadaver; upon exhaustion of such subsistence, it is likely that they will begin to wither.

- No further discoveries are to be made. This observation log is concluded.

→ As the rose is also categorized as an Abnormality, it is reasonable to assume that the entity would not necessarily follow the natural law. (Faust)

→ Corrections to the report will be made, should we discover a sample disproving my statement. (Meursault)

entries.name: Irae
entries.content:
Peccatulum Irae is a dark scrawny figure whose entire body appears to be made up of rigid branch-like structures with glowing red cracks and flickering particles throughout. Two branches emerge from the front half of its body that split into what appear to be humanoid hands resting their fingertips on the ground. Its head has an elongated snout, almost like a beak, one large red eye, and two glowing antennae that twitch frequently.

Its first evolution variant shows a much brawny figure compared to its original variant, making up more of muscular thick structures with similar glowing red cracks and flickering particles. The red eyes on its head appears much larger and fiercer, with its beak looking more like a dangerously-large snout.

Its second evolution variant appears more golem-like compared to its previous variant. Instead of standing quadruped it instead stands upright on four small legs, with its former front legs replaced with two giant heat-blazing sickle appendages. Its eye can be fully seen at the top, brazen in blood red with red fire flickering above its eyeballs. The size of it is much larger than its first variant, towering over most humanoids.

Log(Written by Heathcliff):

Class 1. 
You want me to talk about that pointed thing, aye?
Thing's shaped like a dried tentacle... There was some kind of red liquid in the middle.
Smacked it a couple times with my bat, and the lanky thing was a bit more durable it seemed.
Bigger problem, though... That thing's got a weird way of attacking.
It prods poor sods with its long snout, and... It starts shooting that red water into the body!
It gives me a heartburn like I had some hard stuff on an empty stomach... 's irritating...and suffocating...
A-Anyway, it makes you feel all weird. Makes you mad over wee stuff.
Some even blew up after getting hit by that juice. I really don't want that happening to me.
→ Weren't you always prone to getting mad over the smallest things? (Ishmael)
→ Don't piss me off. (Heathcliff)

Class 2. 
Oh! It's grown!
Its eyes are more bloodshot, and they're glarin' at me fierce... It's got a tail, too.
I think I can summarize this report with "it got creepier".
Looks like its wee dried squid legs got hydrated and slightly thickened. It's still got that red juice that gives me heartburn.
It's still got that stabby attack... but it certaintly diversified its pattern.
Here's the most memorable one. It tried to smack me with its tail! Remember? It couldn't do that before.
Or maybe it could, but its stick-bug legs couldn't support its weight.
Well, it's not really my business.
Oh, here's another thing. The bug learned how to spark fire. Watch out for that burn, yeah?

3. … Haah, an even bigger version of these sods, eh.

It’s grown even bigger than before… like it’s gotten physical augmentations or something.

It stabs with its horn-like hands instead of pecking us with its beaks.

It’s just as irritatin’ when it hits me, but… the red water’s now hot like lava. That’s another layer of difficulty.

When it stabs the ground, pillars of fire burst from the earth. Now I see why the Backstreets blokes say that we should avoid death by fire at all costs.

These bastards, they keep… getting in my way. Glarin’ at me fierce with their blood-red eyes, bursting with flames from the top of its head...

What the hell does it even have to be so mad about?

I’m the one that’s frustrated. This… this awful feeling, like I’m about to burst. Like I’m trapped in.

Look, I don’t even have the time to waste on writing shite like this...

I’ve got to go. Right before me, there’s— (The log continues, but whatever was there is now scorched and illegible.)

entries.name: Luxuriae
entries.content:
Peccatulum Luxuriae is a large pale flesh-coloured four-legged creature with vein-like patterns across its body. It has a long, flat tail like a salamander. Large bumps form along its spine that increase in size as they get closer to the head, which is heavily wrinkled, partitioned down the middle, and shaped like a shield. One bloodshot orange eyeball pops out from the right side of its "face." Two scrawny hands made of flesh twisted around each other in the form of a double helix can emerge from its head to attack its enemies.

Its first evolution variant appears much taller and larger, having taken on an erect posture. Its "face" remains mostly the same, though four arm appendages now appear to hold it and control its opening. Instead of a pair of hands, a large fleshy spike now emerges from its face to attack. Instead of moving on four legs, it now moves with its body, supported by its tail and two legs.

Log(Written by Sinclair):

Class 1. Those look like awful lumps of flesh...

Has an ugly maw at the front... I thought it was a tongue at first, but what's inside that maw was a hand.

A hand, made from two twisted arms coiling around each other. I saw the eye inside stare into me.

As if that wasn't enough, it looked eager to devour me and nourish its flesh.

Even if I couldn't hear it, I could tell.

...It wasn't the first time I saw that kind of gaze.

Class 2. The mass of flesh... has only gotten larger.

It was still lifting its upper body, like it was preparing to... pound on something.

The giant... mouth that was almost like its head... split even further, to the point where its entire body seemed to become a vertical maw.

It flesh is just as awful as before. That unpleasant, rotten fruit-like texture...

Ah, yeah... it still has those hands inside its maw, but...

... they've merged together, their nerves and muscle tissue seemingly... all twisted into one big arm. It's no longer in that weird spiral.

The hand at the end of that arm tried to grab anything it could get a grip on... Its eye rolling around furiously to find something that could... fill it up.

But the hand was so unwieldy, like it wasn't made to grab things in the first place...

Eventually, when it failed to grab anything properly, it turned into something like... a nail or a stake, and impaled us...

Which means that... the...

Ah... I'm sorry... I'm feeling a bit nauseous. I promise I'll finish this entry next time...

→ Huh? Where's the rest of the report, then? (Heathcliff)

→ It must've reminded him of that friend from school~ (Hong Lu)

→ If I was the lad, I won't be callin' that girl a 'friend'. (Heathcliff)

→ I think we have everything we need? Don't worry about coming back to this, Sinclair. (Dante)

→ Indeed. This appears to be sufficient information to constitute a report. (Faust)

→ ... Thanks. (Sinclair)

entries.name: Pigritiae
entries.content:
Peccatulum Pigritiae is a large round rock-like figure with wide red cracks along its body, all of which meet at its center, which has a single yellow eyeball nestled deep inside. In battle, red humanoid arms appear from the cracks to attack units.

Its first evolution variant shows a smaller rock with four other rocks jutting near its center, with blood veins supporting the rock-like formation in the form of a cross. Its yellow eyeball still rests at the center of the rock figure, but has gained more mobility in the terms of having red veins aiding it in movement.

Log(Written by Yi Sang):

Class 1. 

It resembled a rock.

I am uncertain how an object of its mass is able to move. Its appearance could not be any less adherent to laws of science, but when I look back, it might have been an inherently scientific object after all.

It would levitate in the air and stay still.

It rolled its eyeball lodged in the center. And when it felt like it, it would ram into some persons.

I am not yet sure what motivates it to move. Even so, I wonder if it's necessary to learn its reasons at all.

It's possible that this pebble is alive.

No one would call it an organism, but by the same token, I may not be alive if no one refers to me as such.

Perhaps it was simply a matter of laziness.

We were lazy to think that it mustn't be what it thought to be.

That pebble is probably a lazy living being.

And the same could be said of me.

Class 2. 

Red things seeped from what resembles a rock.

Its nature could not be determined; it very well could be veins, muscle tissue, or aught else that carries blood. Thus the most ideal nomenclature for the fluid, for the moment, would be ‘red things’.

With its every movement, the four smaller rocks held by the red things wavered precariously.

It rolls its eyeball still, yet naught seems enough to stir it; it refuses to even ram us with its body.

Instead, it merely swings with what is in its grasp.

Though it oft lashes with two or so of what is grasped, it swings all four rocks at once, from time to time.

As those numbers must originate from its own conscious decisions… I consider this to be a living being.

In other words, I am, in turn, alive as well still.

I merely find it regrettable that the rock is no longer levitating.

It is quite miraculous that such a thin thing can endure the weight of such a heavy boulder… Yet, as it is attached to the earth, it is self-evident truth that it can no longer be said to be in a state of levitation.

What has once levitated, though bereft of wings, has fallen to the earth.

And the rock vacillates hither to thither, fettered to the swaying red thing with no freedom to call its own.

Though its form has changed, its nature remains that it is a lazy living being.

Yet, it may also be said that such staunch resilience to change may itself be a form of assiduity.

What changes is slothfulness, yet what changes not is diligence.

What an odd sophistry.

Such is all I have to say.

→ I.D.K.W.T.H.H.T.A. (Ryōshū)

→ C’mon, mate. Even the incomprehensible lass can’t understand what the hell you’re talking about. Write plainly for once, yeah? (Heathcliff)

→ I believe that this record was composed in quite the luculent incontrovertibility… (Yi Sang)

→ Lucu— Incontro— Haah. C’mon, Yi Sang. You’re doing this on purpose at this point, aren't ya? (Gregor)

→ … I have naught else to say. (Yi Sang)

Class 3.

Thus gathered have the stones to raise a mountain.

Yet where lies the green, its placement so rightful upon the mountains? A glacial cold permeates a corner of heart mine.

Rocks are mired in the grasps of the red thing still.

Unchanged are its motions, swinging and lashing the rocks with abandon—or casting them far away.

Yet, the head that had once wavered so is visible no more.

Nay, the stone is now rooted steadfast into the earth, and the rotund sphere has transfigurated into a deltoidal triangle;

an accurate assessment would state as such—while the head remains still, the wavering has ceased.

What stable form, what stalwart balance it has attained.

Indeed, at the edge of change was evolution found for this entity.

Yet even evolution is no deliverance from torpidity.

The entity’s tranquility, a consequence of electing immobility with stability, is no assiduity at all.

I know not what movement shall it take at the end’s end.

Should its motions cease, so too shall it suspend its sentience.

When, in the end, all comes to cease, it cannot be said any longer that it lives.

How unideal, how odd.

Such is all I have to say.

entries.name: Gulae
entries.content:
Peccatulum Gulae is a densely packed bundle of grey flowers with dark green stems trailing behind them. At the center of each flower is an inward spiral of teeth, like a leech's mouth. A few leaves on the stems reach outward, in front of the flowers, and twitch frequently. A few green eyeballs dangle from the highest parts of each stem.

Its first evolution variant shows a much larger loose stalks of 3 grey cottony flowers with a hole gaping open in the middle, messily coated with blood. On the stalks connecting the flowers is a green eye staring in the middle of the stems.

Log(Written by Ishmael):

Class 1. It happened while I was passing by a jungle.
It was a dense green wilderness full of tall flowers and trees, as well as outlandish bees and butterflies.

You can find all kinds of unfathomably strange creatures in a place like that.

For example... That flower.

It's said that a plant can't normally move on its own. One[sic] it takes root, it stays there for the rest of its life.

That's what people consider a major difference between plants and animals.

But those "plants" were like a pack of rabid beasts.

A group of them charged at us, raising their teethed flowers like it was their head.

Their roots morphed into limbs that no longer serve the original purpose, and there didn't seem to be any space in their bodies for storing nutrients.

Yet, those scrawny stems were hungrily seeking the missing sustenance.

Continuously shoving things into the mouth, despite being unable to absorb any of it...

What an odd creature that was.

Class 2. Looks like it’s bloomed a bit more than before, doesn’t it? It looks a bit greener.

I remember it looking completely dried out, like it’s about to wither away… Not that it’s gotten any easier on the eyes, that is.

Now it has three flower heads and stems stretched out like limbs. I think I saw a tail, too… It’s only gotten more unsettling to look at.

Maybe it devoured a human or something. It’s got plenty of blood on its sharp and fearsome teeth that reminds me of a catfish's…

Actually, never mind that. There’s something weird about these things.

The monster snatched us up using its roots… stems… or whatever it is… like arms.

And immediately devoured us like a starving beast.

But… after it devoured us, it immediately spat us back out like it tasted something awful. I suppose this means that it didn’t eat us for nutrients. Not that it could, given that I didn’t see any digestive tracts or any other organs for that purpose.

But it kept trying and trying… to shove something in its maws.

Not because it’s hungry, not because it needs the nutrients…

Knowing that its stomach, if it even exists, can’t be filled.

Maybe, at the end of the day, this monster doesn’t even need to eat.

Maybe it’s all about the desire to devour. And that’s all it’s got.

Like I was myself, not so long ago.

→ Do you still remember the things she said? (Rodion)

→ Well… I doubt I’ll ever forget what that bastard said, but that’s all. I might turn around to look at the path I sailed through… but I’m not going back. (Ishmael)

entries.name: Morositatis
entries.content:
Peccatulum Morositatis is a floating transparent gelatinous figure filled with a blue fluid of some sort. The lower half of its body protrudes outward and a tangled bunch of pink organs can be seen inside. One light blue eyeball floats at the top of the figure, connected to the lower organs by a single thin cable. Two "arms" reach outward from between the "head" and "body" of the figure and curl back into a spiral shape.

Its first evolution appears much larger than its original form, its internal organs at the lower half are more visible with more organs resembling that of humans in clearer view. One light blue eyeballs floats over its newly formed head resembling that of a shrimp, floating with more tiny tentacles at the bottom.

Log(Written by Meursault):

Class 1. -An insect-like entity with a transparent body.
-Unable to identify several physical requirements for maintenance of life; cannot determine it as an organism.
-Its body is filled with water.
-Objects that appear to be organs are observed inside, but they do not appear to function as organs.
-The water does not appear to play any part in biological activities, either.
-The body of liquid appears to be stagnant.
-It has the face of someone lost deep in thought. It could merely be a resemblance to a species of zooplankton.
-Prolonged observation makes my mind sink.
-Sinking… Reminding me of the past.
-…It is not a pleasant feeling.

Class 2. 
- This is a reminiscent of the previously observed insectoid entity with a translucent body.
- More organs required to maintain a biological organism has been identified inside its body. Some of it has matured further.
- However, no physiological characteristics enough to meet the criteria to constitute a living organism has been identified.
- What appeared to be a 'hand' has been identified. It is visible from the outside, and is wielding a round object.
- A close analysis of its behaviors and attack patterns reveals that the round object is a fluid sac of sorts.
- The fluid inside the entity's body appears to be connected with the sac. When the sac inflates, the internal fluid on its main body shrinks.
- Several organs that may constitute a 'leg' or an 'antenna' has been identified. No particular usage outside of offensive uses has been found.
- Prolonged observation of this identity remains inadvisable.
- Reminders of the negative past events remains unpleasant.

Class 3.
- The fluid sac has grown large on the previously observed insectoid entity with a translucent body.
- With the increased volume of internal fluid in this entity, it may be distinguished from the previously observed entities by the fact that the outline of its organs are no longer clearly visible.
- For the same aforementioned reason, it has been observed that using its internal fluid as a means of attack, proportionally speaking, no longer shrinks its reserves significantly.
- A new organ that connects its head to its back has been observed. It is reminiscent of scales, waves, or diaphanous veil.
- A new behavioral pattern has been observed in which it consumes an unknown substance from human brains via a passage that may be assumed to be an oral organ.
- It was speculated that the entity was using parts or blood of the said organ as nutrients, but such was not the case. However, increase in its internal fluid has been observed immediately after the consumption.
- The fluid filling its body cannot properly be defined within the confines of chemical compositions. On sight and on touch, the fluid has a distinctive property of strongly stimulating the memories of negative past events.
- … Mental state that may be evaluated as ‘negative’ has been continuing long after contact.
- It still remains unpleasant.

entries.name: Superbiae
entries.content:
Peccatulum Superbiae is a large blue wheel-shaped entity with spikes along its rim. Red and flesh-colored scraps are tied around its spokes. At the very center of the wheel is one dark blue eyeball.

Its first evolution shows little difference from initial form. However, the blue wheel is much larger, with bigger spikes along the rim, and a pair of blood vein-like arm appendages sticking out below the wheels.

Log(Written by Faust):

Class 1. The wheel has often been the symbol of technological advancement.
It represents humanity's realization of its ability to think up and actualize things that weren't in the nature.
At the same time, it marks the beginning of humanity's transformation into prideful creatures.
That might be why pride takes the form of a wheel.
The steel circle doesn't ever seem to stop rotating.
It doesn't care if it gashes at flesh or crushes patches of grass.
Because, it can roll…
While others cannot.

Class 2. Human hands and arms are not only parts of the body, but also indispensable tools of creation.

From creating small trinkets, to simple mechanisms, to the complicated designs of Workshop weaponry.

They are tools given to humans at the moment of birth; tools used to bring humanity to endless heights.

That is why the second Pride has free use of its arms.

Yet, the fact that it remains bound to a wheel must originate from the comfort-seeking part of the freedom availed by the two free, dexterous arms

Yet Pride will not, as humans have done, use their greatest tools only for creation.

It will trash and rip with its arms and hands... and inevitably be a part of some destruction.

Its motivation for such violence is simple.

Because it can.

→ It is a tragic thing for an invention to grow distant from the mind that first conceived it. A greater sorrow is that such is true of most creations of men. Including those of my design... (Yi Sang)

→ Does it have to be tragic? Destruction is but a beautiful part of creation. (Ryōshū)

→ Such is also not necessarily an incorrect sentiment. (Yi Sang)

entries.name: Invidiae
entries.content:
Currently, Peccatulum Invidiae has only appeared to exist as exact replicas of Sinners and Sinner Identities, the only visual discrepancy being them shrouded in a dark purple mist. Peccatulum Invidiae? instances also radiates a violet electrical current around itself. Notably, Peccatulum Invidiae instances are capable of utilizing Support Passives and E.G.Os.

While Invidiae can appear as replicas, any attempt of speech, notably when using (corroded) E.G.O, would be in the form of a loud garbled gibberish ■ ■ ■ ■ ■ tone.

The true form of Peccatulum Invidiae can be glimpsed through their corpses. Dead Peccatulum Invidiae instances appear similar to the corpses of other dead Peccatula, being a bulblike mass of flesh with a single purple eye at the center.

Notably, unevolved Peccatulum Invidiae and the Stage 2 evolved form (Peccatulum Invidiae?) appears only to be differentiated by additional strength.

Log(Written by Rodion):

1. Eugh, ya sure this is the time to be writing a report?

I mean, the ‘Peccatula’ are supposed to be like those monstrous things, aren’t they?

Like that mass of flesh, or that toothy plant thing…

But… they’re just like us.

Not just in their appearance, too. They’re copying our moves!

Are ya sure you’re not leaving those ‘Identity Cards’ everywhere, Dante?

Phew. Okay. Now that I’m taking a closer look at ‘em… I guess they’re not ‘just like us’.

There’s this dark layer over them, and they all look a bit opaque, too.

Welp, good thing they appear to be weaker than us. They’re just copycats.

Heh heh, there really wasn’t much to worry about, huh?

They’re just cheap knockoffs, right~?

It really freaked me out when they used an E.G.O, though…

Also, um, ya sure ya didn’t let some of our Identity Cards slip out of your pocket? You should check, just in case.

→ I don’t know if they were ‘weaker than us’… I’d say they were about as strong as you guys. Besides, I will never just leave something important like that lying around. (Dante)

→ Hm… I saw you hastily digging your pockets as we left, Manager Bud. Are ya sure? (Gregor)

→ Dante, you must never misplace your Identity Cards. Please take greater care to store them safely. Losing them will result in a consequence greater than having to write an incident report. (Faust)

→ ... Are they really that expensive? (Dante)

→ They are not items that can be measured by monetary value. Please pay utmost care in storing them. (Faust)

2. Mm… It’s like looking into a mirror, but not exactly.

These ones were all covered in some kinda dark, unsettling mist.

The way that the dark mist danced over their bodies... almost felt as though I was staring at my own shadow.

Yeah, a ‘shadow’. Almost like they’re manifestations of our darker sides. I know it makes no sense, but still.

Oh, and… this one was stronger than the last.

They used the same techniques that we do, but the force behind it was way stronger.

Our attacks felt ineffective, while theirs really hurt when they connected.

Haah… They know our moves, but they’re stronger than us? That’s… cheating.

Would’ve helped a lot if we had their dark mist. I really could've used that extra power.

Besides, getting killed by those things isn’t… the best feeling in the world, y’know?

They just stand there quietly, like we weren’t good enough to beat ‘em. It’s super irritating.

Haah… Nah, I shouldn't be such a downer.

Hey, let’s think about it like this. I can look into a mirror, but a mirror only shows a side of me, right~?

I’m sure there’s something that those fakes can’t copy from us. Something they lack.

We’re real, and they’re not. There’s gotta be a way to beat those annoying Peccatula.

→ What they lack is our Executive Manager’s splendiferous command. That will be the deciding factor in turning the tide of this battle. (Outis)

→ It is as Miss Rodya has said. We have prevailed against greater foes in the past; a path shall open for us, surely. (Yi Sang)

→ Totes~ They’re nothing compared to what we…(something was written here, but it’s been erased) faced before! (Rodion)

entries.name: Singularity
entries.content:
A Singularity is the unique, fantastical technology a Wing possesses which seemingly defy all known laws of physics the corporation exploits in order to conduct its business.

Prided as the precious Egg to be protected by the Wing's Nest and 'Feathers', Singularities possess absurd capabilities and often appear to break conventional laws of physics to consumers, such as providing trains capable of teleportation and time travel to produce time loops.

Every Wing personally owns at least one Singularity, as patenting such technology through approval from the Head is absolutely necessary for becoming a Wing in the first place. Wings rarely use only one Singularity, often possessing multiple patents in conjunction to their main Singularity — which for one reason or another may be kept confidential to obscure how it works to secure the Singularity from being stolen by outside influences. For example, while W Corp advertises its teleportation technology to provide convenient transportation, the tech was a Singularity bought from a fallen Wing which now acts as the coverup for W Corp’s real Singularity — its body restoration technology.

When a Wing is destroyed for whatever reason, the patent to their Singularity becomes public domain and is free to be bought up by any other party, that is assuming the Singularity in question is even able to be reacquired and replicatable in the first place.

Patent War: Patent wars are spats fought between Wings and other megacorporations where they sue one another for patent infringement or accuse one another for stealing their patent.

Fixer Offices often arbitrate for the competing corporations involved, either through settling legal disputes as Notary Offices specialize in, or via corporate espionage to sabotage the competition and gain valuable intel.Third parties that are not the corps involved are usually the sole beneficiaries of the conflicts, as the intense resource drain caused by the patent war are often so disadvantageous that even Wings who win such disputes can be irreparably crippled by the legal endeavors.

According to Nemo, there are unspoken rules that important for parties involved in a patent war:

A corporation must patent their technology separately for areas outside of the Nest or any other domain under their jurisdiction.
Avoid admitting to copyright infringement before carefully reviewing the lawsuit.
The rights to a technology cannot be protected if its details were publicized through advertisements or such before the patent was registered.

Ethics: Every Singularity relies on human suffering to at least some degree — either through subjecting a Wing’s workers to inhumane working conditions to literally utilizing human life as a resource for the technology. Human experimentation for the purposes of testing a Singularity is very common among corporations, either for the purposes of improvement at the cost of human lives or developing a technology to become a Singularity in the first place. Abducted test subjects are often dumped into the Outskirts once their purposes have been fulfilled, many developing irreversible changes not only from the inflicted psychological trauma but also from the physical ramifications of the experiments.

By the very nature of most of the technologies, there is no ethical way to utilize nor consume them, as it is an undeniable truth that at some level: a Singularity requires the squandering of a human life to make it function.

Known Singularities:

F Corp.	F Corp.'s Singularity revolves around manufacturing Fairies, which have the ability to 'open' anything, whether it be in a literal or conceptual sense.
G Corp.	G Corp.'s Singularity involves spheres that can control gravity.
J Corp.	J Corp.'s Singularity revolves around producing Locks, which keep anything 'locked', whether it be in a literal or conceptual sense. J Corp. is a casino corporation, and its Nest is known as a gambling haven; the Wing uses its Singularity to keep its assets secure.
K Corp.	K Corp. specializes in biotechnology that allows for the continuous repair of damaged or lost cells at a rapid pace. The most iconic use of their Singularity are their signature Helapoiesis Bullets, or HP Bullets — able to be fired at injured combatants and heal their wounds in almost an instant. K Corp. also produces HP ampules, injections capable of regenerating fatal injuries. In the Project Moon webnovel Distortion Detective, HP tablets are another K Corp. product that can heal injuries overnight.
K Corp. had entered into various partnerships with other Wings due to their very potent technology, supplying SP Bullets which can heal sanity to R Corp's Reindeer Team and the HP-N Bullets for use in L Corp's main facility.
The Singularity is also apparently used for meat production, although it seems to be unpopular among consumers.

The substance is sourced from The Tearful Thing, a giant eyeball-like being that produces the fluid when exposed to tear-inducing narratives, from heartwarming stories to scenes of horror.

M Corp.	MDM Entreprise’s Singularity is their moonlight stone, a material emitting a golden glow which mitigates psychological affliction induced from mental attacks, pressure, and interference. Its abilities are effective regardless of perception, protecting the wearer from mental harm perceived through sight, hearing, physical sensation, or even direct assaults to the mind. While exactly how the moonstone works is confidential, it appears to amplify a single purpose or thought, causing the wearer to forget the mental pain received from outside interference in order to fortify the mind.
The moonlight stone can be used to gild clothes or be made into wearable ornaments and accessories, which are widely used by Fixer Associations and Syndicate members.

N Corp.	N Corp.'s Singularity is unknown, but they are responsible for manufacturing "Canned Experience", which grants anyone who consumes them experience of certain things.
