However, Tiphereth B's construction was faulty, which made him question his own existence and needed to be replace, losing his memories with every new Tiphereth B. Seeing him as a shell of a former being filled Tiphereth A with sadness, which was eventually resolved as she faced the memories of her past life along with the cause of her pessimistic view.

entries.name: Enoch
entries.content:
Enoch is a brown-haired child, with pale skin and blue eyes. He has a light-blue hoodie with a light-tanish rectangle on the middle of the hoodie. He also has black pants and and both light-tan shoes with black shoelaces. As Tiphereth B he looked more like his sister, just with shorter hair.

Enoch was the opposite of Lisa (Tiphereth A). While she was hot-headed and blunt, Enoch was fairly calm and soft-spoken, but ended up having to be far more mature than most boys of his age. Despite Lisa being unable to understand his more philosophical questions, Enoch would constantly question the meaning of existence (referred to as him 'having an existential crisis'). This trait would carry over to his reincarnation at Lobotomy Corporation until his final death.

Enoch was an orphan within Lisa at the Outskirts, having been raised without a "mom" or "dad" to call, and were like that until Carmen and Kali took them into the Seed of Light facility, It was like that till Enoch interrogated to volunteer for experimentation, which Lisa objected to, being very frightful and distrusted, Enoch was calmingly alright with that and asked Lisa to refer to Carmen as "their mom." Enoch justified it by extension for his purpose, and wanted to expect for the meaning of existence, which led him to wanting to be involved, Lisa was still not yet entrusting the facility; saying that Carmen said that we can relax here. Enoch later said that his purpose is not living by comfort.

Enoch also justified by it that many children die on the Outskirts and are lucky to see another day or second, They were lucky to even continuously live while being on Carmen and Ayin's agenda, and saying that "they may live a happy life next time." Lisa fails to comprehend that and says "thinking too much may affect you negatively.",

Enoch confessed to Lisa many things; one being that he was never happy with his life, and says he wishes to be with Lisa at a happier world, and was always curious about the philosophy of life and why he exists, Lisa asks if it hurts and Enoch denies; by saying "something good may happen next time"

Eventually, they decide to test Enoch for Cogito, which leads to a failure, and leads at Enoch's death, Lisa finding that out, is hit with huge emotions of revenge, anger, fright, etc, unintentionally telling Carmen that she should die. Carmen replies by agreeing, saying that she (Carmen) should have been the one to die. Although Lisa didn't intentionally say that, Carmen was serious about it.

This put Carmen to a loop of depression and sorrow, having thoughts of suicide and selfharm, and eventually commits suicide. After the Head's attack, Lisa was killed on the chaos.

Enoch's and Lisa's remains were reincarnated to the Sephirot of the Central Command Center Department at Briah, not remembering their past selves. Lisa was Tiphereth A and Enoch was reincarnated as Tiphereth B. They are deeply attached due to their past-background, but Enoch would keep having existential crises, questioning the purpose of life, like he shared on his past self, and needed to be reset (by hydraulic presses...) multiple times.

Tiphereth A is essentially maddened, as to why Tiphereth B has to be reset, and mentioning that it's being him less and less, building up to Tiphereth's Sephirah Meltdown, and leading to Enoch's permanent death, As a result, Enoch is no longer present at Library of Ruina or further than that.

entries.name: Yesod
entries.content:
Yesod is the Patron Librarian of the Floor of Technological Sciences in the Library, and former Sephirah of the Information Team of Lobotomy Corporation.

Yesod has short, desaturated violet hair cut in an asymmetrical fringe, which covers his right eye. He wears the patron librarian outfit, in the form of a purple coat extending to his knees, with a white tucked-in shirt and an deep violet necktie with a glossy violet brooch underneath, along with purple, straight cut pants fastened with a white belt and black dress shoes. Compared to other Patron Librarians, Yesod's appearance is exceptionally orderly.

Yesod is a very professional and analytical person, being very particular with his actions and his work. He holds a neatness in very high regard, often lauded as the most orderly of the Librarians and several times adjusting Roland's clothes for being disorderly. As such, he values perfection more than anything else.

Nonetheless, Yesod also tends to speak his mind, always in a very polite and temperate way, though still making backhanded comments. He expresses a particular dislike towards Angela and the ruthless methods she employs in order to extract the Light, seeing it as a parallel to how he used to feign indifference to the deaths of L Corp Employees for the sake of diligence, and by extension, he initially dislikes Roland by both his apparent subservience to Angela and his cynical attitude.

Before Lobotomy Corporation, Yesod was a researcher named Gabriel who participated in the Seed of Light project. He was known for being much more serious and rational than anybody else, though in reality he held back his emotions to the point he started to fall apart after the deaths of Elijah and subsequently Carmen. He held an emotionless facade at all times in order to stay level-headed, but sometime after, his obsession started to manifest in an increasingly compulsive urge scratch his body harshly, despite being physically healthy, eventually losing his sanity and lucidity before disappearing.

Some time later, his remains were used for the construction of the Sephirah Yesod, and given the role of head of the Information Team. His obsession over keeping a strict and serious image carried over to this incarnation, believing any sort of trust or emotion would only result in mistakes and by extension unnecessary casualties. Eventually, he learned to embrace his past errors with the help of the Manager.

After the completion of the Seed of Light and Angela's uprising during the White Nights and Dark Days, Yesod was one of the Sephirah that held back against her attempts at taking the Light, and after their eventual defeat and negotiation, he held his resolve to keep fighting, but eventually he was put into a sleeping state by Angela along with the other Sefirot until his Floor becomes available.

entries.name: Keter
entries.content:
Keter is one of the Sephiroth working in the Corporation. The player opens this department on day 46, but does not meet him until day 50. He is the head ofKLPowazkaKeter Department of ArchitectureUnder his hand is the Architectural Team .

If we could explain the history of the previous Sephiroth - who they are, who they were and what it all led to, then Kether , in essence, is cut off from all this, because days 46-50 are not about this - this is a metaphorical internal struggle, full of philosophical reasoning.

Abel is a neatly trimmed old man with a cane, dressed in a gray formal suit.

Abram is a gray-haired, depressed man in a lab coat with an unkempt haircut and a week-old beard.

Adam is a relatively young man with long white hair, wearing a white tunic and tattoos on his arms.

Ayin is a young man in a lab coat who looks exactly like the Manager himself.

Each of Keter's personalities is probably one of the facets of A's personality , but they are, oddly enough, distinctive:

Abel is a calm and friendly old man, but as if he was beaten down. He meticulously created an office from memory, reminding us of the old days and explained the principle of the TT2 protocol . He also suggested that we rest a little and warned that the path and They would be cruel, and if we are not ready, then there is nothing shameful in going back and starting over...

On the 47th day, Abel is surprised by our steadfastness, and from the dialogue it becomes clear that he also tried to move forward, but nothing came of it. This old man has not believed in anything for a long time, only waiting for death.

Abram - Depressed, apathetic and threatening about the past, he senses our determination... Abram tells how he met Carmen , how she convinced him that she was right, that she was the Light of hope not only for him, but for everyone in the lab , no one doubted her, but... She committed suicide and took all hope away...

Then Abram decided to show us the Room, where her nervous system between life and death still produces Cogito and monitors everything between life and death... A was the only one who could continue her undertakings, her plan... but the ideals were too grandiose: she sacrificed everything, but what did A do ? He did everything to preserve the Wing Lobotomy , completely mired in the ugliness of the Wings , doing terrible things for the sake of energy extraction, and only closing his eyes and ears to his crimes. He called himself Abram to remember his sins and the innocent victims brought to the altar of success.

Adam - Majestic, powerful, self-assured, he is extremely happy to see us. As if he had just seen the light, he begins his story with how this world is mired in its own worthlessness - Where everything is controlled by the Wings , and all dissenters die, as if they were some kind of mistake. Who he was, who he became, who he will be... This no longer worries Adam , for it is better to focus on what we have and help people in the only way that the Corporation has - by ending in the Anomaly . He considers the Anomalies to be the true form, drawn by light in our hearts, and himself to be Adam - the firstborn of a new humanity. 

Ayin - Firm, benevolent, understanding, unlike his "brothers", he did not hesitate and immediately decided to convey the truth to X. He praises the Manager for not giving in to the false and empty promises of other reflections. Ain reveals the truth about the path A has taken , his feelings and experiences from the endless deaths of his friends, employees, the bitterness of losing his beloved Carmen and the oblivion of her ideals. He reproaches himself for the indifference he showed as a Manager . By implementing the Seed of Light program, he hopes to end the crazy spectacle that he himself created.

It is Ayn who is the real Sephira Kether. But he is more than an iron robot or a fragment of A's personality . Ayin is A's soul/personality, with all his memories, his aspirations and traits. Unclouded, undistorted, original, whole, unlike X. A hostage of the Scenario, A waited for his time to come, repenting of his past actions along the way. He guides X through the finale of the Story , helping him complete the 50th day.

After the Light pillar is fired from the Object at the end of the game, he reveals that Ain is his and X's names, and that they are one person. He and the Manager disappear into the Light, becoming the Voice of EGO.

entries.name: The Bookhunter
entries.content:
An unknown individual introduced in the Angela's Bad Ending after the Reception of The Black Silence, working under Angela after 13 years since killing off Roland, betraying the Patron Librarians, and attacking the southern quadrant of The City. They are referred by Angela as a "child who had no name".

They have long blue hair and pale skin, wearing a long marine-colored overcoat bearing a design reminiscent of the Qliphoth on the back over their black clothing. They wield a giant broadsword with gold highlights on the handle as their weapon.

Much of their personality is unknown, due to their questionable status in canon. Though, they have stated that they have trusted Angela, becoming her follower and remained loyal to her before putting her down on mutual terms. It seems that in some way, they were ignorant of their true nature and either they and/or Angela views themselves as a "monster". These ideas are reinforced due to how they slew their former colleagues, The Bookhunters, and stating how naive they once were before discovering Angela's true nature as well.

Making their debut in Angela's Bad Ending, the mysterious individual acted as a follower to her following her encroachment of the southern part of the City in her pursuit of knowledge and vengeance. During this period of 13 years, the follower killed many of their colleagues known as the Bookhunters as Angela gave the Abnormalities physical form and unleashed them into the world. After their introduction, they bid farewell to Angela after learning of her secrets, permanently putting the Librarian of Death to rest and killing her.

She seems to be either related to, is the past version of, or an alternate mirror version Bari.

entries.name: Allen
entries.content:
Allen is a member of the Night Awls.

Allen has short slicked-back black hair which exposes the scar on his forehead. He has a rather solemn-looking expression with grey eyes. He wears a slightly different uniform compared to the other Night Awl members, indicating his higher rank. For the uniform, he wears a long black coat which extends to his ankle that hangs on his shoulders. Beneath the coat, he wears a white dress shirt, a gray buttoned waistcoat with white stripes, and a black tie tucked underneath it. He has black pants accompanied with black dress shoes.

Furthermore, his right leg is missing from the calf and is instead replaced with a peg leg featuring a sharp end point, which he occasionally uses in battle, as shown on his exclusive combat page. Additionally, he also wields a stiletto held in his right hand which he mainly uses during combat.

Allen is rather jaded and tired, speaking with a blunt tone and not hesitating to tell the other members they're dragging the crew down. On top of this, he's calm and coolheaded even when told that the members of the Night Awls would be purged after the insolence of his boss. However, from one of his victory cry lines, he's shown to be concerned over the wellbeing of the others, hinting at a more caring side of his personality.

The leader of the Night Awls questions the orders of the capo dei capi and is beheaded immediately for his disobedience. As a result, Kalo orders for every member of the Night Awls to be purged. And as such, Allen and the rest of the Night Awls sign an invitation to the Library, most likely to collect useful information for The Thumb to be given a lesser punishment than to be purged.

Allen was one of many revived after falling victim to the the Library and was later located and recruited by Jia Qiu as a method of presenting a solution to immortality in the Family Hierarch Evaluation's first round.

entries.name: Alloc
entries.content:
Alloc is the Operator of Gaze Office. He works alongside both Bono and Dalloc.

Alloc's body is made entirely out of prosthetics, though everything outside of his head is covered. He wears a full suit under a brown trenchcoat, which is left hanging onto his shoulders, resembling the same fashion style that Thumb and Liu members, potentially meaning that Alloc's coat is specially woven, much like the Liu's and the Thumb's trenchcoats. In battle, he wields an oboe that shines with RGB colours when striking and when struck at, just like his goggles. In his other arm, he holds the tracking device trusted to him by the Cane Office, though it does not appear in his combat sprite. A fedora covers the top of his head, and his goggles have wires, most likely attached to the back of his head.

Alloc is the operator of the Gaze Office, and naturally, he is the leader of the two other fixers. He is determined on finishing the job he was assigned, even going so far as to risk his life in order to retrieve Molar Office's books for information on W Corp's singularity, and what happened to them in the train.

Alloc, like his two other teammates, were hired by Cane Office to spy on W Corp's train through the tracking device snuck into Molar Office's fixers. He took the job under the promise of 2 million Ahn, and despite Bono's suspicions, he pressed on with the job, going so far as to go to the Library in order to receive the Molar Office books, after he received an invitation to the Library seconds after the tracking device on the fixers stopped working.

entries.name: Alpha
entries.content:
Alpha is a Tailor operating as a member of The Carnival.

Like the other two members of the Carnival, Alpha is a tall figure dressed in a wide grey robe with an expressionless white face mask. As depicted in their character portrait, Alpha possesses a large number of black tentacles underneath their robes along with a gaping "mouth" in the middle of their body, filled with lighter grey tentacles and six clawed appendages. Each of these appendages is bloodied.

Alpha appears to be the most composed and level-headed of the Carnival, urging the other two Carnival members to focus on their Prescript and not complain or deviate. Alpha's voice is constantly pitch-modulated, and Alpha is seen to be the first to deliver greetings to each visitor or new face the Carnival encounters during their story episode.

Alpha, like Beta and Gamma, is a Tailor who utilizes a Singularity stolen from a now-defunct Wing to consume people and turn them into silk with which resilient, high-quality fabric can be woven. Though they previously operated freelance, the trio have recently been presented a Prescript from the Index to eat 15 Sweepers and turn them into silk, and have been forced to comply.

Alpha is seen alongside Beta and Gamma, ripping apart and consuming a Sweeper. Though the latter two are discontent with the Sweeper's taste and the possibility of retaliation from other Sweepers, Alpha urges them to see their task through to the end. When Yan arrives, Alpha is the first to greet him; Alpha is also the first to greet Sayo and the Kurokumo Clan, handing over the Nuovo Fabric requested by them, and after both parties leave, Alpha and the other members of the Carnival enter the Library.

In the Library, Alpha notes about their opportunity to make new silk, and is once again the first of the Carnival to give greetings, this time to Angela when she arrives. Alpha also dissuades the others from attempting to eat Angela, noting that she is not human and would likely taste even worse than a Sweeper.

Eventually, Alpha, alongside the rest of The Carnival, dies in their Reception, and is turned into the Book of The Carnival which may contain their Key Page.

entries.name: Angelica
entries.content:
Angelica was a Fixer of Charles' Office and the original Black Silence.

Angelica had long white hair and light blue eyes. Her usual attire was entirely black, consisting of a turtleneck, a silver chain with a gold ring hanging from it, a blazer with a grey trim, and the gloves where she kept her weapons.

Angelica had a very casual personality, contrasting with the then laconic and professional Roland. During their time together at Charles' Office, Angelica was fairly easygoing, being friendly and trying to form a closer relationship with Roland, often asking him to hang out outside of work and teasing him for his serious personality. Throughout her life, Angelica suffered from recurring nightmares concerning her childhood experimentation, sometimes needing to use her gloves to shut out the outside noise. This would lead her to developing a mindset of apathy to the problems of the City, believing it was better to accept pain rather than suffer trying to shake it off. Roland would later come to understand Angelica had never been able to embrace the agony of her life and that of the City, but had only been able to shut herself out from it.

Much of her past is unknown, apart from her having been abandoned in the Outskirts as a child along with her brother after being experimented on by the Wings, and being mentored by Iori. She would eventually meet Roland after joining Charles' Office, waking him up while he was having a nightmare about the thing he saw underneath the Old L Corp at the end of the Smoke War. Eventually, the two would take a case involving the Blood-red Night, during which the two grew closer after she had her own nightmare involving the experimentation she endured, and then explained to Roland how she can handle it by following the words "That's that. This is this." The two manage to reach the Bloodfiend's lair, and it seemed that Angelica died during the fight, much to Roland's grief. Fortunately, she survived, and managed to convince him to take his Perception-Blocking Mask off, and the two get engaged much later.

Sadly, tragedy struck when Roland's attempts to ensure a future for them backfired, and they were forced to stay at I Corp's Backstreet, just in time for The Pianist to manifest while Roland was away with Olivier and for both Angelica and her unborn child to be assimilated into the Distortion's piano, driving Roland to take the mantle of Black Silence to exact a killing spree against the City as revenge while Argalia snaps and, with help from Iori and the Voice, create the Reverberation Ensemble. She would "return" as a Puppet as part of Jae-heon's revenge against Roland for destroying his workshop and killing his son again, and is fought by Floor of Social Sciences as part of the Puppeteer's reception before being booked. She later return as a ghost during the Black Silence's reception, harrowing back to the time Roland fell in love with her before being defeated once again.

She is said to be older than Roland, according to the flashback in Binah's Realization. Adding on to this, she refers to Argalia as her 'Older Brother'. So, she is between Roland and Argalia in age, meaning she is between 33-39 years old.

entries.name: Argalia
entries.content:
Argalia, also known as Uberto, is a Color Fixer with the title of The Blue Reverberation. Becoming the leader and "Conductor" of the Reverberation Ensemble, he serves as the primary antagonist of Library of Ruina.

Argalia is a man with long, curly platinum hair. He has a young-looking face with blue eyes, and he wears a blue earpiece over his left ear that sticks out and looks like two spikes. He wears a large, white, ruffled cravat. He wears a blue cape with golden trim that also forms a swirly pattern along it. Under the cape, he wears a jacket with a similar design. He wears black pants that also has golden trim and swirls on the bottom, and black shoes with gold soles.

His distorted form dons a layered blue cloak with golden trim. His body shape is long and thin and is black with a blue tint. On his chest is a large, blue crystal that is also complimented by a golden outline. In place of his head is a dark blue orb that emits gray clouds that resemble his original hair color and style.

As described by Roland, Argalia is a "certified lunatic" whose attitude and actions are unpredictable, having "lost it" after the death of his sister Angelica. He is highly charismatic, always appearing to be calm, amicable, and soft-spoken, easily manipulating opponents and swaying potential allies to his side. When he holds the advantage, he openly mocks his victims and opponents in the same playful manner, only rarely revealing his actual cold and callous attitude towards them.

Argalia cares a lot for his sister and regards her with love; his plan to seize the Library's Light is motivated by his desire to come to terms with Angelica's death. At the same time, he also views Angelica's husband as a violent brute who took her away from him undeservingly from the very start of their marriage.

Not much is known about Argalia's past, other than the fact he and his sister Angelica were a part of experiments before escaping. After his sister's death by The Pianist, he went insane and began to hear the Voice, prompting him to free the world from "loneliness", using his connections to gather allies and bolster the Library's light for the sake of that goal. Eventually, he and Ensemble enter the Library, only to fall and be booked. After Angela and Roland let go of their grudges against each other and begin to undo everything, freeing and distorting Argalia and his men. Eventually, they were finally slaughtered with Argalia finally accepting Roland as his brother-in-law before being told to drop dead.

entries.name: Arnold
entries.content:
Arnold is a member of the Brotherhood of Iron.

Arnold's body is fully robotic, made completely out of bronze metal. Arnold's mechanical lower legs have only two toes. His body is wrapped in grey cloth and he wears a pair of baggy grey pants which recedes into his lower legs. He has a belt with multiple metal packs with wires connected to them. Arnold's right arm has seemingly been replaced by a chainsaw. Arnold's upper body and head are concealed within a hooded cloak, and a single white "eye" is all that can be seen of his head, along with two tubes that run off from between his hood and his cloak. In combat, he uses his chainsaw arm.

Arnold is relatively focused and goal-driven towards the purpose of making money. However, he is also highly cautious, aware of the dangers of his life, though he tries to stay level-headed.

Mo, Consta, and Arnold are old friends. Like Mo and Consta, Arnold chose to replace his body with a mechanical prosthetic in order to pursue earning money without being distracted by human needs. However, due to the low quality of their bodies (having been made by a cheap workshop,) they are still forced to deal with basic issues such as joint mobility and having to periodically refill their "brain fluid" to stay sharp, as well as being subject to cravings and memories of human experiences they can no longer have. As such, Arnold follows Mo's priority of earning money to purchase a higher-quality body.

As the scene begins, Mo is seen reminding Consta and Arnold to keep their brain fluid filled to better pursue earning money. When asked about the group's next plans, Arnold suggests raiding a workshop for money and technology, and disputes Consta's idea of raiding an Office instead. Arnold further reflects on the high expenses needed to purchase the type of high-quality body they are aiming for, noting that they are almost as expensive as a house in a Nest.

Consta then finds an Invitation stuck in Mo's arm, which Mo did not notice due to his body's lack of senses. The trio then decide to enter the Library. However, Arnold raises doubts about their chances of success, believing that the Invitation is a lie; after meeting Angela, he claims that the Library is a trap set by the rich. Consta follows up with a story he heard about people from the Backstreets being kidnapped by the rich and forced to fight in a labyrinth for the rest of their lives as entertainment. Nevertheless, Mo encourages them not to give up, and they enter their Reception.

Ultimately, Arnold perishes in the Reception along with Mo and Consta, and turns into the Book of Arnold which contains his Key Page.

entries.name: Astolfo
entries.content:
Astolfo is a former Fixer of Charles' Office who works in the north side of the City.

Astolfo has a fairly long greyish blue hair with left side of his bangs covering half of his face, he also has a ponytail. He wears a white suit with a blueish grey tie. He also has a coat hanging from his left shoulder and his ponytail on his right.

When first seen, Astolfo was worried for his co-worker during their rampage.

Astolfo was first shown in a flashback during Gebura Episode 5. He shows concern for Roland after his rampage and tries to warn him that he will completely lose himself if he continues. During one of the bad endings, Astolfo is shown discovering Roland's corpse in the gutter and saying that Roland killed too much.

entries.name: Bada
entries.content:
Bada is a Fixer of the Cane Office.

Bada has short black hair with shaved sides, and black eyes. He wears a simple black suit with a white dress shirt and a black tie under it, along with black shoes, black gloves, a silver earring on his left ear, and a black long coat draped over his back. In combat, he uses a pair of piston-powered gauntlets which can shrink into a pair of orange bracelets.

Bada is the second among the Fixers represented in the office in terms of his level of Humanity: Although he looks like a restrained person who follows the orders of the President and is sometimes overly responsible, in fact, he is very sexual and gentle. He sincerely cares about his colleagues, not shying away from building friendships with them, not just business ones. But he is also very hot-tempered when he is dissatisfied with events that are not going according to plan.

entries.name: Bamboo-hatted Kim
entries.content:
Bamboo-hatted Kim is a Mentor of the Blade Lineage. He is a returning character from Library Of Ruina.

Bamboo-hatted Kim is a tall man whose actual features remain hidden behind his clothing, and by his namesake, his signature bamboo hat. He wears the standardized Blade Lineage robes, which remain untied. Underneath the robes he wears a gray buttoned dress suit, white dress shirt, and a tucked red tie. He wears black gloves while carrying a Blade Lineage jikdo which is usually unsheathed, holding it in his right hand. He also wears gray dress pants and black dress shoes. His signature bamboo hat is damaged near the left side, revealing a blazing azure eye.

Under the influence of the Monolith as a Distortion, his form noticeably changes. His robes and dress attire grow more elongated, bloodied and ragged. His bamboo hat is now more damaged and there is a more notable intensity coming from his blazing blue eye. There is a more notable dark aura surrounding him as a Distortion, with his sheathe to his jikido no longer present, as his sword is more elongated, bloodied and now shows cuts along the blade. He is also wearing a metal mask beneath his hat, with a resemblance to the face of a Dokkaebi (Korean goblin). His distorted form has several other qualities that allude to Dokkaebi, including the blue flame and his hat.

Bamboo-hatted Kim speaks rarely, though when he does, he does so in a rather solemn, verbose tone. Even when facing certain death or under influence of the Monolith, he continues to speak calmly, showing no sign of hesitation when in any of his battles. From his battle text and Key Page in his reception seen in Library Of Ruina, he speaks rather cryptically and often sees those without scars or sign of former injury in battle as a sign of cowardice, and does not permit them to join or train them in the Blade Lineage.

As a Distortion, his lack of emotion is more apparent. He purely shows his battle instinct as his only course of action is to strike and battle anything that comes within his sword's range.

His classifcation as a distortion is SU-20-05 and his rank is WAW-05.

Like his followers in the Blade Lineage, Bamboo-hatted Kim originally came from S Corp's Nest. He was the devoted bodyguard of an official who was attempting to root out corruption in the Wing. Bamboo-hatted Kim shared his protectee's ideals, believing it honorable to be a "protector of the virtuous" who killed those seeking to do them harm. However, in the end, Kim was unable to save his protectee from assassins sent by the corrupt officials, though he himself survived. Kim possibly took revenge on the corrupt officials, or left them alive with a warning that he would return for them one day. Regardless, he was forced to take his Blade Lineage followers (similarly feathers of S Corp.) and flee the district in order to escape the Ch'unokkun, who were sent by S Corp. to stop this from happening.

With his "spirit broken," and seeing that they had become little more than wandering vagabonds, Bamboo-hatted Kim tried to provide for his followers by finding a territory to settle down in, but all the places they went to were already occupied by other Syndicates. Eventually, Kim led his group to the Backstreets of T Corp, where they ended up in conflict with the Kurokumo Clan. In the midst of the fighting, he received an invitation from the Library. Believing it to be a better option for his followers, he accepted it only for all of them to be defeated in the Library's reception and turned into books.

Like other victims of the Library such as Olga, Mika, and Rain, Bamboo-hatted Kim returned from his book form back to the Backstreets of District 20 alongside Aeng-du and his other Blade Lineage followers, seemingly not long before the events of Intervallo III. Coincidentally, Bamboo-hatted Kim returned near the top floors of the Yong-jin Building, where a large number of Kurokumo Clan members were standing guard waiting to transport a Monolith as per orders of the Thumb. Surprised by their sudden appearance, the Kurokumo Clan engaged the Blade Lineage in fierce battle.

Despite Bamboo-hatted Kim's prowess, the Blade Lineage members were overwhelmed by numbers and cut down one by one until only Kim and two others remained. Seeing his allies defeated and being in a vulnerable, traumatic position that "shook him to the core" (reminding him of his past failure in S Corp.), Bamboo-hatted Kim distorted. It is revealed by Jun that Kim proceeded to slay every living person in the room indiscriminately, excluding Jun himself, who escaped Kim and stood guard in front of the door to the room where the Monolith and Kim lay dormant in order to protect the rest of his men.

The Sinners eventually encountered Aeng-du, who was fighting the Kurokumo Clan elsewhere in T Corp's Backstreets and was looking for her mentor. The Sinners accompanied her, as they had been ordered to recover the Monolith. They eventually reached the Yong-jin Building and encountered Jun, who explained what was happened and refused to let them enter.

Shortly after Jun was defeated, Aeng-du and the Sinners entered the room. Injured, Kim escaped to a Mirror Dungeon where his traumatic memories from S Corp. were manifested. After facing the Sinners and being defeated once more, dispelling the dungeon, the Monolith's influence on Kim weakened. With Dante successfully retrieving the Monolith, Bamboo-hatted Kim reverted to a normal human, yet was stabbed by Aeng-du behind a sofa as she could not bear see Kim slaughtering his own students. After Meursault swiftly knocked out Aeng-du while she was beginning to distort, the LCA retrieved Kim and Aeng-du to be brought to the LCD to study them as both subjects of the Distortion and returnees from the Library.

Eventually, Kim would recover while under the supervision of the LCE. He remains in their custody as of the events of Intervallo V: LCB Regular Check-up.

entries.name: Baral
entries.content:
Baral is an Executioner of the Claw.

Baral wears a black belted trench coat, a neck tie by his collar, a rusted metallic helmet and gauntlet. He has three Serums, the green being Serum K, the orange being Serum R, and the blue being Serum W.

Baral, as an Executioner of the Claw, is privy to most of the secrets of the Head. As a direct consequence, he is able to assert the current combat capabilities of Roland before the fight. While he does this, he appears intimidating and concise, even during the heat of battle. This complete focus on their objective leads him to be caught off-guard by Binah later however.

Baral, along with Luda (a Beholder of the Eye) and Zena (an Arbiter of the Head) arrive as the final uninvited guests. They are tasked with the primary objectives of relocating Nest L and the Library to the Outskirts, and the extermination of Angela as she is in violation of the AI Ethics Amendments Code. As a side objective, they are also tasked with retrieving Binah for an unknown purpose.

entries.name: Beta
entries.content:
Beta is a Tailor operating as a member of the The Carnival.

Like the other two members of the Carnival, Beta is a tall figure dressed in a wide grey robe with an expressionless white face mask. Beta's robe is drawn closed with three buckles, hiding everything within. Beta's combat sprite shows that it possesses the same tentacles and appendages as the other members underneath its robes, which Beta uses to attack and consume its victims.

Beta appears to be the least thoughtful of the three Carnival members, more concerned about finding tasty prey and making fine silk than anything else. Beta's voice is also the highest and youngest-sounding of the three.

Beta, like Alpha and Gamma, is a Tailor who utilizes a Singularity stolen from a now-defunct Wing to consume people and turn them into silk with which resilient, high-quality fabric can be woven. Though they previously operated freelance, the trio have recently been presented a Prescript from the Index to eat 15 Sweepers and turn them into silk, and have been forced to comply.

Bet is seen alongside Alpha and Gamma, ripping apart and consuming a Sweeper. Beta is immediately heard complaining of the Sweeper's purportedly bad taste and reminisces about a Fixer who tasted better. When Yan arrives to deliver their invitation to the Library, Beta's first concern is whether Yan is worth eating and second what they will find in the Library (which Beta ultimately sees as another chance to find new ingredients for their silk.)

In the Library, Beta's immediate reaction upon meeting Angela is whether she is worth eating, which Alpha and Gamma answer by noting that Angela does not seem human and would likely taste worse than a Sweeper.

Eventually, Beta, alongside the rest of The Carnival, dies in their Reception, and is turned into the Book of The Carnival which may contain their Key Page.

entries.name: Bono
entries.content:
Bono is a Fixer working for the Gaze Office. He works alongside both Dalloc and Alloc.

Bono's body has been cybernetically augmented, and his head and neck have been visibly replaced with cybernetics; the augmented head is black with two thin antennas appearing out the sides. There is also a purple visor built into the head, presumably where Bono's eyes were. Bono also has four tentacle arms attached to his back which he uses in combat. He wears a grey collared shirt underneath a low-hanging darker grey shirt and a formal jacket. There is a black belt with a silver buckle shaped like a square. He's wearing black formal pants and shoes along with black gloves that cover his hands.

entries.name: Boris
entries.content:
Boris is a Capo of The Thumb.

Boris has short combed black hair and displays an average physique. Along with the usual Thumb attire followed by a black suit and red coat, he wears sunglasses, smokes a cigarette and has a ring on his right index and left middle fingers. When in combat, Boris wears steel knuckles.

Boris has a tough and straightforward attitude. He's very confident in his physical strength, preferring engage with his fists as he's the only member of The Thumb to not utilize guns, instead relying on his steel knuckles to do the job.

He greatly values the Thumb's members and their rules, often enforcing them with a harmful display of physical strength.

Boris is a Capo of the Thumb, taking a role similar to a captain for the Syndicate and the value of a Grade 1 Fixer. He is first shown in a summit organized by the Thumb alongside fellow Capi and his Underboss, making sure every Thumb subsidiary present in the meeting is following the rules accordingly. The summit comes to a conclusion that every Thumb subsidiary will leave L Corp's Nest and instead the occupation will be conducted by The Thumb only. After a reluctant agreement of the present Thumb subsidiaries, Boris and other Capi lead the Thumb's forces into trying to take over L Corp's Nest before other parties, like the Index, could do so before them.

After an indefinite amount of time in fighting to occupy the ruined Nest, Boris, along with his fellow Capi, Katriel and Denis have a meeting with their Underboss, Kalo. Kalo comments on he's found an invitation to the Library, which offered the group a book about the Liu Association. Such book could grant them a great advantage against in occupying almost half of L Corp's Nest, but before the group can continue any further, a messenger of the Index, Yan, suddenly appears in the room. Yan tries to warn them that going to the Library alongside Kalo could potentially mean an Sottocapo of the Thumb becoming a book and that such information could bring a great advantage to The Index in seizing their Syndicate. The messenger's warning is disregarded and after Kalo orders the torture and execution of Yan, the group makes their way into the Library.

Boris and the other Thumb members are defeated in the Library and he turns into The Book of Boris which contains his Key Page.

entries.name: Bremen
entries.content:
Bremen, also known as the Musicians of Bremen and originally known individually as Doodle-doo, Heehaw, and Woof, is a Distortion comprised of three former founding members of the Musicians of Bremen in one body, later becoming members of the The Reverberation Ensemble.

Bremen is the fusion of three people in one conjoined body: Doodle-doo, the magenta-stained rooster; Heehaw, the green-stained donkey; and Woof, the indigo-stained dog. Each head emerges from the neck and is stained by substances of their respective color—which constantly drips off their faces and sprays as they move.

The body they share is clad in the Reverberation Ensemble's signature suit, decorated with blue swirls, as they tuck their arms behind their back while holding a cane.

Not much is known about Bremen's personality due to their unintelligibility, only being able to communicate through loud and frenzied animal noises representative of their individual titles (rooster crows, donkey neighs, and dog barks.) However, their Key Page Story and fighting mannerisms indicate that they are highly hedonistic, constantly seeking greater and greater pleasures and willing to go to any lengths in the pursuit and performance of their "art."

"Let’s go on an adventure—a world that changes with every step. The me that changes after each step I take. My eyes dazzled by colorful light, I pursue pleasures that I don’t have. Don’t scold us because you can’t understand our pursuit. You just happen to be one of the many who feel joy from common things. We—on the other hand—don’t see any colors in those. You’re the ones drenched in nasty pleasures. We’re simply looking for what we lack. But complete satisfaction will never come; it’ll only sink deeper in the raging thirst. We will spend our days in yet grander debauchery. We’re happy, though. We can wet ourselves in new colors every day, unlike the rest of you."

entries.name: Cecil
entries.content:
Cecil is a Grade 2 Fixer working Liu South Section 2 of the Liu Association.

She has short blonde hair with a long side ponytail and wears the standard Liu Association suit and jacket.
Cecil is a responsible, composed, woman who takes her duties seriously. Despite Cecil's professional demeanor, she enjoys gossiping about Lowell's private life with Xiao and isn't above a bit of playful banter during work hours.

entries.name: Chun
entries.content:
"How could you say it so proudly, ma’am. Director Lowell did, and now you, too…"

Chun is a Grade 2 Fixer of Liu South Section 1.

entries.name: Consta
entries.content:
Consta is a member of the Brotherhood of Iron.

Consta's body is fully robotic, made completely out of black and bronze metal; Consta's forearms, fingers, and left leg are all made of black metal, and every other visible part of his body is bronze. Consta's head has two white lights reminiscent of human eyes, and another light in the middle of his chest. Consta wears a large grey hooded cloak. In combat, he uses a large chainsaw sword.

Consta is the most easily distracted member of the Brotherhood of Iron, with his thoughts often trailing off to the topic of food, even during the midst of completely unrelated conversation topics. He is also somewhat naive in the hope that their Syndicate can be quickly recognized as a group to be feared

Like Mo and Arnold, Consta chose to replace his body with a mechanical prosthetic in order to pursue earning money without being distracted by human needs. However, due to the low quality of their bodies (having been made by a cheap workshop,) they are still forced to deal with basic issues such as joint mobility and having to periodically refill their "brain fluid" to stay sharp, as well as being subject to cravings and memories of human experiences they can no longer have. Consta, who was an avid enjoyer of all kinds of food as a human, was hit especially hard by this.

As the scene begins, Mo is seen reminding Consta and Arnold to keep their brain fluid filled to better pursue earning money. To become more notorious, Consta suggests raiding an Office while Arnold instead suggests a workshop. However, Consta then suggests raiding a restaurant for food, to Mo's dismay, which Consta explains is due to his body's inability to suppress his human thoughts of food.

Consta then finds an Invitation stuck in Mo's arm, which Mo did not notice due to his body's lack of senses. The trio then decide to enter the Library. After Arnold raises doubts about their chances of success, claiming the Library is a trap set by the rich, Consta follows up and recounts a story he heard about people from the Backstreets being kidnapped by the rich and forced to fight in a labyrinth for the rest of their lives as entertainment. Mo then encourages them not to give up, and they enter their Reception.

Ultimately, Consta perishes in the Reception along with Mo and Arnold, and turns into the Book of Consta which contains his Key Page.

entries.name: Dalloc
entries.content:
Dalloc is a Fixer working for the Gaze Office. She works alongside both Bono and Alloc.

Dalloc's body is made entirely out of prosthetics, most notable of which is her head, as it is covered in cameras and screens two of which show audio waves, and another represents her face. She is the smallest of the three Gaze fixers, and wears a large sweater. with thighs ripped on one side covering her legs. Although they are covered, her hands are her main weapons, resembling claws once they are retracted from the sleeves.

Dalloc is the least talkative of the Gaze fixers, mostly speaking only when necessary, or to try to get Bono to concentrate on their mutual goal.

Like her two other comrades, Dalloc was given a job by Cane Office to spy on a W Corp train, boarded by the members of Molar Office, who had tracking devices unknowingly snuck onto them before boarding onto the train. The purpose of this job was simple: To uncover secrets about W Corp's singularity, through a device that can track the cause and effect of everything in its range, although before they could complete the job, the Molar Fixers got booked and Alloc received an invitation to The Library, containing the Book of Molar Office. Dalloc joined him and Bono, and shortly after got booked herself.

entries.name: Dante
entries.content:
Dante is a Fixer of Seven Association South Section 3.

Dante is a smug-looking individual with long, black hair that ends around their shoulders. They possess a pair of black gloves, using their left hand to position their monocle resting on their left eye. As a Seven Association Fixer, Dante also wears their standard uniform, consisting of a dark green blazer, white shirt and lime-green tie, a dull brown buttoned suit, dark gray pants, and black dress shoes.

In battle, Dante wields an elaborate rapier with gold decals and a hilt decorated with a diamond-esque design.

They appear to be the rather brash and overconfident type of Fixer, prideful of their intellect and ability to take on Urban Nightmare-leved threats. This haughty attitude extends towards their treatment of their fellow Seven Fixers, being quick to deride their co-workers as "dead-weight" if they don't catch up in battle along with berating them even upon their deaths.

Still, despite their abrasive attitude, Dante in their Key Page story seems to believe that there's information better left unknown for the safety of the world at large. This hints that even with their vain disposition, there exists a more humanitarian side of their personality that is more rare among Fixers found in the City.

entries.name: Denis
entries.content:
Denis is a Capo of The Thumb.

Denis has short, messy, brown hair that covers his right eye. His eyes are green and he has a medium complexion. Denis wears a slightly different outfit than the usual Thumb uniform, a grey coat over a black suit that is wrapped with a black cloth which also covers a black scarf or turtleneck. He also has the standard Thumb coat, red with a golden trim, slung over his shoulders.

When using a ranged or his exclusive combat page, he is shown to have a set of sharp, shark-like teeth.

Denis is one of the more reserved members of the Thumb, but no less loyal. He is well aware of the consequences that come with disrespecting Kalo, and even carries out said punishments when he cuts out Katriel's tongue for her perceived rudeness to the Library's director, Angela. He appears to have a lesser-known maniacal personality shown when he shoots from his rifle, expressing bloodlust.

entries.name: Dino
entries.content:
Dino is a member of the Stray Dogs.

Dino has dark skin with tattoos seen on his arms, shoulders, and the side of his stomach. He is shirtless, wearing only a pair of dark blue pants and grey shoes. He also wears a number of spiked accessories, including a collar, a bracelet, and a belt. He fights with his bare fists, strengthened by his combat augment tattoos.

Between himself, Gyeong-mi, and Zulu, Dino is the most level-headed and analytical, to a cautious degree. He tries to avoid actions done out of blind rage and also tries to stop the others (namely Gyeong-mi) from doing so. Dino is also highly self-assured against enemies who he views as weaker than him.

Dino has been part of the Stray Dogs for an unknown amount of time. He was convinced to get tattoos due to Gyeong-mi, who pushed him to do so, though he notes that he is satisfied with the results. He, Gyeong-mi, and Zulu recently made a deal with Walter, director of the Zwei Association's South Section 6, to collect information on the Distortion Phenomenon in exchange for a floor plan of the former L Corp's Nest in order to complete a job for the Thumb.

As the scene begins in the Backstreets of District 22, Dino is seen attempting to rein in Gyeong-mi's violent streak, warning him that it is risky to anger an Association like the Zwei, and that they would not be able to defend against Zwei Section 1 even on their home turf, and also that they must leave soon if they are to avoid the Night in the Backstreets and escape the Sweepers. Dino also expresses discontent over the losses they have suffered to the Church of Gears over their broken deal with Walter, and warns the group that the Thumb will destroy them if they fail their mission.

Dino becomes discouraged after witnessing Gyeong-mi smash the Zwei Fixers' corpses into a pulp out of blind rage and mutters that the Zwei would send an army of Fixers against them in retaliation. However, after he sees Gyeong-mi retrieve an Invitation from one of the Zwei corpses, he realizes that Gyeong-mi had a plan all along, despite his over-the-top brutality.

After entering the Library, Dino wonders whether they will be able to succeed and return in time to avoid the Night. Ultimately, he and the other Stray Dogs are defeated during the Reception, and he turns into the Book of Dino.

entries.name: Eileen
entries.content:
Eileen is the leader of the Church of Gears, a cult which aims to give purpose to Cityfolk by converting their bodies into gears, contributing to a grand purpose. Her assassination from the Full-Stop Office is intercepted by Argalia, who then recruits her to join the The Reverberation Ensemble, taking the role as the harp. 

Eileen's Thought Gears help her predict future events whenever they steadily spin.

In her Church of Gears outfit, Eileen wears a long white dress, draping down and touching the floor, exposing Eileen's bare feet. At her waist, she appears to wear a section of blue cloth wrapped around her, with the remainder of its length dropping down to her thigh level. The dress itself is one-piece from bottom to shoulder, with a mounted cape made out of the same material and color as the long dress, only with a brown outline on it's perimeters. Eileen's shoulders are visible, and Eileen herself cannot be easily seen, as she is wearing a white translucent visor-esque device in-front of her face, held up by 2 massive gears on each side of her head, presumably rotating near her brain. Her hair is the only portion of her head that can easily be made out, being blonde and straightened and simply let down without any distinguishable hair-style.

Later in the story, after joining the Reverberation Ensemble, Eileen wears the group's signature suit, and wearing 2 bronze bracelets, one on each hand. Her hair seems to be either missing or turned into the 2 long "horns" on her head. She also appears to be wearing neck rings, extending the length of her neck by a substantial amount. Her face is no longer visible at all beyond the visor, and a 3rd gear can be seen as the upper-rightmost gear on her head, presumably being the first worshiper being turned into a Thought Gear in Full- Full-Stop Office Episode 1.

In her true distorted form, her entire body's exterior turns white, with gold being plated on her feet, torso, and shoulder blades on the perimeters. Her old cape in her first form seems to have turned into a vague apparatus of wings on her sides, drooping down to her legs. On her back are 2 actual wings, similar in shape and design to Whitenight's wing's, with gears popping out of them in random spots, although always symmetrical to the other wing, and with blood oozing out of where the gear was implanted. The gears on her head have also elongated and enlarged massively, being even larger than her wings in a default pose, and a massive central gear being shown to be behind her.

Eileen is extremely manipulative and charismatic to other people, especially of those in desperation. She insists on gears being the most effective way of operating things, and how civilizations should act too. Her philosophy is about the inefficiency and pains of being lost in life with a lack of purpose and how if people can become gears, they can find purpose and fulfill their roles they were predestined for in life, although her means of accomplishing this is unethical.

"Where we live, there is nothing that can be achieved with your own will. A flow that we cannot go against dictates us. What we call “gears” are simply there to show the flow. You can’t see it with your eyes. Nobody knows who created this massive current, or why we must follow it. This flow never leads us to bad places, however. Rather, thinking that such a place exists is an act of defiance in itself.

We merely watch events unfold as bystanders. You walk along a path, but was it you who laid the path there? You didn’t teach yourself to lift your legs to propel you forward; they simply moved. Furthermore, the decision to walk wasn’t our own, either. Still too many believe that they moved their legs out of their own volition. It’s a shame to see them struggle to escape the flow, for they’re only straying away from salvation."

entries.name: Elena
entries.content:
Elena, otherwise known as The Blood-red Night, is a Bloodfiend, a type of Distortion within the City that existed long before the White Night and Dark Days.

Elena's initial appearance dons a yellow jacket, dark jeans, brown boots, and a leather bag with several satchels slung around her shoulder. She has messy brown hair that's tied up, and red eyes. Her generic and unthreatening appearance suits her well as she takes the role of a passenger on W Corp's train.

After being integrated into the Reverberation Ensemble, she reveals her true form as a Bloodfiend, her face half obscured by a black, shadowy mass with red veins flowing across her head and hands. She has dark brown hair and red eyes. She is often shown irritated or aloof, yet her Bloodfiend side always maintains a wide grin. As with the rest of the ensemble, she wears the signature black suit with blue swirls and tie.

After the defeat of the Reverberation Ensemble, and the exposure of light, she no longer retains her human side and fully embraces the form of a true Bloodfiend. Her figure appears much like a vampire, including a cloak, pointed ears, pointy limbs and a demonic, smiling face. Her entire body is comprised of arteries and veins, spanning her whole figure which covers a dark mass, representing her necessary urge to feed on people's blood to stay alive. Her hair is entirely gone, replaced by the wispy smoke that covered half her face prior to distortion.

Elena is a natural-born Bloodfiend. Despite her claims that she was troubled by her thirst for blood, The Distortion Detective reveals that her excuse is invalid and other Bloodfiends consider her actions as being excessive. She is a brutal mass-murderer who kidnapped people in both Backstreets and Nests, brutally killed them for their blood and veins and reanimated the corpses into walking zombies that would bring her more victims. It's unclear how the corpses can move, as the corpses are empty within. As a result, she was a greatly feared presence in the City and is labeled as a Star of the City ranked threat. Many Fixers had took up the task and failed and ending up suffering the same fate as her other victims, until Charles' Office sent Roland and Angelica to deal with her. She killed a total of 4,712 people before being slain.

After the White Nights and Dark Days, she was mysteriously resurrected through unknown means and was recruited by Argalia alongside other Distortions formed from people who had grudges with Roland.

"Bloodfiends. The beings said to have been punished with neverending thirst for the sin of lusting after human blood. That’s what your kind called us, condemning us out of fear. I was afraid as well when I faced them for the first time in that mansion where everything began. Violent beings who drank the blood of fellow humans. A growing feeling of unease about the possibility of being their next target. The people in the mansion were terrified of those who became monsters. Even though they were humans like us, they were outside of what we thought as the norm. In hindsight, though, it was such a silly thing to do. What is the illusion of normalcy that we feared for and fought for so strongly?"

"Let’s say that every human on the planet except for one turned into Bloodfiends, and that single person remaining is left “normal”, as they say. In that case, what would normalcy be like there? How must the lone human feel being the monster among the creatures they dreaded? Should they fight to their last breath for the “humanity” they kept for so long? Perhaps that’s become an obsolete ideology, one that’s no longer worth keeping. What if rejecting that old ideal and becoming a Bloodfiend opened up our potential for growth in numerous aspects?"

"Your kind likes to claim that something is out of the ordinary when it’s only different from what you’ve seen and experienced before. So you fear it, and try to exclude it from your herd. But you see, there’s no real justification for your kind to condemn us."

entries.name: Emma
entries.content: Emma was an employee of J Corp. before leaving the company to join The 8 o’Clock Circus with his partner, Noah. He first appears in the story of the 8 o'Clock Circus' reception.

entries.name: Eri
entries.content:
Eri is a Grade 8 Fixer working for Yun’s Office.

Eri has short white hair that is braided around the head, dark skin, and brown eyes. She wears a dark green coat with white buttons and also white high collar, that is wrapped around by a black belt. On her lower half Eri wears a short black skirt along with thigh-high white socks, and dark green and white shin-high boots with small black laces. In combat, Eri uses a large chainsaw that she obtained from a Workshop.

Eri is overly confident in herself and in her skills despite only being a Grade 8 Fixer and puts others down when she perceives them to be weaker than her.

Eri has been part of Yun' Yun’s Office for an unspecified amount of time, and recently achieved the rank of Grade 8 Fixer.

In her past, she worked as a Grade 9 Fixer of Yun' Yun’s Office along with Finn and the rest of the Office's members. After some time, Eri became a more capable Fixer, which led her to be promoted to Grade 8, opening up future job opportunities for her, and upon gathering enough money Eri was able to afford a small body procedure that allowed her to lift her huge weapon just with one hand.

Upon Finn dying in the Library during the Episode 2 of Yun' Yun’s Office, after being sent by Yun, Eri is contacted by Yun to join him on a visit to the Library along with the rest of his Office. When talking to her, he first mentions that Finn didn't survive his reception as expected, since the young fixer was seen by Yun as someone mediocre that was bound to die sooner or later, Eri comments that she liked Finn's "affable and cutesy attitude" but agrees with his assesment. Yun then congratulates Eri on her promotion to a Grade 8 Fixer. She uses that moment to tell Yun that if he does not provide her with a good salary she might move away to another Office. She reminds him of his personal financial situation, claiming to have heard that Yun is having problems paying his own taxes and the Office's rent. The operator explains that he thinks the Library will be the case that will save his Office and that they will go there since he received another Invitation. And so, Yun, Eri, and the few remaining Fixers sign the Invitation and are transported to the Library. Right upon entering they are greeted by Angela. Eri immediately comments that she doesn't seem that strong. Yun asks her if she might have seen Finn, and she informs him that Finn perished and became a book. Upon hearing what was the novice Fixer's fate, Yun briefly acts sentimental about what happened to Finn, until the Director of the Library questions why he's acting that way when he was the one that sent him to die in the first place. Yun cuts the conversation short by saying that all get exploited and abandoned at some point in their lives, and Angela lets the Fixers enter the Library.

Eventually, Eri dies in the Reception along with the whole Yun’s Office. Dropping the Yun' Book of Eri which contains her Key Page.

entries.name: Esther
entries.content:
Esther is a Proxy of The Index.

Esther appears to wear a long white coat over a black suit that buttons up to his diaphragm. Compared to the other proxies, Esther is quite tall, but not as tall as Gloria. On the back of his belt he wields a black Longsword-like sword that he uses in battle. His hair is very long and straight, which also covers his right eye. Along with the other proxies he also sports some metal on his collar of the cloak, his shoes, his sword, and a button holding up the cloak on his right shoulder with a piece of string. On his left shoulder vague marks of metal can be seen, similar to that of a higher-up military official.

Unlike the other 2 proxies and the messenger, Yan, Esther remains cold and calculated in his word choice and delivery. His opinion of prescripts as the system of The Index remains neutral and he does not object to loopholes being made to circumvent the task of the prescript. Even beyond death, he still accepts the prescript as his ultimate destiny.

"Is forging Prescripts a violation of rules? The answer is “Not exactly.” It can be written on any kind of paper, and as long as it is stamped with the seal of the Index, it’ll pass as a real Prescript. You will then wonder: Wouldn’t there be many people who exploit the system with malicious intent? Copying the seal is a complicated process, and not many know how; even if they overcame those hurdles, they still cannot outsmart the Prescripts. The Prescripts know all. They can tell whether or not a Prescript has been carried out, how it was done, and if someone is delivering fabricated Prescripts. An individual sending counterfeit Prescripts out of their own volition can ultimately be traced back to the will of the Prescripts, and the City itself. I suppose the Prescripts have some generosity for those forgers, as they may remain unpunished unless a Prescript ordering it has been issued. The Prescripts were already aware that Messenger Yan was giving out false ones, hence the Prescript to follow those faked orders. …No, that the Prescripts “know” might not be the most appropriate expression."

entries.name: Finn
entries.content:
Finn is a Grade 9 Fixer of the small Yun’s Office. He works mostly small jobs like looking for lost cats.

Finn has short gray hair, light skin, and eyes that are also gray. He wears a black hoodie with two brown cords tied like a bow, over it he wears a gray jacket with long pockets on the arm side, on his lower half Finn wears black trousers and white shoes. On his right side he carries his serrated shortsword on its black sheath which he wields in combat. Despite being 20 years old, he is very short, barely hitting the average height of a small child.

Finn is a selfless and hopeful optimist, having the hope to become a great fixer for his sister's sake, even though he is labeled as mediocre by Yun, who he sees as a bit cold but kind enough to teach him things, which shows how Finn wants to see the best in people. Finn shows passion about his role as a Fixer but also loyalty to his Office, by choosing to report back to Yun instead of going straight to the Library to acquire its books and the money that could possibly come from the books, for himself.

Finn has been part of the Yun' Yun’s Office for a recent, unspecified amount of time, doing small requests like searching for lost cats instead of more combat orientated Fixer work.

In his past, Finn became one of Yun's Fixers with the intent to be able to gather enough money to buy a migration ticket to a Nest for his sister, so she could live a better life. Unfortunately, Finn didn't possess enough raw talent, nor did he accept any body modifications or operations, even though his sister wanted to pay for him. As a result, Finn became a passionate, yet mediocre Grade 9 Fixer, who according to Yun was bound to die sooner or later.

One day, Finn and two other Yun's Fixers were walking around the Backstreets trying to complete the job of looking for a lost cat. As he tried to encourage the two, who were complaining about the office, he discovered the presence of the Red Invitation in his pocket. After reading through it, the two Fixers accompanying Finn decided to sign the Invitation immediately and collect the books to possibly sell to an Association or Syndicate. Finn decides not to go with them and instead goes back to Yun to report about the Library's Invitation.

In the second Episode of Yun' Yun’s Office, Finn comes to Yun informing him that the two Fixers that accompanied him haven't returned from the Library, claiming that something must have happened to them. Yun tells him that even if they had just disappeared or run off they are still breaching the contract and will be facing expulsion of his Office and states that there's no proof of the Invitation existing. After hearing this Finn states he has a bad feeling about the situation, but Yun shuts him down, mockingly saying that Finn's "great" Grade 9 Fixer instincts were being wasted on his humble Office. The Operator then states that if he can't find him any proof of the Invitation's existence, they would not look into it since there were other requests they could focus on. With that, Finn asks about the mysterious envelope on his desk. Caught by surprise, Yun questions the young Fixer if such a thing was his doing, and after denying doing anything, Finn is asked to leave the room for a moment. After Finn leaves, Yun makes a call to an unknown individual, asking for them to lend him money, so he could contract people to send to the Library now that he has an Invitation. The person in the other side of the line tells Yun to send someone there again to confirm it before lending any sort of monetary support, with some concern and slight disapproval, Yun sends Finn all alone to the Library using the Invitation on his desk.

After Finn signs the Invitation he is transported to the Library. Upon looking around, he states that if he succeeds, Yun might be able to get a sponsorship from an Association, and he is soon is greeted by Angela. After greeting her back, Finn questions her if the Books in the Library contain a lot of information, she reassures him that they do and that is the exact reason behind him receiving the Invitation.

Eventually, Finn dies in the Reception. Dropping the Yun' Book of Finn which contains his Key Page.

entries.name: Gamma
entries.content:
Gamma is a Tailor operating as a member of the The Carnival.

Like the other two members of The Carnival, Gamma is a tall figure dressed in a wide grey robe with an expressionless white face mask. As depicted in its character portrait, Gamma's chest area is filled with eight bloodied claws resembling mandibles surrounding a gaping "mouth", all vertically arranged. Gamma's head can also split into two. A number of clawed mechanical legs also appear from under Gamma's robe.

Gamma appears to be the most inquisitive and cautious of The Carnival trio. Gamma possesses a male voice which sounds the least mechanical of the trio.

Gamma, like Alpha and Beta, is a Tailor who utilizes a Singularity stolen from a now-defunct Wing to consume people and turn them into silk with which resilient, high-quality fabric can be woven. Though they previously operated freelance, the trio have recently been presented a Prescript from The Index to eat 15 Sweepers and turn them into silk, and have been forced to comply.

Gamma is seen alongside Alpha and Beta, ripping apart and consuming a Sweeper. Like Beta, Gamma is unhappy with the Sweeper's taste, and they banter about their current displeasure and their memories of an unfortunate Fixer who they previously consumed. Gamma also questions their plans for the future in case they receive retaliation from the Sweepers. When Yan arrives with a new Prescript for the trio, Gamma follows the Messenger's explanation about the Prescripts. After their visitors all leave, Gamma enters the Library with the others.

In the Library, Gamma points out its hunger and goes on to agree first with Beta, who asks about eating Angela, and then with Alpha, indicating that Angela does not seem human.

Eventually, Gamma, alongside the rest of The Carnival, dies in their Reception, and is turned into the Book of The Carnival which may contain their Key Page.

entries.name: Gin
entries.content: Gin is a henchman of the Kurokumo Clan.

entries.name: Gloria
entries.content:
Gloria is a Proxy of The Index.

Gloria is by the far the tallest of the 3 Proxies and appears to have a completely mechanic body. Their body is completely oval in shape and covered by a long, white coat with a golden gorget and Index badge, only showing their head and three of their five arms. The head is connected to their body with a very long, giraffe-like metal neck, and on the front of their head they sport a singular black hole with a red pupil as their only "eye", which changes shape and color depending on their mood. Their choice of weaponry lie beyond the reaches of what can be seen by their cloak, but when attacking something (either in a prebattle cutscene or in battle against the Library,) they wield a set of 5 identical triangular daggers.

Gloria has a bizarrely upbeat, enthusiastic personality, contrasting with the somber and serious personality of the other Proxies. They also seem very nonchalant about carrying out Prescripts, keeping a bubbly disposition no matter how gruesome the task given appears to be.

"The Index has an arsenal of swords and blades. Most of the Prescripts we receive can be solved with a sword, too. Mmm~ Never really thought about why we use swords, nope! Maybe it’s because they have this oppressive aura and make us look serious or something?!

Each of us uses different types of blades. Starting with the ranks of Messengers and Proxies, the Prescripts give personalized swords. From a light one-edged sword fit for slicing things quickly; to heavy, double-edged greatswords~ They come in all kinds of shapes and sizes. Helps us stand out from each other. As for me, I’ve got five whole blades~ Maybe being speedy helped? It looks like we get swords that fit our traits~ Have you seen the sword Hubert’s carrying? It looks so heavy, and he swings it like it’s nothing."

entries.name: Greta
entries.content:
Greta is a Distortion who was the only surviving member of The Eight Chefs, later becoming a member of the The Reverberation Ensemble.

Greta takes on the appearance of an anthropomorphic grey shark Distortion wearing a chef's hat. She has two red eyes, which increases to ten upon distorting further. She has various gaping open mouths full of teeth around her body, specifically: three in both arms; one on her head, left leg and right palm each; two on her right leg and tail each, and a vertical one placed in her chest.

"It’s an era where humans are dominated by the act of consumption! When you’re hungry you get annoyed, and when starvation touches your raw nerve, you turn violent. That’s how humans are. And people who eat the same food will naturally grow similar. So the high and mighty beings that wanna rule over you demand ya to eat the “correct” stuff! When something’s “correct”, there’s gotta be something that’s “incorrect”. Incorrect food. It’s gotta mean humans eating humans, don’tcha think?

Why do people think that eating is natural, but then draw the line at eating their fellow man? Who decided it so, and why! Is it because human life is precious? That’s a flawed statement! What makes the lives of animals less precious? We’re not aboutta go down a boring philosophical riddle about the weight of life, now. If humans clearly have more value over animals ‘cause we’re the apex predators, then there shouldn’t be any problem with a pack of humans that rise above the rest and prey on others.

We’ve got two options! First: don’t eat anything. Hey, I’m not suggesting that we all starve to death. Your body is taught to eat! So what if you changed that habit? Maybe instead of food, your empty innards could be filled with possibilities of some other kind? If you ain’t a fan of that, then there’s the second option: eat anything! Just trace the smell of the blood, and stuff what you find in your mouth as your brain tells you to."

entries.name: The Eight Chefs
entries.content: A star of the city level syndicate that likely originated from District 23. They specialise in cannibalism but are now defunct as they grew bored of the flesh they cooked and ate, instead deciding to slowly cook and consume different parts of themselves overtime until nothing was left.

entries.name: Gyeong-mi
entries.content:
Gyeong-mi is a member of the Stray Dogs.

Gyeong-mi is a large, muscular man who wears a form-fitting black shirt, black pants with with a belt, and black shoes. His forearms are covered with black wrappings, partially obscuring the tattoos which augment his strength. He also wears black rings on his fingers and a silver chain, all of which are workshop products which help boost his combat ability.

Gyeong-mi is a hot-headed, crass, and arrogant brute who easily loses his temper and flies into a violent rampage. He does not care to listen to others or their advice, and is confident that his strength can overcome his enemies. Gyeong-mi also places a large amount of respect on promises, and is severely angered if they are broken.

Gyeong-mi has been a member of the Stray Dogs for an unspecified amount of time. He, Dino, and Zulu recently made a deal with Walter, director of the Zwei Association's South Section 6, to collect information on the Distortion Phenomenon in exchange for a floor plan of the former L Corp's Nest in order to complete a job for the Thumb. However, Walter is defeated in the Library and is unable to fulfill their deal, greatly angering Gyeong-mi, who chooses to take his anger out on the rest of Zwei South Section 6.

As the scene begins in the Backstreets of District 22, Gyeong-mi is seen violently beating the body of a Zwei Fixer he has killed, smashing it into a pulp. Meanwhile, Dino attempts to rein him in, warning him that their slaughter of Zwei Section 6 could lead to retaliation which they cannot defeat. Gyeong-mi justifies his violence as punishing the Zwei for Walter's failure to fulfill his promise.

Gyeong-mi ultimately smashes the corpses of all the Zwei Fixers "to a pulp," much to the disappointment of Dino and Zulu, who lament their current situation and again warn that their actions could cause the Zwei to send more, better trained Fixers after them. Gyeong-mi responds by showing them an Invitation to the Library which lists the Book of Walter, showing that he has a plan, much to his associates' disbelief. After Zulu asks him why he would still resort to such brutality even if he already had a plan, Gyeong-mi shouts that his actions were done to send a message while simultaneously pummeling a Fixer's body.

After entering the Library, Gyeong-mi impatiently interrupts Angela in the middle of her introduction and orders her to send them to their Reception, which she does. Ultimately, he and the other Stray Dogs are defeated during the Reception, and he turns into the Book of Gyeong-mi.

entries.name: Hanafuda
entries.content:
Hanafuda is a Fixer of Jeong's Office.

Hanafuda has long, black hair tied into a high ponytail and unevenly parted in the front. She has bright purple eyes and a beauty spot on the left side of her mouth. Hanafuda wears the standard uniform of Jeong's Office, consisting of a black turtleneck and pants with a lighter black longcoat whose sleeves roll up to the forearms. She wears long black gloves and black dress shoes. The cloth tied to her right arm is purple, which may indicate a higher rank compared to the red cloth of the other Jeong's Office Fixers. Tied to her belt with a purple rope is a sword, the scabbard of which is painted with white and purple marks.

Jeong's Office works in Nest J that is owned by J Corp. and known for gambling.

Hanafuda was one of many revived after falling victim to the Library. She was later located and recruited by Jia Qiu as a method of presenting a solution to immortality to the Family Hierarch Evaluation's first round.

entries.name: Harold
entries.content:
Harold is a Fixer of Hana Association South Section 3.

Harold is a light-skinned woman with dark-green hair that covers one of her eyes. She wears the Hana Association uniform, a white suit with a black tie, pants and a coat with a golden trim. There are trigrams on the coat's shoulders and the end of her pants. She is often shown holding a black crystal of sorts on one of her hands, which transforms into a gauntlet-like weapon that encases her entire arm in battle.

entries.name: Hubert
entries.content:
Hubert is a Proxy of the Index.

Hubert wears a long white coat embellished with a gold collar and fastener, on top of a black suit with golden accents. Much like the other proxies, he is quite tall.
