He wears 2 gauntlets that appear to change shape to suit combat, as shown by his combat pages 'Somber Procuration' and 'Decapitation'. He has short black hair with a loose strand to the side. On his face he wears a metal mask that covers his nose and mouth. He also appears to have some scarring across his eye.

Hubert is one of the more quiet Proxies, following the Prescript with no resistance and completing each job to the agreed consensus of Gloria and Esther. He follows the prescript to its description, but counters action when the Prescript has been followed, as noted by Hubert's comment that the Prescript did not specify to bring down the speared bodies the Prescript ordered dead, as asked by the Blue Reverberation. Like Esther, he does not show anger at his co-worker's betrayal, and reminds Gloria that what matters is that the Prescript is followed.

After a Prescript for the Index Proxies was received ordering the removal of limbs and skewering of Thumb employees was carried out, Hubert, Esther and Gloria are confronted by the Blue Reverberation who requests to take the bodies for his own use, likely to form the army of puppets the Puppeteer uses for the Reverberation Ensemble. Hubert states that they weren't requested to take them down, but Argalia counters that it's a personal request, rather than a question of the Prescript. The Index Proxies are conflicted about giving the Blue Reverberation his way but ultimately allow Argalia to take them as the Prescript has already been fulfilled and doesn't specify that the bodies must remain after the fact. After this encounter, the next Prescript orders the Proxies to enter the Library, as fabricated by Yan, as an act of rebellion against the Index and its cruel treatment of the people of the City. Gloria is upset by this, but Hubert notes that there is no such thing as betrayal to the Index, but whether or not someone has followed their Prescript. Ultimately, since this Prescript exists, it's considered legitimate, and the Index Proxies take their invitations to go to the Library.

"There are a number of ranks within the Index. Proselytes, Messengers, and Proxies are as much as I know.

Those who have been chosen by the Prescripts will decide whether to become a Proselyte. If they accept it, they will cover their eyes with a blindfold as they serve the role. The blindfold has little symbolic significance; it’s to teach the Proselyte to follow the Prescripts regardless of what is happening before their eyes. Usually, a group of five to six Proselytes accompany a Proxy, learning the rules of the Index and the role of each rank. If a Proselyte shows a certain level of competence, the Prescripts will assign the role of a Messenger or a Proxy to them. After being promoted, they are given a blade of their own, and they may take off the blindfold.

The Prescripts are a predetermined path; there is no point for Proselytes to refuse any. It’s still within their choice to decline the Prescript’s offer. Even though they’re free to quit anytime, no one knows if the Prescripts will allow it. The Prescripts might order Proxies to kill the runaway who abandoned their position, or let it slide, or even give the order to resign first. The Prescripts are truly unpredictable."

entries.name: Iori
entries.content:
Iori is a Color Fixer known as The Purple Tear. She is an interdimensional traveler who wishes to see her mysteriously lost son, and attempts to arrange the right circumstances for this to happen through mentoring and teaching young to-be fixers, most notably Argalia and possibly Roland. Though she is hinted about her role by Roland, she is first seen in her namesake following her forced retreat by The Reverberation Ensemble.

Iori is a towering, mature woman with straight dark hair that goes down to her ankles and transitions into a purple color, pulled back with a silver hairband that shows a receding hairline. She wears a purple coat that signifies her Color Fixer title, lustrous and with a snakeskin pattern to it and cinched with a pair of beige belts. Underneath, she wears what appears to be a mesh top that shows her cleavage and black leggings, accessorized with a gold collar, a pair of earrings and a single ring on her left hand.

She additionally wields a set of three blades: A rapier with a white-dashed sheath and a snake-shaped guard, used for pierce attacks, a straight sword entirely colored purple, used for slash attacks, and a massive, rectangular greatsword on her back, with a black-colored blade and red ribbons on it used for blunt attacks.

In combat, Iori has a specific fighting style, that being her use of Stances. Iori has four separate sets that she can switch between constantly. The stances being: Piercing, Slashing, Guarding, and Blunting.

Iori is a smug yet intelligent individual that has taken the task to mentoring Argalia, A certain fixer, and Kali. She seems more knowledgeable than she lets on, leading Argalia astray til he found out through The Voice. Even then, when confronted, she isn't even aggravated and instead decides to talk to him casually.

She is a mother and she cares dearly for the child she lost 40 years ago; her finding him well is the sole reasoning for her actions throughout the game.

She is also a driving force in Leviathan and her action ripples through Vergilius's life.

"If you’re reading this book, it must mean there’s something you want to know about me. I’m sure you have lots of questions, but I sadly can’t give out detailed answers. It’s hard to come up with a definition and explanation for a power that naturally emerged, you see? How should I put it, in that case…"

"I can travel through time and space and see a myriad of possibilities, too many for you to possibly fathom. It’s probably a little bit different from time travel as you commonly imagine it. The future self who experienced a certain past returns to it in order to change the future… Whatever is going on in the past, some kind of paradox is bound to happen to causality. Big or small. Little things can set off massive twists, like the flap of a butterfly’s wings causing a tornado… And even I’m afraid of bearing that risk. It could turn into a cycle of meaningless struggles."

"Yeah. I guess it’s fairer to say that I travel to a completely different space. Ever thought about the possibility that an infinity of different versions of the world you live in might exist? Let’s say that you sidetracked on your way home and were killed by some Syndicate members that ambushed you. But in another world, you might have decided you wanna go straight home, and the assault would’ve never happened. Or, you might have noticed the Syndicate members as soon as you stepped into the wrong alley and quickly got back on track. Those small choices can add up, and result in countless worlds where countless outcomes unfold. …I know what you’re thinking; this isn’t logic that can realistically be proven. I know all of this sounds unbelievable. People can’t understand me because of that, and even I have difficulty explaining myself."

"I made it sound grandiose, but this power isn’t almighty by any means, so I try not to use it carelessly. Not that I expect you to care for such details. It’s already complicated enough as it is, isn’t it? Just know that this power isn’t omnipotent. No power is conveniently given to you in this world, after all; there’s always a price you need to pay, and there is a world I yearn to reach, no matter that price. I’m doing this so I can find the world where I can see that possibility."

"And in the many worlds I’ve been to while doing this job… I saw many people who were lost after losing their precious stuff, just like me. I couldn’t just pass them by. They looked so miserable and pitiful. Well… It wasn’t entirely out of goodwill. The fact that they were worth helping played a big part. Once again, nothing in this world is free. I didn’t quite pity them as much as I weighed up the favors they could give me in return. Thanks to that, I’ve become acquainted with quite a few Fixers… And as corny as it is to say this myself, some even started calling me their mentor, and became my devoted admirers."

"Lots of people ask me what I’m going to such great lengths to see. A leading figure that commands powerful Fixers who are on the level of a Color? I dunno. All I want is to meet my son, whom I had to part with in the most unfortunate way. Meaning I don’t care about the ancillary stuff. I can see it so faintly… It almost seems to be within my reach, but it always ends up being a mirage."

entries.name: Irina
entries.content: Irina is an insurer Mirae Life Insurance.

entries.name: Isadora
entries.content:
Isadora is a Fixer of Section 6 of the Zwei Association's Southern Branch.

Isadora has black hair tied back into twin pigtails. She wears the uniform of the Zwei Association, this being a pale collared shirt and a black tie, tucked into black pants secured with a silver belt, as well as black boots. Over all this, she wears a marine blue Zwei coat. In combat, she uses a black Zwei sword.

Isadora tries to remain impassive and professional as an Associate Fixer, acting strictly by-the-book even to those she considers close friends. Nevertheless, she is highly reliable both in her work and to her friends, and will work as hard as possible within official capability to help them. Despite her seemingly harsh attitude, she is also easily flustered by her friends.

Isadora and San are close childhood friends, having grown up together in the Backstreets of District 21 together. At one point, the two faced a serious danger in the streets at night, and San attempted to protect Isadora with a tree branch despite being equally as frightened as her; this amused Isadora, and the memory stuck closely with her, though not the details of how they managed to survive.

Isadora and San became Fixers at the same time and even ended up being assigned to the same Office, where they met Julia, who was also a first-time Fixer assigned to the Office. The three quickly befriended each other, with Isadora even trusting Julia enough to tell her about San's cowardly past. They eventually left the Office and parted ways; Isadora and Julia joined the Zwei Association and ended up in Section 6 of its Southern Branch, while San created his own Office, Streetlight Office, and became an affiliate of the Zwei. Isadora was assigned to office work in Section 6's headquarters, and has not seen field work for a length of time.

In the introduction of Urban Myth, Isadora is heard being asked for updates on the Distortion Phenomenon by her superior Walter. She replies that Zwei Section 1 and the Hana Association have listed the Laundry of Dreams, Yesterday's Promise, and The Church of Gears as potential suspects. After she adds that the Library, only an Urban Myth at the time, is also being considered as a suspect, Walter scoffs at their superiors' seeming cluelessness and use of "random guesses."

In Episode 1 of the Zwei Association, Isadora and Julia are seen meeting with San as he requests the Association's help in entering the Library and recovering his deceased subordinates' Books. Despite pleas from Julia to help him as a friend, Isadora first rebukes and reprimands him for breaking Association procedure before finally acquiescing, revealing that she was already laying the groundwork to help him through official means; collecting information on the Library to have the Hana Association raise its threat grade to Urban Legend so that the Zwei can formally investigate it, which is a success. This leads both San and Julia to thank her profusely, which flusters her slightly. She then passes an Invitation from San along to several Zwei Crewmembers, who use it to enter the Library.

In Episode 2 of the Zwei Association, Isadora addresses San and Julia, informing them that they are part of the Zwei search team which is set to enter the Library. She urges them to collect as much information (via Books) from the Library as possible despite the mission's main objective being to recover the Books of Lulu and Mars. San then questions why the Zwei is organizing such a mission despite its purpose being peacekeeping; Isadora answers by asking San why he came to the Zwei if he knew that and why he did not ask his brother Bada for help. San refuses to speak of his brother and lets the matter drop, but Isadora decides to reveal the truth: the Zwei Association is investigating the Distortion Phenomenon to try and prevent further incidents like the Pianist, and they believe the Library may hold clues. After Julia notes that she has heard of related incidents and San indicates that he understands, Isadora concludes that the Library is still only one of the Zwei's suspects and thus there will not be any higher-graded Fixers helping investigate it for the time being. Afterwards, San and Julia prepare to leave for the mission and thank Isadora for her help, causing her to stutter and deflect what she did for friendship onto her work once more.

In Episode 3 of the Zwei Association, Isadora is seen in her superior Walter's office, trying to convince him to have Zwei South Section 6 keep investigating the Library after San and Julia fail to return, detailing the Library's modus operandi and even claiming that it is connected to the Distortion Phenomenon based on the Zwei's inability to analyze it. Walter notes that it is rare for Isadora to make "baseless" claims, and hints that Isadora simply wants revenge on the Library for her friends' fates. He refuses her request, citing the many more urgent requests Section 6 already has to handle, and tells her to remember the Zwei's purpose. However, this changes after he finds an Invitation in his desk with the Book of the Distortion on it, and he quickly reverses his decision, assembling a new team including himself and Isadora to enter the Library - the first field mission either of them have received in some time. Inside the Library, Walter is self-assured, commenting on their chance to elevate their careers, complete their mission, and satisfy Isadora's revenge all at the same time, but Isadora is hesitant and does not like the situation. When greeted by Angela, Walter goads her over her true nature as an AI, and Isadora tries to convince him that it is unwise to do so.

Ultimately, Isadora falls during the Reception and is turned into the Book of Isadora, losing her chance to avenge her friends.

entries.name: Jack
entries.content:
Jack is the sous-chef of Pierre’s Bistro from District 23. He cooks and prepares dishes using human flesh as the main ingredient but also hunt his ingredients with the help of the Bistro's owner Pierre when they're unable to receive any meat from their vendors.

Jack has long black hair, slightly tanned skin, black eyes and pierced right eyebrow. He wears a long white chef suit under a leather apron and gloves along with long gray pants and black boots which all have blood stains over them. In combat, he wields a cleaver.

Jack has a calm temperament and is careful when hunting ingredients to insure that they don't get bruised and lower their quality value.

Although being a cannibal and probably a sadist, he is loyal to Pierre who he has a lot of respect for, to the point he wishes to help her achieve her dream of becoming part of 'The Eight Chefs' and tries to keep his promise to her until the end.

Jack is the sous-chef of Pierre’s Bistro, a small restaurant in District 23 that uses mostly human meat. He works side-by-side with, and is unflinchingly loyal to, the head chef Pierre. In his past, Jack joined Pierre when she opened her Bistro to help her achieve her dream of joining 'The Eight Chefs', both promising that they wouldn't abandon one another.

Pierre was trying to come up with a new dish, but she is left frustrated because she is unable to do it since nothing has struck her with inspiration. Moments after, Jack enters the room bringing some "ingredients" (captured humans) with him. Both converse about how their vendors, Lil' Piggy's and The Musicians of Bremen, stopped trading with them and that also they have to find a new place to hunt their ingredients since their old spot is now being safeguarded by the Zwei Association. Pierre and Jack also comment about how she desires to become one of 'The Eight Chefs' and about changing some of their dishes, with Jack suggesting using more aged ingredients instead of the younger ones, but Pierre had another idea in mind.

The Bistro's owner states that she wants their dishes to have a more original flavor which she wishes to achieve by using the meat of monsters instead of human flesh. Pierre mentions the Library as the place they will seek for such ingredient since otherwise, they would have to travel to the Outskirts to get it and she reveals that she received an invitation to enter the Library a while ago. She asks Jack to join her in such adventure for monster meat, which he accepts.

While Pierre prepares to sign the Red Invitation, Jack questions her about what he should do with the ingredients he brought, she answers him saying that they should be made into meat jam and states that Jack must put them legs first, not head first in some sort of not mentioned machinery to prevent the ingredients to die too quickly claiming that the more they suffer the tastier their meat will be.

Upon being transported to the Library, Pierre comments on the place's smell and how it is brand new for her, but Jack states his dislike of said scent. The chef de cuisine affirms unfamiliarity similar to the one brought by it is what brings forth new ideas. Upon ending that conversation both are greeted by Angela. Pierre loudly comments on her exterior, saying she appears to be a wonderful-looking ingredient with a glossy appearance, Jack also says that Angela appears to be a fresh and top-grade ingredient but shows uncertainty on his remake and silently inquires Pierre about the Director of the Library. The bistro's owner confirms his suspicions by stating that she is aware that Angela is, unfortunately for them, not human, but remaking that such a fact only makes her more excited. After Angela is questioned about what her taste would be, she reveals to her guests that she can't be harmed, to which Jack replies that they will only be able to know if such a thing is the truth after testing her. Pierre decides to intervene saying that they should keep their manners to the individual that sent them the Invitation, the sous-chef apologies to the Library's Director for his rudeness. At least Pierre politely requests Angela's permission to enter the Library, which she concedes.

Eventually, Jack is defeated in the Reception along with Pierre, and is turned into the Pierre' Book of Jack.

entries.name: Jae-heon
entries.content:
Jae-heon, otherwise known as The Puppeteer, is a Distortion and a member of The Reverberation Ensemble, taking the role of Second Violin.

Jae-Heon whilst disguised, and likely before distorting, is a man with voluminous white hair and yellow eyes. He wears a brown sweater, a tan overcoat, blue jeans and brown shoes.

His true appearance is that of a multifaceted metal head with circular red eyes from various sides. He wears the Reverberation Ensemble's uniform, however he uniquely wears an overcoat version.

Like all other members of the Ensemble, Jae-heon is sadistic and thinks little of others' lives other than entertainment or means to an end. This is a sentiment that that is more intense towards the wealthy, despising them for their ignorance towards the lives of the people in the Backstreets and blaming them for the death of his son.

Little is known about Jae-heon's past, other than that he used to be a technician. Some time ago, his son died at the hands of an unattended road roller. He attempted to reconstruct his son by molding the bodies of other dead children into a puppet fashioned after him. However, he was tracked down by Roland, who was rampaging after the death of [[Angelica, who burned down his workshop after being disgusted at his creation in spite of Jae-heon's pleading.

Some time after this, Jae-heon became a Distortion, though not fully conscious, describing it as "[his] head was brimming with all kinds of thoughts" before meeting Argalia and joining the Reverberation Ensemble.

"Had I been busy with an urgent appointment as any other tragic tale should go, your death wouldn’t have felt so miserable. Yeah. I would’ve cried until my tears had run their course, and I would’ve been ready to send you off. It was an ordinary day. The sort of day when there were no meetings or gatherings to attend to after I came home from work. Your body was crushed beyond recognition—I couldn’t have noticed on my own that it wasn’t a random chunk of flesh. They put your remains in a stasis box and sent it to me; that was their gesture of condolence. I’d have refused to believe it was you, if it weren’t for the clothes. I spent hours sitting there in numbed silence, vacantly staring at a lump I couldn’t even dare to hug."

"A stuffed doll you were carrying, now next to the box, caught my eye. Even though it was shredded and soaked in blood, the cotton filling was still clustered together, as if it remembered the volume of the doll. It seems some cotton remained even after the roller crumpled all the outer fabric. Then for reasons unknown, I brought the other dolls out of your room and cut them up with a pair of scissors. I don’t know what possessed me to cut them into pieces of fabric. There wasn’t even enough to fully cover the doll, so I scraped together the pieces of clothing to sew it back up. With the same, gentle hands that made your doll the first time."

"The outcome was creepier than what it used to be, but it was the same doll I remembered nonetheless. The appearance didn’t matter. Maybe, just maybe, the same could be said for you? I gazed at the box where you, my son, rested for what would no longer be an eternity. My two hands were once so busy that it was a bother; they had paused for the time, but now they are about to move again—just for you."

entries.name: Jikan
entries.content:
Jikan is member of the Rusted Chains.

Jikan has pale skin with messy, dull pearl-colored hair. They wear a brown tanktop, a belt, a pair of deep green pants and black boots. They have rusty chains wrapped around their torso and arms. They are notably littered with scars across their face and arms, some of which appear to be bleeding.

"The Rusted Chains ain’t the biggest Syndicate, but each member’s got strength to boot n’ boast. The only weapon we use is these spiky chains. Tie ‘em, smack ‘em, anythin’ goes. We gotta be careful not to get swung or swayed around, or bind ourselves with our own metal. My body’s full of scars thanks to that, but hey… It’s not too bad, is it?"

entries.name: Jin
entries.content: Jin is a member of the Smiling Faces.

entries.name: Julia
entries.content:
Julia is a Fixer in Section 6 of the Zwei Association's Southern Branch.

Julia has medium wavy white hair, light skin, and eyes that she keeps closed at all times. She wears a Zwei uniform constituted by a light yellow dress shirt under a long dull marine blue bomber jacket with two parallel light yellow stripes on the left, two pockets on the sides, and small dull yellow details on both shoulders. On her lower half, Julia has a small black sheath that attaches to her waist, she also wears a short black tube skirt along with pantyhose of the same color and dark almond toe pump shoes. In combat, she uses a black Zwei sword.

Julia is a kind and soft hearted individual that doesn't lose her cool and cares a lot about her friends. She shows a great sense of empathy for San when he begs her and Isadora for help and a greater wish to help him out even thought she knew the Association was not going to give out any support. Julia also adores Isadora's reactions when she gets nervous or flustered.

Julia has been a part of the Zwei Association for an unspecified amount of time since its creation.

In her past, Julia joined an unknown Office where she met Isadora and San, being it the first day for the three of them and they quickly became friends. After an unknown amount of time Julia leaves her first Office and joins the Zwei Association along with Isadora, being put into Section 6 under the orders of Walter.

The First Episode of Zwei begins with San heading to the Zwei Association, Section 6; to talk with a pair of Fixers, Julia and Isadora, who are part of the Association. The conversation starts out with San telling the two that his colleagues, Lulu and Mars, have died on their mission to The Library. His only request to them is for the Zwei Association to help him retrieve their books, if that's the least they could do. Isadora immediately treats San with backlash, telling him that barge in into the HQ to beg for help isn't the best way to get help. However, Julia opposes Isadora, and suggests that they let their superiors have a review of the case. Soon after, we learn that Julia has a friendship with San; Isadora tells her that they shouldn't act on attachment nor friendship, lest it lead to their system collapsing -And others begging and asking for their help.

Isadora reminds Julia again that the records show that this case shows up nowhere in the Zwei records, due to perhaps taking it as an unofficial work and if San wants them to go to the Library to try and get the books back, then she wants him to pay a corresponding reward for the mission, and that San has used the association as much as the association has used him. It also becomes known that San, Isadora, and Julia all used to work in the same Office together in the past.

After a few more arguments, Isadora gets a notification of the news that the Library has been moved up from Urban Myth to Urban Legend by the Hana Association, and that the library is now a good case for them to officially take on. They get the invitation from San and send some Zwei Crewmembers to go to the Library.

In the Second Episode of Zwei begins with Isadora telling Julia and San that they are in the line-up of the search team for the library. Julia is happy to go to the library, and says that they should go retrieve the books of Mars and Lulu and come back safely. Isadora also jumps in to add that even though they should always stay on their objective, they still need to collect as much information as possible (Collect as many books as they can). San then decides to ask Isadora that of all the things that they could do, why are they sending a search team to enter the library; Isadora snaps back and asks San why he came begging to them in the first place. San responds that this place was the only one that he could count on. She also asks him about his younger brother, but he refuses to answer.

Soon, Isadora decides to tell San and Julia about the Distortion Phenomenon, which is classified as an Urban Nightmare. The Distortion phenomenon is an anomaly that has been happening throughout the city ever since the White Nights and Dark Days; this phenomenon turns people into monsters at random, and each occurrence is worse to deal with than the last. This is where we get our first look at "The Pianist", where in its first case alone caused the death of 80% of District 9's population. They had to immediately send in a colored fixer in order to gain control of the situation after they realized how severe the situation was. They have almost no clues whatsoever to track down the cause of the phenomenon; however, the most information they have on it so far revolves around the sudden disappearance of L Corp, and the White Nights and Dark Days that started in the corporation's nest. Isadora claims that the Zwei Association have a hunch that the Library might be one of the keys to understanding this phenomenon.

Julia tells Isadora that a coworker told her about a similar story, where a resident in the area they were peacekeeping transformed into a beast without any warning whatsoever. They managed to take care of that case before the death toll could reach double digits. Another incident involved a restaurant clerk turning into a man-eating sandwich monster. Isadora reassures Julia and San that there hasn't been any cases of the phenomenon that has been nearly as dangerous as the Pianist for now, they thank Isadora for the information before heading to the Library.

Upon reaching the Library's entrance, Julia comments how the teletransportation method used by the Invitation seems akin to something a singularity would be capable of, then San mentions how the Director of the Library will soon arrive to greet them, with Angela showing up moments after. The Office Operator states that with this reception they wish to retrieve the books of Mars and Lulu, Angela affirms that both items can be found in the Library. Finally, Julia inquires Angela about if one really can retrieve the books upon coming out victorious in the Reception and if one does really turn into a book by failing, the Library Director confirms her suspicions and invites them in.

Eventually, Julia falls in the Reception along with San and some Zwei Fixers, and she turns into the Book of Julia which contains his Key Page.

entries.name: Kalo
entries.content:
Kalo is a Sottocapo of The Thumb.

Kalo is a middle aged man with grey hair and shaved beard, he has multiple scars on his face and a prosthetic mechanical right hand. He wears a black suit on top of his red Thumb Coat hanging from his shoulders. Kalo also holds a cane, although, he seems to only do so for style rather than needing the aid of the tool to walk.

While Kalo seems stoic in attitude, he is very strict and brutal, willing to harm his own subordinates as punishment for trivial mistakes through the mutilation of a body part. Kalo deeply values attitude and hierarchy, believing anyone with a position below him has no right to speak to him unless he requests them to do so, but through such belief, he will also follow every order given by his superiors without a second thought. He will also grant a more severe punishment to those who question his superiors' actions.

Kalo is one of the highest-ranking members of The Thumb, having the position of Sottocapo which serves as an underboss of the syndicate, second only to the Capo dei capi. He's been serving the Thumb for an indefinite amount of time. He is shown having interest in taking the territory L Corp's Nest after its collapse and would rather not have the other Five Fingers getting in his way.

In a summit organized by the Thumb, he invites all of the nineteen Thumb subsidiaries and his own subordinates to review the actions regarding the occupation L-Corp's nest, however, he's informed the members of the Rumanos Cartel are absent from the meeting because they're are still recovering from The Black Silence's assault in their group, as a response, he excommunicates the Rumanos Cartel. Now with the summit in motion, Kalo begins by informing all the other Syndicate members to pull out of the L Corp's Nest and leave the occupation of the area for the Thumb only as a result of another party entering the conflict, making the situation even more difficult and unexpected. Various Thumb subsidiaries express their disapproval to such order but are quickly silenced by the subordinates of the Thumb. Kalo then explains the command was given by the Capo dei capi, the main leader of The Thumb's syndicate, and as such, he must follow them thoroughly even if it was within his desire to offer all other Thumb subsidiaries an equal amount of the Nest's land. The Leader of the Night Awls questions why the Capo dei capi has given such order, irritated at gesture of someone questioning his leader, Kalo orders the execution of every member of the Night Awls. Kalo soon reveals he was told personally by the Capo dei capi that the other Thumb subsidiaries don't have the strength to fight against the Index's Proxies, hence the order was given for them to retreat from the collapsed Nest for the time being. Once all other members acknowledge his orders, the meeting ends.

After an indefinite amount of time goes by after the summit, Kalo has a meeting with his subordinates, Katriel, Boris and Denis to discuss the current situation in the L Corp's Nest. Kalo talks about that too many different groups are involved in the fight for the Nest, such as the Index, Liu, R Corp and recently, The Blue Reverberation and Purple Tear. He comes to the conclusion to the conclusion that The Library is attracting them to the area. Boris suggests that whoever takes over the Library gains control of the Nest, then Katriel explains the Thumb has attempted to obtain the invitation to the Library, but was unsuccessful at acquiring an invite because it would suddenly disappear as soon as the Thumb could hold grasp of it. However, Kalo reveals an invitation has come across him, offering the books of the Liu Association which the information inside would give them a great advantage in taking over the Nest. Before the group can continue their conversation, a messenger of the Index, Yan, suddenly appears in the meeting room, stating that perhaps it is not such a good idea for the Underboss of the Thumb to venture into the Library. Yan asks permission to speak with Kalo, which, once he's granted, he explains that he doesn't agree in the that Kalo should go after the Library, because if a Thumb Underboss is turned into a book, the Index could obtain information from him and they could potentially seize the Thumb with ease. Kalo ignores Yan's warnings and instead orders the torture and execution of every Index member remaining in the L Corp's Nest for irritating him, starting with Yan. The Index Messenger is last seen attempting to escape from the Thumb whereabouts.

Some time later, Kalo and his group make their way to the Library's entrance. Katriel expresses her concern over Kalo's safety which he responds that she should look after herself instead. Angela greets the group soon after and Katriel comments about the rumors of the Library Director's being a machine, but Katriel herself is not fully able to grasp if Angela was indeed a human or a machine. Angela is irritated by Katriel's remark and Kalo warns Katriel that since the Library is a Star of the City, Angela has a higher position than even a underboss of the Thumb like himself. Katriel quickly realizes her mistake and apologizes to Angela, requesting Denis to cut off her tongue as punishment. Kalo apologizes on Katriel's behalf and Angela makes a final comment on how the group's view of hierarchy and punishment have a deranged approach.

Kalo and his subordinates are defeated in the Library and he turns into The Book of Kalo which contains his Key Page.

"Capo dei capi (Godfather), Sottocapo (Underboss), Capo (Captain), and Soldato (Soldier/Goodfella)… The Thumb is divided into these four echelons. This hierarchical structure is still effective outside of the Syndicate. For example, a common Fixer is comparable to a Soldato, an Associate Fixer to a Capo, a board member of a Wing to a Sottocapo… This is how the hierarchy is to be interpreted. No outsider is exempt from this rule. No matter how you usually behave, you must remember your place and respect our rules when you’re dealing with the Thumb. If a young, oblivious Fixer walks up to a Capo and speaks to them, that poor picciotto will be rolling in the street the next day with his jaw and teeth missing. On the other hand, someone with the right level of authority or person of a higher class would be a different story. If a person on the same echelon as ours were to approach us, we’d gladly greet them and hear what they have to say with an open mind. Conversations with them are to be conducted with courtesy and decorum. Furthermore, if the person you’re dealing with stands on a higher echelon than yours… They must be treated with utmost devotion and delicacy. Such is the rule of ours, and the respect to their position. Don’t be too bitter over it. Indeed, class is earned, not given for free; it’s only right to give it the respect it deserves."

entries.name: Katriel
entries.content:
Katriel is a Capo of The Thumb.

Katriel is a tan-skinned woman with long, wavy, purple hair with bangs. She has amber eyes and round, wireframe glasses. She wears the standard Thumb uniform, being a black suit under a gold-lined red overcoat draped over her shoulders, a gold badge on the left lapel, and black shoes. In addition to that, she also wears a belt of grenades. In combat, she wields a double-barreled rifle with a bayonet attached.

"The Thumb’s chain of command is simple: Obey the orders issued by your superior unconditionally, and do not question the intentions of your superior. Kill if you’re told to kill, and die if you’re told to die. You cannot defy the orders no matter how baffling it may seem. Those who violate them are punished on the spot. Even if the order is made by someone whose rank is only one step higher than yours, you’re still obligated to follow it. There’s nothing you can do about it, unless another person whose position in the pecking order is even higher than your commander’s decides to step in and take your side.

There is one exception, however; it’s when a high-ranking individual temporarily devolves their power to a subordinate of theirs. Usually, this occurs if they have urgent business that prevents them from joining a meeting, or when they need their peer to know something that the subordinate can explain more professionally… It’s still a rare occurrence even then. No one transfers their authority for the fun of simulated uprising or other trivial reasons. That’s how significant the hierarchy is to us."

entries.name: Lenny
entries.content:
Lenny is a "Rat". She acts as the "surgeon" while gut-harvesting. She belongs to a group of Rats that is composed by her, Pete, and Mang-chi.

She has short light blonde hair that is brown on the roots, light skin, and blue eyes. Lenny carries with her a teal purse with dark brown and red compartments and wears various layers of clothing, a brown t-shirt under two other t-shirts, a white one and then a teal one, around her neck she wears loosely a dark green scarf under a yellow and orange sweater also tied like a scarf by the sleeves and tightly on her neck, she wears a necklace with a little blank slab on it and all of her upper clothing is covered over by an open brown jacket. In her lower half, Lenny uses brownish sweat pants that only go down to her knees, gray high socks, and white sneakers. In combat, she wields a dented and rusty scalpel.

Lenny seems to be the calmest of the Rat trio. Unafraid to shove her hands inside of living people and removing their guts with the cleanest cut possible. Other than being calm she is also very time-aware, paying immediate attention to the fact they only have 7 hours to pay a debt.

Lenny doesn't seem very fond of the other teammates, stating in her Key Page that she would not walk around Mang-chi or Pete if she had another choice, and also labeling the latter as an idiot for having his dream of becoming one of the Fingers of the Backstreets.

Lenny has been part of the Rats for an unknown amount of time, working as the "surgeon" in the gut-harvesting process of the group.

In her past, Lenny joined an examinee town seeking a better fate than becoming a rat. Unfortunately, she was not capable to succeed on her academics and as such, she was unable to join a better workforce like a Wing.

Without a better option, Lenny becomes a rat and joins Pete along with Mang-chi. However, they still face the reality of having to work to pay their debts to other Syndicates and avoid the Offices and Associations that guard certain areas.

During a gut-harvesting, Pete, Lenny, and Mang-chi were almost caught by the Zwei Association. Forcing Lenny to take out the organs of a harvested body, they manage to escape before the Association members arrive. Back in their hideout, Pete and the others check the guts of the harvested body, thinking that once they sell them and pay the Stray Dogs, they will finally join an Urban-Legend Syndicate. But soon Pete points out that the organs are very damaged to be sold for any profit, something that Lenny tried to tell him. Mang-chi says that there is a tattoo of an orange round symbol on the back of its neck, which were of something that they haven't heard of yet, and with the time they have, there wouldn't be enough for another gut-harvesting trip.

Lenny presents the Invitation that she found inside the body to Pete and then after knowing of the Library, they decide to continue there, because else the Stray Dogs or the Zwei who seems to still be in their pursuit will kill them anyway. All the members sign the envelope and then are transported to the Library. Pete remarks how the Library is fancier than he expected, and soon they are greeted by Angela. Pete asks if they really can take any of the Books, which Angela replies that they must 'gain' them. Mang-chi hesitates, doubting at the worth of the Books, but Pete tells them that beggars can't be choosers and need to take this opportunity.

Eventually, Lenny along the rest of the Rats dies in the Reception. Dropping the Book of Rats which may contain her Key Page.

Likes: Rock Music, Collecting (Anything)

Dislikes: Uncleanliness, Tobacco

entries.name: Lesti
entries.content:
Lesti is an employee of W Corp. and part of the WARP Cleanup Crew

Lesti is a young woman with scratched, light skin, brown eyes and messy blonde hair. She wears a black shirt with a blue tie under an armored vest with the W Corp. logo on it, blue pants with a utility belt and various belts attached to it it, and black boots. She wields a technologic polearm in battle.

entries.name: Liwei
entries.content:
Liwei is a Fixer working for the Full-Stop Office.

Liwei has short black hair with bangs covering nearly covering his left eye, blue eyes, and white skin. He wears a dark gray dress shirt with a black tie, on top of those two things two black belts over his chest and over it all he wears a long black trench coat. On his hands he wears black fingerless gloves, and in his right ear he has a earpiece. On his lower half, Liwei wears black trousers with two black straps on his left leg, a black belt, and mid-calf black boots with laces. In combat, Liwei wields both a handgun and a serrated machete.

entries.name: Lowell
entries.content:
Lowell is a Grade 1 Fixer working as the Director of Section 2 of Liu Association's Southern Branch.

Lowell has tan skin, red eyes and short red hair. He wears a white dress shirt with a red tie clasped with a golden tie clip under a black single breasted lapel suit with two golden buttons and the imprint of a golden dragon on the left side. Over his suit and shoulders, he wears a long red coat with high collar, golden details on the extremities, and two drawstring of the same color. Lowell on his lower half wears black suit pants and same colored shoes. He also has black gloves with a golden imprint on it and a long guan dao.

"Xiao was a cold person who wouldn’t easily show her feelings. Even though the Liu consists of those who only face forward and never express any emotion in battle, Xiao was especially hard-edged above the rest. I came to wonder if she was capable of possessing emotions at all. Her tone was dry in the most upsetting situations, and she seemed apathetic to the loss of several colleagues. Never showing her emotions in response anything, but thoroughly looking after herself. That was my impression of Xiao. I thought the path Xiao was walking was completely different from mine. We disagreed on every aspect, from strategies to personalities; I thought my relationship with her would stay a formal relation between two coworking directors of an association.

I don’t remember when and how we got so close to each other. I couldn’t be bothered to push away the person who naturally came to my side. We started spending more time together outside of work; people intersect one another somehow. Though, I have no clue how our paths managed to converge, or what about the paths led them to cross… One thing I can say for certain is that… our relationship isn’t a superficial bond between two directors. We need each other because we cherish each other, not the other way around; can you really call it love if you only cherish your significant other because you need something out of them? At the very least, I don’t think of Xiao as an object of exploitation nor gratification.

However, I know that preaching love is utterly meaningless in this City. A Fixer should never be carried away by emotion. I know well that a person at a position as high as mine should be extra careful. I’ve seen countless Fixers who brought private matters to the official grounds, only to meet undesirable results. The moment you get swayed by something you cherish, you lose yourself; you neglect your own safety. When a human, a creature that always puts itself above all else, loses their edge because of what they hold dear and places higher priority on it over their own life… The consequences will be grim in any case. Knowing this, I decided to remind ourselves of one thing when we plighted our troth: Whatever happens to each other, we won’t put ourselves at risk. As I thought, Xiao agreed plainly and rightly. I could trust in Xiao, and I was glad to have this person as my lifelong partner. It was reassuring to know that Xiao wouldn’t throw away her own life if I ever died. Focus on my own survival, even in a mortal peril. Perhaps my heart has grown stronger since I met her. Having her next to me was already a great help to me at that point."

entries.name: Luda
entries.content:
Luda is a Beholder of the Eye.

Luda appears as a white, staticky projection in a seemingly glass chamber.

Luda, as a Beholder of the Eye, is privy to most of the secrets of the Head. As a direct consequence, she oversees the nest eviction process to The Outskirts and does not participate in combat. During this process, she mocks Angela for her goal. At the end of combat, she successfully manages to teleport The Library to The Outskirts.

Luda, along with Zena (an Arbiter of the Head) and Baral (an Executioner of the Claw) arrive as the final uninvited guests. They are tasked with a primary objectives of relocating Nest L and the Library to the Outskirts, and the extermination of Angela as she is in violation of the AI Ethics Amendments Code. As a side objective, they are also tasked with retrieving Binah for an unknown purpose. Luda, in this case, does not appear in person, instead as a projection, tasked with analyzing the Library and overseeing the nest eviction process to The Outskirts.

entries.name: Lulu
entries.content:
Lulu is a Fixer of the Streetlight Office. 

Lulu has short dirty blond hair, light skin, and green eyes. She wears a black turtleneck under a very light brown parka coat with long dark brown sleeves and asymmetrical white fur on the collar, and dark brown fingerless gloves. On her lower half, Lulu has brown pants with white pant cuffs and brown shoes. In combat, she uses a long baton with yellow and black strips that can be set on fire.

Lulu has an explosive temperament, often exploding at her co-worker and potential love interest, Mars; although she often screams and insults him, she still cares for him on the inside. She is also a very well-connected social butterfly, being surrounded by various trusty friends and claiming that her great connections will get her far in her Fixer career.

Lulu has been part of the Streetlight Office for an unspecified amount of time.

In her past, Lulu has met various people in her life and making many friends. One day she got to join the Streetlight Office where she and her colleagues keep peace in a two blocks area on an unspecified location in the City, often getting in arguments with Mars.

In the first Episode of Streetlight Office, Mars and Lulu are in their office, with Lulu starting wondering why their Office is unpopular with clients even when they are associated with the Zwei and have a 0% crime rate in their secured areas, with Mars pointing out that they just cover two blocks of space. Regardless, they will get work eventually but Lulu is thinking in moving to other Office if they keep waiting. Mars says that he doesn't think she has what it takes to work for a bigger Office, but Lulu respond that she has business connections. She then brings up that his Legendary Fixer mother is too busy while Lulu has friends who can help her. Mars sarcastically replies she is a great Fixer, and Lulu just digs on it.

San arrives afterwards with work, while Lulu starts to argue with Mars because he disposed of her cake of the fridge, saying that it already expired. After San settles in buying another cake for Lulu, he talks about their unofficial work from a friend in the Association. Lulu ask if is the Fixer who works directly under the Association and San confirms it. San explains that this task has yet to be officially addressed by the Hana Association, asking soon after if they know about the Library. Mars and Lulu knows some stories of it that were overheard from the Rats, saying that had very valuable books. San then tells that he retrieved an invitation from his friend, although they start to question the risk of it as they don't know much about it and will not count for their career, as well they might not gain as much money even with San saying that his Associate friend will promise for an Urban-Legend payment. San start to cave in that was a bad idea afterall, but Mars and Lulu agree in going, now that they need money, and will do their best.

After signing the Invitation and entering the Library, Mars and Lulu begin to argue again over taking the work. San has to interrupt and settle them down again by offering to eat in Juli's restaurant once is over and that he will pay for. Afterwards, Angela arrives and notes the conversation of them. They get wary but Angela reassures that the ordeal hasn't started yet. She present herself and San greets her, asking that if they are still able to enter since he borrowed the Invitation from someone else. Angela clarify that it eventually reached to him and they signed it with their names, so it worked as intended. Angela leaves but Lulu notices that she wasn't human, but a machine. San reminds them to stay aware and back up when gets too dangerous, and the fixers enter the Library.

On the second Episode of Streetlight Office, Lulu and San managed to escape from the Library, but Mars died during the Reception. Back in the Office, they are both mourning their death with San blaming himself for taking the work and going to the Library. He says it was out of their abilities and he already sent a report to the Zwei. Lulu reacts harshly, asking about Mars and if his death was pointless. San continues to feel regret and let Lulu blame him all she wants. Lulu goes to check the fridge and notices a cake, and asks if he bought it. San tells that he didn't buy any cake, then Lulu says she is going outside for a bit.

Lulu cries in the streets under the rain, as she remembers Mars, that wasn't like he would buy cake for others, that he bragged of his sword that was a gift of her mother, and that he would become like her. Lulu suddenly receives an invitation that includes in it the Book of Mars. Realizing what happen to the people who die there, she settles in avenge him but cannot go for San to help. She decides to go by herself with some of her friends to help her out.

After arriving at the Library, Angela goes to greet her but is immediately attacked by Lulu. She tells her to shut up as doesn't need a greeting from a "despicable piece of junk." She claims she will get Mars' book, kill all the monsters, and then blow Angela's head off. Angela remarks that she will have difficulty in doing so. Lulu shuts her up again and Angela sighs, finishing her greeting with them getting in.

Eventually, Lulu perishes in the Reception along with her friends, and she is turned into the Book of Lulu which contains her Key Page.

entries.name: Mang-chi
entries.content:
Mang-chi is a "Rat" . He acts as a helping hand to the "surgeon" of the group, Lenny, during the gut-harvests. He belongs to a group of Rats that is composed by him, Pete, and the already mentioned Lenny.

Mang-chi has dark skin and black eyes. He wears a yellowish-brown hoodie, with the hood covering his head and his orange beanie. Over the hoodie, Mang-chi wears a white t-shirt and a brown one with line patterns over said t-shirt, all of his upper half or under a open black jacket with an emblem on the left shoulder. For his lower half, he wears blackish pants, white socks, and brown shoes. In combat, he wields a hammer.

Mang-chi seems to be the most afraid and nervous of the trio. He demonstrates great hesitation in going to the Library since the group is unaware of what type of foes or other dangers await them inside. In other hand he also seems to be better at paying attention to detail compared to his Rat companions, being able to notice the round orange symbol on the back of the neck of their most recent victim and how such the person didn't seem to be the type that would have tattoos, claiming that they were a "desk-working dweeb".

Mang-chi has been part of the Rats for an unknown amount of time, working as the "helper" in the gut-harvesting process.

In his past, Mang-chi lived in the Backstreets along with his parents and brothers. Unfortunately, one day his neighbourhood was unable to pay protection fees to a Syndicate, and when night fell Sweepers rose up and slaughtered Mang-chi's family along with some neighbours before his eyes.

Eventually, Mang-chi becomes a rat and joins Pete along with Lenny. However, they still face the reality of having to work to pay their debts to other Syndicates and avoid the Offices and Associations that guard certain areas.

During a gut-harvest, Pete, Lenny, and Mang-chi were almost caught by the Zwei Association. Forcing Lenny to take out the organs of a harvested body, they manage to escape before the Association members arrive. Back in their hideout, Pete and the others check the guts of the harvested body, thinking that once they sell them and pay the Stray Dogs, they will finally join an Urban-Legend Syndicate. But soon Pete points out that the organs are very damaged to be sold for any profit, something that Lenny tried to tell him. Mang-chi says that there is a tattoo of an orange round symbol on the back of its neck, which were of something that they haven't heard of yet, and with the time they have, there wouldn't be enough for another gut-harvesting trip.

Lenny presents the Invitation that she found inside the body to Pete and then after knowing of the Library, they decide to continue there, because else the Stray Dogs or the Zwei who seems to still be in their pursuit will kill them anyway. All the members sign the envelope and then are transported to the Library. Pete remarks how the Library is fancier than he expected, and soon they are greeted by Angela. Pete asks if they really can take any of the Books, which Angela replies that they must 'gain' them. Mang-chi hesitates, doubting at the worth of the Books, but Pete tells them that beggars can't be choosers and need to take this opportunity.

Eventually, Mang-chi along the rest of the Rats dies in the Reception. Dropping the Book of Rats which may contain his Key Page.

entries.name: Mars
entries.content:
Mars is a Fixer of the Streetlight Office.

Mars has short white hair, light skin and red eyes. He wears a white dress shirt under a black vest with a gray tie, a grayish blue jacket with two small belts on the right arm, and black fingerless gloves. On his lower half, Mars has gray pants and brown shoes. In combat, he uses a rectangular metallic greatsword given to him by his mother.

Mars has a calm temperament, maintaining his cool while Lulu made a great fuss over him disposing of her cake even though it would expire that day. On the inside, Mars tends to hold in and hide some of his feelings, be it sadness when he did not meet other's expectations or his romantic feelings for Lulu.

Mars has been part of the Streetlight Office for an unspecified amount of time.

Mars' mother was a legendary Fixer, and he was usually targeted by Syndicates that opposed his mother, and was faced with high expectations put upon him by her acquaintances. Although he worked hard and shed many tears, Mars never managed to become anything more than an average and ordinary Fixer with no great talents. As such, he entered an average and ordinary Office, the Streetlight Office. Even though his mother was proud of him and his achievements, Mars himself was extremely disappointed with his own failure and then left without making eye contact until they said their farewells and Mars left.

In the first Episode of Streetlight Office, Mars and Lulu are in their office, with Lulu starting wondering why their Office is unpopular with clients even when they are associated with the Zwei and have a 0% crime rate in their secured areas, with Mars pointing out that they just cover two blocks of space. Regardless, they will get work eventually but Lulu is thinking in moving to other Office if they keep waiting. Mars says that he doesn't think she has what it takes to work for a bigger Office, but Lulu respond that she has business connections. She then brings up that his Legendary Fixer mother is too busy while Lulu has friends who can help her. Mars sarcastically replies she is a great Fixer, and Lulu just digs on it.

San arrives afterwards with work, while Lulu starts to argue with Mars because he disposed of her cake of the fridge, saying that it already expired. After San settles in buying another cake for Lulu, he talks about their unofficial work from a friend in the Association. Lulu ask if is the Fixer who works directly under the Association and San confirms it. San explains that this task has yet to be officially addressed by the Hana Association, asking soon after if they know about the Library. Mars and Lulu knows some stories of it that were overheard from the Rats, saying that had very valuable books. San then tells that he retrieved an invitation from his friend, although they start to question the risk of it as they don't know much about it and will not count for their career, as well they might not gain as much money even with San saying that his Associate friend will promise for an Urban-Legend payment. San start to cave in that was a bad idea after all, but Mars and Lulu agree in going, now that they need money, and will do their best.

After signing the Invitation and entering the Library, Mars and Lulu begin to argue again over taking the work. San has to interrupt and settle them down again by offering to eat in Juli's restaurant once is over and that he will pay for. Afterwards, Angela arrives and notes the conversation of them. They get wary but Angela reassures that the ordeal hasn't started yet. She present herself and San greets her, asking that if they are still able to enter since he borrowed the Invitation from someone else. Angela clarify that it eventually reached to him and they signed it with their names, so it worked as intended. Angela leaves but Lulu notices that she wasn't human, but a machine. San reminds them to stay aware and back up when gets too dangerous, and the fixers enter the Library.

Eventually, Mars perishes in the Reception alone while Lulu and San escape the Library, and he turns into the Book of Mars which contains his Key Page.

"My mother was a Fixer with a high grade that every one of my peers would dream of reaching. She was the envy of all, a radiant individual who received endless supplies of various expensive equipment and garnered constant recruit offers from other Offices. Does that mean I had a safe, comfortable childhood under the care and wealth of such a wonderful person? Had that been the case, I would’ve earned a position in one of the Wings already. Being the son of a high-rank Fixer, I was often targeted by Syndicates opposing her, and my mother’s acquaintances held high expectations for me.

At first, I was okay with their expectations. I was already dreaming to follow the path of my mother. In fact, I was hoping to live up to it and hear compliments such as “I knew you could make it!” from others. “Yes. I’m going to become a great Fixer just like my mother. Then she’ll be proud of me one day, right? She’ll proudly say ‘That's my boy’, in front of others.” I studied hard day after day, taking no breaks in-between… Countless times, I held my sword with a strong resolve, and many days I spent weeping alone. Even if I faced setbacks and failures, I believed I could overcome them and stand strong like the protagonist of a movie. As if I could actually be someone great.

But in the end, I grew into an ordinary aspiring Fixer, and I learned that I was only an average person with no talent to show off. When I entered an ordinary Office with my ordinary capabilities, my mother seemed very glad to hear the news. She said an associate Office of the Zwei is a good start, and that I’ll certainly be able to become successful if I work my way up slowly. However, I was greatly disappointed in myself, and I couldn’t look my mother in the eyes until I said my final goodbyes and left the house."

entries.name: Martina
entries.content:
Martina is a Fixer of the Cane Office.

Martina has a notable lanky stature and long black hair that covers her eyes. She wears a simple black suit with a white dress shirt and a black tie underneath a black trench coat with sleeves long enough to cover her arms, along with black leggings and high heels of the same color. She carries a black briefcase filled with black tendrils which she uses as a weapon.

entries.name: Maxim
entries.content: Maxim is the Captain of the Rhino Team in the Fourth Pack of R Corp.

entries.name: McCullin
entries.content:
McCullin is a Fixer of the brutal Hook Office.

McCullin is bald but has what appear to be two bolts stuck into his head, as well as a stitched-up scar. He has dark skin and a white mask which shows black eyeholes, a sharp smile, and a crack across it over his face. He wears a black jacket with a white t-shirt with red stripes under it, and black gloves. On his lower half, McCullin has brown trousers with a chain attached to in on the right side and black shoes with three white dots on them. In combat, he uses a large machete that he always carries in one hand.

McCullin is a calm man but still baleful and quite serious, and he shares a firm bond of camaraderie among his colleagues.

McCullin has been part of the Hook Office for an unspecified amount of time.

In his past, Naoki and McCullin, along with other people, used to be together in a Syndicate from District 23 that was infamous for holding their killed targets on the open streets, hanging them from hooks. They spent time dealing with tasks given by poor people who couldn't afford the prices of the Offices and Associations. They were friends with the Axe Gang, another Syndicate of their area, and used to cause trouble together. Later on, they recruited Taein, and after some more raids to other Offices, the operator of one them came over to their Syndicate and told that wanted people like them. The members of the Syndicate accepted, now becoming officially Fixers of the Hook Office. Although their work consisted of the same methods of gruesome executions and hanging corpses from hooks to send messages to the others, they still find it strange how they got hired by an Office. Even with them joining an Office, the Axe Gang has no grudge towards them for doing so.

In the first Episode of Hook Office, Taein, McCullin, and Naoki are some undisclosed location in the Backstreets discussing their last job of yesterday and about Taein's new bionic weapon, as they got excessive with their destructive attacks and killed more people than they should have, and since it was their mistake, they wouldn't get paid by the additional kills. Taein points out that Naoki was the one who spent more time on the rampage and that McCullin had to calm her down. After expressing she was sorry, McCullin doesn't mind as he still owes them a few things, and that now they must remain low.

Afterward, they reflect how they ended up in their new Office in the first place; due to their Syndicate's methods and outfits that made them stand out, Hook Office hired them so that it would also stand out. Naoki comments that it feels more like a pack of Rats than a proper Office. Just then, McCullin gets a message from their operator and they are informed that their next work is to handle the Library. Along with additional Hook Fixers, the group is given the Invitation and they are instantly transported to the Library.

On their arrival, Angela greets them but Taein attempts to strike first but doesn't harm Angela due to her body. Soon Naoki notices that Angela is not human and to the Hook Fixers' surprise, discover she is an AI, now thinking of how much they are going to profit from this task. The group enters after Angela leaves.

Eventually, McCullin falls in the Reception along with Naoki, Taein, and some of Hook Office's other Fixers, and is turned into the Book of McCullin which contains his Key Page.

entries.name: Mei
entries.content:
Mei is a Grade 3 Fixer working under South Section 2 of the Liu Association.

Mei is a petite woman sporting fair skin and amber eyes, as well as short black hair that is stylized in two buns akin to a panda's ears. She wears a black suit with a red tie, with the overcoat featuring a golden dragon motif seen in the other Liu uniforms. Much like her most notable coworkers, she wears the Section 2 coat by having it drape from her shoulders much like a cape, the coat itself being of a mostly red color with golden trims.

Differing from what most would expect of a high-graded Fixer in the City, Mei is often seen in high-spirits, her demeanor outside of combat being easy-going and cheerful. She enjoys gossiping about Director Lowell's private life with Xiao alongside her fellow Fixers in Section 2 and isn't above prying onto his personal matters as well as directing playful comments at him even during work hours, suggesting she has either formed a bond with the Director over time or is simply too cheeky to think about her words. Despite this peppy attitude, however, Mei appears quite aware of the stressful life imposed upon the denizens of the City and hasn't grown attached enough to be left demoralized by a colleague's death during battle. She also appears curious at the notion of a machine being intrigued about the life of a human, as seen during Angela's brief chat with Lowell in the entrance of The Library.

Mei is first seen in the Southern Base of the Liu Association, discussing the ongoing attack of The Crying Children in Nest V alongside Lowell and Cecil. Though she initially believes the situation to not be as severe as that caused by The Pianist due to the much lower number of casualties, Mei is soon made aware of how much more dire the circumstances are by Xiao, who arrives to check up on Section 2, requesting their thoughts on the matter. After giving a briefing on the information acquired by the Liu Association on the latest case of the Distortion, Mei is seen easing Director Lowell's concerns about Xiao and her workforce being tasked with taking on The Crying Children, though not without teasing him by calling him a lovebird.

During the second episode of the Liu Association Section 2, Mei is invited by Lowell to watch the record of Section 1's mission of disposing of the Crying Children, becoming distraught by the footage's display of The Blue Reverberation's interference leading to the team's failure at eliminating the threat. After further discussion on the specifics of the Distortion phenomenom as well as how the Liu are faring at their tasks pertaining to the Library and Nest L, Mei buckles up alongside her fellow Fixers to personally visit the former, asking Lowell about how his marriage is going and giving him an idea of just how prevalent the gossiping about his life in Section 2 is. She soon further pries into the Director's tastes while in the Library, asking whether or not its decoration is something that appeals to his tastes to the point he'd want to decorate his house in such fashion. The conversation is cut short by both Lowell and Angela, and Mei remains mostly silent as they exchange words, only showing intrigue at the Director Librarian's apparent interest in how humans went about their lives.

Eventually, Mei meets her end in the Library alongside her co-workers, turning into the Book of Mei which contains her Key Page.

entries.name: Meow
entries.content:
Meow is a member of the Musicians of Bremen. She is one of the four founding members of the Syndicate, and the only one who did not leave.

Age: 41 Years
Height: 155cm (~5'1")
Birthday: April 14th
Hobbies: Looking for new instruments
Specialties: Perfect Pitch
Likes: Beautiful Melodies, Soft Food
Dislikes: Hot Food

"Heehaw, Doodle-doo, Woof… and me. The four of us were moved to the core by the Pianist’s performance. To recreate the performance half as splendid as what we heard that day, we formed the Musicians of Bremen to study the music. We tried flicking strings here and there… Playing music while sitting, on our backs, and even while handstanding! We still couldn’t come close to the Pianist’s level, but we managed to make our own brand of music, something that only the Musicians of Bremen can play. Our performance was actually pretty fantastic, you know?

Sadly, our time didn’t last long. One day, a mysterious person approached us and asked us to join his ensemble and perform with him… Woof, Doodle-doo, and Heehaw took the offer and left with that guy. I had to stay because of new members that had just joined our band, though. Yep, MuMu and Oink. It’s kinda… uncomfortable to just leave them behind, you know? We can’t let them mess around and taint our name, either. I’ve been practicing with them to create a performance that could get a standing ovation once my old bandmates come back. But at their current level of skills, the three would just cluck at these newbies’ performance and go back to whatever they were doing."

entries.name: Merry
entries.content:
Merry is an ordinary city citizen who took a Warp Train to go on vacation with her lover, Tommy.

Merry is a woman with brown hair in a braid that goes over her shoulder, and green eyes. She wears a red turtleneck sweater, a knee-length gray skirt, brown leggings and brown boots.

Merry has a cheerful and flirty personality, often flirting with Tommy. she always worries about Tommy and loves him more then anything.

Merry seems to call for Tommy when they merged together as Tomerry.

entries.name: Mi
entries.content:
Mi is a member of the Smiling Faces. 

As a member of the Smiling Faces, Mi appears similar to other members, being an entirely ash gray and maroon figure asides for a silver Hahoetal mask. She seems to be slightly more gaunt than other members, and also has distinctive silver soles. Upon her body, she has a ruddy cloth-like material upon her waist and right shoulder, and several gray ribbons at her back. Her knees, elbows, and left shoulder appear to have exposed muscle. In combat, she uses the Smiling Faces' standard smoking pipe, albeit slightly longer and with a silver mouthpiece, and a silver sword.

entries.name: Mika
entries.content:
Mika is a Fixer belonging to Molar Boatworks. She is a returning character from Library of Ruina.

Mika is a short woman who wears her red hair in a tall ponytail with small, circular orange glasses resting on her forehead. She is generally covered in grease and dirt, with a similarly dirty rag rested around her neck. She wears a large, dirtied, short sleeve t-shirt with blue, oversized, overalls with tools held in its pocket. She wears large black boots and white gloves with a red underside. She carries a wrench.

Mika is generally quiet, with a mind much more focused on logic when compared to her coworkers. She is highly knowledgeable and skilled whilst working in the Molar Boatworks workshop, something she attributes partially to her father who did the same.

Mika has been part of the Molar Office for an unknown length of time. In the past, her father was a workshop owner who fell victim to fraud; he was requested to make weaponry from unknowingly stolen technology, violating the Head's patent laws. Once he completed the job, his client took the weapons without paying, and after realizing what had happened he was unable to pay the patent infringement fees to A Corp. It's implied that he was executed by the Claw as a result.

Mika later joined the Molar Office and received a warm welcome from Olga and Rain. Eventually, due to Olga's business dealings, Mika was dispatched alongside her and Rain to fulfill a request given to them by Myo, the captain of the Rabbit Team in the Fourth Pack of R Corp, to investigate the Library and its connection to Lobotomy Corporation.

After the events of Library of Ruina Mika and her fellow Molar Office Fixers, Olga and Rain, return from their book forms and open the Molar Boatworks workshop in the Backstreets of District 21. They are contracted by Limbus Company to modify Mephistopheles to be capable of nautical travel and, while The Sinners spend days killing Trash Crabs to acquire the materials needed, Mika, Olga, and Rain work at completing the requested modifications. Despite some set backs with missing materials and forgetting to add the mode needed to keep Mephistopheles afloat, Mika and her friends soon see LCB off on their journey across the Great Lake.

entries.name: Mirinae
entries.content:
Mirinae is the Director of Hana Association South Section 3.

Mirinae wears the Hana Association uniform, a long 3-piece combo of a jacket, coat, and white pants with black embellishments at the bottom, likely Trigram patterns. She has long, pale brown hair tied up in a ponytail and wears glasses. She wields a spear, though she can utilise parts of her body for combat, as shown by Combat Pages like 'Augury Kick', where her body takes up the same texture as her spear, likely an ability provided to her for being in the Hana Association.

Mirinae is a level-headed, forward-thinking leader that delegates and controls the Hana South Section 3. She is unafraid of the Library and understands the consequences should she fail, accepting her role as director and pressing on should she die in the Library, as someone else will pick up where she left off. She also seems to show some awareness of the City's restrictions, noting that the "everyman is working overnight, restrained to the office desk", and commenting on the Library's status as 'Star of the City' as being the freest. She also displays sportsmanship to her opponents, insisting Angela shakes her and her associates hands, likely solidifying the fact the Library will be seeing the Hana frequently.

Following the disorganisation of several key factions in the City, such as the Thumb and the Index, as well as an increase in Distortions as catalysed by Receptions from the Library, the Hana Association is tasked with investigating the Library, which had become a Star of the City. Mirinae relays to Harold and Olivier that the only real threat remaining in L Corp's Nest would be the emerging Reverberation Ensemble led by the Color fixer, the Blue Reverberation. She notes the strange occurrences that were happening simultaneously to the fall of the Liu and the Thumb, such as integration of the Vermillion Cross into the Ensemble and the dissolution of the Eight Chefs, with one member being unaccounted for. Despite the rising tensions in the city, Mirinae and the rest of Hana South Section 3 proceed to the Library to investigate its purposes and its capabilities.

entries.name: Miris
entries.content: Miris is a Fixer in the Liu Association's South Section 1.

entries.name: Mo
entries.content:
Mo is a member of the Brotherhood of Iron.

Mo's body consists of a full robotic prosthetic with grey cloth wrapped around each limb. A pair of black tubes connects from Mo's head to a tank on his back. Mo wears a grey button-up tunic with a crossed black belt, as well as a grey cape.

Mo is the most driven and focused of the Brotherhood of Iron, reminding his fellow Syndicate members to take care of their robot bodies and focus only on earning money, also encouraging them not to falter in pursuit of this goal. As a result, it also cares little for leisure or enjoyments in life, discarding them as distractions on its single-minded pursuit, though ultimately it does still regret "giving up all the joys of life" to an extent.

Like Consta and Arnold, Mo chose to fully replace its body with a robotic prosthetic in order to be able to pursue earning money with less sensory distractions. However, due to the low quality of their bodies (being cheaply made by a low-grade workshop,) they still suffer from basic issues such as joint mobility and having to periodically refill their "brain fluid" to stay sharp, as well as being subject to cravings and memories of human experiences they can no longer have. As a result, Mo is determined to earn money to eventually purchase a higher-quality body.

As the scene begins, Mo is seen reminding Consta and Arnold to keep their brain fluid filled to better pursue earning money. To become more notorious, Consta suggests raiding an Office while Arnold instead suggests a workshop, but Consta then suggests raiding a restaurant for food. This prompts Mo to remind them that their robotic bodies cannot eat and they only bought them to help them earn money. Mo also reflects on its own human cravings, which its body is also not advanced enough to suppress.

The trio then find an Invitation stuck in Mo's arm, which it did not notice due to its body's lack of senses. They then decide to enter the Library, with Mo encouraging Consta and Arnold to win their Reception for Books and then leave. Though the others quickly become hesitant, especially after meeting Angela, Mo continues to stay confident.

Ultimately, Mo perishes in the Reception along with Consta and Arnold, and turns into the Book of Mo which contains its Key Page.

entries.name: Moirai
entries.content:
Moirai is a Weaver of The Index.

Moirai has a short, chestnut brown hair with a midpart along her left ear. She wears a black, gown with a fingerless evening gloves, topped with a white hooded Index cloak and a golden clasp, and black boots.

Moirai has a carefree attitude, as shown when she welcomed Yan in the facility and her response to his confrontation about the brutal state of the Prescripts.

Moirai is introduced in 얀샋ㄷ요무 Episode 1, as Yan's final Prescript led him to an underground facility within a room with a staircase. She greets Yan and introduces herself as a Weaver in charge of the facility, revealed to be the birthplace of the Prescripts. Moirai then demonstrates and explains how the Prescripts are made: every vibrations of sound made--from the beating of someone's heart and thuds from a falling person, to quakes in construction sites and echoes of peoples' screams--moves the pendulum. As the pendulum swings, Moirai manages the production by spinning the wheels and applying thread on it to create a fabric for the pendulum to transcribe into one of the City's languages.
