After the Prescript is made, it is transported through one of the many golden pipes to the recipient at the surface.

Age: 28
Height: 186cm (~6'1")
Birthday; March 5th
Hobbies: Sitting down and listening to the sound of spinning wheels
Specialties: Ventriloquism
Likes: A Warm Cup of Tea, Chit-chatting
Dislikes: The Stillness, The Loneliness

entries.name: MuMu
entries.content:
MuMu is a member of The Musicians of Bremen.

MuMu is a person who, like all the other members of The Musicians of Bremen, wears an animal mask, in their case a white rabbit mask with black eyes and a blue 'X' where a mouth would be. MuMu wears a black shirt under a black and white striped jacket with blue sleeves, a gray belt with a gold buckle, bloodstained black slacks, and black-tipped white shoes with gold soles. They wield a metal bat wrapped in barbed wire.

"They say the Backstreets are a nigh-inhabitable hellscape, but the people here live on somehow. There’s lots of people who live in fear every moment, but… The others live a pretty normal life. Some think the Backstreets are totally shady and poorly aged slums… But we do have all the amenities we need here. For one, the supermarkets Oink likes aren’t as good as those in the Nest, but it’s got everything people need. Clothing stores, groceries, dry cleaners, etc… I heard the details are different for each District, so there’s that… I’m just telling you how things are where I live. People here aren’t too unkind to each other. Those Nest dwellers like to gossip about how we’re cruel and dreary and all that, but the truth is, we’re doing just fine.

Oh, and there’s tons of good restaurants here. It’s the street of flavor, after all. Freshly baked meat pies, spaghetti made of special pasta… Your tongue and stomach have a wonderful time if you ever go on a trip to our District. We used to hand over the leftovers from our performance here to local restaurants. That meat would go to waste if we left it on the spot, so we might as well give it to the people who can make good use of it, ain’t that right? When Woof, Doodle-doo, and Heehaw were around, we got enough chow to share with several eateries, but our find was halved since they were gone… And Oink kept making silly mistakes with it and ruined those ingredients too often, so we quit that biz altogether. Which is a tad bit unfortunate~ We sometimes got tasty meals for free when we gave them our meat."

entries.name: Naimon
entries.content:
Naimon was a Fixer of Charles' Office. They first appear in Roland's bad ending.

Although Naimon's full appearance is blocked out by shadows, they appear to be an average-height individual, with shaggy, medium length hair. They wear a large coat with several pockets, and have pants tucked into boots. They also wield a long weapon with two strings or wires coming off of it.

Naimon, compared to Ogier and Renaud, seems to be the most forgiving of Roland, stating that they'd like to visit him. They also seem philosophical, stating that very few people can live their lives without change.

Naimon, along with Ogier and Renaud, appear only in Roland's bad ending, at a bar, talking about Roland's sudden reappearance and his actions.

entries.name: Naoki
entries.content:
Naoki is a Fixer of the brutal Hook Office.

Naoki has short brown hair, light skin that possesses one scar that goes across the right eye, both eyes are brown. She wears a black respirator mask, a brown parka coat with white fur and sleeves with the pockets on the sides, and a black t-shirt under it. On her neck, Naoki wears a black collar with a broken chain attached to it, and on her hands two dark brown fingerless gloves, plus a backpack on her back with cables that connect to her machetes. On her lower half Naoki has baggy black sweatpants and gray knee-high boots. In combat, she uses the pair of machetes connected to her backpack mentioned before, and her eyes become completely red upon landing a hit.

Naoki is mostly a calm person outside of combat but once before a foe she will become rapidly hostile and probably go on a rampage, she is also very thoughtful, being aware of how peculiar the Office she works for is and quickly finding a good reason as to why. She also seems quite knowledgeable about Workshop equipment and what precautions should be taken before buying anything such as one doing their own research about it.

Naoki has been part of the Hook Office for an unspecified amount of time.

In her past, Naoki and McCullin, along with other people, used to be together in a Syndicate from District 23 that was infamous for holding their killed targets on the open streets, hanging them from hooks. They spent time dealing with tasks given by poor people who couldn't afford the prices of the Offices and Associations. They were friends with the Axe Gang, another Syndicate of their area, and used to cause trouble together. Later on, they recruited Taein, and after some more raids to other Offices, the operator of one them came over to their Syndicate and told that wanted people like them. The members of the Syndicate accepted, now becoming officially Fixers of the Hook Office. Although their work consisted of the same methods of gruesome executions and hanging corpses from hooks to send messages to the others, they still find it strange how they got hired by an Office. Even with them joining an Office, the Axe Gang has no grudge towards them for doing so.

In the first Episode of Hook Office, Taein, McCullin, and Naoki are seen at some undisclosed location in the Backstreets discussing a job they took the day prior and about Taein's new bionic weapon, as they got excessive with their destructive attacks and killed more people than they should have, and since it was their mistake, they wouldn't get paid for the additional kills. Taein points out that Naoki was the one who spent more time on the rampage and that McCullin had to calm her down. After expressing she was sorry, McCullin doesn't mind as he still owes them a few things, and that now they must remain low.

Afterward, they reflect how they ended up in their new Office in the first place, as they used to be from a Syndicate that killed and hanged their victims from hooks on the streets, which got the attention of an Office. They were hired due to their methods and outfits that made them stand out, which meant the Office would also stand out. Naoki comments it feels more like a pack of Rats than a proper Office. Just then, McCullin gets a message from the operator and their next work is handling the Library. Along with additional Hook Fixers, the group is given the Invitation and they are instantly transported to it.

On their arrival, Angela greets them but Taein attempts to strike first but doesn't harm Angela due to her body. Soon Naoki notices that Angela is not human and to the Hook Fixers' surprise, discover she is an AI, now thinking about how much they are going to profit from this task. The group enters after Angela leaves.

Eventually, Naoki falls in the Reception along with Taein, McCullin, and some of Hook Office's other Fixers, and is turned into the Book of Naoki which contains her Key Page.

entries.name: Nemo
entries.content:
Nemo is the president of the Cane Office.

Like those from the Brotherhood of Iron and the Gaze Office, Nemo has a full prosthetic body, which has a rectangular screen instead of a head that displays emotions such as: his default smile, joy, annoyance, anger and static. He wears a simple black suit with a white dress shirt and a black tie under it, along with black shoes. His head is able to shoot a large beam of energy as a weapon, as shown by his exclusive combat page, Energy Beam. His choice of melee weaponry is a walking cane.

Nemo is an optimistic and somewhat unorthodox businessman. Being mostly comprised of prosthetic parts, he makes up for his lack of human features in colloquial speech and expletives, expressing sarcasm and anger which seems to be hard to calm down from. Although he is very diligent in his work, exchanging patents and uncovering secrets of the City's various singularities, it serves to be his downfall as he signs away the lives of the Cane Office under Pluto's 'Yesterday's Promise'. Despite his dire circumstances, he encourages Bada and Martina to do their best to fulfil the bogus contract and not to think too seriously about it.

Following W Corp's first class passenger disappearance scandal and the subsequent disposal of the W Corp. Clean-up Crew, Nemo during this time agreed to a contract with the Blue Reverberation to uncover the extra details of W Corp's singularity and inner workings to gain leverage in the unending patent wars of the City. In exchange, Nemo agrees retrieve books from the Library that Argalia requests. However, Argalia with the help of Pluto creates a hidden clause that stipulates Nemo and his team must be the ones to go, else he is free to take whatever he wants off the Cane Office, that is demonstrated by Pluto taking Bada's heart out of his chest, and holding it in front of him. This is then reverted, and Nemo is left with little choice but to take the office to the Library to retrieve the books with high chance of death, or suffer at the hands of the Blue Reverberation.

entries.name: Nikolai
entries.content:
Nikolai is the Commander of the Fourth Pack of R Corp.

Appearance: Black beret, orange lining, 4 white stripes, 2 at each side next to 1 white star. White hair. 2 scars on side near the eyes. White eyes. Black gloves. White undercoat. Orange tie. Black trench coat, 6 black buttons. Black coat, orange lining, reaches down to knees, 2 white strings at right side. Black pants. Black shoes. Black shoelaces.

entries.name: Noah
entries.content:
Noah was an employee of J Corp. before leaving the company to join The 8 o’Clock Circus with his partner, Emma.

Noah has pale skin, long black-purpleish hair tied up and appears to be quite short in stature. He wears a long brown coat embellished with various pockets and straps, much like the coat Emma wears, likely being a part of their uniform from J Corp. Underneath his coat, he wears a black sweater that reaches up to his neck, as well as a pair of plain back trousers and combat boots.

Noah has a very pessimistic outlook to life, lamenting about his mistakes in J Corp. and expecting termination from his job because of it. He strongly dislikes J Corp. and aspires to "watch the world and the skies from a higher place", rather than "stare at boring screens" given that he has worked his way up from the Backstreets. He smokes, likely as a consequence of his mundane and occasionally stressful life. He seems to hold some resentment against Emma for being more fortunate financially, and being more stable in life, though this does not undermine his friendship, as he relies on him for moral support and companionship as evidenced by his decision to take Emma with him for a smoke break after a work incident, as well as being a friend of 5 years. This dependency and aspiration for higher things culminates in the 8 o'Clock Circus.

After entering The 8 o'Clock Circus tent with Emma, Noah reflects on his life as a corporate drone with chagrin and resolves to join the circus. After being sedated, Noah comes to wake up with Emma's eyes grafted onto him, and his legs grafted onto Emma, as a way to see the world from 'new heights' as Noah wished prior. After this transformation, Noah and Emma travel to the library at Oswald's behest, and attempt to retrieve books for their new boss. As well as their physical bodies, their mindsets also change to be more hedonistic, promising Angela's 'cold stare' will change into a 'hearty smile' once they retrieve some books.

"J Corp. owns the Nest of gambling. Every person here devotes their life to those insane games of chance. Emma and I check the security cameras placed in affiliated facilities and spot anyone who cheats. We get hundreds of calls each day. Please check if the person in a dark red coat at N-9281-R231 used a sleight of hand to switch cards, I think my table was rigged at Q-198-OF1929, I think they’re using marbles that weigh 0.1g more in the roulettes at K-1928-R029, etc… A variety of creative and absurd calls flood the lines all the time.

What’s so difficult about watching the security feed all day, you ask? Sure, you could think that if you’re unfamiliar with how things work here. But imagine having to check the feeds for tens and even hundreds of rooms that have ten cams each. The workload is spread over multiple people, of course, but each of us still has dozens of screens to stare at, it makes my eyes spin like a top. Besides, some people are sneaky enough to pull trickery off camera, and some incidents might occur during maintenance hours. This job is such a busy one, two eyes just aren’t enough. When you’re checking one case, another call comes in, when you’re done checking that, more calls wait for you… The shortage of manpower is driving me crazy, I swear."

entries.name: Ogier
entries.content:
Ogier was a Fixer of Charles' Office.

Although Ogier's full appearance is blocked out by shadows, they appear to be a tall individual with short hair and earrings. They also appear to wear a large coat with 2 belts and large sleeves. Boots can be seen under the large coat.

Ogier, along with Naimon and Renaud, appear only in Roland's bad ending, at a bar, talking about Roland's sudden reappearance and his actions.

entries.name: Oink
entries.content:
Oink is a member of the Musicians of Bremen.

"The Seven Association is a Fixer Association specializing in investigation and intelligence, and it’s knowledgeable in pretty much every affair that takes place in the City. Details about a Syndicate gaining infamy in the Backstreets of some place (the Association probably knows what District it is exactly, but I left before I checked the details of it.), all the information revealed about the Distortion Phenomenon which has been going around lately, when and where Fixer Offices start up and close business, and the beat goes on… The Association treats all kinds of information about the City. Oh, they don’t have access to top-secret intels like the secrets of the Singularities each Nest holds, obviously speaking. When they solve cases, they usually cooperate with other Associations like the Shi and the Liu.

If you ask how the Seven Association can secure its confidentiality despite holding lots of juicy info that could attract the many, it’s likely because its staff aren’t bad combatants by any means. They don’t use fancy but crude workshop weapons that are basically large amalgamations of various technologies. Regular informants are armed with nothing more than a simple bladed tool. It sounds very underwhelming judging from the weapon alone, but they use the minimum technique with pinpoint precision to take down their foes."

entries.name: Olga
entries.content:
Olga is the Operator of Molar Boatworks. She is a returning character from Library of Ruina, where she appeared in the Reception of Molar Office.

Olga is a tall woman with dirty-blond hair (cut in a bob hairstyle), light skin and light blue eyes. She wears a dirtied white tank top that is tied in a knot on her lower left, slightly exposing her stomach. The tank's shoulder straps are loose on her shoulders, showing her black bra underneath. Olga also wears baggy denim overalls, with the shoulder straps hanging by her hips and red and white working gloves tucked into her waist. To complete Olga's casual wear, she is also seen wearing a white bandana around the top of her head, tied in twin knots, as well as black sandals. While working in the Great Lake, she wears a full-body black wetsuit equipped with a leather utility vest, diving helmet, fishing net, and a harpoon-like weapon made to combat Trash Crabs.

Olga is a rather flippant fixer, sometimes to the point where she misjudges things, or even forgets important details. These traits are furthered by her enjoyment of alcohol, in which she currently gets her fix from mutant crab brain juice. This combined with her easy-going nature have a tendency to cause problems, often Mika and Rain to have to clean up her mess.

Olga is old friends with Myo, the captain of R Corp's Fourth Pack's Rabbit Team, and in the past they had often worked together in the Backstreets as Fixers supporting each other in life and death situations. They drifted apart as Olga joined Molar Office and became its Operator, but recently reunited after Myo invited her to go drinking together. During this time, Myo revealed R Corp's interest in the Library and hired Olga to have the Molar Office investigate the Library for them. In celebration at the sudden prospect, Olga got herself heavily drunk (again) and even used her Office's funds to pay for their celebration.

The following morning, Olga sets out with Mika and Rain to fulfill the request despite having woken up with a massive hangover.

Olga had recently also resolved a major request given to her Office, but wasn’t paid due to forgetting to make a contract for the case.

After the events of Library of Ruina Olga and her fellow Molar Office Fixers, Mika and Rain, return from their book forms and open the Molar Boatworks workshop in the Backstreets of District 21. They are contracted by Limbus Company to modify Mephistopheles to be capable of nautical travel and, while The Sinners spend days killing Trash Crabs to acquire the materials needed, Olga, Mika, and Rain work at completing the requested modifications. Despite some set backs with missing materials and forgetting to add the mode needed to keep Mephistopheles afloat, Olga and her friends soon see LCB off on their journey across the Great Lake.

entries.name: Olivier
entries.content:
Olivier is a Fixer of Hana Association South Section 3.

He is dark-skinned with long dreadlocks typically styled in a ponytail that extends to his lower back, complemented by an undercut. In terms of attire, Olivier dons a white suit paired with a black necktie, and a long white coat adorned with trigram stripes on the shoulders and a gold lining along the lapel that runs to the coat's hem. His white trousers feature trigram accents near the ankles, and he completes his ensemble with white shoes featuring grey soles.

Olivier is a serious and straightforward individual, known for being observant and intellectual. However, he finds himself entangled in complications while explaining the T-corps gadget, which leads to Roland catching him off guard. During which he comments that he had contact with the Purple Tear. He values accuracy, evident when he corrects Roland's exaggerated claim that Olivier's arm nearly got caught in a blender during their first Urban Nightmare case. Olivier pointed out that the incident would not have occurred if Roland hadn't tasted the sauce from the ladle, curious about the flavor that led to the mishap.

entries.name: Oscar
entries.content:
Oscar is the Operator of the Wedge Office.

Oscar is an old man with grey combed back hair, mustache and beard. He wears a black tricorne which conceals one of his eyes, a grey eyepatch, a black dress shirt with a white jabot, a black vest secured with belt-like straps, a black long coat with black leather vambraces and black gloves, black pants, and black boots. He wields a large spear in combat.

entries.name: Oswald
entries.content:
Oswald is the ringmaster of The 8 o’Clock Circus and later a member of the The Reverberation Ensemble. He first appears in the story of the 8 o’Clock Circus' reception, though he does not visit the Library himself until much later.

Oswald is a Distortion with a clownlike appearance. His body is mostly red, with a red and white diamond pattern covering his upper left and lower right body and the rest being solid red. Around his waist and shoulders are golden chains, likely accessories, and his feet are adorned with large golden bells. His head possesses two protrusions in a similar manner to the sleeves of a jester's cap, each of which ends with a single golden loop. He appears to wear a red and white mask with crosses for eyes and a jagged smile, but it is possible that may be his real face.

Later in the story, after joining the Reverberation Ensemble, Oswald wears the group's signature suit but otherwise his appearance is unchanged.

Oswald is a very whimsical and often childlike man who speaks primarily in nonsense and metaphor. He has no regard for what is considered 'normal', and is willing to go to any lengths to bring smiles to the people of the city. Despite this and his generally creepy nature, Oswald is shown to genuinely care about his fellow circus performers, preparing feasts for them and becoming very upset when they are slain.

Oswald cares for the people of the city more generally, too. He believes that people are suffering due to expectations placed on them by other people and expectations they hold themselves, arguing that these expectations are what gives rise to 'unnatural' emotions such as sadness and anger. He wants the people of the city to be free from expectation, able to simply be themselves and support others in doing the same, able to laugh from their hearts without a care.

Oswald's origin is mostly a mystery. He Distorted after a voice, dubbed by him as "Ms. Sun," presumably Carmen; tempted him and achieved the Distortion that it is now and the The 8 o’Clock Circus.

"People have hopes and dreams!

“I wanna eat three blossoms of flowers!” “I wanna be a swifty nifty thrifty kitty!” “I wanna earn a fortune!” And then they add: “Maybe I’ll find delicious flowers someday!” “Maybe I’ll get fat stacks of cash in my paws someday!” “Maybe I’ll be showered in the loudest applause someday!” “Someday! Someday! Someday!”

That dastardly “someday” just won’t stop popping up. But to have a hope, you’ve got to prepare incense to offer those wishful prayers upon. A world where one can’t eat flowers! A reminder that you’re a sluggish turtle right now! The beggarly reality! Setting the stage for the performance we call hope!

Thus and therefore, people have the wrong idea about how to have hopes! If they believe that the hopes will come true “someday”, they’ll just keep parroting that contemptible word! The day will never actually come! Having expectations this way will only leave you with bitter anger!

“I’ll change someday?” “That person will turn over a new leaf someday, if I count on them and wait?” Nyeh, tch.

People entertain the hopes as they please, and then bite at each other when the change they expected doesn’t happen. Clowns can’t give out smiles in a world full of mean teary friends!

So we should all do the stretches, starting today! Abandon all expectation—just keep a merry positive attitude and laugh no matter what you see! Let’s make a performance about what’s already come true, not of a supposed reality you hope for “someday”! I’m already on the stage, standing under the brightingest spotlight ever."

entries.name: Pamela
entries.content:
Pamela is a Fixer of the Wedge Office.

Pamela is a petite woman who has short silver hair. Like Pameli, she sprouts a monochromatic color scheme with a black coat and white streaks at the end. Underneath, she wears a black body suit and a frilled hairband with a black bow on top of her head. In addition, she wields a spear to pierce enemies.

Pamela has a aloof personality but is more willing to give Philip comfort than the other member. She is the one that gave Pameli her cloned body as a way to save her. Though the relationship with Pameli still is sour as they were willing to fight when Pameli started to complain extensively.

entries.name: Pameli
entries.content:
Pameli is a Fixer of the Wedge Office.

Pameli is a petite woman with light skin and long yellow hair. Due to her body being cloned and donated by Pamela via fixer insurance, her appearance is largely the same. she sprouts a monochromatic color scheme with a black coat and white streaks at the end. Underneath, she wears a black body suit and on top of her head is a frilled hairband with a black bow. In addition, she wields a spear to pierce enemies.

Pameli has a bright yet disrespectful tone causing conflict with others, especially Pamela. In fact, she is particularly ungrateful for the body that Pameli give her and instead, tries to incite a fight with her before Oliver, Boss of Wedge Office, deescalate. Otherwise, another example could be seen with her attitude to Philip, sharing no sympathy for his loss and quickly trying to get him to move on.

entries.name: Pete
entries.content:
Pete is a "Rat". He acts as the leader of his own group of Rats, with Lenny and Mang-chi.

He has ruff dark hair, dark skin, and black eyes. He wears a gray jacket with white fur around the neck, a collar of beads around his neck, a tainted green shirt with white words on it spelling 'Rock Festiv-' being cut out, blue pants with various red belts, and white shoes. In combat, he wields an army/combat knife.

Pete is gruff and the most foul-mouthed of the trio of his group. He isn't afraid to get his hands dirty and do anything possible to chase his dream of becoming one of the Fingers.

A risk-taker, he tries to use all the options available for obtaining a good payment, climb higher the positions, and join a better Syndicate. He is aware of the many rumors of the Backstreets and can spot when things are very uncommon to just be actions of other groups.

Pete has been part of the Rats for an unknown amount of time, working in gut-harvestings with his members of the group, Lenny and Mang-chi.

Pete has a dream of becoming part of one of the Fingers of the City, the Syndicates that rule the Backstreets. Although he is aware that having a silly dream will probably do nothing with his petty skills, he desires to have one anyway.

He seems that has convinced Mang-chi and Lenny in helping him to reach that dream, with Mang-chi being the most willing to help him. However, they still face the reality of having to work to pay their debts to other Syndicates and avoid the Offices and Associations that guard certain areas.

During a gut-harvesting, Pete, Lenny, and Mang-chi were almost caught by the Zwei Association. Forcing Lenny to take out the organs of a harvested body, they manage to escape before the Association members arrive. Back in their hideout, Pete and the others check the guts of the harvested body, thinking that once they sell them and pay the Stray Dogs, they will finally join an Urban-Legend Syndicate. But soon Pete points out that the organs are very damaged to be sold for any profit, something that Lenny tried to tell him. Mang-chi says that there a tattoo of an orange round symbol on the back of its neck, which were of something that they haven't heard of yet, and with the time they have, there wouldn't be enough for another gut-harvesting trip.

Lenny presents the Invitation that she found inside the body to Pete and then after knowing of the Library, they decide to continue there, because else the Stray Dogs or the Zwei who seems to still be in their pursuit will kill them anyway. All the members sign the envelope and then are transported to the Library. Pete remarks how the Library is fancier than he expected, and soon they are greeted by Angela. Pete asks if they really can take any of the Books, which Angela replies that they must 'gain' them. Mang-chi hesitates, doubting at the worth of the Books, but Pete tells them that beggars can't be choosers and need to take this opportunity.

Eventually, Pete along the rest of the Rats dies in the Reception.

entries.name: Philip
entries.content:
Philip was a Grade 5 Fixer of the Dawn Office. However, after somehow escaping the Library, he would go on to become a member of the Reverberation Ensemble as a Distortion known as The Crying Children. Philip's E.G.O. is named "Waxen Pinion."

Philip is a young man with short dirty-blonde hair and a stern expression behind a pair of square glasses. His outfit consists of a black turtleneck, a beige two-button blazer, dark navy-blue pants, and a pair black gloves. He wields a short sword with a metal handle wrapped in leather bindings in combat.

After partially manifesting his E.G.O., Philip's main body is relatively unchanged apart from his head injuries but it is now clad in an incomplete, almost knight-like armor, covered in orange stains reminiscent of burning flames. Philip's right arm is now protected by this E.G.O. armor, donning a radially-segmented orange pauldron connected to the rest of the arm, whereas the forearm guards seem to be held together with multiple lames leading down to the gauntlet. The arms are also connected to an incomplete and cracked breastplate where Philip's black turtleneck is visibly stained with an orange substance as well. On Philip's left-hand side, he has a large angel wing coming out of his back which acts as a shield—also stained with a burning orange. The wide sword Philip now uses in combat is covered in orange veins.

Later in the story, after joining the Reverberation Ensemble, Philip wears the group's signature suit but is completely changed since his Distortion. Philip's skin is entirely pale, being made up of the numerous marble Crying Children statues tightly packed together, which are apparent in his face—with folds and wrinkles coming from his mouth, held by a pair of hands. In his black-tipped left hand, Philip wields a long facsimile of a sword resembling a sort of katana, albeit with a texture similar to that of burnt, cracked marble with a wrap of bandages around the handle.

When empowered by the Library's Light, Philip returns as a distortion wreathed in orange flames. His body itself being a cracked statue in numerous segments and fragmented at the limbs, a flaming core in his chest, and crowned with a burning diamond-shaped halo. Philip's face is now a covered in wrapping hands -lacking any discernable facial features- as he holds a burning black orb in his right hand, carrying over the angel wing from his previous incarnations on his left-hand side. A fiery aura engulfs Philip's body, similar to the biblical descriptions of real angels.

When first seen, Philip has a meek and reserved demeanor, mostly out of respect and subservience for his superiors. When complimented or asked for an opinion, he tends to be laconic, speaking few words compared to everyone else around him. This, however, hints at Philip's feelings of inferiority, believing he's not fit for his grade as a Fixer and he's simply being carried through by Salvador's benevolence and is barely tolerated in his Office. When the Dawn Office falls at the hands of the Library and is ordered to run away by Salvador, he takes it as a test to see if he had the courage to fight along them to the end, but ultimately escapes, something that solidified his opinion of himself as cowardly and selfish.

Philip first appears in the Dawn Office as an apprentice. He, along with his mentor Salvador and love interest Yuna, enter the Library in order to gain Book of Walter. Before departing, Salvador makes a quip about celebrating when their return, which causes Philip to believe that Salvador and Yuna were secretly going out behind Philip's back, which worsens his emotional state. During the Dawn Office reception, for some reason, Philip manages to escape the Library as its only survivor. As a result, he would make his way to Wedge Office, Dawn's sister office to request aid in the recovery of Salvador and Yuna's books. However, Wedge Office falls as well. But Phillip manages to resolve himself by accepting his cowardliness and sorrow, gaining a wax based E.G.O. as a result. Just as Philip is about to be booked, he suddenly vanished, which Roland theorized as Wedge Office's Operator, Oscar, having secretly planted a teleportation device on Philip before entering.


Oswald tortures Philip into breaking down.
Philip is transported out of the Library and ends up in The 8 o'Clock Circus, encountering Oswald and recognizing him as its ringleader. In an attempt to avenge the Wedge Office, he attempts to kill him, only for Oswald to casually dodge his attacks while taunting him. Seeing his E.G.O waver from his feelings of inferiority, he decides to corrupt him into distorting, describing it as "Giving him his stench". Oswald has his crew torture him, showing him illusions based on his insecure thoughts on the Dawn Office, with visions of Yuna and Salvador manifesting to insult him for being a coward, even taking a blow at how he thought Salvador was having an affair with Yuna. Stressed and in the verge of tears, Philip's vision goes dark as Pluto shows himself in front of him, claiming he can give him the power to either slay Oswald or enact revenge on the Library. Signing a contract with him, Philip simply asks Pluto for him to make him "cry out loud" by "listening to the voice". Giving into the Distortion, his body is divided into a group of wax cherubim statues, becoming known as The Crying Children.

The wax angels would be sent to the Library again by Pluto, only for all but one part of the Distortion to be booked. The remaining angel would regrow and goes on a destructive rampage across V-Corp's nest, killing 80,000 people and destroying all but Dawn Office building. This action causes him to be identified as a Star of the City and has him targeted by Liu Association. He would be saved thanks to his tormentors and later become a member of the Reverberation Ensemble as its "Cello", as revealed when Argalia sics his whole Ensemble on Iori.

After all of the other competitors for the Library are either weakened, dead, or booked, Philip and the rest of the ensemble breaking into the Library to try and steal the Light for themselves, wanting to use it for their "performance". After scattering, Phillip enters the Floor of History, where he reveals to Malkuth that he can no longer remember the person he once was, and now wants to create a world where no one needs to better themselves for the sake of others, before finally being booked. However, when he and the rest of the Ensemble are released and distorted further thank to Angela letting go of the Light in her atonement, he dies for good in the ensuing battle against Roland and the Library, finally putting the fallen angel to rest.

entries.name: Pierre
entries.content:
Pierre is the owner of Pierre’s Bistro from District 23. She cooks and prepares new dishes using human flesh as the main ingredient but also hunt her ingredients with the help of her sous-chef Jack when they are unable to receive any meat from their vendors.

Pierre has long white hair with long bangs that is tied down on a loose braid with a yellow hairband, light skin, and gray eyes. She wears a long white chef suit with pockets on both sides of the waist with one the left side of the chest and long white pants, both with blood stains over them, and also wears dark yellow moccasin shoes with white socks. In combat, she wields a cooking knife.

Pierre is a sadist that doesn't seem to be afraid of speaking her mind. Despite her sadistic tendencies, she tries to be very polite to others. Pierre also shows a deep sense of care for her sous-chef Jack and tried to keep her promise to him until the end and wishes that both of them become part of 'The Eight Chefs'.

Pierre is the proprietor and head chef of the eponymous Pierre's Bistro, a small restaurant in the Backstreets of District 23 which uses human meat in pursuit of the ultimate flavor. In her past, to achieve her dream of becoming one of 'The Eight Chefs', Pierre decided to open her bistro with her loyal companion Jack after both promising that they wouldn't abandon one another.

Pierre was trying to come up with a new dish, but she is left frustrated because she is unable to do it since nothing has struck her with inspiration. Moments after, Jack enters the room bringing some "ingredients" (captured humans) with him. Both converse about how their vendors, Lil' Piggy's and the Musicians of Bremen, stopped trading with them and that also they have to find a new place to hunt their ingredients since their old spot is now being safeguarded by the Zwei Association. Pierre and Jack also comment about how she desires to become one of 'The Eight Chefs' and about changing some of their dishes, with Jack suggesting using more aged ingredients instead of the younger ones, but Pierre had another idea in mind.

The Bistro's owner states that she wants their dishes to have a more original flavor which she wishes to achieve by using the meat of monsters instead of human flesh. Pierre mentions the Library as the place they will seek for such ingredient since otherwise, they would have to travel to the Outskirts to get it and she reveals that she received an invitation to enter the Library a while ago. She asks Jack to join her in such adventure for monster meat, which he accepts.

While Pierre prepares to sign the Red Invitation, Jack questions her about what he should do with the ingredients he brought, she answers him saying that they should be made into meat jam and states that Jack must put them legs first, not head first in some sort of not mentioned machinery to prevent the ingredients to die too quickly claiming that the more they suffer the tastier their meat will be.

Upon being transported to the Library, Pierre comments on the place's smell and how it is brand new for her, but Jack states his dislike of said scent. The chef de cuisine affirms unfamiliarity similar to the one brought by it is what brings forth new ideas. Upon ending that conversation both are greeted by Angela. Pierre loudly comments on her exterior, saying she appears to be a wonderful-looking ingredient with a glossy appearance, Jack also says that Angela appears to be a fresh and top-grade ingredient but shows uncertainty on his remake and silently inquires Pierre about the Director of the Library. The bistro's owner confirms his suspicions by stating that she is aware that Angela is, unfortunately for them, not human, but remaking that such a fact only makes her more excited. After Angela is questioned about what her taste would be, she reveals to her guests that she can't be harmed, to which Jack replies that they will only be able to know if such a thing is the truth after testing her. Pierre decides to intervene saying that they should keep their manners to the individual that sent them the Invitation, the sous-chef apologies to the Library's Director for his rudeness. At least Pierre politely requests Angela's permission to enter the Library, which she concedes.

Eventually, Pierre is defeated in the Reception along with Jack, and she is turned into the Pierre' Book of Pierre.

"Most cooks who live here have the same dream: becoming one of ‘The Eight Chefs’! They’re the people who pursue the ultimate delicacy. Their way of cooking will… give you a thrill just hearing about it! You don’t feel it? No no, I’m sure you can feel it inside. I sound crazy? Nyeh, listen up, you stubborn square! This is why I can’t talk with people whose brains are too old. They taste bad, too!

There’s a limit to the flavors people can draw forth. The height of taste the human tongue can feel isn’t as impressive as you might think, really. The most delicious food doesn’t come close to sending chills down your spine. At most… it’s just good enough to make your eyes spin! And the food you guys casually eat, going “Mm~ Tasty~”, are way! Way, way way way waaaaaay~ below that! So, many chefs gathered round one time… pondering what to do to pursue a taste beyond this limit… And then inspiration struck all of them at the same time like lightning! What if they sublimated the experience into taste, something beyond what the tongue can feel? You know, they say the presentation of food adds to its taste, right? What if the whole process of cooking could be tasted! They performed several experiments in an attempt to make that dream come true.

“So?” What do you mean, “So?” I wouldn’t be trying so hard if there was an end to delicacy! All the chefs are continuing their research to this day, seeking more stimulating flavors. And I just want to be as good as the stain on their apron at least!"

entries.name: Pluto
entries.content:
Pluto is a Distortion known as Yesterday's Promise.

Pluto is a monochromatic skeleton donning a dapper top hat and old-fashioned monocle on his left eye. Wearing a completely ash-gray blazer and pants, plaid undershirt, and gray tie—the most visually striking detail other than his skull head being his scorpion tail, covered in spiked barbs. He also possesses black hands with sharp claws.

Later in the story, after joining the Reverberation Ensemble, Pluto wears the group's signature suit. His new black top hat also possesses the Ensemble's signature blue highlight and is taller than Pluto's first.

Pluto is polite and unfailingly formal, retaining this stance even when actively antagonizing another party or participating in an attack. He even repairs the Library's front door during the first Uninvited Guests reception when his fellow ensemble members barged in, and apologizes to the Librarians if he happens to defeat the Floor of Religion in his initial reception.

However, Pluto is also notably sadistic and cruel amongst his fellow Ensemble members, in a vein similar to Jae-heon. He would grant people premise of power or knowledge in the form of his contracts, but when they violate the terms (which is incredibly easy) he could take whatever he wants from them. He also acted as the last straw for Philip to Distort through one last push that compels him to fall to the distorting voice.

He follows Argalia devoutly like Eileen and believes that he could give him a world without lies of deception through stealing the Library's Light. This stems from the implications that he was blackmailed by Roland, who cocerced him to sign a bogus contract that could easily destroy his career or get him executed by O Corp. This event also acted as the basis of his contract-related powers.

According to the cutscene prior to the realization of the Floor of Social Sciences, it's heavily implied that Pluto was a victim of a bogus contract from Roland that required him to smuggle Enkephalin to O Corp, so Roland can earn enough money to migrate into a Nest. The Wing presumably slaughtered his entire Office over the smuggling incident, but he survived. Roland was presumably rejected Nest immigration after this incident, which caused him to be stuck in I Corp's Backstreets where The Pianist manifested and killed his wife Angelica.

He distorted afterwards and was capable of making bogus deals known as the "Yesterday's Promise", which grants its victims whatever they want in exchange for an unfavorable side term written in miniscule fine print. If the side term is violated, Pluto then can take anything or do anything he wants to with that victim. Yuna was responsible for handling an attack he instigated known as "Thousand Needles".

Argalia later recruited him to form The Reverberation Ensemble alongside other distorted victims of Roland's direct and indirect actions.

"The world is one massive aggregation of delusions. A world where individuals can shape their own reality as they see fit. Every person is susceptible to deception, for they have knowledge. For that reason, it is impossible for a pure being untainted by knowledge to see the world as we mistakenly observe it, in the same way they cannot discern the end point of a line or tell between blue and red. A world devoid of wants. It would be unfit to call that place a world. In fact, to even call it a “place” would be yet another misconception amongst us knowing ones. The more one learns, the more delusions they invite.

However, if most people observed the same place and felt the same sentiments, then it might not be your own delusion after all. Wouldn’t you say so? For instance, take a look at the blue sky. The celestial dome is higher and farther than one can fathom, and as blue as it can be. Most will agree that the sky is tall and blue. Alas, those who think as such are ultimately within your view. It’s only natural that they agree with you as they’re figments born out of your delusional mind. Indeed, the sly entity that prevents you from seeing the world in its sincerest form would be none other than yourself. Even the holy entity in which you believe and to which you devote yourself is going to be a projection of your own self, so how can I trust anything that my eyes show me?"

entries.name: Rain
entries.content:
Rain is a Fixer belonging to Molar Boatworks. He is a returning character from Library of Ruina.

Rain is a short man with black hair reaching his ears, with large orange-lens goggles resting over his bangs. He wears a black choker with a silver piece dangling at the center. He wears a large blue overcoat adorned with tools over his bare chest, with a similarly stocked toolbelt crooked over a pair of black swim trunks. He wears dirtied white sneakers on his feet. He is also shown to carry his weapon at times, a large sword with chainsaw-like teeth across its edge.

Rain cares a lot about keeping up a good reputation for Molar Boatworks and will give unsubtle reminders to Olga to stay professional in front of their customers. He might be strict, but it is clear that it comes from a place of caring about Olga and Mika and a desire to keep working with them.

After the events of Library of Ruina Rain and his fellow Molar Office Fixers, Olga and Mika, return from their book forms and open the Molar Boatworks workshop in the Backstreets of District 21. They are contracted by Limbus Company to modify Mephistopheles to be capable of nautical travel and, while The Sinners spend days killing Trash Crabs to acquire the materials needed, Rain, Olga, and Mika work at completing the requested modifications. Despite some set backs with missing materials and forgetting to add the mode needed to keep Mephistopheles afloat, Rain and his friends soon see LCB off on their journey across the Great Lake.

entries.name: Renaud
entries.content:
Renaud was a Fixer of Charles' Office.

Although Renaud's full appearance is blocked out by shadows, they appear to be a large individual with spiky hair. They wear what looks like to be a jacket and has a large sword behind their back.

Renaud seems to be harsher than both Naimon and Ogier, saying that Roland has changed too much and that he'll die sooner or later.

Renaud, along with Ogier and Naimon, appear only in Roland's bad ending, at a bar, talking about Roland's sudden reappearance and his actions.

entries.name: Roland
entries.content:
Roland is the servant (friend) of Angela, following his story in the Library. He used to be a Grade 9 Fixer of a one-man Office before he wandered into the Library. He becomes the Patron Librarian of the first Floor to be unlocked: the Floor of General Works.

Now Roland works for Angela by getting her Books through receiving Guests, who are brought to the Library by the Invitations, fighting them during the Reception stage.

Roland has black short hair, pale skin, black eyes, and wears a simple black suit with a white shirt, a black tie, and black shoes.

Roland has a casual and relaxed personality, often clashing with Angela and the Patron Librarians. Being a person who has hit rock bottom, he has come to accept what he cannot change or control, while trying to survive and do his best in any situation, expressing this through his saying "That's that and this is this". He also believes that everyone is responsible for their own choices and that any resulting consequences are entirely their own fault - even if someone else's choice led to those consequences.

In his conversations with Angela, he is shown to have a rather deadpan and sometimes sarcastic demeanor, often teasing her about her lack of knowledge about the City, and how she does not open up to him very much. This usually makes Roland explain the various aspects of the City - the different Districts, the many Associations, Syndicates, and the other groups that operate throughout the City. He is not always knowledgeable of all its aspects, such as the Ruins.

Overall, Roland is a person who tries to make the best of his current situation, has a sense of logic and fairness, and shows some aversion when in stressful situations.

His sarcastic personality, however, is a facade hiding Roland's nihilistic and cynical worldview, having witnessed first-hand the ugliness of the City and the Wings as a Fixer during the Smoke War. Back then he donned a black perception-blocking mask, both from his grandmother's advice on that he should never be recognized, lest somebody took revenge on him, and out of shame due to participating in the ruthlessness of the City. This, along with having failed to protect his wife Angelica, brought Roland to have a low sense of self-worth, often describing himself as a "worthless lump".

According to Roland, he was formerly a "kickass" Grade 1 Fixer who mainly dealt with intelligence and information (and did not participate in actual combat) before being demoted to the lowest rank, Grade 9. He then started a one-man Office to continue making a living as a Fixer, before mysteriously finding himself inside the Library while trying to visit a HamHamPangPang sandwich shop.

Also according to Roland, he does not have any surviving family; his parents died when he was young, and he used to live with his grandmother until she mysteriously disappeared one day. He was also married, with his wife being another high-graded Fixer. However, both his wife and their unborn child were killed when their house collapsed in a disaster that happened in Roland's home district while Roland was away. Despite this, he claims to have accepted his loss, insisting that his tragedy was nothing special amongst the denizens of the City.

In truth, Roland is much more than he lets on. As a child, Roland was an orphan, and was adopted by a person who he refers to as his grandma, who disappeared later on. Roland became a Fixer at a young age, having been taught to survive as one thanks to his aforementioned grandmother, and was motivated to fight in the Smoke War for a chance at migration into a Nest. During this time he met Salvador, who showed him the former L Corp's Singularity, causing him to realize the ugliness which allows the City to survive. This affected him greatly, and he became distraught with the City's ruthless cycle of violence.

Nevertheless, Roland joined Charles' Office, impressing its Operator Charles enough for him to make Roland the Office's effective operational leader. It was there that he met his future wife Angelica, who was the Black Silence and the sister of Argalia, another Color Fixer. All the while, he hid his identity behind a black mask, partially due to his grandmother's warnings (that those that recognize him could potentially come to get revenge on Roland) and partially due to his shame at participating in the violence of the City, killing on others' orders. Over the course of his work, Roland became familiar with various groups and individuals in the City, including Oscar and Yujin. At some point he was involved in an Enkephalin shipping deal, and tricked a Fixer called Pluto.

Under Charles' Office, Angelica and Roland were responsible for the original defeat of the Blood-red Night, a Star of the City-class Distortion. Angelica was wounded, and Roland took off his mask out of concern, the first time he had ever shown someone his face as a Fixer. Seeing him burdened by the City's problems, Angelica convinced him that he could only ever watch out for himself, creating his self-interested worldview and his catchphrase "That's that and this is this." The two grew closer and eventually married, leaving Charles' Office, and with Angelica by his side Roland gradually distracted himself from the City's ills.

However, things began to go downhill. Roland was denied the Nest Migration Ticket which K Corp. and I Corp. had promised for veterans of the Smoke War. Roland and Angelica, who was pregnant, were forced to live in the Backstreets of District 9. Disaster struck when Roland was given one final Fixer mission by his former partner Olivier and he left to District 25. While he was away, the Pianist Distortion manifested in District 9, causing a massive death toll. Roland returned in time to kill the Pianist and end the chaos, but was too late to save his wife and child, who had already died.

In the aftermath, Roland went mad with grief and wrath. He turned his skill as a Fixer against the City, massacring anyone he believed was responsible for the Pianist - Fixer Offices, Syndicates, and even the Five Fingers. He even took his wife’s gloves (the signature equipment of the Black Silence) and went under the guise as the Black Silence. These included a scientist who kidnapped people and turned them into gears (Eileen's father), a factory used by Jae-heon to try and resurrect his son, the Thumb subsidiary Rumanos Cartel, and even the Middle. The death toll of his blind killing spree, as warned by his former colleague Astolfo, caused him to be demoted all the way down to a Grade 9 Fixer. Nevertheless, he successfully hid his true identity and thus avoided any potential fallout from all but his closest associates.

Shortly afterwards, he was contacted by Iori, The Purple Tear, who sent him into the Library as part of a plan to discover the source of the Distortions and help Roland resolve his desire to avenge Angelica's death, one way or another.

After hearing about Angela's plans on releasing the Abnormalities onto the City, he disgustedly states that she and Argalia would get along.

As the Ensemble becomes classified as a Impuritas Civitatis, the Hana Association is forced to enter the Library to destroy what they're after; the Library itself. While there, Olivier separates from the rest of the group to get the drop on Angela. After the Hana Association's reception, Olivier, using the advice he got from the Purple Tear, nearly kills Angela by using a TimeTrack to make Angela experience a thousand years at once, only for Roland to step in and save her. Once alone, the two former partners recount their past friendship before Oliver gives Roland the Black Silence gloves. Olivier is then defeated by Roland in a one-on-one duel. After this, Angela questions Roland as to why he didn't say anything about his true standing sooner, with him "stating" that he was trying to "find the right moment". However, she brushes his lies as he saved her, and was too close to her goal of becoming human to stop.

With all other competitors after the Library turned into books for its' Light, the Ensemble raids the Library without an Invitation. While there, Argalia soon reveals that he had his members Jae-heon and Elena repurpose Angelica's corpse as a one of the Puppeteer's Puppets. The mere sight of which infuriates Roland to such a degree that Angela becomes disturbed and begs him to calm down. After the Ensemble mocks Angela for being unable to realize she's responsible for the Distortions that made Roland's life hell and scatter, the Fixer makes it clear that Argalia and his members come first.

During The Blue Reverberation's Reception, Argalia explains to Roland his intentions to use Light gathered in the Library to "break the mold of the City", while Roland accuses the Blue Sicko of doing it all because underneath all of his "reasons", his performance is just a means to lash out and get revenge for losing Angelica. Despite losing the battle, Argalia hauntingly states that it won't end like this as he's booked alongside the rest of his Ensemble.

With the defeat of the Ensemble and Angela's gaining of a human body, however, Roland betrays her, revealing his grudge against her for instigating the Distortion phenomena that took Angelica away from him, calling out her selfishness and desire for power for the sake of it, like any other cityfolk. In the following reception, Roland's true emotions soon cause him to Distort into forms based on his misanthropic and nihilistic view of the world before being defeated and reverting back into a human. Despite having a bloodied Roland dead-to-rights, Angela, having been purged of her materialism, instability, greed, lust, and ignorance, gives up her dream of humanity and decides to free the Light and everyone the Library has booked.

This initially drives Roland into distress, seeing the act as a slap to his struggles and despair, but despite Angela having her back turned to atone, the Fixer, freed from his ugliness, cruelty, insensitivity, and arbitrariness, lets go of his revenge and instead decides to follow where she'll go next. He proves this by protecting her from the now freed Ensemble, Distorted thanks to the light, leading the charge against them for the next seven days, and then saving her from fading from existence just as she was about to disappear. Roland then finishes off the Distorted Argalia for good, with The Blue Reverberation finally accepting him as brother-in-law before being told to drop dead. With the battle over, Roland reveals that his act of saving Angela (as well as his entering of the Library in the first place) was thanks to the Purple Tear.

Just then, the exhausted Library is then raided by agents sent by the Head and is subsequently expelled into the Outskirts, in spite of his, Gebura, and Binah's efforts. In the aftermath, Roland asks what Angela will do now, and accepts her plans on reopening the Library to rebel against the Head for perpetuating the City's cycle of misery, but warns her that as a former cityfolk, the path she intends to take will be difficult, as she has no idea where to start, and that all tragedies are as common as flowing water. Still, Angela decides to give it a shot, saying "that is this, and this is that". Angela then makes him reveal his other wish; to write a book based on all he knows about the City. However, as he believed to be inadequate when it came to writing, thinking of it as crude, and as such, he abandoned that dream. Roland, somewhat embarrassed, tells Angela to not tell the other librarians, but Angela proceeds to reassure him. As they set back off into the Library, Angela offers to help write the book, but not as the Library Director, but as a friend.

entries.name: Rose
entries.content:
Rose is an employee of W Corp. and part of the WARP Cleanup Crew.

Rose is a woman with long blue hair tied into a ponytail, dark green eyes, and tanned skin. She wears the standard uniform of a WARP Cleanup Agent, which consisted of a black shirt and a blue necktie underneath a chestplate with the W Corp. logo imprinted on it, blue jeans with a utility belt, and a baseball cap bearing the logo of W Corp.. As her means of combat, she fights hand-to-hand with a pair of space-ripping gauntlets and boots.

entries.name: The Black Silence
entries.content:
The Black Silence was a Color Fixer, known for its gloves that, along with storing all its weapons, muffled all sound around its surroundings save for its weapons cutting through the air. Originally a title held by Angelica, her gloves were used by Roland after her death at the hands of The Pianist. Donning his Perception-blocking mask, he went on a rampage, killing Fixers, Syndicates, and anybody who seemed suspicious enough in a vain effort to find out the culprit behind the incident. He was eventually exposed, however, losing his status and demoted to Grade 9, with the only option left for him being cooperating with Iori to infiltrate the Library. After defeating Argalia, he turns his blade on Angela, revealing to have been waiting until she was human to enact his revenge on her for killing his wife.

This Reception immediately follows completing the Reception of The Reverberation Ensemble. It consists of five phases, acting as the final boss of the game if the player has failed to complete all Floor Realizations.

Following the defeat of the Ensemble and Angela's gaining a human body, Roland betrays Angela and reveals everything that he had been hiding; that the reason he came to the Library was to investigate it, hoping to figure out the cause of the phenomenon that created Distortions like the Pianist, which soon became clear it was Angela, who ruined Ayin's Seed of Light plan out of revenge for the hardships his Script put her through, mocking her by saying none of it would've happened if she "hadn't thrown out a tantrum at the last moment".

When Angela asks why didn't he attempt to kill her when the two first met, he reveals four reasons: One, she was unkillable back then. Two, he wanted to know why she made the choices she did. Three, he had hoped Angela would go down a different path, and then maybe he could as well. And four, in the event she didn't; to make her suffer at the end, making her experience "the greatest loss", by killing her as soon as she acquired a human body, now that she has the ability to wholly feel pain. While acknowledging that what she suffered for millions of years during the events of Lobotomy Corporation was terrible, and that his pain is nothing but dust compared to that, Roland still vowed to make the City, and by extension, her, suffer for stealing Angelica away, much like Angela did by rejecting Ayin's plan.

Angela, having finally gained a human body, feels the sting of betrayal, unable to say anything for a few moments before she timidly says she wanted somebody to pay her suffering, that she unable to do anything else and filled by an overwhelming desire to make them all pay. Baffled, Roland answers that if he knew the answers to any of that, he wouldn't have helped her come this far, but he knew one thing for sure: this is all the result of attempting to wash blood with blood. Grief-stricken and with tears in his eyes, he condemns Angela to make her suffer the same sorrow he did, having taken Angelica — his true love — away from him; watching as he killed the people he knew, even his own friend Olivier; suppressing everything he felt in the form of a pained smile. Declaring that he's done with that facade now, Roland is determined to do everything he can to make Angela suffer the most painful death possible, right before she took the final step to her freedom, to rob her of it all.

Stammering and hurt, Angela feebly tries to justify her actions with the same reasons she had given all along: that she wanted to be compensated for her suffering in L Corp, that the Library's methods weren't forceful and the Guests came from their own volition. Roland is simply amused at how Angela seemed to hesitate at the very end, before coming to the conclusion that she simply doesn't want to give up all the power, knowledge, and her proper life as a human now. He then shoots down her excuses, pointing out that was the same reasoning she had when she had taken the Light in the White Nights and Dark Days, using it to kill all who came to the Library in what they considered a fair price for their lives. Roland accuses her of never having stopped to think of the consequences of her own actions, after all, that's how she's always ever been, not caring about anybody other than her own self.

Nonetheless, Roland can't bring himself to fully blame Angela, her suffering is just how the City has ever been and how it works, saying "That's that, and this is this". With that, he places his perception-blocking mask on, declaring he will kill her with the mindset of the City's folk: all he needs to do is kill Angela and exact his revenge; all Angela needs to do is kill him and reach for her freedom, adding that, for her own sake, Angela must stop getting any ideas and just stick to her desire for freedom and vengeance. The screen fades to black, and in a low voice, Roland recites "Prayer for Loving Sorrow" to himself.

Bloodied and exhausted, Roland falls to his knees, calling both himself and Angela "dimwitted egoists, their sight limited by their own selfishness, fools chasing immediate results". He adds that their own logic that dictated their decisions was destined to be their downfall one day; had any of them actually cared for themselves, neither would've made this choice, after all, selfishness isn't simply keeping your eyes to yourself, but also taking a good look at everything around them and engraving it on their hearts. He then requests Angela to kill him and claim the human life she spent so long working for, and that hesitating like this is a bad habit that would get her killed in the City, giving her one final choice: To either finish him and finally reach for the one perfect book, or spare his life, letting go of her grief.

The millennia of solitude Angela had experienced in L Corp flash before her eyes, making her stop for a moment, while Roland sarcastically comments that if she keeps going for a bit longer, he'd take her head as soon as she lowered her guard. Stuttering and vulnerable, Angela decides to spare Roland, letting go of everything, determined to finally break the cycle of suffering, even when she became part of it through the Library. She declares that if her freedom meant perpetuating that cycle, repeating the same horrible deeds she had done, she could not live that life further, crushed under the cycle once again, the freedom she wanted to attain was meaningless in the City.

Roland is completely baffled, he cannot believe that after all she's done she has decided to let go at the last moment, who sarcastically asks if she was hit by a big revelation. Outraged, he asks what will become of all the people that faced certain death in the Library, who he reluctantly killed with his own hands; all his determination and despair would've been for nothing, screaming that Angela must have a desire; the cycle can't simply be broken so easily, specially when somebody has taken this much blood and power to not even have a full-fledged wish.

Angela explains that she feels the weight of all their sacrifices, having become unbearable, even though when she believed this would be the last time she'd have to kill in the name of what she believed was something greater, but notes that she could never be free as long as she was chained to the cycle of violence of the City; she, Roland, and the Library itself soaked in the blood of many. Even though she convinced herself that it was one last inevitable sacrifice, for the sake of her freedom and closure to her pain, the cycles of the City are powered by those sacrifices, crushing everything in their path. She decided that even if she has to snuff out her wish by her own hand, if she had to spill more blood, she'd let go of her goal, or at least, refuse to die being part of the cycle.

Roland whispers that it can't simply be done like that, stating "If one extorts once and again and again, what would they do if they lack the resolve to finish the job?". Angela answers that she will let go of all the knowledge that the Library has captured, maybe that way those who died within the Library could be brought back. Bewildered, he asks if that's really what she wishes for, now that she's finally free and do whatever she wishes for, emphasizing on the million years she spent, waiting for revenge, and now her deepest wish is within her reach. Angela answers that this is a decision she made by her own will, the first wish and the last choice she'd take since she "became free of all restraints". In a low voice, Roland repeats that she won't forgive her; she can't simply let go of everything by her own hand, that's not how things work in the City.

Angela asks Roland for one last favor: Since releasing everything the Library had obtained won't be a simple feat, she asks him to leave her be for a moment, leaving herself vulnerable for a while, weighting on that she's asking for this as a friend, at least, is he still considered her his friend. Angela adds that she won't stop him, but after she's finished, everything will go to the way it was, and she'll disappear from the City without a trace.

As all of Roland's pain flashes before him and decides to leave Angela, the Library bursts into a pillar of Light, giving path to the final Realization.

entries.name: Floor Realization
entries.content:
The Floor Realization of the Floor of General Works is the final Floor Realization available. It becomes available after defeating The Black Silence and choosing to forgive Angela and Roland, which only is possible if all other Realizations have been cleared. Unlike other Realizations, each phase is a separate reception, giving the ability to change Assistant Librarian's key pages, combat pages, and passives at the start of each phase. This also resets their Emotion level to 0, however.

After choosing to let go of the Light she gathered, Angela soon finds the process interrupted by a mysterious person resembling her past self back in Lobotomy Corp. This person is disappointed with the choice Angela has made, and tries to stop her from releasing everything, though Angela remains steadfast to this decision that she made of her own free will.

With Angela's decision to release the Light, a pillar of Light blooms at the center of the ruined Nest L, attracting the attention of everyone around. Angela speculates about what will soon happen: the Light will permeate the City and the hearts of its inhabitants. While the changes will not be immediate, the cityfolk will eventually be able to face, and realize, their true feelings. She laments that she won't be able to see it herself, now understanding how the Sephirah felt when the Seed of Light was released back in L Corp.

From the Light, a voice sounding similar to Angela's asks if she is truly fine with giving up her million-year long goal. The voice reveals itself in the form of Angela back from her time at Lobotomy Corporation, shocking the present Angela. The voice assures Angela that she merely wants to talk to her, and the release of the Light will not be affected. It disapproves of Angela letting go of the wish they both held for a million years, instead wishing to claim freedom for both of them now that the path is clear. Angela refuses to change her mind, as this is the first choice she has made out of her own will. Seeing this, the voice says it will make Angela's emotions "bloom" once more.

The voice, appearing as Angela's old self, manifests the Wrist Cutter EGO to "sharpen" the anger and sadness she felt and bring Angela's negative emotions back out. Angela holds to her wish to spread the Light, while the voice pities her for supposedly suppressing her true emotions. Angela and the voice prepare to fight one another.

Images of Carmen's suicide flash into Angela's thoughts. She remembers how much she wanted to live once she had already made the decision to sacrifice herself, regretting the action she took.

Carmen speaks directly to Angela, admitting she's a human just like anyone else. She believed her own selfless sacrifice would help lead everyone else to a perfect ending, but it clearly wasn't the case.

The voice expresses doubt anybody could truly sacrifice themselves for others' sake. In her own words, "humans can only love themselves, after all."

Carmen talks about her role as the voice, "whispering into people the essence of life" so that they would learn to prioritize their emotions and their emotions alone.

Once defeated, the voice's facade as L Corp. Angela disappears, revealing her true identity to be Carmen. Carmen points out the irony in how Angela, who was supposed to be her exact replacement, ended up being so different from her. Although their goals are now different, Carmen wishes Angela the best, telling Angela she will only stop leading the cityfolk to Distortion if they learn to love and accept their true selves. While Angela laments Carmen's decision, she remains steadfast, warning Carmen that she will do whatever she can to stop Carmen's plans while she is still part of the Light.

Now alone, Angela reflects on the continued release of the Light. With everything that had been collected by the Library being returned, the guests turned into books will also find themselves back "in the places they belong." As she begins to fade into the Light, Angela recalls, at some point, hearing a faint voice offering her a simple apology and the acknowledgement she had longed for from the beginning.

As the guests of the Library are returned to life, the Reverberation Ensemble rises once again with newfound strength, beginning the reception of The Reverb Ensemble Distorted.

entries.name: Rudolph
entries.content: Rudolph is the Captain of the Reindeer Team in the Fourth Pack of R Corp.

entries.name: Salvador
entries.content:
Salvador was the Operator of the Dawn Office.

Salvador is an old, white-haired man with a moustache. He wears a brown trench coat, a black blazer with a white tie, black gloves, and blue slacks. He carries 3 swords with him, 2 broadswords on his waist and 1 claymore on his back.

Salvador is a kind old man who works alongside Philip and Yuna at the Dawn Office. He's blunt with his feelings as shown by his disinterest in Walter, stating that he never had the potential to be a capable man, had one-dimensional thoughts, and had a habit of making rhetorical questions, which Salvador found to be annoying. He shares a kinship with Philip and Yuna, making a joke stating how Philip's ssanghwa-cha expertise would have made him a Grade 1 Fixer and gotten a color.

Salvador is a veteran who participated in the Smoke Wars. He worked alongside Roland as a hired mercenary, and it is unclear as to which side of the war he was hired on. After the war had ended, Salvador set up his Fixer office, Dawn Office. He shares a close connection to his sister office, Wedge Office, where both offices help each other as needed.

Philip prepares ssanghwa-cha for Salvador when Salvador asks Philip if he has heard of the Library. Philip responds, stating that he does know of its existence but only that it's an Urban Legend. Salvador then states that the Library has recently exalted to an Urban Plague, and that Zwei Section 6 has fell victim to it, regarding that his old friend Walter has died, lamenting that Walter struggled through the ranks and yet died in the end. Philip consoles Salvador, to which Salvador shows no pity and states how he was never fond of Walter, stating he didn't quite have the potential to be a capable man, his thoughts were one-dimensional, and that he had a habit of making rhetorical questions, which Salvador found annoying. He does remark Walter's talent, however, though he puts it off to "savoir-faire", or mere luck. Yuna then walks in after completing her job, remarking the stronger scent of ssanghwa-cha and how she's getting tired of it. Salvador compliments Philip's tea-brewing skills stating how he should learn from Philip so that he can make some for his wife. In addition, he jokes on how Philip could become a Grade 1 Fixer and receive a color if his tea brewing expertise counted towards grade evaluations, and that his color would be bright yellow, like the hue of the egg yolk floating atop the tea and the color of his favorite flower, forsythia.

Yuna cuts him off and states that the request regarding the Thousand Needles has been taken care of, to which Philip congratulates her. Yuna describes how the Thousand Needles formed together as one and caused chaos. She suspects that Yesterday's Promise is the culprit, stating in disbelief that magic really does exist and that strange symbols were carved onto every needle. Salvador compliments her stating that she's the pride of the office, to which Yuna states that she feels like the only working member and that the monthly rent is intimidating since their office is located in the Nest. That's when Salvador explains that an Urban Plague-class job has been assigned to them by the Zwei Association to investigate the Library. Salvador tried contacting the Wedge Office for assistance, but states that they seem to be busy with their own work (which is later revealed to be the 8 o'Clock Circus).

After entering the Library, Yuna states that the interior is slick, to which Philip is reminded of the factory they raided as part of the Midnight Pancreas Burgers request, much to Yuna and Salvador's disgust. When Angela arrives, Salvador greets her and asks what to do to kill her, to which Angela responds that she'd like to know as well. Salvador is intrigued, stating that she has the capability for casual banter. Salvador then threatens Angela, stating not to meet a peaceful end after imbruing her hands in so much blood, to which Angela reciprocates the feelings. Ultimately Salvador is defeated and turned into the Book of Salvador.

entries.name: San
entries.content:
San is the Operator of Streetlight Office.

San has short black hair, dark skin, and blue eyes. He wears a white shirt with a dark gray tie under a black vest, a black and dark blue jacket with two pockets on the sides, and black fingerless gloves. On his lower half, San has black pants with a black sheath attached to his right thigh and black shoes. In combat, he uses a long black baton.

San is a calm individual and cool headed most of the time, but once the situation becomes alarming, his cowardly nature gets the best of him, making San usually flee the location. He also has a strong bond with his two old friends, Isadora and Julia, and his co-workers, Lulu and Mars, whom he calls his juniors and holds a great sense of responsibility for, to the point of barging into Zwei HQ to beg Isadora, Julia and the Zwei Association for help retriving his junior's books from the Library.

San has been a Fixer of eight years and has spent an unknown period of time as the creator and Operator of Streetlight Office.

San grew up in the Backstreets of District 21 with his friend Isadora, he used to "train" himself so he "doesn't lag behind" and although being a coward San would try facing his fears and put himself in dangerous situations, only to end up running back to Isadora. When they were kids, the two of them hanged out until dark one day and almost got themselves into a dangerous situation, San having to pick up a stick from the floor and stand his ground with his shaky legs to protect himself and Isadora from an unknown threat. Later in life, San joins an Office along with his childhood friend, there they met Julia in their first day; all of them having recently become Fixers, the three quickly befriended one another. After an unknown amount of time San left his first Office and created his own, Streetlight Office, which in no time became an Affiliate Office of the Zwei Association, the same Association his two friends joined. San ended up recruting two Fixers for his Office, Lulu and Mars, who usually got into petty arguments. Together the three keep peace in a two blocks' area on an unspecified location in the City and following other types of orders from the Zwei Association.

In the first Episode of Streetlight Office, Mars and Lulu are in their office, with Lulu starting to wonder why their Office is unpopular with clients even when they are affiliated with the Zwei and have a 0% crime rate in their secured areas, with Mars pointing out that they just cover two blocks of space. Regardless, they will get work eventually but Lulu is thinking in moving to other Office if they keep waiting. Mars says that he doesn't think she has what it takes to work for a bigger Office, but Lulu respond that she has business connections. She then brings up that his Legendary Fixer mother is too busy while Lulu has friends who can help her. Mars sarcastically replies she is a great Fixer, and Lulu just digs on it.
