San arrives afterwards with work, while Lulu starts to argue with Mars because he disposed of her cake of the fridge, saying that it already expired. After San settles in buying another cake for Lulu, he talks about their unofficial work from a friend in the Association. Lulu ask if is the Fixer who works directly under the Association and San confirms it. San explains that this task has yet to be officially addressed by the Hana Association, asking soon after if they know about the Library. Mars and Lulu knows some stories of it that were overheard from the Rats, saying that had very valuable books. San then tells that he retrieved an invitation from his friend, although they start to question the risk of it as they don't know much about it and will not count for their carreer, as well they might not gain as much money even with San saying that his Associate friend will promise for an Urban-Legend payment. San start to cave in that was a bad idea afterall, but Mars and Lulu agree in going, now that they need money, and will do their best.

After signing the Invitation and entering the Library, Mars and Lulu begin to argue again over taking the work. San has to interrupt and settle them down again by offering to eat in Juli's restaurant once is over and that he will pay for. Afterwards, Angela arrives and notes the conversation of them. They get wary but Angela reassures that the ordeal hasn't started yet. She present herself and San greets her, asking that if they are still able to enter since he borrowed the Invitation from someone else. Angela clarify that it eventually reached to him and they signed it with their names, so it worked as intended. Angela leaves but Lulu notices that she wasn't human, but a machine. San reminds them to stay aware and back up when gets too dangerous, and the fixers enter the Library.

On the second Episode of Streetlight Office, Lulu and San managed to escape from the Library, but Mars died during the Reception. Back in the Office, they are both mourning their death with San blaming himself for taking the work and going to the Library. He says it was out of their abilities and he already sent a report to the Zwei. Lulu reacts harshly, asking about Mars and if his death was pointless. San continues to feel regret and let Lulu blame him all she wants. Lulu goes to check the fridge and notices a cake, and asks if he bought it. San tells that he didn't buy any cake, then Lulu says she is going outside for a bit.

Lulu cries in the streets under the rain, as she remembers Mars, that wasn't like he would buy cake for others, that he bragged of his sword that was a gift of her mother, and that he would become like her. Lulu suddenly receives an invitation that includes in it the Book of Mars. Realizing what happens to the people who die there, she settles in avenge him but cannot go for San to help. She decides to go by herself with some of her friends to help her out. Lulu ends up dying in the reception alone.

The First Episode of Zwei begins with San heading to the Zwei Association, Section 6; to talk with a pair of Fixers, Julia and Isadora, who are part of the Association. The conversation starts out with San telling the two that his colleagues, Lulu and Mars, have died on their mission to The Library. His only request to them is for the Zwei Association to help him retrieve their books, if that's the least they could do. Isadora immediately treats San with backlash, telling him that barge in into the HQ to beg for help isn't the best way to get help. However, Julia opposes Isadora, and suggests that they let their superiors have a review of the case. Soon after, we learn that Julia has a friendship with San; Isadora tells her that they shouldn't act on attachment nor friendship, lest it lead to their system collapsing -And others begging and asking for their help.

Isadora reminds Julia again that the records show that this case shows up nowhere in the Zwei records, due to perhaps taking it as an unofficial work and if San wants them to go to the Library to try and get the Books back, then she wants him to pay a corresponding reward for the mission, and that San has used the association as much as the association has used him. It also becomes known that San, Isadora, and Julia all used to work in the same Office together in the past.

After a few more arguments, Isadora gets a notification of the news that the Library has been moved up from Urban Myth to Urban Legend by the Hana Association, and that the library is now a good case for them to officially take on. They get the invitation from San and send some Zwei Crewmembers to go to the Library.

In the Second Episode of Zwei begins with Isadora telling Julia and San that they are in the lineup of the search team for the library. Julia is happy to go to the library, and says that they should go retrieve the books of Mars and Lulu and come back safely. Isadora also jumps in to add that even though they should always stay on their objective, they still need to collect as much information as possible (Collect as many books as they can. San then decides to ask Isadora that of all the things that they could do, why are they sending a search team to enter the library; Isadora snaps back and asks San why he came begging to them in the first place. San responds that this place was the only one that he could count on. She also asks him about his younger brother, but he refuses to answer.

Soon, Isadora decides to tell San and Julia about the Distortion Phenomenon, which is classified as an Urban Nightmare. The Distortion phenomenon is an anomaly that has been happening throughout the city ever since the White Nights and Dark Days; this phenomenon turns people into monsters at random, and each occurrence is worse to deal with than the last. This is where we get our first look at "The Pianist", where in its first case alone caused the death of 80% of District 9's population. They had to immediately send in a colored fixer in order to gain control of the situation after they realized how severe the situation was. They have almost no clues whatsoever to track down the cause of the phenomenon; however, the most information they have on it so far revolves around the sudden disappearance of L Corp, and the White Nights and Dark Days that started in the corporation's nest. Isadora claims that the Zwei Association have a hunch that the Library might be one of the keys to understanding this phenomenon.

Julia tells Isadora that a coworker told her about a similar story, where a resident in the area they were peacekeeping transformed into a beast without any warning whatsoever. They managed to take care of that case before the death toll could reach double digits. Another incident involved a restaurant clerk turning into a man-eating sandwich monster. Isadora reassures Julia and San that there hasn't been any cases of the phenomenon that has been nearly as dangerous as the Pianist for now, they thank Isadora for the information before heading to the Library.

Upon reaching the Library's entrance, Julia comments how the transportation method used by the Invitation seems akin to something a Singularity would be capable of, then San mentions how the Director of the Library will soon arrive to greet them with Angela showing up moments after. The Office Operator stats that with this reception they wish to retrieve the books of Mars and Lulu, Angela affirms that both items can be found in the Library. Finally, Julia inquires Angela about if one really can retrieve the books upon coming out victorious in Reception and if one does really turn into a book by failing, the Library Director confirms her suspicions and invites them in.

Eventually, San finally perishes in the Reception along with Julia and some Zwei Fixers, and he turns into the Book of San which contains his Key Page.

entries.name: Sayo
entries.content:
Sayo is a captain of the Kurokumo Clan.

Sayo wears a loose-fitting, off-the-shoulder black Kimono fastened with a sash and wears a pair of Zori. Her hair is tied up in a bun, decorated with chopsticks. She has tattoos plastered on her shoulders in a similar fashion to Irezumi, a style of tattooing on the body performed by permanently in-laying the ink beneath the outer epidermis of the skin, using handheld tools to do so. This style and method is most commonly done from within the Japanese mafia, the Yakuza. She also wields a Katana, to further implement the idea of the Kurokumo clan being in similar nature of the Yakuza.

Sayo is a cunning and ruthless woman and clan leader. She has strong business sense, entrusted to carry out delivery of Nuovo Fabric to the Thumb , as well as producing income through 'protection' rackets that force Nest dwellers to pay a fee, else they face violent mutilation. Sayo is rather merciless, likely a mindset she adopted growing up in the Backstreets "covered in filth and blood". Though her policies are extreme, she understands her strength and decides to back away from fighting the lone Index messenger, knowing he would overpower her. However she still challenges formidable enemies to duel, such as the L'heure du Loup, to which she loses, and accepts the terms to go to the Library or face death.

Eventually, Sayo along the rest of the Kurokumo Clan dies in the Reception. Dropping the Book of Sayo which may contain their Key Page.

entries.name: Sen
entries.content:
Sen is an employee of W Corp. and part of the WARP Cleanup Crew.

Sen is a man with graying brown hair, brown eyes, stubble, and a scarred, tanned face. He wears a black shirt under a chestplate with the W Corp logo imprinted on it, blue jeans with a utility belt, black boots, and black fingerless gloves. He carries a hatchet with three holes punched in it.

entries.name: Stephan
entries.content:
Stephan is a Fixer working for the Full- Full-Stop Office.

Stephan has a fair complexion, green eyes, and short, fluffy, blond hair. He wears a white striped turtleneck and a washed out olive green jacket. Stephan's pants are baggy, black slacks pushed up by a pair of black combat boots. Additionally, he sports red-lensed goggles over his neck and a set of shoulder straps and belt in the middle of his chest.

Unlike the other known members of Full-Stop Office, he has a nervous demeanor and cynical outlook. He quickly loses hope in a situation if it becomes to overwhelming.

entries.name: Taein
entries.content:
Taein is a Fixer of the brutal Hook Office.

Taein has short black hair, light skin, brown eyes and bionic hand prosthetics. He wears a black cloth mask, two belts over an orange parka coat with white fur and sleeves with the pockets on the sides, and a black t-shirt under it. On his lower half, Taein has light gray trousers and dark gray shoes. In combat, he uses two scythes of Union Co. that are attached to his back.

Taein is mostly an impatient person, being cold and arrogant to other around him except for his colleagues. He seems to appreciate and be quite knowledgeable about bionic technology, stating their benefits and how it's a safe choice when one can't find a procedure or equipment that suits them well.

Taein has been a part of Hook Office for an unspecified amount of time.

In his past, Taein was recruited by a Syndicate from District 23 that was infamous for holding their killed targets on the open streets, hanging them from hooks, there he met Naoki and McCullin. They spent time dealing with tasks given by poor people who couldn't afford the prices of the Offices and Associations. They were friends with the Axe Gang, another Syndicate of their area, and used to cause trouble together. After some more raids to other Offices, the operator of one them came over to their Syndicate and told that wanted people like them. The members of the Syndicate accepted, now becoming officially Fixers of the Hook Office. Although their work consisted of the same methods of gruesome executions and hanging corpses from hooks to send messages to the others, they still find it strange how they got hired by an Office. Even with them joining an Office, the Axe Gang has no grudge towards them for doing so.

In the first Episode of Hook Office, Taein, McCullin, and Naoki are some undisclosed location in the Backstreets discussing their last job of yesterday and about Taein's new bionic weapon, as they got excessive with their destructive attacks and killed more people than they should have, and since it was their mistake, they wouldn't get paid by the additional kills. Taein points out that Naoki was the one who spent more time on the rampage and that McCullin had to calm her down. After expressing she was sorry, McCullin doesn't mind as he still owes them a few things, and that now they must remain low.

Afterward, they reflect how they ended up in their new Office in the first place, as they used to be from a Syndicate that killed and hanged the victims from hooks on the streets which got the attention of an Office to hire them, due to their methods and outfits that make them stand out, which means the Office also stands out. Naoki comments it feels more like a pack of Rats than a proper Office. Just then, McCullin gets a message from the operator and their next work is handling the Library. Along with additional Hook Fixers, the group is given the Invitation and they are instantly transported to it.

On their arrival, Angela greets them but Taein attempts to strike first but doesn't harm Angela due to her body. Soon Naoki notices that Angela is not human and to the Hook Fixers' surprise, discover she is an AI, thinking now about how much they are going to profit from this task. The group enters after Angela leaves.

Eventually, Taein falls in the Reception along with Naoki, McCullin, and some of Hook Office's other Fixers, and he is turned into the Book of Taein which contains his Key Page.

entries.name: Tamaki
entries.content:
Tamaki is a Fixer working for the Full- Full-Stop Office.

Tamaki is a short dark-skinned woman with very long white hair that is tied into a ponytail by a black hair tie and with small bangs. She wears a grey dress shirt with a black tie under a long black two button jacket which is envolped by a utility belt of a darker shade of black and which contains at least four pouches. Tamaki also wears a short black skirt which is barely visable under her jacket, grey pantihoses, and brownish army boots with one strap each and white laces. The Fixer carries with her a black should bag and possess a ear piece on her left ear and black knee gear on each knee.

entries.name: Tanya
entries.content:
Tanya is a Distortion known as L'Heure du Loup and a member of The Reverberation Ensemble.

Tanya is a Distortion with a wolf-like appearance, her most prominent feature being her black wolf head. She has long black hair that goes down her back, glowing yellow eyes, and a scar that runs through one of her eyes. She wears a golden chain collar around her neck, a pair of ear piercings on one of her ears, a patterned purple button-up underneath a black leather jacket, a belt with a golden chain attached to it, brown pants, and black shoes. She is also shown to smoke out of a pipe.

Later in the story, after joining the Reverberation Ensemble, Tanya wears the group's signature suit.

Tanya was an executive of The Middle. It appears as if she followed most of the Middle's beliefs about brotherhood until Roland massacred her entire gang during his rampage across the City. After witnessing the full-blown decimation of her gang, she likely discarded her former Middle Finger ideals in place of a social darwinist ideology and Distorted. Just like other Distortions of the Reverberation Ensemble, Tanya is perfectly in-control of her actions and desires despite having been distorted.

"Fighting for survival is a natural thing. Even now, we’re all in battle. There’re more people born than folks dying of natural causes, and the living struggle in their own positions every day. A fight to protect, and to avoid falling behind. Maybe it’s all ‘cause there just ain’t enough seats for the ever-growing population of humans to take? Sure, extra jobs and stuff could be made in the future, but that’s nothing more than a hopeful estimate that might not happen until it’s too late for you. The world we live in right now is what matters. There’s got to be a way to weed out the unfit without straining all of us. And that’s when strength plays its part.

I don’t get why you vilify this. Aren’t we all doing the same thing, directly or not? We elbow our way past others so we can survive, and the losers are knocked outta the race. You say this is fair, but say no to physical conflicts, to “respect life” or whatevs? Then lemme ask: what’s the reason to respect life? Do you think you’re respecting life right now?"

entries.name: Tenma
entries.content:
Tenma is a Fixer of Section 2 of the Shi Association's Southern Branch.

Tenma is a young woman of short frame who wears the Shi Association uniform. It consists of a black jacket with red stripes at the hem, sleeves and collar that covers her lower face. It's embellished with a fastened belt, various buttons and an insignia on her shoulder like Yujin. She wears a red skirt, black leggings and ankle boots with stripes and steel trim. She has long black hair decorated with a red ribbon, a white eyepatch over her right eye and cheek, and wears black gloves. Like Valentin and Yujin, she fights with a katana and carries a saya, as she is a fixer of the Shi that work much like assassins. However, she also carries a wakizashi, a shorter katana and uses both swords in combat.

Tenma is an empathetic and loyal fixer that fights alongside Valentin and Yujin in the Shi South Section 2 division of the Shi Association. She has a great amount of respect for Yujin, claiming she will become 'president of the Shi' one day and resolve the corruption that lies in the organisation. However, she is not blind to the fact that the team's condition is deteriorating, showing concern for Yujin who has fought harder than the rest of the group to make sure Valentin and Tenma don't have to carry the whole of the struggle. Like Valentin, she knows that winning each conflict will mean another will ensue, and the struggle will never end if the Blue Reverberation remains at large. In spite of this, she follows Yujin to battle, only hoping she won't harm herself for the sake of the Section 2 fixers.

Following the Blue Reverberation's abandonment of his post, Yujin, Tenma and Valentin fight their way through his assigned requests and eventually are ordered to infiltrate the Library. Yujin aims to replace the Shi's leaders, like Thelma, in order to bring back its former glory and stamp out the corruption in the association, with full support from Tenma and Valentin. However, they are not in condition to fight, and make their last stand in the Library in order to find the root of what Argalia is planning through the memories of the Musicians of Bremen, and potentially gain an edge in the political stage of the City.

entries.name: The Pianist
entries.content:
The Pianist was a Distortion that manifested in District 9 during the "White Nights, Dark Days" incident after the fall of Lobotomy Corporation. When compared to an abnormality The Pianist would be a WAW class.

The Pianist appears to be a well-dressed humanoid entity with six arms, clad in a black trench coat with a featureless black face. It is shown playing a pipe organ, albeit twisted to appear like a piano.

During the "White Nights, Dark Days", the Pianist manifested in District 9. It started to play the piano, killing 80% of population as victims were killed and transformed into piano notes. It was eventually killed by The Black Silence, but not without leaving behind a massive trail of death.

It was later revealed that the Pianist was responsible for Angelica's death and a major source of Roland's trauma. After being forced to stay in the Backstreets of District 9 as he was denied access to the Nest, Roland was given a task by Olivier only for the Pianist to manifest right on spot. Zwei Association called Argalia to suppress the monstrosity, but Roland went in first and claimed the kill. However, it was too late -- Angelica was already dead and her corpse was absorbed into the Pianist's piano.
After this incident, Roland lost it completely and vowed to make whoever caused the mishap that killed his wife from nowhere pay dearly. He began compiling a list of suspects and went door to door killing them or their loved ones, with Eileen's father and Jae-heon's son being killed in his wrath. During his rampage, he also virtually decimated the Middle's Southern branch (with Tanya implied to survive the attack), followed by an attack against the Rumanos Cartel. He then began to aimlessly raze Fixer offices, Syndicates or even civilians for the sake of, and Astolfo has to arrive and convince him to stop. Following this incident, Roland lost all of his standing and was sent to the Library by Iori.

Meanwhile, after Roland left, Argalia went to the scene and saw Angelica's corpse, driving him insane and making him capable of hearing the voice of the distortions. He then started to recruit many of Roland's victims and founded the The Reverberation Ensemble with them. Angelica's corpse was also dug up and made a puppet by Jae-heon for the sake of taunting Roland during the Ensemble's initial confrontation against the Library.

entries.name: The Vermilion Cross
entries.content:
The Vermilion Cross was a Color Fixer. He was killed along with the Hana Association's Southern Branch 1, only to be revived by the Blood-red Night, used as a minion during her Reception.

His body is a bleeding mess, with twisted arms holding up a massive, super-heated cross on his back. He has long black hair with a single red eye shining through, and his skin is covered in burn marks.

Not much is known about the Vermilion Cross, aside from his high status as a Color Fixer. In Dong-hwan's page story, it's noted that when he was alive, he was under the employment of the Hana Association to eliminate the Blue Reverberation and his Ensemble. However, he fails to do so and dies at their hands. Given his rank in the City and strength as a fixer, his body is taken and revived by Elena, which is then put to use in her Reception as a servant made to kill.

The Vermilion Cross does not drop a page of his own, and therefore has no Page Story. However, insight is given into his background in Dong-hwan's Page Story, given he was a friend.

"Hana Association seems to have taken an interest in the Library and the Blue Reverberation—the two entities at the center of all the problems that have been happening in L Corp’s Nest lately—now that they’ve marked their presence in the City’s sky as Stars. I asked a Color who happens to be a friend of mine about it… and he said the Association’s going to recruit him to hunt down the Blue Reverberation and his cohorts soon. They’ve been making quite a scene in L Corp’s Nest… In particular, the lives of many Syndicates, Fixers, and residents close to the Library were lost to their hands, so the Association couldn’t just sit and watch anymore. They’ve apparently set up a camp at the door of the Library, though no one knows what they’re waiting for. A couple other things I heard are that all sorts of sounds and noises are coming from that camp… and that a large number of firearms belonging to the Thumb were abandoned on the ground. Maybe they launched an assault on the Syndicate while it was still struggling to recover from the loss of the Underboss and his Capos. The ensemble’s not like most Syndicates just trying to make money off the turf of the wingless Nest, that’s for sure… But we still don’t know what their goals really are, and I can’t shake this bad feeling.

Anyways, since I was asked to pay a visit to the Library… It’ll be worth investigating the case some more after I get this job done."

entries.name: Thelma
entries.content:
Thelma is the general manager of the Shi Association Southern Branch.

Thelma first appears after you unlock Urban Plague, where it’s disclosed that he was risen to the head of the southern branch of the Shi Association with the help of Argalia. Attempting to return the favor, Thelma offers to do whatever tasks Argalia has for him, one of which is entering the Library. His team was Section 2 of the Shi Association, which would explains the sudden surfeit of missions handed towards them shown in the cutscene before the Reception of Shi Association.

Thelma next "appears" in the Backstreets, gagged and blindfolded. Argalia has requested the Smiling Faces to flake some meat off Thelma. Wang asks how many slices, and Argalia settles on ten thousand. They then remove Thelma’s gag. He then tells Thelma to not give him that look, as he failed to fulfill a promise. As Argalia tells him, since this happens during the Night in the Backstreets, no one will dare to investigate what happened to Thelma, and it will be as if he simply disappeared from the world. Thelma is then re-gagged and left to suffer a torturous death at the hands of the Smiling Faces, to be cut into ten thousand thin flakes and cannibalized alive by them.

entries.name: Tomerry
entries.content:
Tomerry is the amalgamation of various individuals created after Elena and Jae-heon stitched together Tommy and Merry, later becoming the "hero" of Love Town.

They appear to be a hideous, viscous meat in a vaguely humanoid shape, albeit uneven and disjointed with limbs of various sizes, eyes, and mouths, along with Tommy and Merry's original heads. They wear an apron-like clothing with the words "LOVE ♥ TOWN" on it.

When the head of Tommy is destroyed, a giant claw-like arm protrudes from the flesh lump on the back of their body. The Merry part of Tomerry can be seen visually distressed from the death of Tommy, and the middle left arms hand is destroyed.

Tomerry has the mind and personality of a child, speaking simply and showing inquisitiveness for the greater 'world' outside the train. They refer to Elena and Jae-heon as "mommy" and "daddy", likely conditioned to do so to uphold absolute obedience and dependency on them. Tomerry's mind has degraded to the point they no longer understand concepts such as Fixers and the Library, people and places that are integral to the City and how it runs. They also appear to be quite frightful of Elena when they don't understand what she's asking of them, fearing punishment and scolding, likely suggesting that Elena has hurt Tomerry before in order to control them. Despite their size and potential for destruction, they seek the approval of their 'parents' and go to the Library unquestioningly.

They appear as a result of Tommy and Merry's deal with Elena and Jae-heon to stay together, becoming a giant creature that would become Love Town's "hero". After at least 724,284 days in the Warp Train (1984.3 years), Tommy and Merry's original selves have long since faded, being replaced with a loyal and childish personality. After being told to enter the Library by their "mother" Elena with several other Love Town residents, Angela would greet the being, asking if they could remember anything about their previous lives as Tommy and Merry. When it answers in confusion, Angela drops the topic, seeing it as proof that the people they once were are gone. During the reception, the "Tommy" head gets destroyed halfway through, prompting the "Merry" component to go berserk and as it gets booked, it can be heard begging to be reunited with Tommy, implying that their previous lives were still in the monster, just smothered underneath a mountain of time.

entries.name: Tommy
entries.content:
Tommy is an ordinary city citizen who took a Warp Train to go on vacation with their lover, Merry.

Tommy is a man with blue, messy hair and blue eyes. He wears a light gray shirt, covered by a gray sweater, along with gray pants and gray shoes.

Tommy is an anxious but caring individual. He loves Merry deeply, but often relies on her to care for him.

Tommy is hesitant to be merged with Merry, but chooses to in the end.

entries.name: Valentin
entries.content:
Valentin is a Fixer of Section 2 of the Shi Association's Southern Branch.

Valentin wears the Shi Association uniform consisting of a black jacket secured to his left side with red stripes around the hem of his clothes. His jacket also features an unsecured belt, various buttons, and an insignia on his should like Yujin's. He wields a red katana and saya, which he uses in battle. He has short black hair, and his right eye is obscured with bandages. He also has several small scratches on his face, likely from the constant combat he had to endure under the Shi. As with the other assassins, Valentin wears black gloves.

Valentin is a loyal and rather 'fresh' member of the Shi Association. He points out and actively detests the injustices thrown at Yujin and his team, calling out the injustices Thelma and the Blue Reverberation have placed on the Shi, as well as noting how its reputation and morals have degraded over time. Although he is slightly naïve to the reality of overtaking an association like the Shi, he understands that resources are strained and shows concern for South Section 2. He also has great admiration and respect for his superior Yujin, who has sacrificed a lot for her team and ambition, to which Valentin supports by continuing to fight at her side, despite knowing that victory will lead to endless fights, and failure will result in death.

After Yujin's briefing of the City's current political climate involving the Blue Reverberation and Thelma's abandonment of Shi South Section 2, he follows the team into the Library in order to obtain the book of the Musicians of Bremen in order to uncover what Argalia is planning, and why he dropped his duties to pursue them.

entries.name: Walter
entries.content:
Walter is the Director of Section 6 of the Zwei Association's Southern Branch. 

Walter has short black hair along with a goatee. He wears a yellowish collared shirt with a black tie under a black coat and pants, along with black gloves and shoes. Over all this, he wears a marine blue Zwei overcoat. In combat, he wields a large black Zwei sword.

Walter maintains a stoic attitude in his work, acting in his supposed role as a "shield" of the Zwei Association. He seemingly espouses the values of the Zwei, but is also willing to resort to backhanded means like collaborating with the Stray Dogs to advance his mission. According to Salvador, Walter also has a habit of asking rhetorical questions, and tries to act clever while his actual thoughts are merely "one-dimensional." Salvador goes as far as implying that Walter is nearly talentless, only barely holding on to his position due to either his social skills or just pure luck.

Walter has been a member of the Zwei Association for many years, and was a colleague of Salvador before the latter left the Zwei. Despite reaching a relatively high position as the Director of South Section 6, he is still attempting to climb higher, and seeks to complete only whatever missions his Section is officially given as quickly as possible to maximize his chances. As a result, he is willing to resort to shortcuts and relatively unscrupulous means, such as brokering deals with Syndicates and Backstreets criminals. Currently, this mission is to gather information on the Distortion Phenomenon; as such, Walter made a deal with the Stray Dogs for information on the Distortion in exchange for giving them a floor plan of Lobotomy Corporation's Nest. Walter is also known to avoid field work himself and instead have his subordinates deal with it, which makes it all the more unprecedented when he chooses to personally enter the Library.

In the introduction of Urban Myth, Walter is heard asking for updates on the Distortion Phenomenon from his subordinate Isadora. She replies that Zwei Section 1 and the Hana Association have listed the Laundry of Dreams, Yesterday's Promise, and The Church of Gears as potential suspects. After she adds that the Library, only an Urban Myth at the time, is also being considered as a suspect, Walter scoffs at his superiors' seeming cluelessness and use of "random guesses."

In Zwei Association Episode III, Walter is seen meeting with Isadora, who reports on the failure of Julia and San to return from their expedition into the Library. She then requests to send more manpower to the Library, insisting that she believes it is connected to the Distortion Phenomenon. Walter refuses on the grounds that Isadora is merely acting out of a desire for revenge, though he secretly also simply sees it as a distraction from Section 6's mission. This changes after he finds an Invitation to the Library in his desk, on which the Book of the Distortion is offered. Walter then immediately reverses course and takes Isadora and several other Zwei Fixers to the Library, intending to capitalize on the opportunity to get a lead on his Section's mission, advance his own career, and also satisfy Isadora's request all together. When Angela greets them, he replies in a seemingly amicable way but then goads her over her false human appearance and her true robotic form.

However, Walter falls during the Reception (along with Isadora and several other Zwei Fixers) and is turned into the Book of Walter. As a result of his death, he is unable to fulfill his end of his deal with the Stray Dogs. The Syndicate views this as a betrayal and targets Section 6, massacring many of its remaining Fixers. They then use an Invitation to enter the Library, intending to use the Book of Walter to gain the information they need.

entries.name: Wang
entries.content: Wang is a member of the Smiling Faces

entries.name: Xiao
entries.content:
Xiao is the Director of the Southern Branch of Liu Association Section 1, she's also known as the Lady of Iron, due to her constantly stalwart and professional attitude. Following the entirety of the Association's Southern Branch being hired by V Corp in order to neutralize and investigate The Crying Children incident, Xiao and her subordinates find themselves forced to fight The Library in order to investigate the cause of the Distortion.

Xiao has pale skin, red eyes and long black spiky hair partially tied up as a small high bun with a golden circular Chinese barrette. She wears a white dress shirt with a red tie clasped with a golden tie clip under a black single breasted lapel suit with two golden buttons and the imprint of a golden dragon on the left side. Over her suit and shoulders, she wears a long red coat golden details on the extremities, two drawstring of the same color, and white fur on the bottom, on the sleeves, and on the collar. Xiao on her lower half wears black suit pants and same colored shoes. With her she also has black gloves with a golden imprint on it. She carries a guan dao and a longsword.

After partially manifesting her E.G.O, Xiao acquired dark scales on her face and two black dragon horns on the left side of her head. She also manifested scale like patterns over parts of her body and a red and golden combat armor which is fragmented and has the same golden dragon of her suit. She now carries with a her a dao instead of the guan dao and longsword she previously had.

When totally manifesting her E.G.O, Xiao wears her red long coat as a cape and a full suit of chinese inspired red and golden armour with bows made of red rope, claws and a helmet with holes for her four black dragon horns. Xiao has also manifested a pair of wings and long sash made of fire around her. In this form, Xiao has an enormous guan dao with a long red handle and a golden blade with a dragon's head on it.

Xiao first comes off as a very cold and iron-willed person, both in combat and in everyday life, shapen by combat and past-experiences and uses traditions and culture of ancient Chinese history in her appearance and combat style, but after the death of Lowell, it is revealed she has a soft spot for love, only revealed when it is too late.

"I was in no way a soft person, though I don’t view myself as particularly tough or rugged, either. A straight and honest person. Accusations would be brought against me for being unmoved by the death of any person however close they may have been in life, a point not everyone would see as criticism. How could a person be so cold and heartless, even if the basic bearing of a Fixer is to look after oneself first and foremost? At first, I spent much time thinking over it, and asked myself many questions. Xiao as a person valued the lives of her colleagues, although her position forced her to keep her farewell to deceased teammates short, since carrying out her duty and emerging victorious came first. Shedding fewer drops of tears than the number of fallen was all the tribute I could pay. Bawling my eyes out would have stirred uneasiness in my colleagues. In the early days, the responsibility sometimes felt too heavy and burdensome."

"I had never once thought that my method was incorrect; I believed it to be the best method for myself, and I deemed that problems couldn’t be solved any other way. Most Fixers will probably think in the same way. Therefore, I could not understand the manners of Lowell, the newly appointed Section 2 Director at the time. A person who tries to look after everyone, and doesn’t hide his grief-stricken face when a coworker passes away. It seemed clear as crystal that his tenderness would one day lead his team to death, yet he was faring better than I thought. A polar opposite to me. The ways I wanted to pursue but gave up because I was faced with my limitations. It might have upset me for a moment. A principle I could not follow, for I was not allowed to openly express sadness over the death of the few in order to protect the many; and my obligation to seize any chance of victory compelled me to march forward if there was something to count on. My capability wasn’t vast enough to embrace every member of the team. Was my choice wrong? What did he have that I did not? Looking back, I don’t think what I felt was envy or jealousy. The indignation certainly was not a toxic emotion. I’m sure each of us had different specialties."

"It is said that people intersect with one another in some manner. I don’t think the process to be natural at all; I was not a believer of fateful meetings. After all, two parallel roads could never cross. A relationship begins with a desire to know. Simple curiosity. To know more about a person, or to go further and see what they are seeing together. People open up new roads to merge into the roads of others for various reasons."

"I thought I would never care about him since he was so different from me, but my expectations weren’t quite right. I wanted to learn more about him, and I wanted to know what this emotion I felt was. And I thought I could perhaps become a better person if I saw what he was seeing together. If there’s one thing I realized, it’s that relationships between people always start from such small curiosity."

"Taking in what I have said so far, you would think that this is such a peculiar and untruthful love. You might think it’s fussy. I cannot give out a clear answer, for I can’t dare define what love is. What could I say or add about an emotion I felt for the first time, one that I am still struggling to figure out? Furthermore, every person carries a different form of love. There will undoubtedly be some people who don’t place much importance on that emotion. You might even think that such emotion is absolutely useless in this City. Even if I were to define my love, this wouldn’t come across as a sweet story if you cannot understand it."

"However, I can be certain that my sentiment towards Lowell was sincere. The so-called curiosity and sympathy… They bring about attention, admiration, and a little bit of obsession. I learned soon enough that this isn’t much different from what people call “love”. It may not have been something out of a fairy tale or a drama, but we still cherished each other in our little relationship. Perhaps I had been under the impression that love is a concept that is utterly distant from me. The love that I came into was cramped, yet big… and it felt burdensome at times."

"You said I am strong, but the truth is that I was weak and fainthearted until the very last time I faced you. I have only grown so ironclad after I lost you. Why did I miss everything while you were still by my side? Why do I spend the whole night longing for you and regretting only after you have parted from me? I do have one regret regarding you: that I could not trust my feelings for you. That I was too afraid to tell you that you’re my everything the night before you left me."

"Moments of loneliness will come as I live. It won’t be a thirsty longing for love, however. It is when I look to my side, yet there is no one next to me; when I am worn out from running somewhere; when I feel that my heart grows heavy rather than painful. Trying new things might let me forget it for a moment, but the memories will still follow me for life. When I feel such things, I can go back to familiarity. A familiar place, a familiar mind, a familiar person. And I plan to reunite with you soon. I want to tell you that I no longer have shame for the path I’ve chosen, and that I have finally freed myself from the guilt."

entries.name: Yan
entries.content:
Yan Vismok is a Messenger of The Index, having only begun to work as one less than a month ago by the time of his first appearance. He first appears in the pre-battle dialog for The Carnival.

Ultimately, Yan turns into a Distortion known as 얀샋ㄷ요무 (cipher for Distorted Yan). This originated from his feelings of powerlessness after having seen the truth of the Prescripts, and even after conspiring directly against them by making forgeries of Prescripts, new ones were created from his own, as if they were intended to be created after all. With this, Yan realizes that his own will and the City's are the one and the same, and thus, he has no will of his own. This causes him to blindly turn to the Prescripts for guidance, becoming the one thing he despised the most.

Yan is a light-skinned young man sporting white hair with black streaks tied into a long side ponytail. Much like other notable members of the Index, he dons a white cloak fitted with gold ornaments over a black suit. As a Messenger, Yan was bestowed a personalized greatsword adorned with golden chains and a lock.

After distorting, Yan becomes a towering, mannequin-like creature. It bears the white color and gold accents of the Index, along with black ink stains. His skull is broken where his face would be, revealing a gold padlock on its place, and has a similar ponytail made of a cloth tied to the side. On his chest his robe is torn, revealing what seems to be a loom of glowing blue strings, similar to the ones where the Prescripts are created. Instead of limbs, he had a pair of gold chains that connect a pair of gigantic claws drenched in ink, having the same padlock and chains that his greatsword had. Whenever he speaks, his voice is drowned out by the sounds of typewriter keys.

Despite being a Messenger of the Index, Yan differs noticeably from his associates, being much more skeptical and choosing to view the Prescripts as a mere ordinance with no higher significance to it instead of revering them. He's largely somber and ceremonious, but he also expresses discomfort at the lengths some citizens have to go in order to carry out their Prescripts as well as sympathizing with their woes. He cares for others, including his enemies, as he pleads with The Thumb not to assault the Library, as that would severely weaken their forces on Nest L, even if that'd bring him nearly to death.

It's later revealed that Yan has experiences carrying out abhorrent acts under the guidance of Prescripts before becoming a Messenger, causing him to hate it. He wants to show his free will by forging Prescripts for others instead of letting them follow the Prescripts' will.

After falling into despair and distorting, Yan becomes a mindless drone, having been shown that his own will simply ended up being assimilated into the will of the City, and thus only attempts to find purpose and direction in the Prescripts by following them.

During his time as a follower of the Index, Yan's faith in the Prescripts was put into question as he carried out dreadful orders, some of which resulted in the deaths of his friends and family, until one day he was bestowed the rank of Messenger. Feeling resentful, Yan took to fabricating Prescripts as an expression of free will.

In The Carnival's episode, Yan is seen delivering a Prescript to the trio of tailors which turns out to be an invitation to the Library. While they initially show resistance in virtue of the invitation not being an official Prescript, Yan eventually convinces them with threatening words regarding what could happen were they to not carry out a Prescript. As he is leaving, Yan runs into three of the Kurokumo Clan members, who are quick to point out the strange nature of his behavior right before a Finger Bow-Bell is about to start.

Yan is later seen during the Index Proselytes segment, delivering Prescripts to a multitude of citizens. During one of the encounters, he assists a girl with carrying out the order of sneaking needles into a friend's birthday cake by pointing out that warning her friend about the trap does not go against the Prescript. Yan also attempts to comfort an old man faced with one of the more gruesome orders, and is seemingly pained at a young man's enthusiastic praising of the Index's ways due to receiving a rather easy Prescript, with the Messenger stating that "nothing is truly free in this city." He eventually meets up with the Index Proxies to deliver more orders, including one of his fabricated Prescripts demanding the elimination of the Thumb.

During The Thumb's second episode, Yan intrudes in a meeting of Kalo and his capos. He attempts to reason with the rival group about how the decision to go to the Library may put the Thumb in a disadvantageous position in the midst of the raging battle between their syndicates in L Corp's nest. Yan's warning is taken as an insult, and the Messenger is promptly attacked by the Thumb's members who leave him to a state of near-death, his eyes and jaw destroyed. Yan is later found and patched up by his fellow Index members.

Once the Index Proxies finish carrying out the order to dismember and impale all Thumb personnel in L Corp's nest, Yan is ready to deliver another fabricated Prescript ordering them to head to the Library. Much to the Messenger's surprise, Proxy Esther seems to already know about it, and reveals that the Prescripts told them to obey his Prescripts, implying that they're fake. At this point, Yan laments his past experiences with the Prescripts, having come to the realization that his rebellious acts ultimately amounted to nothing. After a brief exchange with Proxy Esther, Yan is ordered to head to an unknown place by the Prescript.

Yan follows the directions given by his Prescript, finding a staircase that goes deep below the City, hiding a massive vault containing a set of machines, all connected to a massive loom with a pendulum over it. There, he meets an outstandingly cheery woman wearing Index robes, who welcomes him as if she had been expecting him all along. When Yan asks who she is, she simply answers that she's a Weaver, and that it's nice to have a guest after spending so much time alone. Yan is shocked that the woman refers to herself with a title that he's never heard before and has a suspicious amount of knowledge about his Prescripts, who explains that nobody could ever find this place without the Prescripts help, and adds that they only invite people they consider exceptional, congratulating Yan.
When Yan asks if this place has anything to do with the Prescripts, the woman happily explains it's "where Prescripts are born". She is amused seeing how Yan is confused by her choice of words, and after properly introducing herself as Moirai, and lamenting how she doesn't have any tea to offer, let alone warm water, she tries to go into more detail on the creation of the Prescripts, but Yan tries to stop her to have his turn to talk, already overwhelmed by Moirai's chattiness. He introduces himself by his first name and last name, and explains that he became a Messenger about less than a month ago, adding that he felt guilty by delivering Prescripts containing gruesome and absurd orders. Moirai simply agrees that the Prescripts can be cruel and knotty at times, giving orders that sometimes end with their recipients killed. Yan expresses anger at her, believing she's the one who wrote all those Prescripts. Moirai explain that she simply manages the machinery in the vault, stopping for a moment and asking Yan if he feels a small tremor on his feet. When he dismisses it as something trivial, Moirai moves on to explain the "birth" of a Prescript:

The pendulum swings to the rhythm of the tremor she calls "the heartbeat of the City", making trails of ink over the strings on the massive loom. Yan again dismisses them as being nonsensical, but Moirai calls it the language of the City, something incomprehensible to mere humans like them. Those threads then move to one of the 57 spinning wheels in the vault, where they are woven into cloth and made into Prescripts that can be read by them. She hands one of them to Yan, where it orders a man to follow somebody waving their hand seven times. Yan is shocked, remembering he forged a Prescript to order the latter to wave, but Moirai quickly moves on to stamping that Prescript and sending it, sending it via pneumatic pipes to another Messenger.

After seeing the creation of a Prescript, Yan only has more questions and asks who even created the machinery in the first place. Moirai shrugs, excusing herself by having been sent by a Prescript as well, only finding her predecessor who in turn left after being issued a Prescript. Yan is outraged, saying at Moirai if she had ever questioned the Prescripts, having been ordered to kill countless times by seemingly randomly generated words on a piece of cloth, further adding that she could at least tampered with them to not make them as cruel or senseless. Moirai excuses herself that she was only ordered to make and send Prescripts, and if she disobeyed that order, they would kill her. Yan says that she's the one creating and sending them out in the first place, but Moirai holds on to the possibility of another Weaver.

Yan starts to reason with himself, saying somebody in particular must be behind the creation of the contents of the Prescripts, but Moirai interjects that'd be the City itself. The pendulum swings to the vibrations of the City above: footsteps of pedestrians; quakes from construction sites, impacts by somebody falling over, echoes of screams, every little movement of the City's denizens, even the sound of the two talking right next to it. She comments that the will of its citizens are ultimately part of the will of the City itself, and the Index is simply another representation of it. Yan wonders why would the Prescripts would be so cruel if they came from the inhabitants of the City, with Moirai responding that'd be because the people are cruel as well, after all, the City was made by its citizens, and their nature would naturally be reflected in their creation. Yan is confused at what she just said, why would the citizens create the City and in turn be shaped by it? Moirai dismisses his concerns, believing that the point of it is that the City cannot be separate from its inhabitants. This further enrages Yan, seeing how Moirai dismisses those heinous acts he creates and sends while she peacefully weaves cloth. In turn, Moirai shrugs: that was all she was ordered to do, expressing that's out of her concern as a Weaver.

Moirai moves on to tell Yan about being born out of the citizens' wants; to walk a path given to them, afraid of the consequences and the responsibility of their own actions, knowing they'd only fail if they follow their own will, and they'd rather rely on something else and expect things from it. Moirai says people without purpose yearning for something to open up a way for them. She compares it to the way people long ago created gods; they simply didn't exist because of a single person, it's something that can't be made up or oppressed, people had a need for something greater than them to follow. Moirai further adds that this isn't something Yan can blame somebody for; this is plainly something the City's inhabitants wanted, their fear of failure and their wishes of security culminating in the creation of a god.

Yan falls into despair, realizing people, and even himself weren't doing cruel acts simply because the Prescripts ordered to. In the end, that was their own volition as residents of the City. They themselves were cruel and merciless, and that nature in turn made them desperately wish for something safe and sacred, no matter if those wishes were well intentioned or ambitions of power, the Prescripts is what resulted from them. No matter whatever he did, he was just another individual, one that wouldn't stand a chance against the collective wishes of the people. Forging Prescripts and sending the Proxies to wage war against the Thumb and die in the Library could all be traced to the will of the City, even if it was Yan's own. After all, Yan was just another part of the City. Giving in completely to this feeling of helplessness, Yan distorts into 얀샋ㄷ요무 and asks Moirai for the City's next order, where he shortly receive another Prescript telling him to go to the Library.

entries.name: Yang
entries.content:
Yang is a henchman of the Kurokumo Clan.

Yang wears an open, partially-buttoned with sleeves rolled up to his elbows, exposing Irezumi-style tattoos of similar style to Sayo and Gin. He wears plain black pants and shoes, fashioned with a studded belt and brown wristband on his left hand. He has black hair tied back into a ponytail, and can often be seen with an unlit cigarillo in his mouth. His weapon of choice is a katana.

Yang is a loyal subordinate to Sayo in the Kurokumo Clan. He has little sympathy for nest-dwellers, readily carrying out orders of mutilation without hesitation, and even making light of the situation by responding, "Yes, dame~" when given the order. He's rather sadistic in how he carries out 'punishments', though his methods hardly differ from the likes of Sayo or Gin who are equally unmerciful.

Yang, along with the other members of the Kurokumo clan are seen claiming debts from a protection racket in an unspecified Nest, doling out 'punishment' to residents when they fail to pay the Kurokumo Clan to ward off the violent consequence of non-payment.

During this, Sayo and her team are in charge of delivering Nuovo Fabric to the Thumb, which is then intercepted by the L'Heure du Loup, who beats the Kurokumo Clan in a fight, leaving Yang, Gin and Sayo to use an invitation to the library or face certain death.

Eventually, Yang along the rest of the Kurokumo Clan die in the Reception. Dropping the Book of Yang which may contain their Key Page.

entries.name: Yujin
entries.content:
Yujin is the Director of Section 2 of the Shi Association's Southern Branch.

Yujin is a mature woman that wears the Shi Association's uniform, that consists of a long, red and black coat, black trousers, steel embellished boots, and wields a katana. Her jacket has various buttons, an untied belt, and an insignia on her shoulder likely representing her rank. She has short black hair, black eyes, and a large, thin scar spanning from her chin to the top of her face, as well as a small scratch on the left side of her face and nose. She also wears black gloves, a necessity for an assassin.

Yujin is a methodical and ambitious woman who fights in the face of adversity. She has high tolerance for stress and fighting, as evidenced by her elimination of several Urban Nightmare-class within the span of 10 days. She appears to be unhappy with the current Shi Association's leadership and seeks to complete her work and overthrow the Shi over time for her and her teammates' freedom. She is also described as self-sacrificing, showing concern for her subordinates as well as an firm resolve in achieving her goals by striking at the opportune moment.

After the Blue Reverberation abandons his requests, the Shi Association is bombarded with a mass of Urban Nightmare-class requests that Yujin and her crew are left to deal with. For 10 days, Shi South Section 2 deals with the Naraku Clan patriarch, destruction of the Fragment from beyond, demolishing the Thin Beef Skirt Factory, and eliminating The Steel Comrades command. These cases were dealt with back-to-back with no stop, when typically the Shi only processes one of these Urban Nightmare requests a week. As a result, Shi South Section 2 is in no condition to fight, especially Yujin, who took the brunt of the combat to hold her position as leader, and protect Valentin and Tenma from grievous harm. Yujin's orders from the Shi are to infiltrate the Library, though she also has her own agenda of obtaining the books of the Musicians of Bremen, in order to discover what the Blue Reverberation is doing, and take control over the situation.

entries.name: Yun
entries.content:
Yun is the Operator of the small Yun’s Office.

Yun has short blonde hair slightly covering his right eye, light skin, brown eyes and a brown cigarette in his mouth. He wears a gray trench coat with two pockets on each side and shirt with a brownish gray tie with gingham pattern, on his right hand a black glove and on the left one a black ring on the ring finger. On his lower half, Yun wears black trousers, a gray belt, and black shoes. In combat, Yun doesn't use any weapons other than his own two fists.

Yun is a mostly cold-hearted and cynical man, but secretly still has some sympathy for his Office's workers, especially Finn, whom Yun mostly treats as a brat and even knowingly sends to his death. Despite this, he still ends up showing a limited amount of grief and regret upon finding out about his demise.

Yun has been the Operator of Yun' Yun’s Office for an unspecified amount of time since its creation.

In his past, he opened Yun' Yun’s Office and employed various low-tier Fixers such as Eri, Finn, and other Grade 9 Fixers. Eventually, the Office started facing financial difficulties due to the fact most requests it acquired were low-paying and were even considered "garbage" by some of its own Fixers.

In the second Episode of Yun' Yun’s Office, Finn comes to Yun informing him that the two Fixers that accompanied him haven't returned from the Library after signing its Invitation in the first Episode, claiming that something must have happened to them. Yun tells him that even if they had just disappeared or run off they are still breaching the contract and will be facing expulsion of his Office. After hearing this, Finn states he has a bad feeling about the situation, but Yun shuts him down, sarcastically saying that Finn's "great" Grade 9 Fixer instincts were being wasted on his humble Office. The Operator then states that if he can't find him any proof of the existence of such Invitation, they would not look into it. Finn then points out the mysterious envelope on his desk. Caught by surprise, Yun questions the young Fixer if such a thing was his doing, and after denying it, Finn is asked to leave the room for a moment. After Finn leaves, Yun makes a call to an unknown individual, asking for them to lend him money, so he could contract people to send to the Library now that he has an Invitation. The person in the other side of the line tells Yun to send someone there again to confirm it before lending any sort of monetary support, with some concern and slight disapproval, Yun sends Finn all alone to the Library with the Invitation on his desk.

Upon Finn dying in the Library during the Episode 2 of Yun' Yun’s Office, Eri is contacted by Yun to join him on a visit to the Library along with the rest of his Office. When talking to her, he first mentions that Finn didn't survive his reception, but states that it was unsurprising and he was bound to die sooner or later. Eri comments that she liked Finn's "affable and cutesy attitude" but agrees with the Office's operator. Yun then congratulates Eri on her promotion to a Grade 8 Fixer, she uses that moment to tell Yun that if he does not provide her with a good salary she might move away to another Office, reminding him of Yun’s Office's issue paying taxes and rent. The operator explains that he thinks the Library will be the case that will save his Office and that they will go there since he received another Invitation. Yun, Eri and the remaining Fixers sign the Invitation and are transported to the Library. Right upon entering they are greeted by Angela. Yun asks her if she might have seen Finn, and she informs him that Finn became a book due to the fact he perished during his reception on Episode 2. Upon hearing what was the novice Fixer's fate, Yun briefly acts sentimental about what happened to Finn, until the Director of the Library questions his hypocrisiy, stating that he was the one that set him up to fail even knowing he would certainly die. Yun cuts the conversation short by saying that all get exploited and abandoned at some point in their lives, and Angela lets the Fixers enter the Library.

Eventually, Yun dies in the Reception along with the whole Yun’s Office. Dropping the Yun' Book of Yun which contains his Key Page.

entries.name: Yuna
entries.content:
Yuna was a grade 4 Fixer of the Dawn Office.

Yuna has teal hair, and green eyes. Her arms appear to be replaced by a pair of prosthetic ones. She wears a gray trench coat with rolled-up sleeves, a grey blazer and matching skirt, a white dress shirt, black leggings, and brown shoes. Her weapon is a cello case created by Stigma Workshop, which contains a series of bladed, mechanical appendages which strikes at her opponents for her.

entries.name: Zena
entries.content:
Zena is an Arbiter of the Head.

Zena has black chin-length hair with short bangs, equally black eyes, and white skin. She wears a black button up shirt dress with same colored fur and golden details at the bottom, over it Zena has a hoodless black cape with the Head's honeycomb pattern to the right side and same dark fur and golden details at the bottom, but this time as well at the top of it. Zena's legs are covered by black fabric, presumably socks, and she also wears black boots with no laces but with golden liners and one black bow on each shoe. Zena on her hands has 5 golden rings on each finger of each hand.

Zena, as an Arbiter of the Head, is privy to most of the secrets of the Head. As a direct consequence, she is able to answer most of Angela's questions about their intent. While she does this, she seems overconfident and uses much verbosity, even during the heat of battle. This tendency to deliver flowery speeches can often leave an opening, as Binah later remarks.

Zena, along with Luda, a Beholder of the Eye, and Baral, an Executioner of the Claw, arrives as the final uninvited guests. They are tasked with a primary objectives of relocating Nest L and the Library to the Outskirts, and the extermination of Angela as she is in violation of the AI Ethics Amendments Code. As side a objective, they are also tasked with retrieving Binah for an unknown purpose.

entries.name: Zulu
entries.content:
Zulu is a member of the Stray Dogs.

Zulu is a bald, large, muscular man with brown eyes, dark skin, a scar near his left eyebrow, and a large amount of strength-augmenting tattoos on his arms and chest. He wears a form-fitting black tank top, black camo-patterned cargo pants with a black belt, black boots, brown gloves, and a black bandana covering his mouth. He fights bare-handed.

Zulu is a relatively calm but also cynical individual who dislikes unnecessary brutality and considers consequences before taking action.

Zulu has been with the Stray Dogs for an unknown amount of time. He, Gyeong-mi, and Dino recently made a deal with Walter, director of the Zwei Association's South Section 6, to collect information on the Distortion Phenomenon in exchange for a floor plan of the former L Corp's Nest in order to complete a job for the Thumb.

After Dino warns the group to leave to avoid the Sweepers, Zulu complains about Walter's seeming betrayal of their deal and the heavy losses the Stray Dogs suffered to the Church of Gears while trying to fulfill their end of the deal, also describing Eileen as an "inhuman freak." Meanwhile, he also notes that Walter would not have broken such a promise without a good reason, and that it would not make sense for him to have died so suddenly.

Zulu is discouraged after witnessing Gyeong-mi smash the Zwei Fixers' corpses into a pulp out of blind rage and warns that such violence could cause them to be pursued by higher Zwei Sections in retaliation. After seeing Gyeong-mi take an Invitation which lists the Book of Walter on it, he becomes annoyed that Gyeong-mi still resorted to such brutality despite already knowing why Walter had failed them.

After entering the Library, Zulu states that they will most likely finish their Reception just in time to return before the night falls. Ultimately, he and the other Stray Dogs are defeated during the Reception, and he is turned into the Book of Zulu.

entries.name: Aeng-du
entries.content:
Aeng-du is a member of the Blade Lineage.

Aeng-du wears a battle-worn and bloodstained Salsu outfit, common to the Sinners' Blade Lineage Salsu identities - comprised of a black Dopo robe with white and red accents. Her long hair is neatly tied with a red hairband and adorned with two hair beads in red and white, mirroring the seemingly traditional colors associated with the Blade Lineage.

Aeng-du is a very loyal and determined person, willing to push herself through even extreme injuries for the sake of Bamboo-hatted Kim, the Blade Lineage's mentor. She has a lot of pride in being a member of the Blade Lineage and her relationship to both the Syndicate and its leader is a core part of her identity. When her understanding of her mentor is challenged, it shakes her and leaves her vulnerable to the Monolith's influences. As seen with her conversation with Yi Sang about their shared home District, she shares a kinship with others who have been forced to leave S Corp. behind.

Aeng-du was a resident of District 19 and member of the Blade Lineage, attempting to fight against the corruption found in the district. Eventually, they would be forced to leave for their safety, and the mentor of the Blade Lineage, Bamboo-hatted Kim, would lead them in search of a new home. While attempting to find territory to call their own, they came into conflict with the Kurokumo Clan and Bamboo-hatted Kim decided to accept an invitation from the Library to escape the other Syndicate. At the Library, Aeng-du and the other Blade Lineage members would be defeated and turned into books.

Shortly before the events of Intervallo III, the Syndicate returned from their book forms and found themselves in the Backstreets of District 20, although not all would awaken in the same place. Aeng-du and a group of her fellow Blade Lineage members were separated from their mentor and, in their search for him, would run into the Kurokumo Clan and were forced to fight them. Despite their best attempts, the Blade Lineage was outnumbered and unprepared, leading to their near total defeat. Luckily for Aeng-du, the Sinners get involved with the fight while searching for information and, upon seeing her severely wounded state, Don Quixote requests that they fight to save the woman. Dante has a gut feeling that Aeng-du has the information they seek, so they bring her back to Mephistopheles after defeating the Kurokumo Clan members.

On the bus, Yi Sang treats Aeng-du's wounds and calms her down when she assumes the Sinners are a threat to her. The two bond over both being from District 19 and she explains to him the story of the Blade Lineage and how she came to be here. Recalling those memories reminds her of her of how Bamboo-hatted Kim is still missing and she urges the Sinners to make their way to the Yong-jin Building to help find her mentor. It turns out that Dante's assumption that she would be related to their mission was correct, and the group makes their way to the building where they fight their way upwards past groups of Kurokumo Clan members. At the top floor, they run into Jun, a Captain of the Kurokumo Clan, and Aeng-du draws her blade against him. Unfortunately, due to her extremely injured state from the earlier battles, she collapses to the ground without landing a hit on him. The Sinners defeat Jun in battle, and Aeng-du recovers enough in the meantime to tie him up and interrogate him.

In this conversation with Jun, Aeng-du learns what happened when Bamboo-hatted Kim awoke from being a book. Jun explains that after witnessing the death of many of the Blade Lineage members that had appeared alongside him, the man began to cut down ally and foe alike. In order to protect his men, Jun decided to lock Bamboo-hatted Kim in the room and wait for The Thumb to arrive for the object the Kurokumo Clan was guarding before the sudden arrival of the Blade Lineage. This information shocks Aeng-du, but she still wants to talk to her mentor in the hopes he can explain what happened. She knocks Jun out and opens the door to find a distorted Bamboo-hatted Kim standing before her. He gives no response to her questions, and when she steps too close, prepares to strike. Sinclair manages to push her out of his blade's path, saving her life, and the Sinners prepare to suppress the Distortion.

Inside the Fathoms of Bamboo-hatted Kim's ego, the group learns the truth of his past and Aeng-du begins to understand the circumstances that lead him to become the person that he is. The Sinners successfully suppress the Distortion and learn that the object the Kurokumo Clan was guarding is known as the Monolith and can influence nearby people to distort. With help from the LCD, Dante brings Bamboo-hatted Kim to his normal form. Aeng-du is still distraught over the fact he had cut down his fellows and drives her blade deep into her mentor's flesh. She mentions hearing a voice becoming more clear as she gets closer to distorting herself, and Dante quickly orders Meursault to knock her out. This stops the distortion process, and Aeng-du and Bamboo-hatted Kim are both taken by the LCA so that the LCD can study the Monolith's effects on them.

entries.name: Ahab
entries.content:
Ahab was the captain of the Whaling ship The Pequod, before becoming the leader of the town constructed from its wreckage.

Obsessed with hunting down the Pallid Whale, she gathered an entire crew of sailors onto her whaling ship, including Ishmael, as they sailed through the Great Lake and the Outskirts. A ruthless woman who led Ishmael's crewmates to their doom, she is the "bastard" Ishmael swore revenge on and became the reason she joined Limbus Company.

Ahab is a tall elderly woman with curly, mid-thigh length greying hair. Like her namesake, she has a black-and-gold peg leg starting from her left knee. She wears a green captain's jacket over an untucked button shirt and darker green pants, one leg of which is tucked into the prosthetic, a crooked captain's hat, white gloves and a thin belt around her midsection. On her back is a harpoon around her height with a narrow, transparent cylinder behind the tip and a loop at the other end. This cylinder contains a small flame, the intensity of which varies.

After being trapped in the Pallid Whale, Ahab gains Pallidification membranes across her entire body. Her peg leg is also modified to have a harpoon-like tip.

When using GasHarpoon, Ahab's left eye and arm are completely consumed by Pallidification, producing an oversized, white biomechanical arm with blue and red veins terminating in a harpoon. Additionally, she loses her captain's hat.

Within the shoulder is the flame-bearing cylinder on her harpoon, whereas on her shoulder are seemingly three crooked gas pistons, each bearing a monochrome face and ending in a lantern-like element with a luminous gas. Ahab uses these in battle to change the end of her mutated arm; doing so causes the corresponding piston to retract and the gas to transfer into her shoulder. Following her defeat, these pistons are snapped off and her shoulder displays its original orange flame.

Topmost: Bears Queequeg's face and a purple light. The last to be used, it gave Ahab a massive harpoon that she can fire.
Middle: Bears Starbuck's face and a green light. Changes Ahab's arm into tuft of rhomboid blades.
Bottom: Bears Pip's face and a blue light. The first to be used, it granted Ahab a floor-length bludgeon.

Ahab's most defining feature is her extreme and single-minded desire to hunt the Pallid Whale, with little regard for anything else. Initially, she appears to be highly charismatic, bringing in and unifying individuals from all walks of life for the goal of hunting the Calamity. However, she is highly manipulative, egocentric and selfish, seeing her crew as nothing but a means to an end. Even pre-Pallidifcation, she kept an extremely tight hold on her crew, and later admitted that she cared not about their reasons or desires, believing that they should've devoted themselves to her cause the instant they set foot on The Pequod.

Her end-justifies-the-mean mindset leads her to make extreme sacrifices, decimating her crew on their voyage to the Whale's heart without a second thought, seeing her leading the crew to their deaths as sending them to greatness. Her viewing her crew as tools is reflected in her GasHarpoon E.G.O, where she uses her most loyal crewmates as fuel for her weapon.

Ahab believes herself responsible for giving the crew conviction and meaning in their lives, and their sacrifices are merely recompense for her actions while blaming them for their fate, calling them "flimsy" and their hearts "shallow". Ahab's egocentrism is further shown when she outright rejects distortion and instantly gains an E.G.O, declaring herself as the only being that matters, and her existence itself as the world.

When her life's purpose, killing the Pallid Whale, was stolen from her by Ishmael, Ahab suffers a mental breakdown and roars for her crew to set sail for the Pallid Whale, despite the Calamity already being dead and her crew gone.

Before the events of the game, Ahab had a ravenous obsession with the Pallid Whale, believing it to be "the source of all evils". Ahab's charisma allowed her to gather a devoutly loyal crew, including Ishmael who had just quit her job at U Corp.'s Nest. Together, she would lead the crew of The Pequod into the Great Lakes, to join in her mad search for the Calamity. However, the beast would soon prove too much for the crew and destroy The Pequod, swallowing Ahab together with most of the crew. She and the survivors, alive in the belly of the Whale, soon began undergoing a slow process of Pallidification, only kept at bay thanks to Ahab's sheer determination. Eventually, she would form a community named after her ship, the Pequod Town, with as many other survivors as she could find, with the goal of locating the Pallid Whale's weak point, its heart, and slaying the Calamity.

When Ishmael's plan to enter the Pallid Whale to locate the Golden Bough works, members of Pequod Town bring them to their community, where she welcomes the Sinners with open arms. When Ishmael tries to attack her, only to cause a riot with the Sinners against the town, Ahab calls them off and convinces them into her office, where she convinces the Sinners that following her plan is the best course of action, much to Ishmael's agitation. When Ishmael again tries to kill her, she promises that so long as the Sinners help her reach the heart, she'll offer herself up to Ishmael. She then states to reach the heart, she divides the whole group in two; Her group would traverse the pancreases, a labyrinth full of mermaids and acid, while the other travels a blood vessel with had become infested with Abnormalities that the Whale had swallowed beforehand to the heart.

As revealed by Dante's new power, she would then sacrifice all of Pequod Town in her odyssey to reach the heart. Once the remains of her group meets with the Sinners again, she reveals those infected by pallidification are unable to attack the whale, and only the Golden Bough can reverse the effects. She then demands Dante gives her their head so she can slay the beast, but the manager refuses, and the two groups fight. However, once beaten, she begins to hear the Voice trying to temp her into distorting, only for Ahab to manifest her personal EGO; "GasHarpoon", based on how she sees her crew as extensions of herself and takes control of the pallidification. Using Pip, Starbuck, and finally Queequeg as ammunition for her battle, she continues to lambast Ishmael for falling the crew. Once GasHarpoon is broken by Ishmael's Snagharpoon and is left vulnerable, she then takes delight in Ishmael's bloodlust. However, she soon falls apart when Dante is able to convince Ishmael into killing the Pallid Whale instead. Left without purpose, she collapses into sputtering nonsense about finding the Whale again as the Sinners leave her within the dying beast.

Ahab miraculously survived the whale’s destruction; drifting on the remains of the foe she was robbed of slaying. Muttering her hopeless delusions as she aimlessly floated on The Great Lake, Ahab was eventually rescued by Hermann and her fleet of battleships.

When Ahab questioned if Hermann was here just to mock her, the N Corp. Director gave her a proposition: if Ahab joined her, she would allow the captain to kill any and every Pallid Whale across the countless mirror worlds. Reasoning that it was simply just a ‘single’ Pallid Whale out of potentially countless others, Hermann would give Ahab her purpose again.

All Hermann asked of Ahab was her “staunch determination and conviction”.

entries.name: Aida
entries.content:
Aida is the leader of Los Mariachis.

Aida is a young-looking woman with messy brown hair down to her chin, with spiky bangs concealing her forehead. She wears a large orange sombrero on her head, with a single strand of wheat in her mouth. She wears a white-and-orange jacket with puffy sleeves, holding the maracas she uses for combat. Beneath her jacket, she wears a black collared shirt fastened with a crimson brooch, tucked into an ornate orange belt with several holes along it. She wears green dress pants and dark shoes on her lower half.

Aida is someone who values entertainment above almost everything else life has to offer, with her love of gambling being an extension of that. While she is willing to follow the rules while playing a game, she will not accept a losing outcome when she knows that she has the ability to overwhelm the winner with force. Even when starting a fight, she keeps her usual relaxed and calm attitude.

Aida is the boss of Los Mariachis, one of the major Syndicates in the Backstreets of District 10, and a participant in the poker game for control over the casino as well as the Golden Bough found underneath it. Aida and the other players play the game normally until Rodion begins to act suspicious, causing the Tieqiu Boss to accuse her of cheating.
