Camille first appears when the Sinners arrive at the Fixer conference in the District 16 Backstreets, being one of the numerous parties assigned to the mission, along with his "sidekick" Paula. After the details of La Manchaland are explained, the pair explain that they are on a recovery contract for a specific "guest" at the park. To Don Quixote’s disapproval, Paula reveals that there are no plans to rescue every stranded person in La Manchaland. Don Quixote reacts in confusion, wondering who will save the rest of the visitors, and Camille mocks her for this delusion which sparks their argument and duel. A short time after winning the duel, Camille and the rest of the Fixers at the conference move on to entering La Manchaland.

Along with Paula, Camille is Corroded by the Four-hundred Roses Abnormality after entering the fathoms, and is fought and killed by the Sinners.

entries.name: Paula
entries.content:
Paula is a Fixer of the Zwei Association's Western Branch who is working on a joint operation with Camille to retrieve a missing person from La Manchaland. She is a supporting character in Canto VII: The Dream Ending.

Paula is a tall woman with a pale complexion. She has short light brown hair parted in the middle, and round light brown eyes. She wears the uniform of the Zwei Association Western Branch, consisting of a suit of white metal armor over a yellow shirt and blue tabard, and a long blue cape. She can be seen carrying the standard-issued Zwei West greatsword.

Paula is a rational and reserved Fixer, focused on her mission. In contrast to her partner Camille, Paula prefers to stay quiet in most situations, only speaking when asked or to find details about her mission.

Paula first appears when the Sinners arrive at the Fixer conference in the District 16 Backstreets, being one of the numerous parties assigned to the mission, along with her subordinate Camille. After the details of La Manchaland are explained, the pair explain that they are on a recovery contract for a specific "guest" at the park. To Don Quixote’s disapproval, Paula also reveals that there are no plans to rescue every stranded person in La Manchaland, this partially leads to the duel between Don Quixote and Camille.

Along with Camille, Paula is Corroded by the Four-hundred Roses Abnormality after entering the fathoms, and is fought and killed by the Sinners.

entries.name: Romero
entries.content:
Romero is a Fixer of Fanghunt Office, an Office specialized in killing Bloodfiends. He and the other Fixers of Fanghunt Office are participating in the eradication of La Manchaland.

Romero is a youthful man with silver hair, parted slightly, with longer bangs swept over his face. He has blue eyes and a pale complexion. He wears the standard uniform of Fanghunt Office, featuring a dark coat with a poncho built into it, with man straps and pockets lining both sides. He has a bandolier across his chest, atop a similarly gray waistcoat. He has a large striped ribbon tied over his dress shirt beneath this waistcoat. He wears dark pants, stuffed into calf-height boots with laces down the center.

Romero is a kind man, though one who views professionalism as the most important facet to the jobs he and his Fixer Office choose to take, viewing Camille as an example of unprofessionalism. He carries a grudge against Bloodfiends, viewing them as less than worthy of living, something shared with the majority of his Office of hunters.

Romero would first meet the Sinners as they battle members of his Office, only speaking up once the battle was concluded. Conversing with the Sinners, he would mention wishing P Corp. and the Hana Association were more picky with who they hired, knowing of the status of Bloodfiends involved in this job. Later, during Alessio's briefing of the groups involved, he would beat the employee to mentioning Bloodfiends, causing a stir among the Fixers present.

At the opening of La Manchaland, he would witness a member of the Firefist Office hastily approach one of the Bloodbags coming from the area, commenting on the failure of the Fixer to expect the betrayal and bloodthirst of those leaving the amusement park. In his expertise against Bloodfiends, he would tell everyone to accept their death if they plan to fail in the eradication.

During his assignment to Area 3, his Office would be betrayed by those accompanying him, leading to him and several of his men to be transformed into Bloodfiends and Bloodbags by Dulcinea and her men. Enthralled, they would attack the Sinners. After the battle against the overseer of Area 3, Sansón would arrive to participate in another of Don Quixote's tales, wherein Romero would attempt to betray the natural urges of Bloodfiends and their Kindred, attempting to attack Sansón, though he would be killed before he was able to cause any damage.

entries.name: Hugo
entries.content:
Hugo is a Fixer working for an unnamed Office participating in the eradication of La Manchaland. He is a supporting character in Canto VII: The Dream Ending.

Hugo is a man of average height and build. His gray-blue eyes and large nose are underlined by a cheeky grin, which itself is accentuated by his brown hair, that drapes down his cheeks. The rest of his hair is covered by a blue hood from an overcoat that gradually shifts its color into a dark gray, whilst remaining bright orange on the inside. He also wears pitch black gloves, dark gray trousers and tall boots.

Hugo is a smug and overconfident Fixer in most cases, initially being condescending to the Sinners prior to knowing they will be assisting with the eradication of La Manchaland, though backing down once the Fanghunt Office got involved. Despite his overconfidence, he agrees that he is a small-time Fixer, attempting to scrape up however much Ahn is possible through contracts. Through this mindset, he is quick to sell others out to ensure his safety or a paycheck.

As the Sinners first arrive in the Backstreets of P Corp., finding the management tent organized by the Fixers aiming to take down La Manchaland, Hugo would condescendingly tell the Sinners that they aren't allowed into the area, believing them to be civilians. As he tries to tell them off, he meekly leaves the conversation as Fanghunt Office members arrive to interrogate the Company. During Alessio and Han-ul's briefing of the job to the groups, he would arrogantly whisper to Hong Lu, before later being assigned to the same area as Limbus Company, aiming to take down Area 1.

Within Area 1, he would accompany the Sinners in defeating Bloodfiends and Bloodbags while playing the games of The Barber, all the while being closely watched by Ryōshū due to his greedy and untrustworthy behavior. As the overseer arrives at the conclusion, she would demand to know who Don Quixote is, allowing whoever admits to being the user of the name to push the button of the area. Hugo would take this opportunity to sell out Don Quixote and begin to rush for the button, though Ryōshū would sever both his hands before he has the chance to push it. Lamenting on his lack of creativity in betrayal, he would bleed out while the Sinners battle The Barber.

entries.name: Garnet
entries.content: Garnet is a young Fixer who grew up alongside Lapis in Vergilius' orphanage. Not long after getting his Fixer License, Lapis goes missing and he requests the help of Vergilius in discovering what happened to her and saving her life.

entries.name: Jumsoon
entries.content:
Jumsoon, was a Maestro of the Ring. He debuts in Book2 of Leviathan as a major antagonist.

Jumsoon and N Corp. scientist Aseah were responsible for kidnapping the children from Vergilius’ orphanage and subjecting Lapis and Garnet to the glass window’s refraction experiments.

Jumsoon is an androgynous man with extensive red spot tattoos that spread from his torso to his neck and face. He has wavy, chin length black hair streaked with white and red, and is seen wearing the Ring’s signature white dress suit, as well as a fascinator with a veil that covers his eyes. He wears a three-coiled ring on his left hand’s ring finger, signifying his rank as a Maestro. In combat, Jumsoon wields a red nangseon (otherwise known as a Lang xian) a multi-tipped spear with blades attached to its branches.

As a Distortion, Jumsoon transforms into a grotesque, pale lizard-like humanoid with a reptilian tail, claws, and feet, with blue dots all over his body. He retains his human head, although his dark hair is instead streaked blue, and his eyes glow with a faint indigo shine.

entries.name: Catt
entries.content:
Catt is one of the main characters in WonderLab. They're first introduced in Episode 1: Dingle-dangle where they introduce the Control Team transfers to the abnormalities located in the Disciplinary Department. They quickly show their ruthlessness after one of the transfers, Parker, gets entangled by Dingle Dangle, killing them to prevent the abnormality from escaping.

The captain of the Disciplinary Team of branch O-5681. Despite their indifference to the employees around them and overall ruthlessness, they're said to be one of the most capable employees within the facility.

Catt may come across as innocent at first glance, but their true nature is anything but warm and welcoming. They have a tendency to speak in the third person. They could be described as callous, with even themselves declaring "Catt has no soul. Catt doesn't love."

When they first joined Lobotomy Corporation their demeanor was starkly different, they were soft and humble. Seeing the hearts and minds of those around them. Upon witnessing the mental break and death of a close friend. That is when Catt decided to "throw away their heart" and distance themselves from others in order to survive in the corporation.

 Catt is heavily associated with cats. They take to hunting Abnormalities as if the fights are little more than sport, their pupils occasionally shown expanding and contracting like a cat's pupils, and they often refer to other, weaker Agents as "rats" and "mice". The Abnormality that represents their lingering humanity, Gone with a Simple Smile, even references the Cheshire Cat of Alice in Wonderland fame.

Catt takes an inordinate amount of joy in fighting Abnormalities, constantly leaping into battle with a grin, or even laughing. This even extends to the panic suppression aspect of the job, where they take glee in the idea of clocking someone on the head to bring them back to their senses. Not even the prospect of mercy killing a fellow employee can do much to dampen their smile.

In their early days of working in the Lobotomy Corporation, Catt was a timid, uncertain person who looked up to their seniors and was afraid of the horrific events they saw unfolding around them. The stresses of their job and having to constantly watch their seniors die or lose their minds one by one made them unable to cope with living in society among regular people, and eventually pushed them to the point of attempted suicide. Even after surviving that, they made the conscious decision to cut off their own emotions for the sake of keeping themself alive and relatively sane.

After witnessing a senior they admired beat a fellow employee to death while undergoing a Murder-type panic reaction, Catt decided to cut off their heart for the sake of surviving within the facility.

When Catt crosses the Despair Event Horizon in their backstory, their attempt to eat the cake on top of Bottle of Tears was this, but it didn't work because Catt was too physically and mentally strong to die.

Though most Agents eventually get used to the horrors within Branch O-5681, Catt is particularly depicted as one of the most well-adjusted characters in the series (though their adjusted mindset is likely a result of their Despair Event Horizon). In addition, Catt doesn't hesitate to act when an Abnormality breaches or when an employee goes insane, regardless of the horrors that ensue.

They're almost always wearing loose-fitting pants with their outfits (exceptions being their sleepwear and casual wear, which have them wearing shorts).

Catt has a tendency to come across as creepy due to their willingness to commit violence on their fellow employees, along with their unnervingly high threshold for gruesome sights. Nevertheless, they're firmly on the side of humanity, and will take actions that can benefit other people as well as the Corporation.

Catt has black hair and black eyes.
Despite acting emotionally distant to their fellow agents, Catt begins to act kinder to Rose and Taii after the suppression of Hookah Caterpillar, though unintentionally.

After watching a senior employee - someone they deeply admired - beat another innocent employee to death, Catt seems to have snapped; they decided that not having a heart was the safest way to survive in Lobotomy Corporation, and intentionally activated Bottle of Tears' ability, ignoring the original advice their senior had given them.
Undergoes another one in Episode 48. After discovering that the branch they'd worked in had basically been operating without a Manager for all of that time, Catt had come to the conclusion that all of the suffering they and the rest of the L-Corp employees had been subjected to was for nothing. They felt that the human heart cannot be discarded or strengthened, and that the heart has no choice but to die. Shortly afterwards, they begin to undergo a Distortion.
Catt: "On the way up here, I wished our deaths and sorrows would yield a better result of some kind. I wished there'd be something done by the human heart. The heart was doomed to wither. It was doomed to twist and distort."

Catt has possibly the palest skin tone out of the whole cast, with jet black hair to boot. Their unsettling manner, constant wide-eyed stares, and penchant for smiling or laughing at inappropriate times only serves to hammer home to other characters just how eerie they tend to act in the eyes of their peers.

Their E.G.O weapon is a large spoon capable of dealing BLACK damage.

If their conversation with the Piscine Mermaid is anything to go by, Catt thinks of themself as soulless and incapable of love.

On occasion, Catt will stare directly into the lens of a nearby security camera, as if to let the Manager or whoever else is at the monitor know that they're aware of their presence. In a somewhat sadder moment, Catt in their early days talked into the camera at points, venting their worries and voicing their hopes for the strength to survive their dangerous workplace.

Catt is by and large one of the smallest combatant Agents in Branch O-5681, and often engages in combat with Abnormalities several times larger than them, yet they firmly remain one of the strongest Agents their branch has to offer.

Taii manages to un-distort Catt, but Catt ends up re-distorting soon afterward, since they find it hard to both forgive themself for what they've done and lean on the help of others. However, Catt states they won't forget who they are, and departs the facility.

Catt keeps their E.G.O weapon on their back for easy access in case it's needed. Slightly Averted in that there's a strap on the back of their shirt for the weapon to slide through.

Catt refers to themself in the third person. This is done as as a way to distance and protect themself from the chaos that occurs within the facility; they spoke in first person beforehand.

Trademark Favorite Food: Catt likes foods with beef in them. They've also acquired a taste for a particular brand of soda called "Suck My Energy", and can be seen drinking it throughout the comic.

Catt is by no means stupid, as they are aware of the capabilities of their fellow employees, and they certainly have the strength to take on enemies. However, there are times where they underplay the potential value of their coworkers a bit too much, especially in the case of Rose and Taii. The same thing also goes for certain abnormalities like The Road Home and Piscine Mermaid.

entries.name: Toma
entries.content:
The captain of the Control Team of branch O-5681. Good-natured and chivalrous.

Keeps their axe attached to themself by tying it to a long, dark gray ribbon/bandage to the handle, allowing them to wield it at both close and long range.

When describing Toma, Beozzi calls them "too chivalrous". In general, Toma is shown to be a very kind individual who attempts to help others when they're capable of it.

entries.name: Rza
entries.content:
The captain of the Information Team of branch O-568, and a friend of Dal, the Safety Team Captain. Cool-headed and rational.

Rza's E.G.O. weapon of choice is a red bladed sword with a blue hilt.

Rza's everyday haircut consists of a long blue mohawk that falls to one side of their head. However, unlike the usual trope, they're actually very logical and not exceptionally rebellious.

While Rza doesn't act like a bad person, they tend to be very cold and serious, and don't show others too much warmth due to their focus on logic. But ultimately they do show their care for others when it comes down to it, such as when Purin is recovering from the fight with Pygmalion. Despite calling Purin a "kid" for believing in the power of friendship, they're still there to check on them in their sick bed, carrying a stuffed animal as a gift for them.

entries.name: Dal
entries.content:
The captain of the Safety Team of branch O-568.

Dal was initially assigned to be the temporary Safety Team Captain while the captain at the time, Beozzi, would step away from the position for a while to have their body examined for any negative influence left by their E.G.O Gift, given by the Servant of Wrath.

Unfortunately, Beozzi was uncooperative and went to work on the Servant anyway, which would eventually lead to them being transformed into a Hermit by the Servant before being killed off, and so Dal was left to take the role of the Safety Team Captain permanently.

Dal has a tendency to excessively apologize for both things that are not within their control (apologizing to Beozzi for being selected as their temporary substitute) and for not behaving as they should (politely requesting that Agents take on certain work, rather than simply relaying it as an order).

Dal took on this position within Beebi's vigilante group after the fall of the Lobotomy Corporation.

Dal has black hair and black eyes.

When their E.G.O weapon is activated, a few purple wisps can be seen floating near it.

Their E.G.O. weapon appears to give them limited control over water, which they mostly use to manipulate it into portals.

Dal's E.G.O weapon creates portals made of water, which allows for short-distance teleportation within the facility.

Dal's promotion to Safety captain was initially only meant to be temporary. However, after Beozzi was killed after being transformed into the Hermit of the Azure Forest by the Servant of Wrath, Dal took on the position permanently.
Weaponized Teleportation: Mostly used as an assist or defensively, but Dal's E.G.O. weapon has been shown to be able to teleport a charging enemy like the Piscine Mermaid away from an area to protect it, and into the path of other people who can more effectively deal with it.

entries.name: Purin
entries.content:
The captain of the Training Team of branch O-568. Has a vibrant personality, and a soft heart.

Is revealed in the Epilogue to have lost their right arm off-panel while trying to help the other employees escape the collapsed facility.

Expository Hairstyle Change: Supplementary materials posted by MIMI reveals that Purin had dyed their hair purple after the collapse of L.Corp in the Epilogue.

Purin's E.G.O. sleeves have two large poofs around the shoulders.

Purin's hair is blonde, and they have a very warm and cheerful personality.

Purin's scythe is adorned with a small heart on either end of the staff.

Has been shown to like the idea of Toma and Beozzi being together in some fashion, such as in Episode 25, where they admit that thinking of the two is what kept them from succumbing to Pygmalion's WHITE attacks.

Purin's E.G.O. weapon is a scythe. It deals BLACK damage.

entries.name: Rose
entries.content:
An Agent of the Disciplinary Department of branch O-568, said to come from a wealthy family.

They tend to regularly show compassion towards employees who might have issues to handle, especially Catt and Taii. This apparently stems from their goal of wanting to start a new Wing that's actually nice to people.

What Rose believes to have done by volunteering to work on the Staining Rose. Despite knowing that they'd die a dog's death when working on Staining Rose, Rose volunteers anyway, believing that they'd be able to protect Catt (who had the same qualifications as Rose for the job) from the same fate.

After realizing how poorly people have it outside the Nest, Rose hates their past self, who couldn't have been more comfortable with the status quo.

Rose is killed by the Staining Rose, but somehow their soul transferred itself into the Abnormality's E.G.O. suit, which Taii happened to be wearing at the time of the Party Everlasting arc. The two of them are capable of communication in a manner reminiscent of the brain sending signals to the body.

Rose grew up in a wealthy household and had a bountiful childhood within a Nest. Things went well, but eventually, the Smoke War had happened, which made Rose question things surrounding their privilege, including if the Wings truly were the "good guys". After discovering just how much suffering was born as a result of the Wings' actions, Rose became disillusioned, made major changes to their lifestyle, and now aims to create a new system that embraces all.

Rose wants to change the world and everyone for the better despite the numerous flaws and problems thrown at them. This ends up badly in the end when Rose decides to sacrifice themself to the Staining Rose so Catt doesn't have to.

Rose's E.G.O. weapon is a pair of gloves that come with wicked-looking claws.

entries.name: Taii
entries.content:
A timid employee who used to act as a counselor in the Training Department of branch O-568. After the death of an employee they were counseling, they were promoted to an Agent in the Disciplinary Department.

Taii displayed an enthusiastic fascination towards the Abnormalities, and had a desire to figure out what made each one happiest.

For all Taii's timidness, as the series goes on they become fully capable of handing breaching Abnormalities, with Episode 36 revealing they have a very high justice stat. Taii proves it when they manage to beat down Blue-Smocked Shepherd, the same Abnormality that took Shasha's eye, one on one with ease.

Blue Is Heroic: When they manage to awaken their E.G.O. (which was Staining Rose's at the time), their suit changes from pink to blue.

Although they still find many of the day-to-day occurrences at Lobotomy Corporation terrifying, Taii has nonetheless grown from a weak Clerk to an Agent capable of taking on dangerous breaching Abnormalities (albeit not alone).

Taii is generally a very optimistic person who manages to not let their job get to them too much. They also end up associated heavily with the color pink, from their hair to their belongings, and even the E.G.O. they wear the most.

During the epilogue, Taii is shown to have grown their hair out as a Fixer.

Occasionally Taii will have two tufts of hair curve upwards on both sides of their head, normally when they're very excited, curious, or happy.

Out of all the Agents seen, Taii seems the least bothered by the darker aspects of the Abnormalities, and is often even interested or excited to learn about them. While wearing an overleveled E.G.O suit—which Catt explains could cause them to essentially mutate if worn too long—Taii just chipperly smiles and nods (compared to Rose who is openly unnerved and worries about growing insectile joints).

Taii is too well-adjusted, empathetic, and accepting of their own faults for the Hookah Caterpillar's usual feeding tactics to work on them. All it manages to do is create a sense of kind familiarity. While others are left deeply stressed and disturbed by working with the worm, Taii finds it relaxing... but also deeply draining as it desperately tries to pull what little it can out of them. Likely justified as their previous job as a counselor in the Training Team likely gave them the skills needed to help themself and others cope in the long term with stressors and trauma.

During Taii's confrontation with A Party Everlasting, they've switched out their E.G.O. that they got from My Sweet Home (a cute pink suit) to Staining Rose's E.G.O. suit, "Blooming" (a blue suit resembling the armor of a knight) to symbolize how they Took a Level in Badass since the start of the comic.

Taii's E.G.O. produces smoke that allows them to move at high speeds within it, making its effects somewhat similar to this.

entries.name: Canto I: The Outcast
entries.content:
The Outcast is the first Canto in Limbus Company, and Gregor's focus chapter. It was available at game launch on February 27, 2023, alongside Season 1: Orientation, and was followed by Canto II: The Unloving.

Shortly after picking up their Executive Manager, the LCB journeys to retrieve the Golden Bough within District 4's Lobotomy Corp. Branch.

Along the way, it quickly becomes apparent to Dante that the Sinners have only recently met, and as of now is only barely functioning as a team: Don Quixote's Fixer fanaticism upon learning of their current destination annoys Heathcliff, quickly escalating to a full-on skirmish among some of the Sinners and resulting in the deaths of Heathcliff, Ishmael, and Ryōshū. The Guide, Vergilius, intervenes at this point, and asks Dante to "wind back the clock" as they did previously to revive the dead Sinners.
As Dante seemed clueless as to what they are supposed to do, Vergilius asks Faust to guide them. Following Faust's instructions, Dante experiences visions of a "gateway to Hell", is able to revive the dead Sinners while experiencing the pain of their deaths. Further incidents occurred, showcasing major character traits of other Sinners.

Shortly after, Mephistopheles runs out of fuel. Vergilius orders the Sinners off the bus to gather some Hooligans, which are then fed to the bus (to Dante and Sinclair's horror). Faust explains that the bus runs on Enkephalin, which it can extract from the nervous systems of living humans.
Just as the bus is finishing its meal, Vergilius notifies the Sinners that they are to have a "guest": a former employee of the D Corp. Lobotomy Corp. Branch, named Yuri, who will accompany them to the now-buried facility and act as a guide. In return, her contract with the Fixer Office she is currently working at will possibly be extended.

As the bus approaches their destination, the LCB begins running into people with insectile features, not unlike that of Gregor. As the buglike people (explained by Faust to be employees of the Old G Corp.) are intent on obstructing the LCB's journey, the Sinners leave the bus to negotiate, with Gregor unwillingly taking the lead on Vergilius' "advice".
In the ensuing conversation, it is revealed that Gregor has been a major focus of propaganda for the Old G Corp. during the Smoke War, which the Old G Corp. employees are veterans of. The veterans continue to refuse to let the LCB pass, leading the Sinners to resolve to violence to open the way.

As the LCB arrives at the entrance to the District 4 Lobotomy Corp. branch, they find two Fixers from Yuri's Office, Aya and Hopkins, waiting for them. While Aya holds a laid-back, friendly attitude towards the Sinners, Hopkins initially adopts a contemptuous attitude when seeing the Sinners' ragtag appearance, though this is quickly replaced by awe when he learns that the Guide of the LCB is none other than the Red Gaze.
Vergilius drags Dante aside and advises them to not have too high hopes for the Grade 8 Fixers, then retreats back to the bus with Charon as the Sinners and Fixers enter the decrepit facility.

Within Story Dungeon
Main article: Branch D-02
The Sinners and Fixers encounter more Old G Corp. veterans upon entering the underground facility. Similarly to the veterans aboveground, the G Corp. veterans recognize Gregor from war propaganda, and immediately shows great animosity towards him, describing him as a traitor for his "abandoning" his comrades to the side effects of the insectification operations.
After making their way past the veterans, the LCB runs into the Peccatula; Yuri isn't able to recognize the monsters, which she is chastised by Hopkins for. Shortly thereafter, the group encounters an Abnormality, the Ebony Queen's Apple, which kills Aya, and combat ensues. After defeating the Abnormality, the team makes their way down into the second floor of the Dungeon.

In the second floor of the Dungeon, the Sinners run into Gregor's old superior, who attempts to kill Gregor for his "desertion". Near his death, however, upon learning of Gregor's plights after the war, he appears to be satisfied in knowing that Gregor is "no different from [them]". Gregor borrows a cigarette from Ryōshū, which he gives as a last token to his Head Manager.

Proceeding farther into the facility, the group enters a hallway full of corpses, and toxic gas grenades start going off. The Sinners begin falling one by one, while Hopkins, who learned of the poison through scans conducted previously, and completed a satisfactory gathering of Enkephalin, puts on a gas mask and bids his farewell; Yuri, who was treated by the Office as an expendable, was not informed of the gas, nor was given a gas mask, and begins coughing.
Gregor gives her a gas mask he found on Aya's corpse, and they briefly discuss Yuri's feelings about her survival of the site's burial during Lobotomy Corp.'s collapse, before Gregor dies to the gas. After the gas dissipates, Yuri and Dante, who was unaffected by the gas, drag the bodies of the dead Sinners away to be revived.

After defeating the Doomsday Calendar, the team makes their way to the final floor of the facility. As Gregor approaches a containment unit pouring with golden light, everybody is suddenly transported to the midst of a battlefield, right from Gregor's memories.
Very soon, flashbacks from Gregor's past begins materializing, presenting memories of his youth, from the surgery which replaced his arm with an insectoid bio-prosthetic, to his subsequent alienization from society as the Old G Corp. collapsed after the end of the Smoke War. Eventually, hands begin to descend from the sky, crushing everything on the battlefield. The Sinners try escaping them, albeit to no avail. Gregor points out that since the battlefield is a figment of his own ego, the only way out would be to follow how it played out in reality, by allowing them to be grabbed by the owner of the hand.

Back in the real world, the Sinners battle the Abnormality housing the Golden Bough, defeating it and reverting it to its "egg" state. However, the Abnormality evolves into its second form, and Yuri, who steps forward to investigate, is devoured by it. After defeating it for a second time, the Abnormality deployed Yuri's head as a final attempt at self-preservation, a tactic that stays the Sinners' hand for enough time for a newly arrived party, consisting of old acquaitances of several Sinners, to take the Bough. The Sinners return to the bus dejected, awaiting their next mission.

entries.name: Canto II: The Unloving
entries.content:
The Unloving is the second Canto in Limbus Company, and Rodion's focus chapter. It was available at game launch on February 27, 2023, alongside Season 1: Orientation, and takes place between Canto I: The Outcast and Canto III: The Unconfronting.

The LCB is informed by Vergilius their next mission to claim the Golden Bough will take them to District 10, a place that the Guide mentions Rodion should already be familiar with. The Golden Bough is known to be buried underneath a casino currently occupied by various Syndicates, all of which are attempting to claim it. In order to get their hands on the Bough before the others, the Sinners are tasked with following a plan created by LCCB agents Effie and Saude, involving them sneaking into the casino as one of the Syndicates, and win a card game to claim the rights to the Bough through the use of "wish power", a resource produced by J Corp.'s Singularity. However, the plan quickly falls apart after Don Quixote's attempt to save a elderly pawn shop owner from some thugs from the Tingtang Gang: as more Syndicate members show up to the shop, the pawnbroker pretends to not be involved, and the LCB ends up having to fight the gang. The Sinners then decide to steal the Tingtang Gangsters' outfits, and use those to enter the casino.

Once inside, the Sinners face off against the Casino Security, the Tieqiu Crew and Los Mariachis, wasting wish power on their race to the top of the casino. After reaching the top, Rodion requests to play the game, claiming she'd stolen a bit of wish power and felt capable of winning the match. She faces off with the Tieqiu Boss, the Mariachi Jefe Aida, and an old acquaintance, Sonya, the founder of the Yurodiviye Syndicate. Rodion manages to win the match, despite having lied about having wish power left, and the Sinners enter Branch J-03.

Within Story Dungeon
After reaching the Dungeon under J Corp., the Sinners are forced to do battle against more security, debt slaves, and even Abnormalities. Reaching the final floor has Rodion's past as a former Yurodivy revealed. Wanting to help her community, yet tired of Yurodivy doing nothing but plan and discuss all the time as people were dying in hunger, she would kill a corrupt pawnbroker who was extorting her neighborhood. Unfortunately, the pawnbroker was under the protection of The Middle, resulting in a retaliation that left the entire neighborhood dead. However, Sonya states her reasons for killing the pawnbroker were less about actually helping people, but more of the fact she wanted to be special.

The Sinners are then chased by a castle-sized Abnormality, Baba Yaga, and are forced to run to the exit, while Sonya and his Yurodivy appear to protect them as they flee, allowing the Sinners to claim the Bough in the process. Sonya also offers Rodion an offer to rejoin his group, but she declines it, stating she needs to be in "the cold" more. He also mentions something about a "mark", one that only Sinclair can see.

Afterwards, Rodion uses the gambling chips she stole from the casino to pay for drink and food to celebrate their first successful mission. Though underneath her cheerful demeanor, she still shows signs of distress.

Post-credits, Sonya is revealed to have survived the encounter with the Abnormality, and currently have an arrangement with Hermann for the Boughs.

entries.name: Canto III: The Unconfronting
entries.content:
The Sinners enter District 11 to claim the Golden Bough in Calw, Sinclair's hometown, but end up fighting while in a immigration checkpoint due to Don Quixote trying to save a family from being separated. Eventually, K Corp. calls one of their "star Fixer" Siegfried to deal with the Sinners. After killing all the Sinners on camera, Siegfried allows them to go, and Vergilius gives Don Quixote a dress down for her repeated offensives. The LCB then makes their way to Calw, only to be stopped by the Nagel und Hammer Inquisition, that call both Dante and Mephistopheles "tainted".

Eventually reaching Calw, the LCB discoveres that the entire town was targeted and destroyed by the Inquisitors, who carry a profound hatred for prosthetic users. The Sinners are welcomed by the voice of the leader of the Inquisition, Kromer, playing through the speakers of the town, and calling for Sinclair. After making it to Sinclair's family's mansion, they find Effie nearly dead from having been tortured by the Inquisitors, with Outis giving him a coup de grâce and Sinclair going into a blind rage.

After Sinclair's rage is quelled by Don Quixote beating him to a pulp, the Sinners reach the dungeon, where they fight Inquisitors having been corroded into monsters with E.G.Os. While there, they also learn how Sinclair caused Kromer to target and eventually kill all members of his family (save for Sinclair himself) by discovering that it was housing an L Corp. Branch Facility filled with Abnormalities in an attempt to escape prosthetic replacement.

Within the dungeon, they find more people being tortured and killed by the Inquisition, with many of said Inquisitors having corroded with EGO as well.

Deeper in, they find a heavily wounded Saude, who asks if Effie was still alive. Outis claims that he is, but just then, Guido, who the Sinners believed was dead, turns up again and attacks Dante. Guido gives Saude a chance to save herself by killing Dante with her gun, and she seemingly turns against the Sinners. However, it's just a trick to let Guido's guard down so he can be killed for real. After he is dealt with, Saude admits that she knew that the Sinners were lying and asks to be left behind so she can keep the Inquisitors off the team's back. They reluctantly do so, but doubt she'll do much.

Eventually reaching Kromer, she reveals that she wants Sinclair to join her, seeing it as preordained as she has seen it happen in an alternate timeline. Using the power of the Golden Bough, she then mutates into a monster resembling a Lust Peccatula. During combat, one of her attacks melts nearly everyone but Dante and Sinclair, who are then saved by Demian's sudden appearance, with him killing Kromer in one blow. He then talks to Dante and gives them the Golden Bough before leaving.

Members of the LCCA then arrive to rescue the Sinners, injecting Dante with a K Corp. ampule and healing their wounds. While Dante calls it a dismal defeat, back on the bus, the Sinners enjoy chicken kebabs as a reward for claiming their second Bough.

entries.name: Intervallo I: Hell's Chicken
entries.content:
Hell's Chicken is the first side chapter in Limbus Company, taking place between Canto III: The Unconfronting and Canto IV: The Unchanging.

The LCB continue their activities in District 11 after the adventures in Calw to perform a request from the manager of a fried chicken establishment called Bodhisattva Chicken, relayed through a representative from K Corp. named Samjo. The restaurant is currently suffering from trouble caused by the Distorted owner of a restaurant from across the street.

The LCB takes on the request, mostly due to the request as a valuable chance to study the Distortion Phenomenon. Heathcliff was briefly parasitized by a subsidiary entity of the Distortion, and the Sinners were able to glean that the restaurant owner had Distorted due to a "lost recipe". An attempt to recreate the recipe by cooking was decided upon to resolve the Distortion, and a cooking competition quickly arose from arguments between Gregor and Ryōshū.

Several more rounds of cooking were required after both Gregor and Ryōshū failed miserably at producing edible food, with Meursault's cooking coming very near to perfection and Outis's successfully opening the heart of the restaurant owner. As Outis's cooking passed, a portal leading to a Mirror Dungeon of the Fathoms of the restaurant owner opened, and he entered.

Upon initial entry of the Mirror Dungeon, it is revealed that the cause of the restaurant owner's Distortion is the manager of Bodhisattva Chicken stealing his prized chicken recipe and tossing it into a concept incinerator--effectively removing all traces of its existence. The restaurant owner suffered a breakdown due to his cooking chicken being connected to childhood memories of his mother, leading to his Distortion. As the Sinners defeat him, he comes to the realization that his mother did not like chicken, and promptly un-Distorts.

The Intervallo ends with the Sinners opening a gift box from the restaurant owner, only to find that it contains only a plush mascot of the restaurant that never went into production. Irritated, some Sinners propose to get rid of it; however, Charon shows a liking for the plush, and she kept it. Additionally, Samjo was shown in a "post-credits scene" talking to one "Chief Dongrang", informing him of the Sinners' capability; Samjo then prepares for a second meeting with the LCB.

entries.name: Canto IV: The Unchanging
entries.content:
The Unchanging is the fourth Canto in Limbus Company, and Yi Sang's focus chapter. It was released on Season 2: Reminiscence and takes place between Intervallo I: Hell's Chicken and Intervallo II: S.E.A..

The LCB discover an Abnormality suddenly rampaging through District 11 and manage to suppress it. Following this, they reach the K Corp. building and meet its Branch Manager Dongrang, who is also an acquaintance of Yi Sang. He promises to give the Golden Bough to the Sinners as per their "contract". However, the building is suddenly attacked by terrorists known as the "Technology Liberation Alliance", who hijack the building and the machines within to force the K Corp guards in killing the LCB. The Sinners are forced to deal with the Bots sent by the Alliance, L Corp. E.G.O. users, and even a Workshop that were payed by a mole to act as backup for the Alliance, with said mole suddenly being assassinated by a Shi Association member. All the while, the Sinners learn more about both K Corp.'s dark side and Dongrang's callousness.

Following Shrenne's death, the leader of the Technology Liberation Alliance's group, Dongbaek, another old friend of Yi Sang's, reveals herself to have the Golden Bough, and stabs him through the heart before leaving. After Dante saves Yi Sang, the Sinner admits his most distressing moment was being brought back to life. Continuing forward, the Sinners confront Dongbaek at the top of the building, where she reveals her intent to destroy the source of K Corp.'s healing ampules, stating their danger. Dongrang's assistant Samjo tries to prove their safety, only to die when he dives in a vat full of it. After Dongbaek loses to the Sinners in combat, Dongrang reveals the source of the ampules; a massive eye that cries when witnessing cruelty happen, such as the massacre of Calw and the aforementioned rampage of the Abnormality, which escaped from the Alliance's control. As Dongrang berates Dongbaek's failings, she begins to distort, only to instead gain a personal E.G.O and keeps fighting the Sinners. She loses again, and Dongrang kills her with the Golden Bough, claiming that it is an act of compassion as their former compatriot Gubo has been assisting N Corp. reassemble the League of Nine and killing any old members that don't join, but it is clear he has other motivations for ending Dongbaek's life. As she turns into petals in front of Yi Sang, the death is recorded and played for the Tearful Thing.



Within Story Dungeon
The Bough however resonates with Yi Sang, causing the building to become distorted, and all the K Corp. Security and Technology Liberation Alliance members are reanimated without their consciousness. Fighting their way past them, they reach a gate that leads into a dungeon based on Yi Sang's memories of the League of Nine, and the Sinners are forced to act out the other members to progress. During the play, it is revealed that Yi Sang was created a "mirror" that could peer into other worlds, and would become the base of the LCB' Identity system, and that Dongrang had sold out the rest of the League to T Corp., and received secure employment with K Corp. in return. The Sinners also learn the nature of K Corp.'s Singularity: the Tearful Thing was once a human boy who explored the Outskirts together with Stephanette, a girl who would go on to become K Corp.'s Chief Executive. The boy, after expressing his wish of being able to help people, was turned into the Tearful Thing, and started being used as a Singularity.

In the aftermath of the fall of the League, Yi Sang, with nowhere else to go, and believing he could never "fly" again, went with Gubo to N Corp., where he was regularly drugged and used to help advance N Corp's works. Eventually, Yi Sang managed to work the courage to escape.

After reaching the bottom of the dungeon, Dongrang, who had been struggling with living under the shadow of the League even after its downfall, starts distorting, but then manages to reverse the process and gain a personal E.G.O, Farmwatch by casting away such thoughts and deciding to kill Yi Sang so his copy of the "mirror" can be the only one left standing. Dongrang nearly wins, but Yi Sang gains helps from not only Hong Lu and Dante, but Dongbaek and Sang Yi's words of encouragement. This allows him to gather the courage to fight back, killing Dongrang.

With Dongrang's death, the contract signed with K Corp. becomes null, and the current K Corp. Chief Executive Alfonso requests for the LCB's memories of the Singularity erased as the condition for giving them the Golden Bough. Despite the Sinners', particularly Ryōshū's, protests, they go forth with the procedure. Only Dante manages to walk away with the memories intact, apparently being immune to the process, although they do not share this fact with the others. As they return to the bus, they question Yi Sang on his wishes, asking where it was that he wished to fly to. Yi Sang replies that he would have been satisfied with the feelings it would give, and that currently he still has to reflect on what he truly wishes for himself. However, he is resoluted to keep on living and facing what the future has in store for him.

Afterwards, during a victory party over the third Bough successfully retrieved, Dante meets Demian again, who explains why he believes the Mirror to be a cruel piece of technology, then asks Dante to draw a sheep for him as they had once promised to, before leaving. The last scene has Dante's clock head begin moving towards midnight.

entries.name: Intervallo II: S.E.A.
entries.content:
Intervallo II: S.E.A. is the second side chapter in Limbus Company, taking place between Canto IV: The Unchanging and Canto V: The Evil Defining.

The LCB arrive at the Backstreets of District 21, stopping by the shores of The Great Lake to wait and gather materials for the modification of Mephistopheles to become amphibious for the impending Golden Bough retrieval mission in U Corp.'s territory. Of note is the Workshop that Limbus Company chose for the modification--Molar Boatworks, featuring three Fixers who was ejected there from The Library. The Molar Boatworks Fixers utilizes technology from U Corp. to work and fuse scrap gathered from Trash Crabs in the area to modify the bus, though the large amount of raw materials needed means that the Sinners must actively hunt Trash Crabs to keep up with the modification process.

The impending trip to the Great Lake makes Ishmael highly anxious, as she believes that the Sinners are far from ready to participate in missions on the Great Lake, even with Dante's resurrection capabilities. Dante tries to liven up the general heavy mood caused by Ishmael's anxiety by organizing a game of beach volleyball, though the plan backfires with the game ending prematurely: Heathcliff knocked the ball out of bounds due to Ishmael's incessant grumbling, leading to its destruction.

This series of events eventually culminated in a full-out argument between Ishmael and Heathcliff, which came very near to full-out blows. Vergilius intervened at this point; although Heathcliff was able to calm down and continue participating in scrap collection quickly, Vergilius tells Dante in a later chat that Ishmael's problem cannot be resolved at this time: to be precise, there is no reason to solve it.

After much Trash Crab hunting and scrap collection under this heavy atmosphere, the modifications to Mephistopheles is finally complete, and the Sinners go on for a stormy voyage on the Great Lake.

entries.name: Canto V: The Evil Defining
entries.content:
The Evil Defining is the fifth Canto in Limbus Company, and Ishmael's focus chapter. It was released on Season 3: Bon Voyage and takes place between Intervallo II: S.E.A. and Intervallo III: Miracle in District 20.

With Mephistopheles now sea-worthy, the Sinners travel the Great Lake to locate the Golden Bough. During the voyage, Ishmael, who during the events of Intervallo II had refused to return to the Lake, resolves to no longer collaborate with the LCB unless explicitly ordered to. As a result, the rest of the Sinners struggle to learn the so called "Laws of the Great Lake", and barely escape some close encounters with the Whales and Mermaids that populate the various lakes. In the meantime, Dante discovers another power to their clock prosthetic, the ability to see into people's mind and their desires.

In Marlin Portship, the LCB learn that the LCCB agent they were supposed to rendezvous with has been kidnapped by the Twinhook Pirates, a Syndicate backed by the Middle. Ishmael brings up the name of "Queequeg" at the Pirates' hideout, which leads to their boss, the First Mate Smee requesting to know Queequeg's location, as the Middle has put a large bounty on her head. After the LCB defeats the Pirates, Smee mentions that their Syndicate is backed by the Middle, and that killing her would result in them sending a Big Brother to avenge her; despite this, she eventually reveals the LCCB agent's location. Afterwards, Ishmael attempts to kill her, only to be physically stopped by Dante, who takes a heavy blow in her stead.

After rescuing the LCCB agent, Pilot, he reveals to the Sinners that his team had located the L Corp. Branch that housed the Bough, which had been taken over by the Pirates backed by a Big Brother of the Middle. The LCCB team was found and held hostage by the Pirates, until a Calamity know as the "Pallid Whale" closed in: the team was wiped out, while the Pirates and the Big Brother fled, taking Pilot with them. Pilot also reveals that Saude survived the N Corp. Inquisition's purge of Calw and has become one of the managers of the LCCB. With a destination in mind, the Sinners travel the Great Lake to reach the Branch, battling various Whales along the way.

During the travel, Ishmael's past is slowly revealed to Dante, who peers into her mind to learn that of her old Captain, who had led her fellow crewmates to their death in her obsession with hunting the Pallid Whale. Dante finds out that Ishmael's greatest desire is to kill her to avenge her comrades.

Eventually, the LCB reaches the L Corp. building, which had been spat out by the Whale, but was affected by its tremendous abilities, which covered every part of the building, including the LCCB agents trapped inside, in a thin white membrane, an effect which Faust defines as "pallidification". The Sinners are also approached by Rim, one of Yi Sang's friends of the League of Nine Littérateurs, who has seemingly become a Distortion, and who reveals to them that when the Whale ate the L Corp. building, it swallowed the Bough and all Abnormalities contained there.

As they leave, the Middle suddenly arrives, lead by Big Brother Ricardo, who intends on taking revenge on the Sinners, after having seen Heathcliff steal his hair coupons from the club run by the Twinhook Pirates. All the Sinners but Ishmael are all killed off in the slaughter, and are only saved by the arrival of another Color: the Indigo Elder, a man whose mission is killing the Five Calamities of the Great Lake.

The Sinners, together with the Elder, return on Mephistopheles, where Ishmael hatches a plan to locate and enter the Pallid Whale, taking advantage of the Sinners' immunity to the effects of pallidification. With the Elder backing them up from the outside, the LCB manages to enter the belly of the Whale, although Ishmael becomes more and more entranced in her quest for revenge.

Within Story Dungeon
Inside the Whale, the Sinners are saved from being digested by semi-pallidified humans from Ishmael's old crew, led by Ishmael's former captain, Ahab. Ahab proposes a deal to Ishmael and the Sinners: if they will help her reach the heart of the Whale, she will allow them to take the Golden Bough which they seek, and Ishmael to kill her. The Sinners and Ahab's party separate as they traverse the beast, with the Sinners being joined by Queequeg, Ishmael's closest friend, whom she believed dead. Ishmael questions Queequeg on the life the crew led inside the Whale, with Queequeg revealing that they all managed to survive the pallidification by following Ahab's lead; furthermore, Queequeg speaks of having "buried" her memories of Ishmael to focus on survival, leading Ishmael to reminisce on the desire they had shared to live on together after the voyage.

The LCB and Queequeg thus travel through the Whale's insides, slaying many Mermaids and fighting off some of the Abnormalities from the L Corp. Branch that had been swallowed by the Whale, while Dante's powers reveal more of Ishmael's past on The Pequod. However, once they reunite with Ahab at the beast's heart, it is revealed that the Captain has sacrificed her party to ensure she reached it.

Ahab then reveals that she wants Dante's head, which contains part of a Golden Bough, to be able to kill the whale, as the effects of pallidification prevent her from actually attacking it. The Sinners and Ahab do battle, but when corned, Ahab's obsession and determination lead to her awakening her E.G.O, GasHarpoon, that absorbs her remaining crew, Queequeg, Starbuck and Pip, and sacrifices them to empower herself further. The LCB defeat her, and Ishmael is able to break the Captain's weapon, but as the witnesses the pallidification claim Queequeg, and finally facing the object of her obsession, she begins to lose her direction, and nearly becomes pallidified herself, before being pulled out by Heathcliff.

The battle closes, with the crew of the Pequod being taken over by the pallidification. Ishmael shares a tearful goodbye with Queequeg, who asks Ishmael to introduce herself to her once more, in memory of their friendship and affection; Ishmael does so, as Queequeg's body disintegrates.

She is ultimately convinced by Dante to not strike down Ahab, but rather, her prize: the Pallid Whale. Ishmael briefly reflects on Ahab, remembering the awe she felt of her the first time they met, and how she'd yearned to become like her, someone capable of facing her destiny without hesitation, and she considers how the voyage turned into Ahab's Mermaid, devoid of her own beliefs, only blindly following along. She then agrees to Dante's suggestion, and tears through the Whale's heart, claiming the Golden Bough within.

With her desire denied, Ahab breaks down, but Ishmael reveals her intent to spare her, to serve as a testament to her own sins and failures, as her own Whale. As the beast collapses, the Indigo Elder throws down a rope, allowing the LCB safe passage. Following the successful return to the Mephistopheles, Ishmael states her intent to stay with the Sinners until it comes time to separate, after which she will go on her own adventure, having now found purpose beyond revenge.

Post-credits, its revealed that Ahab survived the Whale's collapse, and is recruited by Hermann with the promise of slaying every Pallid Whale across infinite worlds.

entries.name: Intervallo III: Miracle in District 20
entries.content:
Intervallo III: Miracle in District 20 is the third Intervallo in Limbus Company, taking place between Canto V: The Evil Defining and Intervallo III: Yield My Flesh to Claim Their Bones.

As the journey on The Great Lake drags on after the closing of Canto V, the Sinners begin to feel the weight of tedium. Heathcliff, however, is anxious, especially after he gains the knowledge that their current destination is District 20. He explains to the other Sinners that after Ishmael's "turn", he has a mounting suspicion that his "turn" will be coming up next; this suspicion is further consolidated with Vergilius giving him "something" after his last consultation session. As a result, Heathcliff wishes to refine his looks for a certain upcoming occasion at T Corp., starting with the procurement of a suit.

When everyone else turns in for the night, Don Quixote convinces Heathcliff and Dante to join in on a "plan" to help Heathcliff get a suit. This involves a journey through one of the doors in Mephistopheles' Backdoor to a gift factory run by short, round creatures called Gnomes. The trio initially receives a warm welcome by a manager Gnome named Dodoru, though it is quickly revealed that the Gnomes were procuring human matter as raw material in their production. The three fights through a crowd of gnomes, defeating Dodoru and rescuing a girl named Crayon from the materials sleigh. However, reinforcements quickly arrived, putting all except Dante to sleep using gas and carrying them off for processing.

At this point, the other Sinners barge in, having noticed Dante's disappearance. It is at this point that it is made clear that the gift factory is located in The Outskirts, a significant distance from the Great Lake. The Sinners fight through the factory, arriving just on time to save Heathcliff, Don Quixote, and Crayon from becoming gifts. They then defeat the gnomes' leader, a red-skinned giant named Santata, who started the factory to take revenge for the Outskirts monsters' denial from entering the City.

As Santata falls, his gut begins to swell alarmingly. A figure leaps out suddenly, puncturing the dead giant's abdomen and releasing an extremely malodorous, but otherwise harmless, gas. He then inquires as to the Sinners' origins, and reveals that he is Domino the Hunter of Cloud Town, where Crayon came from. The gift factory usually performed raids on another village at this time of year, so Domino went over to help; however, the Gnomes instead attacked Cloud Town instead, overcoming its defenses and taking all its inhabitants. Both Outskirts residents express thanks for their aid in destroying the gift factory. Though Don Quixote offers for the two to accompany them to the City, they refuse as there is little chance they could pass the paperwork for immigration, let alone integrate into City society. Faust advises for quick return to Mephistopheles as the portal back could close at any moment, and Domino gives Dante an antique carved wooden doll as a parting gift.

Back on the bus, Vergilius leaves Dante to deal with the mess after he claimed responsibility over the incident. Don Quixote had grabbed a sackful of gifts and decorations from the factory on the way out and promptly began decorating the bus's cabins. Heathcliff agrees to show the "something" Vergilius gave him, and it was revealed to be an invitation for Heathcliff to attend a certain event (specifics were blotted over) at "Wuthering Heights". At the bottom of the letter is a handwritten note from one "Cathy", personally entreating Heathcliff's attendance.

The Intervallo ends with Rodya and Hong Lu experimentally dressing Heathcliff up. Dante goes out on the deck for some air; Faust accompanies them, telling them to focus on the stories of those in the City for now.

entries.name: Intervallo III: Yield My Flesh to Claim Their Bones
secondary_keys: Yield My Flesh to Claim Their Bones
III: Yield My Flesh to Claim Their Bones
entries.content:
Intervallo III: Yield My Flesh to Claim Their Bones is the fourth Intervallo in Limbus Company, taking place between Intervallo III: Miracle in District 20 and Canto VI: The Heartbreaking.

Having exited the Great Lake some time prior, the colors begin to fade from the bus as the LCB enters the Backstreets of District 20. The Sinners are told by Vergilius to find and extract a "target" in the middle of a gang war between the Kurokumo Clan and the Blade Lineage outside the bus, where they find a wounded Blade Lineage Salsu, Aeng-du, and bring her back to the bus. Once she awakens, she explains that the Blade Linage had fled to the Library to escape from enemies, only to succumb and then find themselves in the District 20 Backstreets. She requests the Sinners help her return to the building to rescue her mentor, Bamboo-hatted Kim, who happened to reawaken in the 'Yong-jin Building', which is not far from here. After dealing with more Kurokumo Clan reinforcements, the Sinners meets an unexpected visitor by the name of Caiman, an LCCA Team Leader, who, after heavily berating them for their "careless" actions, relays extra duties to the LCB: the Sinners are to go to the Yong-jin Building to 1. Resolve the Distortion and 2. Retrieve a 'Monolith' from the same site.

After reaching the building, they are contacted by the walkie-talkie given to them by Caiman, warning them about the growing signal from the Monolith in the building, which could "force people to Distort". As they battle their way through the building, they come across evolved instances of Peccatula, which Faust attributes to their continued collection of Golden Boughs. As the conversation regarding Peccatula continues, Dante suddenly has a "breakdown", uttering heavily obfuscated comments on the discriminatory factors between Peccatulum transformation, Distortion, and E.G.O manifestation as their clock head begins to violently overheat.

As Dante recovers, Aeng-du goes on ahead, where she runs into the Kurokumo Clan Captain, Jun, who is guarding the door to where Kim and the Monolith are. The Sinners arrive just on time to see her being defeated by Jun, and subsequently defeat him. He confesses that the Kurokumo Clan members stationed at Yong-jin Building are tasked with guarding the 'Monolith' pending delivery to The Thumb; when Bamboo-hatted Kim and some other Blade Lineage members suddenly appeared, the anxious Kurokumo Clan members attacked them. The ensuing battle and Blade Lineage casualties caused Kim to "snap" and attack indiscriminately, forcing the Kurokumo Clan to retreat.

An appalled Aeng-du enters the door the Kurokumo Clan had been guarding, finding that Kim has Distorted. After defeating Kim, a Mirror Dungeon of the Fathoms manifests, into which Kim flees. The Sinners follow him inside, where they uncover Kim's memories of a not dissimilar battle at S Corp., where the Blade Lineage hailed from. Aeng-du believes the Kurokumo Clan's slaughter of Kim's fellows reminded him of this incident, and Faust states that this shock, along with influences from the Monolith, was the cause of his Distortion. They eventually reach and defeat the fully distorted Kim, allowing Dante to be walked through how to safely seal the Monolith, reverting Kim's Distortion. The person on the other end reveals their name to be Ezra from The Distortion Detective, who thanks them before leaving.

They are then met by agents of the LCA to collect the Monolith, only to ask where the former Distortion is. It turns out the Aeng-du had dragged Kim away to kill him as revenge for being responsible for the death of other Blade Lineage members, and is beginning to distort; Meursault was able to halt the Distortion process by knocking Aeng-du out, and both were then carried away by the LCA agents.

When questioned about whether Limbus Company can handle the complications with the Thumb that this incident is sure to spark, an LCA agent replies with the cryptic message "A foe is a friend, and a friend is a foe for Limbus Company". Dante returns to the bus filled with questions, though Vergilius replies that all their questions will eventually be answered in due time. The Intervallo ends with Charon setting course for "the famous Heights" of T Corp.
entries.comment: Intervallo III: Yield My Flesh to Claim Their Bones

entries.name: Canto VI: The Heartbreaking
entries.content:
The Heartbreaking is the sixth Canto in Limbus Company, and Heathcliff's focus chapter. It was released on Season 4: Clear All Cathy and takes place between Intervallo III: Yield My Flesh to Claim Their Bones and Intervallo IV: Timekilling Time.

The LCB arrives in T Corp.'s Nest without incident. On the way there, the Sinners spot a man with colored clothes being mugged by gangsters low on "time". They learn from the man that a lot of people have been going missing, possibly victims of a "mass kidnapping" by a Syndicate. During the trip, the Sinners question Heathcliff on the invitation he received from Catherine; during the discussions, Heathcliff reveals he was taken into Wuthering Heights as a child, where he suffered great abuse due to being born in the Backstreets.

Before leaving the bus, Ishmael questions why Vergilius never participates in the missions in any way. The Color responds that the contract he signed with Limbus Company prevents him from interfering. Rodion and Hong Lu then dress up Heathcliff in fancy clothes to look presentable to Catherine.

Upon reaching Wuthering Heights, the Sinners are surprised by the violent weather, particularly the thunder striking down in strange patterns, often following Heathcliff's mentions of the life he led in the manor. The Sinners are welcomed by Nelly, the manor's Chief Butler, who introduces them to the other guests: Linton Edgar, backed by the Edgar Family staff, and Hindley Earnshaw, backed by the Dead Rabbits, Heathcliff's old syndicate. Heathcliff learns that Catherine married Linton after his departure, and upon requesting to speak to her, he learns that Catherine had passed, and that he was invited to her funeral. The Öufi Association proceeds to read Catherine's will, which leaves Linton the estate and Hindley a ticket to M Corp. to a rehab center, while Heathcliff would receive her Golden Bough when "the seventh lightning strikes". Dante then realizes there are two Golden Bough located in the manor.

Heathcliff refuses to believe the claims of Catherine's death, and requests to see the body, affirming he had heard her voice upon arriving to the manor. Crushed by grief, he cries out for her, causing the first lightning to strike and the manor to suddenly reshuffle, after showing a memory of Catherine and Heathcliff's childhood. The event causes the Dead Rabbits to go berserk and start attacking. During combat, the Sinners begin to notice strange things about the Syndicate, whose members don't carry watches and appear to be civilians.

After saving Hindley from the Wuthering Heights Butlers, the Sinners reach Catherine's old room, ransacked by the Edgar Family Butlers in search of her diary. The Butlers are unable to find it, and end up being chased away; Heathcliff easily recovers it, and is the only person capable of reading it. The diary leads them to the fireplace, where Linton awaits and cruelly disparages Heathcliff; in response to Linton's claim that Catherine did not truly love Heathcliff, a second lightning strike hits the manor, showing another of Catherine's memories. Upon witnessing Heathcliff's ability to read from the diary, Linton stands aside and opens the way into the basement, claiming this to be "Catherine's will".

After fighting off evolved Peccatula, the Sinners discover a laboratory based on Yi Sang's mirror tech, in which are stored the victims of the kidnappings in Nest T, as well as a coffin inside which Catherine and one of the Golden Boughs rest. The laboratory is operated by the Öufi Fixers, revealed as ex-Ring scientists led by N Corp. researcher Aseah, a member of the old League of Nine. The Sinners are then attacked by Hindley and the Dead Rabbits. The Dead Rabbits Boss, however, aggravates Hindley's fragile mental state until he hints that he was the one who made him lose the manor in a gambling match, causing Hindley to start claiming him, Catherine, Linton, and Heathcliff to be traitors who had taken everything from him, and to distort. Hindley is killed by the Sinners, while the third lightning strike hits the manor.

The Dead Rabbits Boss then attempts to activate a device, but is stopped by Heathcliff, who demands to know who he actually is. The Dead Rabbits Boss reveals himself to be an Identity of Heathcliff, who seeks to kill every Heathcliff from the various Mirror Worlds, claiming them to be the cause of every Catherine's miseries. After the Sinners first defeat the Identity, Heathcliff, overwhelmed by the revelations received ever since returning to the manor, begins hearing a voice that pushes him into Distortion, and rampages across the laboratory. The Sinners defeat him, and the fourth lightning strike hits the manor; in the memory revealed by the diary, Heathcliff speaks with a younger Catherine, leading him to fall out of his state of Distortion.

The Sinners then learn that the Identity had been summoned over the body of Isabella, Linton's sister. Linton himself appears soon after, commenting on the death of his "foolish sister", and revealing the laboratory had been built by Catherine, with him collaborating with the Ring to provide test subjects for their research. He reveals to the Sinners that the lightning signifies Catherine's heart breaking, and is overjoyed to find the fifth one striking for him; he then attaches mirror tech machinery to himself and pulls one of the switches, melting away into a puddle of flesh. Aseah explains that Linton has become a "dough", a pure form of humanity, which Aseah then uses to summon the Identity once more: Faust dubs the perfected Identity Erlking Heathcliff, leader of the Wild Hunt, an army of spirits he had killed in various Worlds.

The Erlking takes off with Catherine's coffin and the Golden Bough, and sends a seemingly endless horde of spirits and Peccatula after the Sinners; they are saved by Vergilius, who comments on how familiar the laboratory is to one he'd seen before, and holds the horde back while the Sinners run to stop Erlking Heathcliff from reaching the second Bough. Dante awakens a new Seedling of Light ability that allows them to slow down time and catch up to the Erlking, with Meursault using the Chains of Others to hold him in place. The Sinners then realize the events can be traced back to whoever sparked Catherine's interest in Mirror research and involved her with N Corp.; Outis points out Nelly's strange behavior, and her suspicions are confirmed by the Erlking, who recounts how she invited him to the manor and introduced him to Isabella.

Nelly then frees the Erlking, and while he makes his way to the rooftop, she explains her motives: after receiving a Mirror from Hermann, she saw countless worlds in which she wasted her life away dragged into Heathcliff and Catherine's strife, a revelation which shook her to her core, and led her to attempt anything to change her fate. She thus gave the Mirror to Catherine, who, already heartbroken and weakened, spoke to someone on the other side, and began the creation of the laboratory: Nelly would help her bankrupt Hindley with the collaboration of the Erlking, and Catherine was able to purchase the manor. Afterwards, she was introduced to Hermann, who offered to help her with her Mirror World technology and her scientists. Linton agreed to the plan as well, purchasing a Golden Bough required for the experiments.

After her defeat, Nelly disparages Heathcliff, revealing she'd been the one to destroy Heathcliff's attempts to keep in contact with Catherine, out of disgust of their slothfulness and cowardice: in response to her betrayal, Heathcliff begins to sink into a deep despair, his consciousness slowly dragged away. Upon seeing him disappear, Nelly goes on to claim she'd brought upon a better ending, as he could never have changed his fate of becoming a devil like the Erlking. This causes the sixth lightning strike to hit the manor, and Heathcliff relives the conversation that motivated him to leave Wuthering Heights; Dante's powers allow him to stay longer, and learn that Catherine's intention had been to help him out of love. The diary itself then reveals another memory, which Heathcliff understands to be a sign of Catherine having always shared his feelings.

Returning with newfound determination, Heathcliff, the only person left in the will and therefore heir to Wuthering Heights, frees Nelly from her contract and marches ahead to the rooftop. After managing to get his hands on the second Bough, he stabs himself with it to drain it of its power, having understood that Catherine had thought it best to destroy herself for his sake, much like he and the Erlking had. Through the power of the Bough, he calls out to her and asks her to stop, as the final lightning strike hits the manor.

The final memory in the diary confirm his theory. Having witnessed many Mirror Worlds in which their lives ended in tragedy, Catherine sank further into depression, and eventually met an Identity who claimed to be every Catherine from every world, and convinced her that her very life was the cause of Heathcliff's misery. The Identity suggested Catherine help her kill all Catherines in order to free all Heathcliffs, leading to the creation of the laboratory. In the end, Hermann would provide her a second Golden Bough, obtained from Branch D-02, and ask to use the laboratory to create a "dough", which Catherine would agree to, before entering her coffin. Hermann would warn her the subterranean River that flowed beneath the manor might arrest her consciousness, and make her witness the events to follow. Hermann's words proved to be true, with her consciousness scattering across the manor, and her grief, in the form of lightning, powering the summoning itself.

While the summoning is completed, and Every Catherine takes over Catherine's body, Heathcliff's efforts allows her to resist and fight for control as the Sinners fight her and Erlking Heathcliff. Eventually, Catherine contacts Dante through their PDA. Using the opportunity, Heathcliff finally confesses how he feels to Catherine, much to her happiness. She then directs Dante to use the power of the Golden Boughs to erase all versions of herself from existence, an act which leads the Erlking to disappear, now without purpose.

With everyone wounded from the battle, Nelly takes the Bough attached to the rooftop, determined to bring it to Hermann, while the Sinners reclaim the one that was used to summon Every Catherine, now white and burned. In the aftermath, only Dante and Heathcliff have any recollection of Catherine existing; Heathcliff thus vows to reclaim the Bough and restore his Catherine.

Post-credits, the Sinners are tracking down a small-scale Distortion. Demian appears before Dante and presents them with a metaphor of finding a vast garden of roses after abandoning one once cared for by them. Dante replies that the rose they truly loved must've been the one they had left behind, and Demian comments on how similarly, Heathcliff and Catherine cared for each other instead of the infinite Heathcliffs and Catherines of the Mirror Worlds. When Dante asks about the other flowers, Demian states he'll answer when they can "draw him a sheep", before leaving.

entries.name: Intervallo IV: Timekilling Time
entries.content:
Intervallo IV: Timekilling Time is the fifth Intervallo in Limbus Company, taking place between Canto VI: The Heartbreaking and Intervallo IV: Murder on the WARP Express.

Following the chaos at the Wuthering Heights manor, the Sinners remain camped out in T Corp's Nest. Having begun to make a name for themselves, Don Quixote is delighted to find that they had been featured in the local newspaper for their conclusion of the mass kidnappings carried out by the Edgar Family. During, they are confronted by a T Corp. Collector who reveals they owe T Corp. a Time Tax of an entire 10,040,000,000 Ahn. No one understands either why they owe tax or what made the number so astronomically high, and Outis eventually steps forward and starts a fight with the Collectors. Vergilius intervenes and proposes going to T Corp.'s office to sort out the problem.

The Sinners are informed that the absurdly large tax was a result of Dante's Sapling of Light ability, "Pigritia", which had generated a large physical field of slowed time and disturbed the TT4 Protocol active at the Wuthering Heights manor. Whilst Vergilius and Faust have a meeting with the T Corp. staff in order to solve the problem, Meursault is approached by a talkative T Corp employee. He suggests they use his invention in order to pay off their debt with "time" instead of money. Unfortunately, the machine errors out and does nothing. When Faust and Vergilius return, they have a proposal for the Sinners. A Distortion known as the Time Ripper has been causing trouble by "killing" people's time, and it turns out that if the group can solve the case, their debts will be forgiven. Due to the prestigious nature of the "Special Investigator" badge which must be distributed to those working on the case, only four Sinners (including the manager) are permitted to work on it. Vergilius selects the Sinners for Dante, picking Rodion, Ryōshū, and Hong Lu. The rest of the Sinners are locked in a prison cell until the case is resolved. Before they leave, Don Quixote provides the detective team with outfits and a book written by "Agatha", a famous Grade 1 Fixer from the Seven Association. As the four set off, they are accompanied by the same talkative T Corp. employee from earlier.

The Sinners quickly warm up to their new assistant as he guides them to the killer's third victim, a factory owner named Bumble. The Sinners originally struggle to question him due to how much time he has, which allows him to condense many hours into a day and move faster than those who have less time. He is ultimately able to communicate with the detectives through a recorder. He tells them about how he was attacked by the Ripper whilst making his way through the street. During the interview he scolds his destitute factory workers and demands the impossible from them, agitating Rodion. Ryōshū mentions how the culprit must have moved faster than Bumble in order to strike him and kill his time. The detectives reach the conclusion that the culprit must despise the rich and status quo of T Corp., while also having plenty of hours to spare. The group sets off again.

Questioning a Collector reveals the Yurodiviye are active in T Corp. and have been committing petty thefts whilst providing detective services to the poor. Suddenly, Hong Lu is killed by an explosion caused by a handful of Yurodiviye activists and is swiftly revived by Dante. The three Sinners engage the activists in battle and defeat them, with the Yurodiviye fleeing upon realizing they were losing. Their T Corp. assistant questions Dante about their ability to "turn back the clock", wondering what machinery makes such a thing possible and where all the time comes from.

When the Sinners and their assistant return from their scuffle with the Yurodiviye, they find that the Collector from earlier had been attacked by the Ripper, her time now killed. They examine the scene and discuss how the woman appeared to be frozen in time. Then, Dante senses the Distortion nearby, and Ryōshū and Hong Lu run off to pursue the Yurodiviye sighted nearby. Ryōshū manages to capture the activist for interrogation, who uses an invention to summon all Yurodiviye in the area to come to his rescue. After their reinforcements are defeated, the activist eventually gives up the location of their hideout. Rodya, Hong Lu, and Ryōshū confront the Captain of the Yurodiviye and engage him in battle. Upon defeating him, they question the nature of his inventions and whether he's responsible for the time murders. He denies any guilt and insults the detectives for being amateurs. During, he mentions Sonya "the Saint" and asks if Rodya was really an old friend of his. She says yes, and the captain gives the detectives advice on the case.
